entries.name: jkudish/jev-browser (@jkudish/jev-browser)
entries.what: A Jev-driven headless-browser agent (Playwright/Chromium) exposed as an MCP stdio/HTTP server with a single tool, jev_navigate, plus a CLI, a library, and an optional SKILL.md. Given a task and a start URL, code owns the loop: each step it sends page state (up to 240 clickable, typeable and selectable elements) to Jev as a typed Choice ("which action") plus goal-reached and stuck probabilities, then executes the action in the browser. Jev never writes text, so a separate small "typing model" generates any string typed into a field. It returns the final page (text, markdown, html or aria), a step trace with confidences, console errors, cost and a screenshot. It is browser automation for web tasks, not a coding-assistant helper.
entries.autoInvocation: Model-discretion MCP tool, plus an optional skill description trigger. No hook, no proxy. Claude Code would only call jev_navigate when Claude judges that a real-website interaction is needed, and the user already has playwright MCP, WebFetch and Chrome tools that compete for that role. The bundled SKILL.md nudges the model toward jev_navigate for forms and JS flows but only after it is manually copied into ~/.claude/skills. It does not make Jev automatically assist coding decisions such as permissions, routing, review or classification.
security: API keys are read from environment variables only and never taken from argv, but the README's `claude mcp add ... -e` and JSON config examples put TYPESAFE_API_KEY in a config file. The README notes some MCP clients filter env and drop the key.

Serious prompt-injection surface: it browses arbitrary web pages and returns their text, markdown or html into Claude's context. The SKILL.md itself says to treat the page text as untrusted. It is an active browser (click, select, submit) and can perform consequential writes on real sites.

SECURITY.md admits pages it visits can reach private endpoints, so localhost and internal services are reachable via the start URL. It says to run it in a container or restricted network. This matters for client projects.

Password and cookie handling is unusually careful: handoff files (0700 dir, 0600 files, no symlinks, one-shot delete), JEV_PASSWORD_* and JEV_COOKIE_* env allowlist, exact-origin binding, multi-encoding redaction, screenshot suppression.

Install risk: the npm package has a postinstall (scripts/ensure-chromium.mjs) that runs `npx --yes playwright install chromium`. It also has a `prepare` build script and about 13 runtime deps, including the AI SDK for four providers, @typesafe-ai/sdk and @jkudish/jev-agent-tools, a 1-week-old single-author package.
The README's recommended `npx -y @jkudish/jev-browser` runs unpinned latest code with the user's keys on every start. Pin the version if it is used at all.
entries.dataEgress: To the judgment provider (OpenRouter POST /api/alpha/decisions with this key): the task text, the current URL and page state (page excerpt text, plus descriptions of up to 240 interactive elements) and the questions, on every step (up to 24 steps by default). To the typing provider (OpenRouter google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite by default if only an OpenRouter key is set, or OpenAI/Anthropic/Google if those keys are in the env): the task and field context, once per typed field. To the visited websites: normal browser traffic from the user's IP, plus any seeded cookies or passwords for the configured origin. It does NOT read the local repo, diffs or Claude's transcript on its own. Only what Claude puts in `task` or `start_url` leaves the machine, along with what the pages contain. Local files created: ~/.jev-browser/handoff only if the password flow is used.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open at the Claude Code level, because it is an on-demand tool. If the key is missing the tool returns a config error and the server does not break Claude. If OpenRouter fails or is slow, the transport throws 'OpenRouter decisions API HTTP <status>'. The run ends with status error and the tool returns isError. Runs have a hard wall-clock deadline (max_seconds default 180, cap 600) via an AbortController (src/navigate.ts:552), a step cap, and per-action Playwright timeouts of 4-30 s. Schema-invalid Jev answers stop the run before any action executes. Nothing blocks Claude's normal work, but a hung navigation can occupy a tool call for up to 3 to 10 minutes, and the README warns that client tool-call timeouts (60 s in the TS SDK) may need raising. If the typing model fails, fields are left empty with warnings.
entries.contextCost: 1 MCP tool (jev_navigate). Its description is about 1.1k chars, and the input schema (13 params including nested cookie_file/cookie_env objects, each with long descriptions) is about 5k chars, so roughly 1.5k to 1.8k tokens of tool definition (chars/4 estimate from src/index.ts:54-154). No server `instructions` field. No hooks inject text. Each call returns a large JSON trace (page content 8k to 16k chars or up to 1MB for html, plus per-step trace) and a base64 JPEG screenshot into context, so every use costs several thousand tokens. The optional SKILL.md is 5.6k chars, and only its frontmatter description (about 350 chars) is always loaded. Playwright MCP is already installed and overlaps in role.
pros: Genuine OpenRouter support in code, not just the README: alpha decisions endpoint with typesafe/jev-1.13, and one sk-or- key also covers the typing model (openrouter.js:5-27; navigate.ts:164).

Real, well-engineered Jev use: typed Choice actions plus calibrated goal and stuck probabilities gate the loop, and the returned step trace with confidences is auditable. It is one of the few Jev integrations that uses Jev for what it is good at, structured decisions, rather than chat.
Strong credential hygiene (handoff files, env allowlists, origin binding, redaction) and a hard wall-clock and step budget; the failure mode is a clean error, not a hang of Claude Code.
Active and popular for a 2-week-old repo: 297 stars, 27 forks, 67 commits, v0.8.1 released 2026-09-29, MIT, CI, and about 3.8k lines of tests including a live e2e suite.
Cheap per run (README claims about $0.0016 for a 4 s navigation) and only a single low-cost tool definition (about 1.7k tokens).
Useful niche for a web dev: verifying a deployed page, smoke-driving a login-walled staging app or a JS-only flow with an evidence trace (screenshot, console/network errors).
cons: Not a coding-workflow integration at all: it does not touch code, diffs, tests, permissions or Claude's decisions. It fails the user's core goal of Claude Code using Jev automatically to add value in daily coding.

Duplicates tools the user already has (playwright MCP with 30+ tools, WebFetch, Chrome) and its own SKILL.md says to prefer the client's own browser automation for local dev servers and signed-in profiles, which is most of a developer's use.
Auto-invocation depends entirely on Claude's discretion and competes with playwright MCP; the SKILL.md must be manually copied. It cannot be made deterministic without a custom hook.

Heavy, brittle install: npx -y of an unpinned package with a postinstall that runs `npx playwright install chromium`, roughly 13 dependencies, and single-author deps (@jkudish/jev-agent-tools is about 6 days old). The Playwright download duplicates what playwright MCP already has.

Sends page content and element lists to OpenRouter on every step, and typing prompts to whichever provider key is in the env (a stale OPENAI_API_KEY silently wins). Client sites and staging pages would leave the machine, which is a client-confidentiality concern.

Untrusted page content is returned straight into Claude's context, which is prompt injection exposure in bypass or auto permission mode. SECURITY.md also warns pages it visits can reach private endpoints on the local network.

OpenRouter Decisions API is alpha and adds a hop (the README itself recommends direct TypeSafe). Jev 'browser use' quality is claimed on Wikipedia and DuckDuckGo tasks and the README admits rough edges and thresholds tuned on those only.
Long-running tool calls (up to 180 to 600 s) can exceed client tool-call timeouts.
entries.verdict: Well built, honest and genuinely OpenRouter-capable, but it is a web-browsing agent that competes with the playwright MCP the user already runs, not a way to make Claude Code use Jev automatically for coding decisions. Skip it for the daily-coding integration. At most, install it pinned and opt-in later for occasional evidence-grade site checks, and never with client credentials.

entries.name: jev-browser
entries.what: Node MCP server (stdio) plus library and CLI for browser automation. Claude sends one-outcome goals (browser_do); the server describes the page in Playwright and calls Jev via the System One API with several noul/choice/score questions (which element, action, value, done, error, irreversible). Playwright then acts. It is a domain-specific browser tool, not a general coding aid.
entries.autoInvocation: Model-discretion MCP tool. Claude Code will only call it when a browser task arises, and it will compete with the existing playwright MCP. There are no hooks, no skill and no proxy, so it will not fire during ordinary coding.
security: API key read from env or from a .env in cwd or repo root by a hand-rolled parser (src/jev.mjs:17-22); the documented install passes it via 'claude mcp add -e TYPESAFE_API_KEY=key', which lands in ~/.claude.json in plaintext (not in the MCP process argv, but in the config file and at 'claude mcp add' command time in shell history)
Reading .env from process.cwd() means the server can pick up a project's .env, though it only extracts the TYPESAFE_API_KEY key name

Runs npx -y -p jev-browser at each launch: an unpinned npm package fetched at start unless pinned (supply-chain risk); no postinstall script in package.json, but playwright dependency plus a separate 'npx playwright install chromium' download
Drives a real Chromium with page.goto on any URL the LLM supplies (src/session.mjs:134), with no allowlist; a persistent profile via JEV_BROWSER_PROFILE keeps logins and cookies
Prompt-injection surface: browser_do returns page_text/candidates and visible_text from arbitrary web pages into Claude's context; page content is also sent to Jev as state

browser_do values can include credentials and are sent to Jev inside task.values (session.mjs:185-196, criteria truncated to 200 chars); browser_act upload takes an arbitrary local file path from the LLM
entries.dataEgress: To the Jev endpoint each round: goal text, the values map (including any passwords or emails the LLM passes), action history (last 12), diff from the previous page, and a description of the current page (element list with labels and state, visible text, counts, URL) as the System One 'state' (about 2.7k input tokens per call by NOTES.md). No source code, diffs or Claude tool outputs unless the LLM puts them in goal or values. The Chromium session also loads whatever sites are visited, and screenshots and snapshots go to Claude, not Jev.
entries.failureMode: Fail-closed per tool call: jev() retries twice with 0.8 s and 1.6 s backoff on network errors, 429 and 5xx, with a 60 s per-request timeout (src/jev.mjs:28,42,47); after that it throws and the MCP wrapper returns isError with the first line of the message (bin/jev-browser-mcp.mjs:26-27). Missing key gives an immediate error. This only breaks the browser tools, and Claude Code itself continues. Worst-case one browser_do stalls for up to about 3 minutes per Jev call.
entries.contextCost: 8 MCP tools. About 1.6k tokens of tool names, descriptions and schemas (about 6.4k chars in the registerTool block, chars/4), of which browser_do is about 500 tokens. No MCP server 'instructions' field. No hooks injected. Tool results are small JSON, but browser_snapshot and page_text can be large on big pages. The overlap with the already-installed Playwright MCP (about 25 tools) is significant.
pros: Real, working use of Jev's typed primitives (noul, choice, score) for a task where fast calibrated decisions fit; the design (LLM plans, Jev decides, code acts) is well documented in NOTES.md and RESULTS.md

OpenRouter switch needs no code change: src/jev.mjs:8-9 exposes JEV_API_URL and JEV_MODEL, and the key is only sent as a Bearer token, provided OpenRouter's /api/v1/systemone matches the TypeSafe schema
Small surface: 8 tools, about 1.6k tokens, no hooks, no instructions and no telemetry; MIT; only 1346 lines of code, which is easy to audit

Safety defaults: pauses before irreversible actions (needs_confirmation), dismisses confirm dialogs, reports likely_done instead of overclaiming; the test suite is offline and CI is present with OIDC provenance publishing
Claims about 5x fewer page tokens than a Playwright-MCP loop on the same tasks and 0 false 'done' across the runs, which is useful if the user does browser work often
cons: Narrow scope: browser automation only. It gives no Jev help for editing, review, routing, permissions or commits, so it doesn't meet 'Claude Code uses Jev whenever it adds value' for daily coding

Not automatic: it is a model-discretion MCP tool that competes with the already-installed playwright MCP (about 25 tools), so Claude will often pick playwright; there are no hooks or skills to steer it

Key variable is TYPESAFE_API_KEY only (jev.mjs:12); the OpenRouter key must be stored under that misleading name, and the documented 'claude mcp add -e KEY=...' writes it in plaintext to ~/.claude.json
OpenRouter compatibility of the /api/v1/systemone request and response schema is assumed, not proven by the code; the default is api.typesafe.ai and no OpenRouter path was tested by the author
Very young: created 2026-09-16, v0.1.1, 15 commits, 3 contributors, beta Jev backend; most of the authorship is one person and the benchmark is self-reported

Sends page content and any credentials in 'values' to a third-party model API (Jev/OpenRouter), and returns untrusted web text into Claude's context (prompt injection); the browser has no URL allowlist and browser_act upload accepts arbitrary local paths, which matters on client projects
npx -y fetches an unpinned package at each start unless the version is pinned; also needs a Chromium download (about 150 MB)
entries.verdict: A clean, small and honest Jev integration, but it only does browser automation and overlaps with the installed playwright MCP; it is optional at best, and does not answer the 'Jev used automatically in daily coding' goal. If installed, pin the version and route via JEV_API_URL/JEV_MODEL to OpenRouter after checking that the schema matches.

entries.name: jiawei686/jev-ultrafast-mcp
entries.what: Python MCP server (10 browser_* tools) that drives a local Chrome over CDP. Its main tool, browser_goal, runs a server-side loop. Each step it sends the page text, an element table, and the last 10 actions to Jev's decisions endpoint as typed Choice questions, then executes the chosen ref. Jev is used as a browser-action policy, not as a general coding decision service. Free direct tools (open, observe, act, assert, macro) work with no key.
entries.autoInvocation: Model-discretion MCP tools, strongly nudged. The server INSTRUCTIONS say 'Do not drive a task yourself, click by click; that is what this server is for', and the optional skill description triggers on any browser or URL-plus-action request. Nothing is deterministic, no hooks. It only fires on browser tasks, not on ordinary coding decisions.
security: OPENROUTER_API_KEY is read from env and sent as a Bearer header. It is not passed in argv by the server itself. It is only visible in argv if the host config or scripts/install.py bakes it in.
No shell execution or telemetry found in the package. subprocess is used only to launch Chrome (cdp.py:243), with output sent to DEVNULL.

Prompt-injection surface is real. Untrusted page text goes to the model, and the prompt tells it to treat page text as data (policy.py:30). The server limits agents to observed refs. It has no JS eval or click_at, JS assertions are off by default (JEVMCP_ALLOW_JS=0), and there are domain allow/deny lists and confirm patterns. Uploads are ON by default (JEVMCP_ALLOW_UPLOADS=1), so a hostile page could try to induce file uploads.

Persists a Chrome profile and macros under ~/.jev-ultrafast-mcp. Attach mode can drive the user's real logged-in Chrome (Chrome 144+ DevToolsActivePort). That is a large blast radius on client accounts.
Optional Chrome extension and mcpb/smithery packaging widen the surface. scripts/install.py edits other tools' config files, so review before running.
MIT licence. Single anonymous-ish maintainer, brand-new repo, 2 forks, 19 stars. No supply-chain track record.
entries.dataEgress: Per browser_goal step, sent to OpenRouter: page URL, title, up to about 6000 chars of page text (JEVMCP_MAX_TEXT), the full element list (ref, role, name, value, options, checked), and the last 10 actions (policy.py:355-389). If TYPE_TEXT or select is used, field name, options and goal go too. If TEXT_MODEL inherits OpenRouter, up to 6000 chars of page text plus goal go to the chat model. It does not send source code, diffs or Claude Code prompts, except whatever the goal string contains. Any logged-in page content (client dashboards, admin panels) is sent to OpenRouter and TypeSafe when the browser is in attach mode. The direct tools (open, observe, act, assert) make no external calls.
entries.failureMode: Fail-closed per call and non-fatal to Claude Code. The server imports and runs without a key. With no key, browser_goal returns 'turbo_unavailable' and executes nothing, so Claude falls back to the manual tools. The httpx timeout is 30 s, with 3 attempts and backoff on 429/503/529 (policy.py:153-174). Network errors return TurboUnavailable('Decision model unreachable; no action executed'). Malformed or unexpected responses are rejected the same way. Never blocks Claude's other tools.
entries.contextCost: 10 tools. Tool names, docstrings and args total about 8.5k chars, plus server INSTRUCTIONS of 2,015 chars, so about 2.1k tokens before JSON schema overhead. Realistic estimate is 2.5-3.5k tokens always resident (less if tool search defers MCP tools). The optional SKILL.md adds about 100 tokens to the description list. No hook-injected text.
pros: OpenRouter is a first-class provider in code: JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter plus OPENROUTER_API_KEY posts to https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions with the {model,state,questions} contract (config.py:83-118). No patching needed.
Fail-closed and isolated: with no key or with Jev down, browser_goal returns turbo_unavailable, executes nothing, and Claude falls back to manual tools. The server never breaks a session.

Uses Jev for what a System One model fits: Choice questions with per-option probabilities for 'which ref next', with bounded 30 s timeouts and retries. One of few real Jev integrations that actually runs a decision loop.
Server-side loop keeps page content out of Claude's context, and macro replay uses zero model calls. This is useful for repetitive web QA or check-in flows.
Safety rails are sensible: no arbitrary JS or coordinate clicks, ref-revalidation, JS assertions off by default, domain allow/deny lists, and code-checked verify assertions.
Direct tools need no key. The auto-trigger skill and server instructions mean Claude uses it without being told to.
cons: It is a browser-automation server. Jev is used only to pick clickable elements, so it does not touch coding decisions such as file routing, commit or test triage, or permission classification. It does not deliver the user's stated goal of Jev deciding when it adds value in Claude Code.

Overlaps the Playwright MCP the user already has. Two browser stacks compete for the same tasks, and the strong 'do not drive it yourself' instructions and skill can pull Claude away from Playwright or make it choose inconsistently.
Sends page text and element names (potentially from client apps or authenticated sessions in attach mode) to OpenRouter and TypeSafe. That is a client-confidentiality concern.

Very immature: created 2026-09-19, 81 commits from one author in 5 days, 19 stars, 2 forks, v0.1.5, beta. The CI unit-test step is continue-on-error. The author's 'the release the registry would accept' style suggests a rapid-fire, possibly AI-generated codebase (CHANGELOG is 109 KB).
About 2.5-3.5k tokens of always-resident context for 10 tools plus 2k chars of instructions, for a feature used only on browser tasks.

Real browser autonomy driven by an unverified small model (skeptics: possibly a router over a flash LLM) on untrusted pages. Uploads on by default, persistent profile, and attach-to-real-Chrome mode give prompt-injection consequences.
Needs a local Chrome, a paid OpenRouter credit purchase (no :free variant), and the TYPE_TEXT path needs a separate chat model, so it is not fully Jev-only.
Not verified by running; static read only. Live latency and quality are unknown.
entries.verdict: A real, well-guarded, fail-closed Jev integration with first-class OpenRouter support. It is a niche browser-automation tool that duplicates the user's Playwright MCP and does nothing for everyday coding decisions. It is worth trying in a sandbox for repetitive web flows, but not as the answer to 'Jev used automatically in Claude Code'.

entries.name: tontoko/jev-browser
entries.what: A Playwright-core based browser-automation SDK, persistent CLI and stdio MCP server (jev-browser-mcp). Roughly 50 MCP tools (browser_*): about 34 native Playwright ops that need no model (click, type, snapshot, assert, tabs, cookies, trace, route, pdf, evaluate...), plus Jev-backed tools (observe, act, extract, semantic_locate/compare/assert and their batch forms, run, resume). Jev is used only for Choice questions that pick one of the page's own candidate elements, options or values. It is a Playwright MCP / Stagehand replacement for browser QA, not a general coding-assistant hook. It has no hook, skill-trigger or proxy component, and it does nothing for code, diffs or Claude Code's own decisions.
interface: browser_click / browser_type / browser_hover / browser_drag / browser_press_key / browser_select_option / browser_check / browser_fill_form / browser_mouse / browser_wait_for / browser_handle_dialog / browser_file_upload / browser_downloads

browser_take_screenshot / browser_screenshot / browser_pdf / browser_resize / browser_console_messages / browser_network_requests / browser_storage / browser_cookies / browser_storage_state / browser_trace / browser_route
entries.autoInvocation: Model-discretion MCP tools only. Claude picks browser_* when a task involves a browser. The shipped skills/jev-browser/SKILL.md has a description, but there is no plugin manifest, so it would need manual copying to ~/.claude/skills. There is no deterministic hook, no proxy, and no trigger on plain coding work. It fires automatically only in the narrow sense that Claude will choose it for browser/E2E tasks instead of playwright MCP, and only if tool descriptions steer it there.
security: Key handling: the OpenRouter key would be passed via the MCP env block (JEV_ENDPOINT_API_KEY), not argv, so it is not visible in the process list. The key is only sent over HTTPS or loopback, or the call fails with CONFIG (decision.ts:47). Hosted keys are never sent to a custom base URL (decision.ts:44-45). The SDK is created with logLevel off and 0 retries (decision.ts:54-56).

No telemetry found: grep for telemetry/analytics in src came back empty. child_process is used only to fork the local session worker (sessions.ts:2) and to run 'playwright install' (install.ts:8). No postinstall script, and no curl|sh installer (README: 'no postinstall browser download').

Prompt-injection surface is large but inherent to browser tools. Web page text is untrusted and is fed to both Jev and Claude. SECURITY.md admits that labelling it as data 'is not a proof against prompt injection'. Jev can only choose among supplied candidates, so it cannot generate selectors or JS.

browser_evaluate and init_script are off unless --allow-evaluate. File upload is rooted at the cwd by default. Artifacts go to .jev-browser/artifacts with traversal and symlink refusal. Named CLI sessions listen on loopback with a bearer token, with private descriptor files in $TMPDIR.

Same as the existing playwright MCP: the browser can reach localhost and authenticated internal services. Client work run under bypass mode gives the model a real browser. SECURITY.md itself says to use isolated contexts and synthetic data.

Supply chain: 13-day-old repo with 11 stars, a single maintainer, not on npm. The lockfile and a pinned SDK help, but you would be running a very new codebase (about 4.6k lines src plus dependencies) with browser powers. Author bot commits are auto-release.
entries.dataEgress: Only when a Jev-backed tool (observe, act, extract, semantic_*, run, resume) runs. Then the natural-language instruction, page URL and title, visible semantic text (each string truncated to 700 chars), element names, row/list/form context, options, href evidence, the action history and the input binding names go to the configured endpoint. That would be openrouter.ai and then TypeSafe (the OpenRouter model page states the data policy). The caller's `values` are withheld by default unless listed in semanticInputs. Text typed into editors and textareas is omitted from neighbouring-context strings. Values echoed by the page, or quoted in the instruction, can still leak, and SECURITY.md says redaction is best-effort. Native tools (snapshot, click, assert, screenshot...) send nothing to Jev. Source code, diffs, repo files and Claude's conversation never go to Jev, because the tool only sees browser pages. Expected literals in semantic_assert are sent.
entries.failureMode: Fail-closed per Jev-backed call but isolated. decision.ts:54 sets timeout 15s (options.timeoutMs) with 0 SDK retries. Single-op decisions do not retry. Goals may retry read-only decisions up to decisionRetries=2. On error it throws BrowserError PROVIDER_ERROR (retryable for 408/429/5xx) or INVALID_DECISION, and the MCP tool returns isError JSON to Claude, which can fall back to native tools (snapshot, click). A missing key only fails the Jev tools (CONFIG). Native tools keep working. Mutations are never auto-replayed. MCP calls are serialized in a queue (mcp.ts:16-30), so one slow Jev call blocks all later browser calls until timeout or cancel. Nothing outside the browser tools is affected, so Claude Code as a whole never blocks on Jev.
entries.contextCost: About 50 tools (34 native schemas plus goto/snapshot/observe/act/extract/6 semantic/run/resume/screenshot/close/screen). src/native-schemas.ts (12.9 KB), commands.ts (16.2 KB) and screen-tool.ts (3 KB) hold about 32 KB of schema and description source. Once rendered to JSON Schema with per-argument descriptions this is roughly 10-15k tokens (my estimate; I did not run the server) of always-on tool definitions if not deferred. Claude Code 2.1.x tool-search deferral may reduce this, but the user already has playwright MCP, which loads about 30 tools. Running both would duplicate the browser surface. The server sets no MCP 'instructions'. No hook-injected text, since it has no hooks.
pros: Genuinely uses Jev for what it is suited to: typed Choice questions over a constrained candidate set (which element or option to act on), with confidence thresholds and inconclusive-never-passes semantics (docs/semantic-verification.md). This is a sound use of a System One model, not a chat substitute.

OpenRouter-compatible with config only: the SDK 0.6.0 appends /v1/systemone to baseURL, which matches OpenRouter's documented System One API. JEV_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api, JEV_ENDPOINT_API_KEY and JEV_MODEL are enough. The key stays out of argv.

Careful data-boundary design: values withheld by default, hosted keys never sent to a custom URL, no telemetry, no postinstall, logging off. The SECURITY.md is honest about limits. 34 native tools work with no key and no egress.

Broad, well-tested surface for a 13-day-old repo: 96 test files, a 7-way OS/browser CI matrix, Apache-2.0, SHA-pinned Actions. A batch API (browser_run, semantic_*_batch) reduces model round trips. Deterministic browser_assert sits beside semantic assertions.
Useful for web E2E and UX verification of the user's own frontend (dougthepug/empat design skills suggest UI work), especially semantic assertions on changing copy.
cons: Wrong layer for the stated goal. It only helps when a browser task occurs. It does nothing for code review, routing, permission gating, commit classification or context triage. Jev never sees code, so it adds no value to daily coding.

Overlaps and would duplicate the existing playwright MCP (about 50 tools versus about 30). It adds a second Chromium stack and a 10-15k token tool-definition footprint unless one of them is removed or deferred.

Not automatic in the sense the user wants. There is no hook or trigger. Claude uses it only if it prefers browser_* here over playwright MCP tools, and it can still choose native or Playwright tools, so Jev calls happen only inside the Jev-backed subset.

Distribution is poor: GitHub Release tarball only, no npm, with peer deps (playwright-core, zod) and a browser download. Setup is per-project or a manual global install. The 13-day-old, single-maintainer, 11-star repo with about 12 releases and heavy bot and AI-authored commits is high churn (pre-1.0, API and removed adapters already noted in docs/migration.md).

OpenRouter path is untested by the project (no OpenRouter mention in code, CI runs keyless). The response-envelope assumptions (usage.input_tokens/output_tokens, model) are unverified against OpenRouter. The model id format (jev-1.13 vs typesafe/jev-1.13) needs a manual check.

Page content plus client-site data (URLs, titles, visible text, form context) would leave the machine to OpenRouter and TypeSafe. That is a compliance question for client projects, and the browser runs with full network reach in bypass mode. Prompt injection from pages remains an inherent risk.
One slow Jev call blocks the serialized MCP queue up to the 15s timeout. Only Choice questions are used, so the Noul and Score primitives, which are the more interesting parts of Jev, go unused.
entries.verdict: Well-built and honest, but it is a browser-automation tool that happens to use Jev for element selection. It does not deliver automatic Jev use across everyday Claude Code work, and it overlaps the existing playwright MCP. Worth trying (about 5 minutes of config) only if the user does a lot of browser E2E or UI verification. For the stated goal, look at hook-based candidates such as permission-prompt gating instead. If adopted, use it as a replacement for playwright MCP, not in addition.

entries.name: nexibeo/jev-browser-control
entries.what: Browser-automation MCP server (20 tools; Playwright-driven own Chrome, or a Chrome extension bridge) plus optional skill and subagent. Claude plans; Jev (via OpenRouter Decisions API, choice/noul primitives) picks each click/type/scroll from a numbered-element page snapshot. It is a Jev-powered web-browsing sub-agent. It is not a general coding-assistant integration: Jev is used only to choose browser actions and to verify page statements.
entries.autoInvocation: Model-discretion MCP tools plus a skill-description trigger (SKILL.md: 'use when a task needs a browser ... or user says use Jev') and a Claude Code subagent whose description invites delegation for browser tasks. No hooks, no transparent proxy. Automatic only in the sense that Claude chooses it whenever a browser task arises; it never triggers on ordinary coding.
security: API key: passed via `claude mcp add -e` it is stored in ~/.claude.json env (not argv), and it can be kept out of Claude config entirely in ~/.jev-browser-control/config.env (mcp/lib/config.mjs:1-10). Key is sent only as Bearer to the configured endpoint (provider.js:43).

Supply chain: the recommended install pulls an npx tarball from jevbrowsercontrol.com, not npm or a pinned git commit; the served artifact cannot be verified against the repo. Postinstall scripts: none in mcp/package.json. Single dependency playwright-core.

Prompt-injection surface: page text from arbitrary websites goes both to Jev and (via browser_read/jev_task results) into Claude's context. The README admits injection can still mislead the model. Stop gates in code (buy/pay/send/post/delete confirmation, cost/step/time limits, blocked sites) mitigate but JBC_CONFIRM_IRREVERSIBLE=0 disables them.

jev_task is annotated destructiveHint/openWorldHint; it performs real clicks and typing in a persistent logged-in Chrome profile (~/.jev-browser-control/chrome-profile). Extension mode acts inside the user's real profile with all logins.

Bridge binds 127.0.0.1 only; extension origin check and peer token. Optional remote relay mode exposes the browser to cloud apps via jevbrowsercontrol.com if enabled in the extension (off by default).
Sends X-Title/HTTP-Referer headers to OpenRouter (attribution). No telemetry found in mcp/ (grep for fetch/telemetry/analytics/sendBeacon: nothing besides provider.js).
entries.dataEgress: To OpenRouter (or jevbrowsercontrol.com if a jbc_ key is used): the task goal and details text, the numbered-element snapshot of the current page (roles, labels, values, nearby card text, URL; password and file fields excluded), operation history; and for typed values, the goal/details/field context to the inception/mercury-2.5 chat model. No source code, diffs or Claude conversation leave the machine unless the user types them into a goal or they are visible on a web page in the driven browser. Page text and screenshots also flow back into Claude Code context (and to Anthropic).
entries.failureMode: Fail-soft per call: provider.js retries network errors (3 attempts, ~5 s backoff) and 429/503/529 twice; then throws a ProviderError which the tool returns as an error result. Missing key: jev_* tools error while browser_* tools keep working. No global timeout on Jev calls in provider.js (fetch has no AbortSignal timeout unless the caller passes one); jev_task tool timeout is 35 min; run limits default 30 steps / 120 s / $0.10. Nothing is blocking Claude Code generally, since it is an opt-in tool server, not a hook.
entries.contextCost: 20 tools in browser mode (18 in extension mode). Tool definitions JSON is 12,119 chars, roughly 3,000 tokens (chars/4). MCP server instructions about 1,300 chars (~330 tokens). Total about 3.3k tokens per session if tools are not deferred (with Tool Search deferral just names). Optional skill description adds ~100 tokens; optional subagent adds its tools list. No hook-injected text. Duplicates the user's existing playwright MCP (26 tools) functionally.
pros: Genuinely wired to OpenRouter: default provider hits https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions with OPENROUTER_API_KEY and model ~typesafe/jev-latest (provider.js:8,27; config.mjs:48-50), so no patching needed.

Uses Jev exactly per its design: typed choice for operation/target and noul for goal-done, mapped by code to element numbers so Jev output never becomes selectors or code (policy.js:111-123). One of the few real Jev integrations with recorded traces and cost figures (results/*.json).
Real, deterministic-ish guardrails in code: irreversible-click confirmation, cost/step/time budgets ($0.10 default), blocked-sites list, stale-element re-check, independent goal check.
Cheap: repo benchmarks claim about $0.006 for three tasks vs $0.15-$1.13 for LLMs doing the clicking (author-run, unverified independently).
No hooks and no proxy, so it cannot interfere with the user's secret-guard, GitNexus or caveman hooks; only 1 npm dependency; MIT.
Browser mode uses its own Chrome profile, isolating client logins from the main profile.
cons: Solves browser automation, not coding: Jev never sees code, diffs or repo state, so it adds no value to the user's daily edit/test/refactor loop. Only useful on the occasional web task (checking a deployed UI, filling a console form).
Overlaps with the already-installed playwright MCP, so it would add 20 more tools (~3.3k tokens/session) for a niche.
Not automatic in the way the user wants beyond Claude's discretion: it is a tool set, not a hook; Claude will use Playwright or this depending on descriptions and may never pick it.

Very young and single-author: repo created 2026-09-19, 10 commits, 1 contributor, 5 stars, no releases, no CI; package.json 'check' script points to a missing file. Alpha quality; README benchmark numbers are self-reported.

Recommended install downloads a tarball from the author's website rather than npm or a pinned commit, so the shipped code cannot be verified against the repo; with the user's bypass-permission mode this is a supply-chain and unattended-click risk on client sites.
Adds a second, non-Jev LLM call (inception/mercury-2.5 via OpenRouter) for typed text, and the jevbrowsercontrol.com credits path routes traffic via a third-party relay at 5x price.
Uses the alpha Decisions API only; no use of /api/v1/systemone, no TYPESAFE_API_KEY support in the MCP server (custom endpoint only in the extension settings).
Provider has no per-request fetch timeout, so a hung OpenRouter request stalls a jev_task until the step/time budget check, bounded by the tool timeout of 35 min.
entries.verdict: A real, OpenRouter-native Jev integration, but for web-browser automation and not for coding decisions, so it does not deliver the user's goal of Jev being used automatically inside daily coding. Consider only as an optional, cloned-and-reviewed add-on for occasional browser tasks, not as the main Jev integration.

entries.name: brnyxx/jev-ra (jev-ra)
entries.what: A Python browser-automation MCP server + CLI (PyPI/npm launcher `jev-ra`) that drives a real local Chrome over CDP (via browser-harness). Each browser step sends a snapshot (goal, URL, title, up to 6000 chars of page text, element list, recent actions) plus typed Choice/Noul questions to Jev, which picks the operation, target and goal-achieved probability. Purpose: fast web-browsing/UI automation for coding agents (compares itself with browser-use). Jev is used as a step-by-step browser decision model, NOT for coding decisions.
entries.autoInvocation: Model-discretion MCP tool only. No hook, no skill trigger, no proxy. Claude Code will call browser_* only when the task involves browsing a website, and it will choose between these and the existing playwright MCP by tool descriptions. `jev-ra skill` can print AGENTS.md for saving as a skill, which would nudge it, but it is still model-discretion. It gives Jev no role in coding decisions (routing, commit, permission, test-triage).
security: API key: `jev-ra install claude` runs `claude mcp add jev-ra -s <scope> -e OPENROUTER_API_KEY=<real key> -- uvx jev-ra mcp` via subprocess.run (cli.py:366-377,403), so the key is in argv (visible in process list) briefly and is stored in plaintext in Claude Code's MCP config (~/.claude.json env block). Output is redacted and the displayed command shows $VAR, but argv exposure is real. Mitigation: register manually with the key from a wrapper or config.json (~/.config/jev-ra/config.json is also read, cli skips forwarding when key comes from config.json).
No telemetry/analytics found in grep of jev_ra/, npm/, scripts/. Only outbound calls: the decision endpoint, DuckDuckGo html for search, target sites via Chrome, optional text helper.

Prompt injection: page text is untrusted; SECURITY.md and questions.py state this, and the model only picks among observed operations/element indexes (no selectors, coordinates or JS from model output); password/file/hidden inputs excluded from snapshot; will not invent typed text. Residual risk: injection could steer clicks on legitimate-looking controls; tool results (page text up to 3000 chars in browser_observe, 1500 in summaries) flow into Claude's context as untrusted content. SECURITY.md advises a dedicated Chrome profile not signed into anything valuable.

Shell execution: subprocess used only for Chrome launch (chrome.py:315-332, launches Chrome, may retry with --no-sandbox), desktop notification (present.py), and `claude mcp add`. npm launcher (npm/bin/jev-ra.js:62) can offer `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh` after prompting (--yes skips; --no-install refuses). PyPI install itself has no postinstall hook.

Recommended runtime `uvx jev-ra mcp` fetches unpinned latest from PyPI on each cache miss (supply-chain exposure from a 12-day-old package by one author); pin `uvx --from jev-ra==0.2.8`. Dependencies: browser-harness[mcp] <0.2 and httpx (uv.lock committed, dependabot on).
Drives a real Chrome with CDP; file:// URLs blocked unless JEV_RA_ALLOW_FILE_URLS=1; `serve` HTTP mode binds 127.0.0.1 with bearer keys. MIT license, SECURITY.md with private advisory route.
entries.dataEgress: To OpenRouter (then TypeSafe/Jev) per browser step: the goal string you gave, current page URL, title, up to 6000 chars of visible page text, element list (roles, labels, values incl. current field values), last 10 actions (incl. typed text), names of supplied values (values_available) but not their contents (policy.py:209-231). Also a random session_id. Bearer key in header. Never sends source code, diffs or Claude's conversation unless Claude copies them into the goal/values. DuckDuckGo receives search queries; visited websites see the browser. Page contents of authenticated pages (if the Chrome profile is logged in) would go to OpenRouter/TypeSafe. A page showing a CAPTCHA/check is deliberately not sent (CHANGELOG 0.2.7).
entries.failureMode: Fail-loud per tool call, not a hook, so nothing global blocks. DecisionClient timeout 25 s per request (httpx), retries once after 0.5 s on 429/500/502/503/529, then raises JevUnavailable; 401/403 -> JevAuthError; bad/unnormalized probabilities -> JevBadResponse (strict validation of sums, choice = argmax). agent.py:525-538 turns these into run escalations (invalid_decision / provider_error) returned to Claude, which can fall back to direct browser_click/type tools (which never call Jev). Run budget default 40 steps / 80 decisions / 120 s (config.py:91-93). Missing key: ConfigError only when a Jev-using tool runs; server still starts and direct tools work.
entries.contextCost: 14 MCP tools (browser_open, run, act, search, observe, extract, click, type, select, scroll, press, wait, screenshot, close). Approx 1.3-1.8k tokens of tool names+descriptions+schemas (short docstrings, optional args; estimate chars/4 from mcp_server.py). Server 'instructions' ~50 tokens (mcp_server.py:36-38). No hooks, no injected hook text. Tool results add context when used: browser_observe returns up to 3000 chars text + element lines, summaries 1500 chars. If claude-code Tool Search defers MCP tools, cost is lower. Overlaps functionally with the user's existing playwright MCP (~25 tools, larger).
pros: Genuine, working OpenRouter integration: default route when OPENROUTER_API_KEY is set, uses typesafe/jev-1.13 on /api/alpha/decisions with session_id (config.py:11-13,125-133; client.py:116-122), tests cover key precedence and route selection (tests/test_config.py, test_client.py).

Real use of Jev's typed primitives (Choice for operation/target/value, Noul for prev_ok/goal_achieved) with strict client-side validation of probabilities (client.py:60-103), i.e. the closest thing found to a faithful Jev design pattern.

Solid engineering for a 12-day-old repo: 960 test functions across ~100 test files, CI matrix on Python 3.12-3.14 with real headless Chrome, ruff/ty, dependabot, SECURITY.md, CHANGELOG, tagged releases (0.2.8), PyPI + npm launcher, MIT.

Safety design: model can only pick among observed elements, passwords/file/hidden inputs never observed, no invented input, pacing per host, human-handoff for CAPTCHAs, file:// blocked by default, no telemetry found.
Failure is contained: provider errors become structured escalations; direct tools (click/type/observe/extract) never call Jev so browser use degrades gracefully.
Small tool surface (14) and tiny server instructions, lazy startup.
cons: Not a coding-workflow integration: Jev only decides browser clicks. Nothing for routing, permission decisions, test triage, commit classification, code review gating. Fit for a daily coding loop is limited to occasional web tasks.

Not automatic in the sense the user wants: only a model-discretion MCP tool; Claude must choose it over the already-installed playwright MCP, and the user asked for Claude to use Jev when it adds value without prompting. No hook/skill trigger shipped.
Redundant with playwright MCP already configured; adds a second browser stack (separate Chrome profile) and its own Chrome launch/--no-sandbox fallback.
README's own known-gaps: real-site corpus passes 102/120 (85%) vs a stated 90% bar; benchmark speedups are self-reported, single machine, browser-use compared with its single recorded run.
Sends goal text, page URL/title/6000 chars of page text and field values to OpenRouter/TypeSafe every step; unsuitable for logged-in or client-confidential pages without a dedicated profile.

`install claude` puts the raw OpenRouter key in argv of `claude mcp add` and persists it in plaintext in Claude Code's config env; recommended `uvx jev-ra mcp` is unpinned PyPI code from a single-author package created 2026-09-18 (198 of 200 commits by one person, 5 stars).
Depends on the alpha Decisions endpoint (/api/alpha/decisions); could break as OpenRouter's alpha route changes. Jev has a 32k context, page text is truncated to 6000 chars.
Quality of Jev decisions unverified independently; skeptic claim (router-like behavior) not tested here.
entries.verdict: Best-in-class example of a well-built OpenRouter-native Jev integration, but it is a browser-automation tool that overlaps the user's playwright MCP, uses Jev only inside web tasks, and is invoked at Claude's discretion, so it does not deliver 'Claude Code uses Jev automatically for coding'. Worth installing only as an optional, pinned, dedicated-profile web tool; not the core integration.

entries.name: cooper667/jev-playwright
entries.what: Claude Code/Codex plugin running plain-English browser QA checklists via Playwright; Jev (typesafe/jev on Cloudflare Workers AI) picks elements and judges verify steps; returns one verdict line.
entries.autoInvocation: skill trigger after UI changes / subagent delegation
pros: Concept fits self-verification: 24-step flow in ~35 s for ~1 cent, verdict + screenshots keeps context small
Logs in through app e2e fixture; PR how-to-test as checklist
cons: Requires Cloudflare Workers AI account/token, no OpenRouter path
Repo has only README + skills (minimal tests visible); 3 stars, 6 days old
Sends page accessibility trees to Cloudflare; overlaps Playwright MCP

entries.name: krw82/jev-playwright-mcp
entries.what: A stdio MCP proxy that spawns the official @playwright/mcp 0.0.81 as a child, re-exposes all its tools unchanged, and adds Jev (System One Choice/Noul/Score) judgments: page-state triage (login_wall/captcha/error/paywall...) via a <jev-insights> block appended to tool results, prompt-injection span masking in page text, goal-based snapshot pruning, and pre-call risk gating of click/type/upload-style calls. Without a key it is a pure passthrough of Playwright MCP. It is a browser-automation guard, not a coding-workflow tool.
entries.autoInvocation: Model-discretion MCP tool layer with transparent proxying: Claude calls the usual Playwright tools and Jev logic runs inside the proxy on every browser call with no prompting (triage/masking/gating are automatic once the key is set). Only browser_set_goal is optional model-driven. It fires only when Claude uses the browser, never on ordinary code editing, searching, or reviewing.
security: API key is read from env (or a package-root .env, gitignored) and sent only as a Bearer header to api.typesafe.ai (client.ts:234-240); not exposed as a tool or passed to the child browser per README. Not in the server's own argv, so not visible in ps for the proxy.

Prompt-injection surface is the tool's whole purpose: page text is untrusted and is sent to Jev inside `state` with a note that it is untrusted; Jev returns only typed probabilities, so no free-text injection back. Gate inputs (args, page excerpt, goal) are explicitly treated as untrusted (gate.ts:120-135). Masking is probabilistic, and README itself says confidence is not permission.
Insight markers in page text are neutralized so a page cannot forge <jev-insights> (contracts.ts:309-316).

Deterministic block on browser_run_code_unsafe regardless of Jev (though the user's current playwright server exposes it and this replaces that). Note that browser_evaluate is not in blockTools by default, so arbitrary in-page JS still possible unless gated.

No shell execution beyond spawning the pinned upstream @playwright/mcp and tsx child; no postinstall/preinstall scripts found in package.json or lockfile; no curl|sh installer. Does not phone home besides the Jev endpoint; no telemetry found.

Supply chain: single-author 2-star repo, 1 commit, unpublished; runs from a local clone with tsx TypeScript loader. Pin to the commit hash db7762f and review before use. A hidden .env in the package root is auto-loaded (JEV_MCP_NO_ENV_FILE=1 to disable).
entries.dataEgress: Only when a TypeSafe key is set: to api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone the proxy sends (a) up to a text_excerpt of each browser tool response (detectors.ts:311 `ctx.text.slice(0, TEXT_EXCERPT_CHARS)`) with url and title, (b) candidate injection sentences found by local heuristics (max 32), (c) region labels and 240-char excerpts of accessibility snapshot regions for pruning (prune.ts:196-201, batch up to 40) plus the session goal string, (d) for gated calls: tool name, compacted arguments (element, text typed, url, value, filename, ref; head+tail 120 chars each) and a 300-char excerpt of the previous page (gate.ts:109-121). So page content and text the agent types into forms (which may include credentials or client data) leave the machine. No source code, diffs or non-browser tool output is sent, because it only wraps Playwright. Not routed via OpenRouter as shipped.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open. Jev errors, malformed responses, and exhausted budget all fall back to passthrough (README degradation matrix; gate.ts:191 no verdict means allow; toRiskVerdict returns needs_confirmation on bad shape). Per-request timeout 10 s (client.ts:21), up to 2 retries with 500 ms-5 s backoff honoring Retry-After up to 60 s (client.ts:22-28), so a degraded Jev could add roughly 10 s x 3 attempts plus backoff (~35 s worst case per call) before falling open, an undesirable stall on a gated browser action. Session budget cap default $1.
entries.contextCost: Low, and net-neutral if it replaces the existing playwright MCP. Adds 2 tools (browser_set_goal, browser_jev_status), roughly 250-350 tokens of schema, plus a server `instructions` string of about 300 chars (~80 tokens, proxy.ts:249-253). Tool list of Playwright itself is unchanged (duplicated if both servers are kept: doubles ~25 browser tools, so it should replace, not join). Per-response, appends a <jev-insights> block (one-line hint, up to 3 masked excerpts), tens of tokens; pruning with a goal can save tokens on big snapshots. No hooks.
pros: Genuinely automatic: drop-in replacement for the existing `playwright` MCP with identical tool names and schemas (proxy.ts:6), so no prompt changes and Claude never has to be told to use Jev.

Uses Jev for what a typed calibrated classifier suits: injection Noul scan on untrusted page text, page-state Choice, risk Choice for browser actions; outputs are constrained to probabilities so the guard itself can't be prompt-injected into free text.

Sound engineering for a PoC: fail-open with retries honoring Retry-After, response schema validation, content-hash cache, $1 session budget, off/annotate/gate modes, deterministic blockTools for browser_run_code_unsafe, pinned @playwright/mcp version, marker forgery protection.
Cheap: input-only pricing at ~$0.042/1M; typical call fractions of a cent.
No postinstall scripts, no shell-out beyond the pinned child, MIT license, sizable test suite with stubbed Jev.
Relevant to a user with client projects: shields agent from hostile page content when browsing staging/third-party sites via Playwright, and gating protects against accidental destructive clicks.
cons: Browser-only: does nothing for the user's daily coding (editing, grep, tests, git, PR review). Fires only when Playwright is used.

No OpenRouter support: endpoint hard-coded to https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone (client.ts:20), only TYPESAFE_API_KEY/JEV_MCP_API_KEY, default model `jev-latest`. Using the user's OpenRouter key requires forking; and OpenRouter schema parity for /api/v1/systemone was not verified.
Very immature: 1 commit, 1 author, 2 stars, created 13 days before the audit, no releases, no CI, not on npm; needs manual git clone + npm install and tsx-at-runtime (or manual build).
Page text and text typed into form fields (possibly credentials/client data) egress to a third party (TypeSafe) beyond Anthropic; relevant for client work.
Gate fails open: if Jev is down or slow the destructive-action check is silently skipped; worst-case stall of ~30 s per call from 10 s timeout x 3 attempts + backoff.

Gating and masking are LLM probabilities; browser_evaluate (arbitrary JS) is not hard-blocked by default; only browser_run_code_unsafe is. Injection masking claims are unverified against real attacks, and Theo's skepticism about Jev's actual model is unaddressed.
Replaces rather than complements the existing playwright server, so needs config swap; keeping both would duplicate ~25 tools of context.

Comments/docs partly in Korean; single maintainer bus-factor; API pinned to @playwright/mcp 0.0.81 which lags the user's current tool set (e.g. browser_find/browser_drop appear in the user's server), so swapping may drop tools.
entries.verdict: A well-built but narrow, brand-new Playwright guard proxy: it is the only candidate that makes Jev run automatically, but only during browser use, and it is hard-wired to TypeSafe rather than OpenRouter. Worth a fork-and-pin only if you regularly let Claude browse untrusted pages; not a solution for daily coding.

entries.name: dtduc-git/jevnav
entries.what: A Python Playwright-based browser automation MCP server / CLI / pytest plugin / GitHub Action. Jev (System One Choice primitive) is used only to pick which page element an intent refers to (with a probability), a confidence gate (auto/review/blocked) decides whether to act, and every decision is traced to JSONL for offline replay in CI. It is a browser-testing/agent tool, not a coding-assistant helper. 33 MCP tools (browse, goal, goto, page_state, summary + fill_form, upload_files, press_key, read_js, route, emulate, lighthouse, tabs, screenshot, etc.).
interface: fill_form, upload_files, press_key, drag, scroll, resize, emulate, route/unroute, dialog_policy, read_js, wait_for, new_page/select_page/close_page/tabs
console, network, network_detail, dialogs, outline, styles, perf_metrics, heap_snapshot, lighthouse, screenshot, trace_start/trace_stop
entries.autoInvocation: Model-discretion MCP tool only. Claude would call browse/goal only when a task involves driving a web page; it never fires for ordinary coding, edits, search or commit decisions. There are no hooks, skills or proxy.
security: License Apache-2.0
API key read from TYPESAFE_API_KEY env or ~/.config/typesafe/apikey.txt (cli.py:36-39); passed via MCP env block so it is not in argv; sent as Bearer header only to TYPESAFE_BASE_URL
No telemetry/analytics/hosted component (SECURITY.md); grep found none

33 MCP tools give the agent a full browser: read_js runs arbitrary JS in-page (disable with --no-eval), route/emulate/upload_files, goto to any http(s) URL (file:// blocked unless --allow-file-urls); with --cdp/--user-data-dir it can act as the user's logged-in sessions

Prompt-injection surface: web page text and element names flow to the agent via page_state/outline and into the Jev question; gating covers only browse/goal/intent variants, direct primitives run ungated (SECURITY.md 'MCP primitives')
lighthouse tool shells out to 'npx -y lighthouse@<pinned>' (mcp.py:~960-975) -> runtime npm fetch/execute
entries.dataEgress: Per Jev decision to TypeSafe (or OpenRouter if repointed): page URL, page title, candidate element list (roles, accessible names, hrefs, placeholders, current field values with password fields masked), the intent string; goal loop additionally sends up to 700 chars of visible page text and the goal string/context values. No source code, diffs, file contents, prompts or Claude Code tool outputs are sent, only what the browser page exposes. Screenshots, cookies, storage never sent. Also the page contents reach Claude via tool results (outline/page_state/console/network) as with any browser MCP.
entries.failureMode: Fail-closed per step but non-fatal to the session: on JevError (missing key, HTTP error, transport error after retries) the decision is recorded as failed_decision with verdict 'blocked' and nothing is executed (decide.py:74-87; SECURITY.md verdicts). Client uses httpx timeout=60s default with retry+exponential backoff on retryable statuses and transport errors (jevassert client.py:80-141), so a slow/down Jev can stall a browse call up to minutes. Missing key does not fail server start; only Jev-deciding tools error. Non-Jev tools keep working. Not on any hook path, so it never blocks ordinary coding.
entries.contextCost: 33 MCP tools; tool descriptions/docstrings/param signatures ~12.4k chars by rough extraction (~3.1k tokens) plus JSON schemas, so realistically ~4-6k tokens loaded whenever the server is enabled (deferred/ToolSearch mode lowers this). No MCP server 'instructions' field found (no instructions= in mcp.py). No hooks, so no per-turn injected text. Overlaps heavily with the existing playwright MCP (~25 tools), doubling browser tool surface.
pros: Genuinely integrates Jev (Choice primitive with calibrated probabilities) in a sensible way: element selection + confidence gate, which matches Jev's typed-decision design
Endpoint and key are configurable: TYPESAFE_BASE_URL + /v1/systemone matches OpenRouter's System One path, so OpenRouter routing is likely a pure env change (no fork needed)
Apache-2.0, no telemetry, key not in argv when passed through MCP env, sensible file-root/URL scheme/--no-eval hardening, pinned lighthouse version
Decent test suite (~256 test functions across 15 files), CI with lint+format+pytest and a replay job, PyPI releases (19 versions), MCP registry entry
Useful side features for frontend work: outline/styles/diff give computed-style facts of a running app vs mockup; replay is offline and needs no key
Low cost per decision (~$0.00004, ~330ms claimed) and a Jev failure blocks only that step, not Claude Code
cons: Only helps when Claude drives a browser; a daily backend/general-coding workflow rarely triggers it, so it is not a general Jev integration into Claude Code decisions (permissions, routing, code choices)
Auto invocation is only model discretion of a browser tool; it will not use Jev 'automatically' for anything else
Duplicates the already-installed playwright MCP: two browser MCPs, ~33 more tools (~4-6k tokens) and Claude must choose between them; needs a separate Chromium download
Repo created 2026-09-21 (9 days old), 74 commits in 6 days, 2 stars, 0 forks, single author (aliases), Development Status Alpha; jevassert dependency also new single-author package

OpenRouter path unverified and non-obvious: hard-coded default model 'jev-latest' is not an OpenRouter id (need --model typesafe/jev-1.13), OpenRouter key must be stored in TYPESAFE_API_KEY, response schema parity not confirmed

Large attack surface for a client-project environment: read_js, route, upload_files, arbitrary goto, --cdp/--user-data-dir can act as logged-in user; prompt injection from pages; sessions leave jevnav-session.trace.jsonl in project dirs (risk of committing it)
Runtime side effects: npx lighthouse fetch, sends page URL/titles/element text/field values (client sites) to a third-party model API
Retry/backoff with 60s timeout can stall a browse step; no configurable timeout flag exposed
entries.verdict: A real, well-structured Jev integration, but scoped to gated browser-element selection, so it only triggers on web-driving tasks and duplicates your playwright MCP. Skip it for general daily coding; consider it only as an optional per-project MCP (with --no-eval --no-trace, TYPESAFE_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api and --model typesafe/jev-1.13, after verifying schema parity) for E2E/UI-regression work.

entries.name: ChenYCL/jev-browser-skill
entries.what: Browser/computer-use skill and MCP server driven by Jev with a code-owned control loop, doctor, web UI, and optional local model tiers; zero dependencies.
entries.autoInvocation: skill trigger / model-discretion MCP
pros: TYPESAFE_BASE_URL configurable so /api/v1/systemone on OpenRouter is plausible
CI, unit and e2e tests, changelog, zero deps, doctor command
Bilingual docs, honest latency notes
cons: Browser use overlaps Playwright MCP already installed; adds another MCP to context
Default host api.typesafe.ai; OpenRouter untested and requires key/base-URL mapping
2 stars, very new

entries.name: legostin/jev-mcp
entries.what: MCP server (plus daemon, Chrome extension, CLI and one skill) that lets an agent drive a real Chrome/Chromium browser via CDP. Jev is used as the browser-step decision model: it finds elements, checks step success, and gates on calibrated confidence. Claude stays the planner and calls jev_task for multi-step web goals. It is a web-automation tool, not a coding-assistant integration.
entries.autoInvocation: Model-discretion MCP tools plus a skill description trigger. No hooks and no transparent proxy. Claude will call jev_task only when a request involves operating a website, so it would never trigger during ordinary code editing, Grep, Bash or test runs. It is automatic only for browser work, and it competes with the already-installed playwright MCP for the same job.
security: Not on npm (package.json has private:true). Install is git clone, npm install, npm run build:web, node bin/jev.mjs install. It pulls the npm dependency tree at install time, including esbuild and @puppeteer/browsers. No curl|sh installer and no postinstall script seen in package.json.

`jev install` mutates user config: it runs `claude mcp remove/add -s user`, rewrites ~/.codex/config.toml if present, and creates symlinks in ~/.claude/skills and ~/.local/bin (install.ts:52-88). Uses execFileSync with arg arrays, not a shell.

API key handling is decent. The key is read from env or ~/.config/jev-browser/config.json (0600) and sent only as an Authorization header (client.ts:68), so it does not appear in argv. `jev settings set ... -` reads from stdin. redactConfig masks keys (store.ts:70-83). Trace store refuses to persist key-like strings (SECURITY.md). Note the resolution order: JEV_OPENROUTER_API_KEY, then config file, then OPENROUTER_API_KEY, so a shared OPENROUTER_API_KEY env var would be picked up implicitly.

Daemon listens on a 0600 unix socket and on 127.0.0.1 (port 47913 for the extension WebSocket and debug UI). The Chrome extension pairs with a one-time 6-digit code. The extension uses chrome.debugger on the user's real Chrome profile, which means full control of logged-in sessions. This is a large privilege surface, and the repo is 1 week old with 1 author.

Prompt-injection surface is real. Web page text flows into Jev prompts and into agent-visible results (jev_observe, results lists). Mitigations: hidden text and injection bait are dropped from the page model (README), secret:true params never sent to Jev, card/password values masked (src/core/safety/privacy.ts), irreversible actions require confirmation. All of this is heuristic and unaudited.

No telemetry or analytics found (grep of src). The only outbound URLs are the provider endpoints and a link builder for console.typesafe.ai playground share URLs (playground.ts:8). Those links compress the payload into the URL fragment, so the payload is not sent unless the user opens it.
entries.dataEgress: To OpenRouter (or TypeSafe) only: POST /systemone with {model, state, questions} (client.ts:55). The state is a serialized view of the current browser page (element names and roles, region text, task goal/intent/params). Non-secret param values are included. Password, card and OTP fields are masked and secret params are excluded. Repo code, diffs and Claude Code prompts are NOT sent. Only web-page content from browsing tasks and the task text the agent writes leave the machine. Locally it stores traces, screenshots and site memory in ~/.local/share/jev-browser. Because the extension drives the user's real Chrome, any authenticated page the task visits can be sent to the provider. OpenRouter's own retention and logging apply.
entries.failureMode: Retry then throw, and only fail-open in the sense that Claude keeps working. client.ts:13-14 sets 20 s per-request timeout and up to 5 attempts (4 retries) with jittered exponential backoff (500 ms base, max 8 s, honoring Retry-After) on network, timeout and retryable statuses. Worst case is over 100 s for one call. A missing key gives a JevError 'config' at once. Failover to typesafe is off by default and needs a second key. It is opt-in and isolated: nothing in the coding loop depends on it, so a Jev outage only breaks browser tasks, and the MCP tool returns an error to Claude. Rate limiter defaults are 1200 requests per minute and 250k tokens per second.
entries.contextCost: 15 MCP tools (jev_task, status, wait, answer, control, result, trace, observe, find, ask, act, tabs, screenshot, settings, doctor). Source of the two registration files is about 34k chars, and descriptions plus zod schemas are roughly 60% of that, so about 4.5-6k tokens of tool definitions (estimate, not measured). Server instructions add about 2.5k chars, roughly 640 tokens (src/mcp/instructions.ts), and are injected every session. Total is about 5-7k tokens per session while connected (about 5% of a 200k window). Every jev tool result also gets an appended 'JEV is waiting for your answer' block when questions are pending. No hooks are shipped, so nothing is injected per prompt. The SKILL.md (119 lines, description-only in context until triggered) adds a little more. This is comparable to the existing playwright MCP, and it overlaps with it.
pros: Only candidate found that uses OpenRouter natively: default provider is 'openrouter', model typesafe/jev-1.13, base https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone (schema.ts:54-56, client.ts:66). It reads OPENROUTER_API_KEY, so it works with the user's planned key with zero patching.

Real, non-trivial Jev use. It sends typed questions with a state payload and consumes per-answer probabilities. Confidence gating (act / verify / ask), calibration reports and traces make good use of the calibrated-probability design of Jev. Also handles retry, Retry-After, rate limiting and OpenRouter usage.cost.
jev_ask exposes raw noul/choice/score primitives over page state, which is the closest thing to a generic 'ask Jev' tool among what was audited.
Clean opt-in: zero hooks, no per-prompt injection, no latency on normal coding turns, MIT license, no telemetry, key sent via header only, key input via stdin.
Good test and eval coverage for its age, with fixtures, integration tests, and a grounding eval.
Careful safety design for browsing: irreversible-action confirmation, secret params kept from the model, masking of card and password values, domain allow-lists and budgets.
cons: Wrong problem for this user. It is browser automation. Jev is used to pick page elements and verify web steps, not to make coding decisions (which file, is this diff risky, which test, permission gating). It does nothing for daily coding in Claude Code and duplicates the existing playwright MCP.
Auto-invocation is only model discretion or skill trigger and only for website tasks. It cannot satisfy 'Claude Code uses Jev whenever it adds value' for code work.
Costs about 5-7k tokens of context per session for 15 tools plus instructions, for a capability that is rarely needed when coding.

Very immature: created 2026-09-23, 1 star, 0 forks, 1 author, 94 commits in 2 days, v0.1.0, mostly AI-authored, no CI, not on npm (private:true). Install is a manual clone, npm install and build. `jev install` edits Claude and Codex config and creates symlinks in the user's home.

Extension path gives chrome.debugger control over the user's real logged-in Chrome, and page content from authenticated sites goes to OpenRouter. That is risky on client projects. Prompt-injection defences are heuristic.

Uses /api/v1/systemone only and not the alpha Decisions API. Full retry cascade can block a call for over 100 s. Channels push needs --dangerously-load-development-channels, which the user's bypass workflow may accept but is a research-preview dev flag.
Claimed benchmark numbers (100% top-1, ECE 0.05, 7-step flight run) come from the author's own local fixtures, not independent validation.
entries.verdict: Best-in-class for native OpenRouter Jev support and a solid code base, but it is a browser-automation server, not a coding integration. It would add about 5-7k tokens of context and overlap with playwright while never fire on ordinary code work. Only worth installing if the user wants Jev-driven web tasks. Do not use it as the primary Jev integration for coding, and if trying it, take it with a scoped, dedicated OpenRouter key and the headless Chromium driver rather than the real-Chrome extension.

entries.name: bothuany/jev-browser-mcp (npm jev-browser-mcp)
entries.what: Browser-automation MCP server (Playwright-based, 13 browse_* tools) where Jev makes per-step decisions (which element, which operation, done?) from a compressed page state that stays inside the server process, and Gemini 2.5 Flash answers page-reading questions (browse_ask). Supports recording goals as recipes, replay without models, healing, and export to @playwright/test. It is a Playwright MCP alternative, not a general coding aid.
entries.autoInvocation: Model-discretion MCP tool: Claude decides when to call browse_* based on tool descriptions and the server instructions ('START HERE for anything you want the browser to DO'). No hook, skill or proxy. The README itself notes GPT-5 initially ignored the high-level tools until instructions were added. It only fires on browser tasks, so it is not a general Jev integration.
security: API key is read from env or a file, not argv, if the user follows the README advice; but the documented 'claude mcp add' line does not place the key in argv, so no process-list leak by default
npx -y runs unpinned latest of a 1-week-old single-maintainer package on every start (supply-chain risk); no postinstall script seen in package.json
Server exits at startup without a Vercel gateway key (fail-closed at boot)

browse_eval runs arbitrary JS in pages and browse_page/tracing can write files; combined with bypass permission mode, a malicious page could steer the calling model (prompt injection via browse_goal/observe results)
Page text is passed to Jev and Gemini with 'untrusted data, never instructions' guards (decide.js:349,486; read.js:134-138) but this is prompt-level only
Refuses typing into password fields unless JEV_ALLOW_SECURE_FIELDS=1 (loop.js:659)
entries.dataEgress: To Vercel AI Gateway (then Jev/TypeSafe and Google Gemini): compressed text state of the visited web page (element list, labels, values), the goal sentence, recent actions, and for browse_ask/browse_verify the full page text plus the question. Form values typed by Claude (e.g. fill fields) may be included in state. Nothing from the user's source code or repo is sent unless the user browses local pages (e.g. localhost dev app) with it, in which case the rendered page content of that app leaves the machine to Vercel, TypeSafe and Google. The gateway is a third party, not OpenRouter, so it adds a second vendor/account.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open in the sense that Jev-loop uncertainty yields an 'escalate' outcome returning the page to Claude. On provider 429/502/503/504, decide() retries up to 6 times with exponential backoff (400ms*2^n, about 25s total) then throws (decide.js:566-600); text reads use maxRetries 6 and wait out the free-tier 5 req/min limit, which can make browse_ask slow. Missing key exits the server at start. No overall per-call timeout found other than abortSignal and maxSteps (max 40). Since it is an explicit tool, a Jev outage only breaks browser tasks, not normal coding.
entries.contextCost: 13 tools; README claims about 3.8k tokens of tool definitions (vs 5.6k for Playwright MCP defaults). Server-level MCP instructions of about 120 tokens (server.js:44-49). No hooks. Cost is additive with the existing Playwright MCP (about 25+ tools) if both are kept, and deferred-tool loading in Claude Code mitigates it.
pros: Genuinely uses Jev's typed Choice decisions (evaluate with choice/probabilities/confidence, done-bar threshold JEV_DONE_BAR 0.7) in a real loop, with 'escalate' when Jev is unsure, a sensible use of calibrated probabilities
Keeps page DOM out of Claude's context: browse_ask reports 266 vs 108,726 tokens on Wikipedia (self-measured, docs/BENCHMARKS.md); relevant for E2E/UI verification work
Record/replay/heal recipes and export to plain @playwright/test specs is a useful side benefit for regression tests on client projects
MCP server instructions steer the model toward the high-level tools so usage is fairly automatic when a browser task arises
Honest README: admits 30% autonomous WebVoyager success, macOS-only testing, no CI
MIT license; small readable codebase (about 4.4k lines), no postinstall, password-field refusal by default
cons: Not OpenRouter: hard-wired to Vercel AI Gateway (vck_ key, ai-SDK experimental_evaluate, gateway model ids); user has no gateway key and wants OpenRouter, so it needs a real code patch, not config
Adds a second paid vendor path (Vercel gateway to Google Gemini) and sends page content to Gemini too, not just Jev; a further data-egress concern on client projects
Scope is browser automation only; does nothing for editing, review, routing, permissions or commit decisions, so it does not deliver the 'Jev used automatically while coding' goal
Duplicates the already installed Playwright MCP (26-ish tools); two browsers/tool sets compete, and Claude may pick either
Immature: 1 commit, 1 contributor, 1 star, 1 week old, no CI, no release, tested only on macOS, author's commit co-written by Claude; npx -y unpinned means each start pulls whatever is published
Autonomous success only 30% on WebVoyager (9/30 vs 6/30 for a competitor, not significant); Playwright MCP comparison was 4 tasks with unverified runs

Depends on experimental_evaluate from ai v7 and on undocumented gateway response fields (providerMetadata.typesafe.confidence), fragile against Jev/gateway API changes; retry loop on 503 can stall up to about 25 s
browse_eval and CDP attach to a real Chrome profile, with bypass permissions, widen the prompt-injection blast radius from untrusted web pages
entries.verdict: A competent but one-week-old proof of concept that uses Jev for browser step selection through the Vercel AI Gateway, not OpenRouter, so it needs a moderate code patch to fit this user. It is only relevant to browser/E2E work (where it overlaps the existing Playwright MCP) and gives no general daily-coding integration; not recommended as the primary Jev integration, at most a later optional add-on after an OpenRouter port.

entries.name: 0pilatos0/jev-browser-mcp
entries.what: Node/TypeScript stdio MCP server exposing 11 browser tools on a persistent Playwright Chromium/Chrome profile. Pages are turned into an indexed element table; browser_act/browser_run send one TypeSafe systemOne request per step (Choice for operation and target, Noul for goal_met and stuck) and code executes the chosen action. It is a Jev-powered browser agent, not a coding-decision tool. It overlaps with the existing playwright MCP.
entries.autoInvocation: Model-discretion MCP tool. Claude Code sees the tool descriptions and instructions and decides whether to call them. There is no hook, no skill trigger, and no transparent proxy, so Claude would use it only when a browser task comes up, and it would still choose between this server and playwright. It cannot cover the coding-time decisions Jev is meant for.
security: API key is read from process.env or a project-local .env (env.ts); it is not placed in argv, so it does not show in the process list. Key handling is fine.

Prompt-injection surface is large: browser_act/browser_run feed arbitrary web page text and element labels into Jev, and browser_extract/observe return page content to Claude. The server instructions tell the caller to treat page content as untrusted. Jev returns only typed choices from an enumerated set, and the code re-validates refs, which limits injection to steering clicks and typing. Claude is still exposed to injected page text through observe and extract.
Launches a persistent browser profile at ~/.jev-browser-mcp/chrome-profile (browser.ts:24-29), so cookies and logins persist across sessions and projects.

Stealth patches (browser.ts:10-15, --disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled, navigator.webdriver spoofing) evade bot detection. This is ethically and ToS-questionable, and it raises the risk of automated actions on client sites.
browser_type can type arbitrary text and click arbitrary elements with no allowlist. Password fields are excluded from refs. Supplied `values` contents are matched locally and not sent to Jev.

No shell execution or child_process in src, no fetch() calls apart from the SDK, and no telemetry seen in the server code. No postinstall script in package.json. The installer is a manual build, not curl|sh.
entries.dataEgress: Every browser_act/browser_run step sends to the Jev endpoint (TypeSafe or, if redirected, OpenRouter): the natural-language goal and instruction, the page URL, title, and up to ~6000 chars of visible page text, the numbered list of element labels/roles/current values, the last 4 actions, and the keys (not contents) of supplied values. The README itself warns that page content leaves the machine. No source code, diffs, or Claude conversation are sent unless a page shows them. Deterministic tools send nothing. Via OpenRouter the payload would also pass through OpenRouter and its logging and provider policies.
entries.failureMode: Fail-closed per call and only for the Jev-backed tools. If TYPESAFE_API_KEY is missing, decide() throws (decide.ts:29-33). SDK timeout is 10s with 2 retries by default. Errors surface as an isError tool result or as status 'error'/'timeout' in browser_run (loop.ts:428). The deterministic tools (observe, click, type, extract, find) keep working, so Claude can fall back. The server does not crash the session, and nothing blocks Claude's normal work, because no hook is involved.
entries.contextCost: 11 MCP tools. registerTool blocks (descriptions and zod schemas) come to about 10k chars, plus about 1.7k chars of server `instructions` injected on connect.
