entries.name: compact-jev
entries.what: Claude Code plugin (early-access "function hooks" module, TypeScript) adding a manual /compact-jev [goal] slash command. It sends the transcript state (user/assistant text, tool inputs, 240-char excerpts of tool outputs) plus 2 boolean questions per tool call (still needed? keep full result?) to Jev via Vercel AI Gateway /v1/evaluate. It then drops stale tool calls and truncates stale results, keeping user/assistant messages verbatim with no summary, by hooking session.compact and vetoing the built-in summarizer during its own run. It also ships a TS library (npm compact-jev 0.5.4) with a pluggable JevAsker/baseUrl.
entries.autoInvocation: Only when prompted: user must type /compact-jev. README states it "runs only when you type /compact-jev"; command.run hook is bound to that command name only, and session.compact only acts while its own pending run is compacting. Auto-compaction and /compact are untouched, so there is no automatic invocation. Would need a fork to trigger on auto-compaction.
security: API key sent as Authorization Bearer header via $.http.fetch (engine-mediated), not argv; stored as plugin 'sensitive' userConfig; fallback AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY env; README warns settings env values leak to child processes
No shell execution, no spawn/exec, no postinstall script, no curl|sh installer in package.json or plugin
No telemetry beyond the Jev call; only outbound host is ai-gateway.vercel.sh

Prompt-injection surface: tool output excerpts (240 chars head+tail) and conversation text are sent as Jev state, but Jev returns only typed probabilities, so injection can at most bias which tool results are dropped; bounded by preserving first message + 6 newest

Relies on undocumented early-access Claude Code function-hooks API; can break on upgrades (typed against 2.1.274; user runs 2.1.285); sole maintainer with 0 stars, 5 days old at first release, so supply-chain trust is low
Enabling CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 globally widens the surface for all plugins
entries.dataEgress: On each /compact-jev run: user and assistant message text, tool call inputs (file paths, bash commands, patterns), and the first/last 240 chars (default outputExcerptChars) of candidate tool outputs, up to 8000-token state per request, repeated per batch (up to 4 concurrent) to Vercel AI Gateway then TypeSafe AI. Full tool outputs are not sent. outputExcerptChars=0 sends no tool output. For client projects this means code snippets and commands leave the machine to two extra third parties (Vercel plus TypeSafe), which is a contractual concern.
entries.failureMode: Fail-safe/fail-closed on the compaction, not on the session: any error (missing key, HTTP error, malformed JSON, oversized history) returns {skip} and leaves the conversation unchanged; built-in summarizer is deliberately vetoed during its run. Retries 429/5xx up to 12 times immediately (no backoff). No explicit per-request timeout in the plugin code (relies on $.http.fetch); a hook overrun is caught and answered with skip. It only runs on demand so Jev downtime never blocks normal work. README reports the Gateway returns random 503s.
entries.contextCost: Zero MCP tools. Zero injected text into context. No MCP instructions. Only registers one slash command (~30 tokens of description in the command list). Net effect is to reduce context after the user runs it (README example -82 to -86% transcript characters on a synthetic 14-call transcript, not measured in tokens).
pros: Genuinely uses Jev in a sensible System-One way (typed boolean probabilities per tool call/result, threshold 0.5) instead of chat, which is a good fit for Jev's design
Fail-safe: on any error the conversation is left as is, and the built-in summarizer is vetoed only during its own run; normal /compact and auto-compaction untouched
No MCP tools and no context overhead; no shell exec, no postinstall, key stored as a sensitive plugin option
Verbatim compaction (no lossy summary) with user/assistant messages preserved; first message and 6 newest always preserved; goal text steers relevance
Small readable codebase (~1.7k LOC) with 59 vitest cases; library has a baseUrl seam, so an OpenRouter fork is a small patch
Privacy-aware defaults: ZDR + no-training requested first; outputExcerptChars=0 option
cons: Vercel AI Gateway only: needs a separate AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY; no OpenRouter support in code, and the plugin hook does not pass baseUrl, so it needs a fork, and OpenRouter schema equivalence is unverified
Not automatic: manual /compact-jev slash command only, which contradicts the user's requirement that Claude Code use Jev without being told; auto-compaction is not hooked

Depends on the early-access, undocumented CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS API, typed against 2.1.274 and documented as possibly changing between releases; user is on 2.1.285, so it could break or interact with existing hooks; global flag affects all plugins
Only one narrow use case (transcript pruning); doesn't help routing, permission decisions, or code choices
Sends conversation text, tool inputs and output excerpts to Vercel plus TypeSafe; Hobby fallback drops ZDR; problematic for client-project code
Very immature: repo created 2026-09-23, 0 stars, 3 contributors (two are the maintainer and bots/Devin AI), no CI, no independent adoption, it's a fork of tamaratran/fast-jev-compaction
Benchmark gains are synthetic character counts, no measured token or quality data; retries up to 12 times with no backoff and no explicit timeout; Gateway 503s reported as frequent
Opus 5.5 subscription users already get good built-in auto-compaction; incremental value is small
entries.verdict: A well-scoped, fail-safe demo of Jev for transcript pruning, but it is manual-only, Vercel-only, and built on an unstable early-access Claude Code hook API, so it fails the "automatic, OpenRouter" requirement. Worth reading as a design reference or forking the compaction core for OpenRouter later; not something to install for daily coding today.

entries.name: fast-jev-compaction (aleksvega fork)
entries.what: Repo bundles (a) a Claude Code function-hook plugin (hooks/fast-jev.ts) that hooks session.compact to replace Claude's LLM summary with a pruned verbatim transcript, using Jev Noul questions (keep call? keep result?) per tool call, plus a turn.complete hook that auto-triggers compaction at 60% context; (b) an npm library; (c) side CLIs on OpenRouter /api/alpha/decisions (jev-compact, jev-gate, jev-qa, jev-find, hermes-compact) that Claude must be told to call; (d) jev-setup installer and a Hermes plugin. Only the CLIs use OpenRouter; the actual Claude Code plugin is wired to TypeSafe direct.
entries.autoInvocation: Deterministic function hooks (session.compact, turn.complete) that fire automatically with no user prompting, but only for context compaction. Everything else (jev-qa, jev-find, jev-gate, jev-enhance) requires the agent to choose to shell out per SKILL.md/AGENTS.md prose, or the user to script a git hook, i.e. not automatic. Function hooks require the early-access env flag CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 (README, hooks/README.md) and were type-generated against Claude Code 2.1.274 while the user runs 2.1.285 (API drift risk, unverified).
security: No npm lifecycle scripts (no postinstall/prepare in package.json 0.4.1); no curl|sh; zero runtime dependencies (devDeps only)
Key handling in the hook is decent: sensitive plugin option or env; sent in Authorization header via host $.http.fetch, not argv. CLIs read OPENROUTER_API_KEY from env, not argv

hooks/fast-jev.ts getApiKey also reads settings.env.TYPESAFE_API_KEY via $.settings.read() (reads user settings); Hermes plugin plugins/jev-layer/__init__.py:54-65 parses a dotenv-style file for OPENROUTER_API_KEY

Plugin runs as in-process TypeScript inside Claude Code with access to the function-hook surface ($.fs, $.shell 'CLI only', $.http, $.settings); trust is entirely in the aleksvega fork author, whose npm/GitHub identity is 1 week old

jev-setup does 'npm install -g' of two other unaudited packages by the same author (jev-prompt-enhancer, jev-skill-router) - extra supply-chain surface; execSync with fixed strings, no user interpolation

npm tarball 0.4.1 ships junk that gitignore excludes: cli/test-transcript.json, cli/test-dump.md, plugins/jev-layer/logs/*.jsonl (author's runtime logs from Hermes usage) - sloppy publishing hygiene, possible info leak of author data
entries.dataEgress: Hook path: on every compaction, the whole conversation state (up to maxStateTokens=25k est. tokens) goes to the Jev endpoint, resent in full with every batched request: all user prompts and assistant text (verbatim, abridged head+tail only if over budget), goal (last 3 user prompts), and every tool call's name and input (Bash commands, file paths, Edit/Write content truncated to 1000/200/60 chars only when over budget); tool RESULTS are replaced by 'ok, N chars (omitted)' so file contents and command output are not sent. So code appears only via Edit/Write inputs and pasted user text; secrets typed in prompts or Bash commands (env vars in commands) would leave the machine, and the user's PreToolUse secret guard does not cover $.http.fetch. Destination as shipped: api.typesafe.ai (needs TypeSafe key); after patch: openrouter.ai (OpenRouter's data policy applies). CLIs: jev-qa sends source file contents; jev-find sends directory listings plus first line of each file; jev-gate sends git diff of last commit.
entries.failureMode: Hook is fail-open by design: any Jev error, malformed JSON, missing key, state that cannot be fitted, or <25% reduction => toast 'fallback to built-in summary' and next(event) hands off to Claude's normal compaction (fast-jev.ts:283-289). Without TYPESAFE_API_KEY it falls back every time (missing key = plugin silently does nothing beyond a toast). No timeout or AbortSignal anywhere in the TS path (grep: none in src/ or hooks/) - a hung request stalls compaction until the host's fetch gives up; concurrent batches via Promise.all. turn.complete swallows errors. jev-gate.py is fail-CLOSED (API failure => BLOCK, 60s timeout) which would block pushes if wired in a hook; jev-qa/jev-find have no timeout.
entries.contextCost: Essentially zero tokens: no MCP server, no tools, no server instructions, no SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit text injection. Only a UI toast/log line per compaction. Root SKILL.md (~1.5k chars, ~370 tokens if loaded) is not registered by plugin.json. If the user instead wires the CLIs through AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md prose, cost is a few hundred tokens but then it is model-discretion again.
pros: Genuinely automatic: session.compact/turn.complete function hooks fire with zero prompting, matching the 'Claude Code must use it by itself' requirement for this one use case
Fail-open design with explicit fallback to built-in summary on any error or <25% reduction (fast-jev.ts:283-289) - low risk of breaking a session
Zero context-token cost, no MCP tools, no npm lifecycle scripts, no runtime deps, MIT license

Sensible Jev fit: cheap batched Noul questions per tool call with state-fitting ladder to stay under Jev's 32k limit; upstream library has ~580 lines of unit tests with a fake Jev (tests/*.test.ts) and a typecheck/validate:plugin script
OpenRouter support already proven in sibling CLIs with the same request/response schema, so patching the hook to OpenRouter is ~5 lines (buildJevRequest already accepts baseUrl)
Keeps user/assistant text verbatim and in order, avoiding summary hallucination/drift
cons: The Claude Code plugin does NOT support OpenRouter as shipped: hardcoded api.typesafe.ai + TYPESAFE_API_KEY, and README's TYPESAFE_BASE_URL/TYPESAFE_MODEL claim is not implemented in any code - contradicts the fork's own headline ('no TypeSafe key')
Covers only compaction, a rare event; no Jev involvement in routing, permission decisions, review, or per-turn coding, so it barely delivers the user's 'use Jev whenever it adds value' goal

Destructive pruning replaces Claude's summary: dropped tool calls/results are gone with no narrative summary of decisions/reasoning, risky on long client work with Opus 5.5 (whose summary is high quality); Jev's per-call keep probabilities are uncalibrated for this task and the author admits 'a probability is not a proof' (README Limitations)
Depends on early-access function hooks (CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1), types pinned to 2.1.274 vs user's 2.1.285; unverified on OAuth/subscription sessions and may break on any release

Sends full conversation state (prompts, assistant text, tool inputs incl. Bash commands and edit content) to a third party on every compaction, bypassing the user's secret-leak guard; client-project confidentiality concern

No timeouts on the fetch path; no CI, no releases, 0 stars, 0 forks, created 2026-09-19 (11 days old), 3 npm versions in 3 days; only 8 of 38 commits are the fork author's, rest upstream Devin AI/tamara tran

Repo hygiene and correctness bugs: jev-setup uses wrong plugin id (jev-compaction@jev-compaction), opencode writes non-existent 'jev-compact --auto', jev-compact not in package.json bin, jev-find double res.json() read, committed .pyc files, junk and author logs published in npm tarball, plugin.json/marketplace.json still 0.3.0 with upstream owner

Side tools (jev-qa, jev-find, jev-gate) are CLIs needing agent discretion; no MCP wrapper, so they do not give automatic invocation and jev-qa/find semantic quality is anecdotal (author's 15-file test set)
entries.verdict: Only automatic piece is a compaction hook that is TypeSafe-direct as shipped (OpenRouter needs a small local patch despite README claims), rides an early-access function-hook API, and replaces a good Opus summary with destructive pruning. Not a fit as the primary Jev integration; at most a patched, opt-in experiment, and the rest of the suite is just CLIs that need prompting.

entries.name: sohryuu101/jev-vault-gate
entries.what: Plugin that on each main-loop turn asks Jev if it holds durable knowledge and, if so, writes raw text to ~/vault/raw/ (with topic routing), plus /vault-check and /audit-sessions commands.
entries.autoInvocation: deterministic hook (turn.complete, function hook)
pros: Uses Jev's strengths (Noul gate plus Choice routing) and never blocks the turn on failure
Nothing is auto-deleted; deletion candidates only reported
cons: Requires an Obsidian-like ~/vault/compile workflow the user does not have; TYPESAFE_API_KEY and api.typesafe.ai only
Sends every long turn's user and assistant text to an external API, unsuitable for client projects
No tests, no license, 0 stars

entries.name: claude-herdr-jev-compaction (jpwinans)

interface: claude/task-compact.py registered on Stop (and UserPromptSubmit for Codex)
entries.autoInvocation: deterministic Stop hook
pros: Compacts at task boundaries rather than when the window is full, with 600k default gate for 1M Opus and fail-closed guards (stop_hook_active, activity checks)
Stdlib Python only, has unit tests and an evaluations/boundaries dataset with result files
Built-in auto-compaction stays as backstop; no transcript rewriting
cons: Hard requirement on the Herdr terminal multiplexer (types keystrokes into the pane); useless in a plain terminal or IDE

entries.name: jev-context-compaction (PhiDung-hub)
entries.what: Rust rewrite of fast-jev-compaction: loopback Rust server (127.0.0.1:8787) calls Jev via the typesafe-ai SDK; a thin JS function hook posts transcripts to it and falls back to built-in compaction on failure.
entries.autoInvocation: deterministic compaction hook (auto at 60% context, retry after +10pp)
pros: Keeps API key out of the plugin (only the bridge holds it); pooled HTTP client, 3 s deadline, no retries, clean fallback to built-in compaction
Usage-exhausted circuit breaker and rank-by-keep-budget instead of fixed threshold
Rust tests including live integration test (724 ms for 16 Noul questions)
cons: Needs cargo build plus a long-running systemd/loopback service to maintain; heavy for a hook
TypeSafe SDK/key only; no OpenRouter path found in code or README
Selective (not lossless): removes stale tool calls; 0 stars, created 2026-09-24

entries.name: Dharundp6/jev-carryforward (npm: carryforward)
entries.what: Cross-session memory ledger for Claude Code, shipped as a plugin (MCP server + skill + SessionStart hook). Two MCP tools: record appends facts (constraint, correction, decision, measurement, thread) to ~/.carryforward/<project>.jsonl; recall(task) returns pinned rules (constraint/correction) in full and asks Jev one boolean question per remaining entry ("is this still live for the task starting now?"), bucketing by probability (>=0.60 full, 0.30-0.60 one line, else omitted). Jev is only a relevance ranker over the user's own notes. It does not review code and does not route decisions for Claude Code.
entries.autoInvocation: Mixed. Deterministic only for SessionStart hook (pinned rules injection, no Jev call, no task known). recall/record are model-discretion MCP tools nudged by tool descriptions and a skill description. The project's own eval (README 'What the eval suite found') reports the agent called recall 0 out of 4 runs even with skill installed, so the author himself concedes automatic invocation is unreliable.
security: No shell execution, no postinstall script (package.json scripts are build/typecheck/test/prepublishOnly only); reads/writes only ~/.carryforward/*.jsonl (plain text, unencrypted, ledger.ts:117-118).

Key handling: AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY via env; README install command `claude mcp add carryforward -e AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY=$AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY -- npx -y carryforward` expands the secret into argv/shell history and into ~/.claude.json.

Runs via `npx -y carryforward` on every session start (hook) and MCP spawn: unpinned npm fetch of a 2-star, single-maintainer package (dharun7). Supply-chain exposure on every startup; pin a version or vendor if used.
Repo/registry inconsistencies: latest release URL points at github.com/dharun-cohere/jev-carryforward (org rename/transfer), and npm latest is 0.1.0 while repo/plugin manifests say 0.1.1.

Prompt-injection surface: ledger contents are model-authored and are re-injected into context as trusted-looking text, and SKILL says treat 'Always' as binding. A poisoned record (e.g. from a fetched web page or untrusted repo content the model summarised) persists across sessions and is re-injected by a SessionStart hook. Ledger is per-project but global home dir, no integrity or provenance beyond obtained field.
No telemetry in code. SECURITY.md is honest and accurate about egress.
entries.dataEgress: Only recall(task) with AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY set: the one-sentence task string plus all non-pinned ledger entries (id, kind, obtained, date, text, ref, refresh), batched 25 per request, to Vercel AI Gateway model typesafe-ai/jev (recall.ts:263-272). Constraints and corrections are never sent. No source code, diffs, file contents or tool outputs are sent unless the model wrote them into an entry text or ref. record never touches the network. Note: the SessionStart hook runs recall with no task, so no network call there.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open. No key, no task, or any scorer exception returns the whole ledger unscored with a note (recall.ts:286-320). No explicit timeout on the Jev call; the SDK default applies (the hook has a 25s cap, but the MCP recall tool has none besides the client's). If npx cannot fetch the package (offline/npm down), the hook simply fails non-blocking and the MCP server would fail to start.
entries.contextCost: 2 tools. Approx 650-800 tokens of tool defs (record description ~1.0k chars, recall ~0.7k chars, schemas ~0.8k chars), plus the skill description (~60 tokens, ~2k chars body loaded when triggered), no MCP server instructions field. SessionStart hook injects the pinned rules (size grows with user's ledger; plugin hooks.json without --quiet also prints the 'ledger is empty' message at every start/clear/compact). Each recall result is a markdown brief of variable size.
pros: Genuine, well-scoped Jev use: boolean relevance scoring per entry is the type of typed-decision task Jev is designed for (no free text needed), and it fails open cleanly.
Small, readable codebase (~600 LOC src, 3 test files, CI on Linux+Windows, Node 22/24, MIT). Constraints/corrections never sent to any network.
Clean Asker abstraction (types.ts / recall.ts) makes swapping the scorer to OpenRouter a localized rewrite of src/gateway.ts.
Ships as a proper Claude Code plugin (plugin.json with mcpServers, skills, hooks) and a SessionStart hook that re-injects rules after compaction, which is actually useful for a long-running user.
Honest README: admits 9-entry sample is not proof and that the agent skipped recall 0/4 times.
cons: Not OpenRouter-compatible: hardwired to the Vercel AI Gateway via the `ai` SDK experimental_evaluate; needs a second key and account, or a code fork.

Does not meet the goal of automatic Jev use: Jev is invoked only inside recall, which the model must choose to call; the author's own eval shows 0/4 calls. The one deterministic hook does no Jev scoring (no task at session start).

Solves a memory problem, not a coding-decision problem: Claude Code already has CLAUDE.md, auto-memory and compaction; the user already has GitNexus for graph context. Adds a second, parallel memory store that the model must manually curate via record.
Very immature: created 2026-09-18, 6 commits, 1 contributor, 2 stars, 0 forks, v0.1.x; npm latest (0.1.0) lags repo (0.1.1); no accuracy evidence, only a 9-entry, 3-task anecdote.

Persistent-injection risk: model-written ledger entries are re-injected as binding 'Always' rules across sessions and hooks; risky on client projects with untrusted content. Ledger also lives in the home dir, unencrypted, shared across all client work unless CARRYFORWARD_PROJECT is managed.
Runtime `npx -y carryforward` unpinned on every session start adds startup latency and supply-chain risk; plugin hooks.json lacks --quiet so empty ledger prints noise.
Adds about 700 tokens of tool defs to every session for a tool that the model tends not to call.
entries.verdict: A tidy but early-alpha memory ledger where Jev is a niche relevance ranker, wired only to the Vercel AI Gateway and reachable only if the model chooses to call recall (author's eval: 0/4). It does not deliver automatic OpenRouter-hosted Jev in Claude Code; skip it, or at most borrow the Asker pattern.

entries.name: leonaaardob/fast-dev-compaction
entries.what: Codex plugin using PreCompact/PostCompact/SessionStart hooks to score tool calls/results with Jev and re-inject verbatim kept history around Codex compaction; port of tamaratran/fast-jev-compaction.
entries.autoInvocation: deterministic hook (Codex lifecycle)
pros: FAST_JEV_BASE_URL allows pointing to OpenRouter; hooks structure is close to Claude Code PreCompact
Engine in src/ is reusable as an npm library
cons: Author's README says 'I do not recommend using this'; cites critique on cache and reasoning-trace loss
Codex-specific; CC PreCompact cannot replace history, only add context
Reads key from ~/.typesafe_key (conflicts with secret-leak posture); dist committed, no tests seen

entries.name: kolawong/fast-compaction-dsh
entries.what: DeepSeek Harness compaction plugin: Jev noul keep/truncate/drop verdicts per tool call/result instead of an LLM summary; falls back to compaction-basic on any failure.
entries.autoInvocation: harness compaction seam (automatic in DSH)
pros: Clean fallback to stock summarizer on any error; verbatim retention
Has specs for pairing, rebuild, estimate, jev; configurable baseUrl in code

Non-standard license ('other'); ~700 ms round trip on large regions

entries.name: edwardyen724-g/jev-compactor
entries.what: TypeScript library + CLI + stdio MCP server (jev-compactor-mcp) that compacts an agent chat history by asking Jev one keep/drop Choice question per message (plus Noul questions for destructive/exfiltration/thrashing/goal-drift, plus a local regex floor for rm -rf, force-push, DROP TABLE, curl|sh, leaked keys) and returns the kept messages verbatim with a per-message report. Designed mainly as withCompaction() wrapper around OpenAI/Anthropic/LangChain clients in your own agent code. It is NOT a Claude Code hook or plugin: no hooks.json, no plugin.json, no SKILL.md in the repo. The only Claude Code path is the MCP server, where the model itself must pass the message array as tool arguments, and its output cannot replace Claude Code's own context.
entries.autoInvocation: Model-discretion MCP tools only. There are no hooks (no PreToolUse/PreCompact/UserPromptSubmit), no skill, no plugin manifest, no proxy. Nothing triggers it deterministically; Claude Code would only use it if the model decided to, and would need CLAUDE.md prompting to do so, which the user explicitly does not want. It also cannot swap the harness's own context, since MCP tool results do not replace the conversation.
security: Not published to npm: npm view jev-compactor returns E404, so the README's `npx -y --package=jev-compactor jev-compactor-mcp` install path fails or, worse, invites a typosquat/name-claim attack on that name; safe use requires git clone + pnpm build of an unaudited 11-commit single-author repo (running third-party build/deps).
No postinstall/preinstall scripts in root or package package.json; no curl|sh installers; no child_process/exec/spawn in src (grep clean); only network is the SDK to the configured base URL.

API key handling: read from TYPESAFE_API_KEY env; `claude mcp add --env TYPESAFE_API_KEY=...` puts the key in the `claude mcp add` argv once and stores it plaintext in ~/.claude.json; MCP process itself receives it via env (not argv). Code redacts key from errors/reports (redact/redactReport in render.ts) and pins SDK logLevel=warn because debug logs request bodies.

env.ts loadEnvLocal() walks up to 6 parent directories from cwd and reads the first .env.local/.env, setting any not-yet-set keys into process.env. In a client project this reads that project's .env into the MCP process (values not logged, but any TYPESAFE_*/base-URL overrides there would be honored, so a malicious repo .env could set TYPESAFE_BASE_URL and redirect the conversation and API key to an attacker host).

Prompt-injection surface: it feeds full conversation/tool output to Jev as state; Jev output is only probabilities, applied by deterministic code, so injection can at worst bias keep/drop or safety verdicts; the safety gate is documented as not a sandbox (SECURITY.md).
No telemetry in the OSS core; 'Sealed Context Cloud' telemetry app is listed as Phase 2, not started (apps/cloud absent).
entries.dataEgress: An abridged copy of the whole conversation (skeleton state up to ~20k tokens; long tool outputs replaced by 'ok, N chars (omitted)' but user/assistant text, commands, code blocks and file paths retained) plus the goal and the generated questions is POSTed to the configured Jev endpoint (api.typesafe.ai, or OpenRouter if overridden). For check_action, the proposed command text. In the Claude Code MCP flow, the model must additionally serialize the history into the tool-call arguments, so the same content is also re-emitted through the Claude context as output tokens. Nothing goes anywhere else. Sending client-project code and prompts to a beta third party is a compliance concern for client work.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open by default: no key, 401, timeout or Jev error returns the history unchanged with report.skipped='jev_unavailable' (failClosed:true option throws instead); check_action fail-open falls back to the regex floor only and says so. Configurable timeoutMs, cooldownTurns; SDK retries 408/429/5xx. Compaction only calls Jev when estimated tokens exceed maxTokens (default 15000); the safety gate runs on every call. Since Claude Code will not call it automatically, failure mode matters little in practice.
entries.contextCost: Low tool-definition cost: 4 MCP tools (compact_context, inspect_context, check_action, self_test). Descriptions plus zod schemas approx 2.5k characters, roughly 600-800 tokens (compact_context ~1.2k chars, inspect ~0.6k, check_action ~0.6k, self_test ~0.5k). No MCP server-level instructions field set (McpServer created with only name/version). No hooks, so zero injected text. Real hidden cost: every compact_context/inspect_context call requires the model to write the whole history (up to tens of thousands of tokens) into tool arguments and then read the same amount back as the result, which increases context rather than reducing it.
pros: Genuinely uses Jev in the intended way (Choice/Noul/Score, one request with many parallel questions), with well-documented API notes and measured behaviour (docs/JEV-API.md), including honest caveats about Jev's instability (P(keep) varies up to 0.14 between identical requests) and weak multi-hop reasoning.

Base URL is env-overridable through the SDK (TYPESAFE_BASE_URL), and the SDK hits POST /v1/systemone with Bearer auth, which lines up with OpenRouter's /api/v1/systemone, so OpenRouter hosting is likely a config-only change.
Fail-open by default with a regex floor for rm -rf / force-push / DROP TABLE / curl|sh / leaked keys that works with no network; clean code, no shell execution, no install scripts, no telemetry, MIT.
Small tool footprint (4 tools, ~700 tokens) and no injected hook text, so it would not bloat Claude Code's context or disturb existing GitNexus/secret-guard hooks.
Extensive offline tests and CI for a repo this new.
cons: Does not meet the core requirement: no hook, skill or plugin, so Claude Code will never invoke it automatically; the model would have to be prompted (or CLAUDE.md-instructed) to call compact_context/check_action.

Wrong architecture for Claude Code: compaction requires the model to pass the entire message history as tool arguments and the result cannot replace Claude Code's live context, so it adds tokens and latency instead of saving them. It only makes sense embedded in your own API-client loop (withCompaction around an Anthropic client), which is not what Claude Code does.

check_action duplicates what the user already has (PreToolUse secret guard), is not wired as a PreToolUse hook, and its Jev part is probabilistic; the regex floor would be better copied into your own hook.
Install path in README is broken: jev-compactor is not on npm (E404); would need clone and build of an unaudited single-author, 11-commit, 11-day-old, 2-star repo.

loadEnvLocal() auto-loads .env/.env.local from cwd and up to 6 parents, so in client repos a project .env could inject TYPESAFE_BASE_URL/API key and redirect traffic; also leaks project secrets into the MCP process env (not logged).
Sends conversation content (prompts, commands, code snippets) to a beta third party; questionable for client projects.

Jev's documented weaknesses (literal reading, poor multi-hop causal links, drops the cat output that explains an error) make drop decisions on coding transcripts risky; bench evidence is synthetic and author-run.
OpenRouter support is not tested or documented by the project; only a third-party fork (ingebyd/fast-jev-compaction-openrouter) is mentioned in its own landscape doc.
entries.verdict: Real and honestly engineered Jev client, but it is a library for agent builders, not a Claude Code integration: it has no hook/skill/plugin, needs the model to be told to call it, and its MCP compaction flow costs more tokens than it saves. Not recommended for this user; at most mine the regex floor and the Jev question design for a custom PreToolUse hook.

Same design (score, keep verbatim, re-inject) portable to CC PreCompact/SessionStart
