entries.name: poiuyjie/jev_project_context (project-context-v2)
entries.what: An agent skill (SKILL.md, name project-context-v2) for evidence-first long-term research-experiment memory: it maintains a CONTEXT/CURRENT/EXPERIMENTS.md and docs/ tree and has operations init/start/frame/plan/record/end/correct/synthesize/claim-audit/doctor. Jev is only an optional accelerator. jev_context.py ranks memory items against a task with one batched Score call to produce a LOAD/SKIP/SURFACE manifest. jev_doctor.py pre-screens experiment records and claims. Without TYPESAFE_API_KEY, everything falls back to the agent doing the work itself. It is a scientific-research bookkeeping skill, not a general coding-assistant integration.
entries.autoInvocation: Skill description trigger only. Claude decides to load the skill when the conversation is about long-term research experiments (initialize research memory, record experiment results, resume work, handoffs). The Jev scripts run only if the model follows SKILL.md instructions in start/doctor/claim-audit/synthesize AND the env key is set. There is no deterministic hook, and the skill never triggers for ordinary coding tasks such as editing, debugging or reviewing.
security: API key is read from the TYPESAFE_API_KEY env var or a .env file, which is searched in cwd, the scripts dir and the skill root (jev_client.py:25-49). It is sent in an Authorization header, not in argv, so it is not visible in the process list.
The cwd .env search means any project .env containing TYPESAFE_* is loaded. It uses os.environ.setdefault, so real env vars win. It parses only KEY=VALUE lines and does not read other variables.
No shell execution: no subprocess or os.system (grep). HTTP only via urllib to a single configurable URL. No telemetry.
TYPESAFE_BASE_URL is honored without validation, so anything that can set the env or .env can redirect state payloads (including CURRENT.md content) and the bearer key to an arbitrary host.

Prompt-injection surface is moderate: memory-file content (experiment headings, CURRENT.md) is sent as Jev state and returned only as numeric scores. The manifest is printed as file names and numbers, so Jev cannot inject free text. SKILL.md instructs the agent to relay SURFACE lines, which come from local regex matches.
Install is the third-party 'npx skills add', a curl-free flow. There are no postinstall or curl|sh scripts in the repo.
entries.dataEgress: Only when TYPESAFE_API_KEY is set and one of the Jev scripts is run. jev_context.py sends the task string (the user's request), up to 6k chars of CURRENT.md, and one-line 'cards' (file name, heading up to 110 chars, status/validity/protocol) for up to 60 memory items, capped at 24k chars total. jev_doctor.py sends record text and claims rows, capped at 24k chars per call (STATE_CAP, plus CLAIMS_CAP). It does not send source code, diffs or tool outputs. It only sends the research-memory markdown of the project. Destination is api.typesafe.ai by default, or wherever TYPESAFE_BASE_URL points.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open by design. With no key, or on any JevError (HTTP error, URLError, timeout, OSError), the scripts print a [FALLBACK] line and exit 0, and the agent uses the fixed reading order. A malformed or unexpected-shape response is not wrapped in a try: json.loads errors outside the caught types are not handled, but answer_value tolerates missing keys. Timeout is 60 s (jev_client.py system_one timeout=60), which is long; a hung API could stall the agent's Bash call for up to a minute, with no retry.
entries.contextCost: No MCP tools, so 0 tool-definition tokens. The skill's frontmatter description costs about 130 tokens (about 520 chars) in the Claude Code skills listing. When SKILL.md is triggered it loads about 222 lines (roughly 3.5-4k tokens), plus references/schemas.md (319 lines) and lifecycle.md on demand. No hook-injected text.
pros: Concrete, readable, working example of using Jev's Score primitive for a real triage task (relevance scoring of memory items with confidence, using a 3-level ordered scale). It is a useful reference for the request shape: {state, model, questions:{id:{type:score,instructions,criteria}}}.
Zero dependencies (stdlib urllib), no shell execution, no telemetry, small enough to audit in about 15 minutes; key goes in a header, not argv.
Cleanly fail-open (FALLBACK, exit 0) with a --dry-run preview mode; SKILL.md explicitly says Jev is 'never a capability gate'.
TYPESAFE_BASE_URL override makes retargeting at OpenRouter's /api/v1/systemone a one-line env change if the schemas match.
MIT license.
cons: Domain mismatch: it targets scientific experiment logging (EXPERIMENTS.md, hypotheses, claims, provenance). It gives no value to everyday coding in client and personal projects, and would impose a research-memory file layout if it triggered.

Jev is not an automatic layer: only a skill description trigger plus SKILL.md prose telling the model to run a script. Claude Code will not call Jev for ordinary coding, which is the user's requirement.

Direct TypeSafe only. No OPENROUTER_API_KEY support, no 'openrouter' string in the code; requires a hack of putting the OpenRouter key into TYPESAFE_API_KEY and overriding the model name via --model. The OpenRouter response shape is unverified against the parser.

The Jev output is used for a task Claude can do by reading a few files, and it adds a model step (Bash call) to save a few file reads. Value is low; the maintainers themselves call it a 'fallback, not degradation'.
Very immature: 13 commits by one author in one day, created 2026-09-22, no tests, no CI, no releases, 9 stars; half the commits are README diagram polishing/promotion.
60 s timeout with no retry, and the .env loader picks up a .env from the cwd, which in client projects may contain unrelated secrets (only TYPESAFE_* are consumed, but the file is read).
entries.verdict: Not an integration for daily coding: it is a niche research-experiment-memory skill that uses Jev only as an optional relevance and audit triage scorer, is direct-TypeSafe-only, and is triggered only by the model matching its description. Skip it for the OpenRouter/Claude Code goal; at most, treat jev_client.py as a small reference for the System One request/response shape.

entries.name: compactio
entries.what: Claude Code plugin (npm compactio 0.2.3, MIT) with deterministic PostToolUse hooks that rewrite large tool outputs (Bash, Read of data files, Grep, WebFetch, WebSearch, mcp__*) via updatedToolOutput. Lossless cleanup (ANSI strip, repeated-line collapse) always runs. For outputs of 6k chars or more, it asks Jev (Choice primitive with levels full/errors/headtail/stub) how much to keep, then cuts locally and stores the original under ~/.compactio/store, retrievable via a "node cli.ts show ID" line. It also skips unchanged re-reads. An optional "Sweep" local proxy on 127.0.0.1:8787 (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL) asks Jev which old tool results in the history to replace with tombstones. Jev is used as a System-1 decider, and the tool is not an MCP server.
interface: CLI: compactio show ID | gain | proxy [port] | sweep | setup | key
entries.autoInvocation: Deterministic hooks (PostToolUse on Bash|Read|Grep|WebFetch|WebSearch|mcp__.*, UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart). Jev is called automatically without the model choosing or being prompted, which matches the user's requirement. The optional Sweep is a transparent proxy.
security: No MCP server, no npm postinstall script, no curl|sh installer. The plugin runs TS source directly with node (needs Node >=22.18; you have 24). CI publishes to npm with provenance and OIDC trusted publishing.

API key is read from env or from ~/.claude/settings.json env (install.ts:153-156) and sent as a Bearer header from fetch(), so it does not appear in argv. 'compactio key' saves the key in plaintext in settings.json (backup written as settings.json.compactio-bak).

Redaction is regex-only (src/redact.ts): private-key blocks, sk-/pk-/rk- tokens, gh*_ tokens, AWS AKIA, Google AIza, JWTs, Bearer/Basic, and NAME=value for names containing KEY/TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD. SECURITY.md admits it does not catch every secret. Client code snippets and paths in a 6 KB preview still leave the machine.

Sweep proxy (sweep.ts:serve) sits between Claude Code and api.anthropic.com. It sees every API request including OAuth/API-key auth headers and forwards them; README says it does not store them. It listens on 127.0.0.1 only. POST /_compactio/quit exits it, requiring a custom header as CSRF mitigation. Dropped outputs are stored unencrypted on disk in ~/.compactio/store and never pruned.

Sweep edits settings.json (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL=claude-opus-5-5[1m]) and creates a systemd user service. If the proxy dies mid-session, Claude Code loses API access (not fail-open). Routing OAuth/subscription traffic through a third-party proxy is a policy and ToS grey area, which I did not verify.

Prompt-injection surface: Jev is asked with instructions plus attacker-controllable tool output preview. Jev returns only a typed choice, so injection can at worst make it wrongly cut or keep output; low severity. Cut outputs are replaced with 'compactio: ... Full output: node .../cli.ts show ID' text, which the agent will execute via Bash. The ID is only a random uuid slice and safe() sanitises it.
entries.dataEgress: With an OPENROUTER_API_KEY, each Bash/Grep/WebFetch/mcp output of 6,000 chars or more (after lossless cleanup) sends to openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions: the last user prompt (up to 2000 chars, redacted), the tool name, the tool_input (up to 600 chars, redacted), and a preview of about 6,000 chars (first 30 lines, error lines, last 20 lines, redacted). No key means nothing is sent. Sweep additionally sends, per batch of up to 16 old tool results, the goal and 2,400-char previews, but only when at least 40k chars of old results are open. Nothing is sent when the output is under 6k chars, for code Reads that are not data files, or for images/PDFs. Note that this covers client code and command output, and redaction is best-effort.
entries.failureMode: Hooks are fail-open. A Jev timeout (COMPACTIO_TIMEOUT_MS default 1500 ms), HTTP error, unknown choice or confidence below 0.6 all leave the full output unchanged, and errors are logged as engine=fail-open. The main() catch exits 0. The hook timeout is 5s. Without a key, a local-only mode applies head+tail only to outputs over 24k chars. The Sweep proxy is fail-open for its own logic errors (the original body is forwarded, Jev timeout 3000 ms) but fail-closed if the process is down: ECONNREFUSED breaks Claude Code until 'sweep off'. Systemd Restart=always and the SessionStart guard mitigate this.
entries.contextCost: Very low. No MCP server, so no tool definitions, no server instructions, and no skill descriptions. There are 3 slash commands (setup/sweep/gain) with one-line descriptions, about 100 tokens in total. Hooks inject no additional text on the happy path. They only shorten tool results, adding a one-line note of about 40 tokens ('[compactio: kept "errors" view of N lines. Full output: node ".../cli.ts" show ID]') where output is cut. Net effect is a context reduction, in exchange for occasionally hiding data.
pros: Only candidate here that satisfies 'Claude Code must use Jev automatically': deterministic hooks that never need a 'use jev' prompt.
OpenRouter is a first-class provider (jev.ts:29-42) using ~typesafe/jev-latest on /api/alpha/decisions. It sends the attribution headers and is a zero-patch integration for the user's key setup.
Sensible use of Jev's actual strength: a typed Choice decision with calibrated confidence, gated by MIN_CONFIDENCE 0.6, at negligible cost ($0.042/M input tokens).

Conservative by design: never cuts Read of code the agent may edit (hook.ts:159-178), skips images/PDFs/notebooks, and exempts commands containing 'compactio'. Originals are recoverable by 'show ID'. Hook path is fail-open with a 1.5 s timeout.
Zero context cost (no MCP tools) and it reduces context. It works with a subscription/OAuth login when using hooks only.
Clean, small (about 1.7k lines total), readable source and MIT licensed. Unit tests use a fake Jev and fake API. CI runs on Node 22 and 24, and npm publishing uses provenance.
Works without a key in a lossless-plus-24k head/tail local mode, so it is safe to try before enabling Jev.
cons: Very young and unproven: repo created 2026-09-25 (5 days old), 26 commits by one author in a single day, 3 stars, no releases and no issues history. README admits 'a real session where Jev drops a result is not tested yet'.

The Jev integration is not evidenced against the OpenRouter Decisions schema: I could not verify the {model,state,questions} body from OpenRouter docs (404), and the README does not say which provider its live test used. Test it with a small curl before trusting it.

Sends redacted client-code previews (last prompt, tool input, 6 KB of output) to OpenRouter and its upstream on every large output. It uses regex redaction that SECURITY.md itself says is incomplete, which is a real concern for client projects under NDA.

Sweep proxy is high-risk for this user: it redirects all Anthropic traffic (including OAuth) via localhost, pins ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL to 'claude-opus-5-5[1m]' (stale when Opus changes), and edits settings.json plus installs a systemd Restart=always service. If the proxy fails, Claude Code has no API. Its cache-rewrite gate can cost more than it saves. It is macOS/Windows untested and has a permanent-tombstone problem.

It conflicts in practice with the user's stack: it also mutates tool output through PostToolUse updatedToolOutput on Bash/Grep, the same events where the GitNexus and caveman hooks run, so hook ordering and multiple rewriters are unverified. Its matcher also covers mcp__.* (gitnexus, playwright output).

Cutting risk: Jev sees only head/errors/tail, so it can misjudge a middle-critical output. A short 'continue' prompt gives it a poor goal. Hidden log lines can cause wrong debugging, and the agent must remember to run 'show ID'.

Node process spawn on every Bash/Read/Grep/WebFetch/mcp call. In auto/bypass sessions with hundreds of calls, that costs tens of ms each. Its value is token savings, not better coding decisions, so it does not deliver Jev for routing, permission or review decisions.
Key handling: 'compactio key' writes the key in plaintext into ~/.claude/settings.json. No tests were run by me (static review only); the token-savings claims are unverified.
Unredacted originals of cut outputs and the unredacted last prompt persist forever in ~/.compactio (store/*.txt, sessions/*.json) with default permissions.
Bare `node` in hooks.json conflicts with the user's overridden PATH. Hooks would fail non-blocking (exit 127) and compactio would silently do nothing until node is made resolvable.

/compactio:setup (and the README's step 3) auto-enables the Sweep once a key exists. That sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, which disables MCP tool search (the user's gitnexus and playwright tools load upfront) and Remote Control. It also edits settings.json and installs a Restart=always systemd unit. Users must avoid /compactio:setup and use only `compactio key` or a manual env entry.

Storing OPENROUTER_API_KEY in settings.json env exposes it to every Bash child process and hook. The user's no-secret-leak hook does not yet protect OPENROUTER_API_KEY, so add it to the protected list. The key is global to all projects, but a project-level `OPENROUTER_API_KEY=""` env override disables Jev per client repo (endpoint() checks truthiness, jev.ts:29).
Egress includes playwright, gitnexus and WebFetch/WebSearch content and any `git diff`/`cat` output through Bash, not only test logs.
The model alias ~typesafe/jev-latest floats. Behavior and calibration of the 0.6/0.8 thresholds can shift silently on a Jev release. Pinning needs COMPACTIO_JEV_MODEL=typesafe/jev-1.13.

Cut/tombstone notes embed a plugin-cache path (`node ".../cli.ts" show ID`, hook.ts:128). It is version-specific and breaks after a plugin update or cache GC. In auto or default modes the agent needs a Bash permission for a node call outside the project, which may prompt.
Unlocked session-file writes race under parallel tool calls (store.ts:28-39).

Same-event PostToolUse rewriters run in parallel and the last rewrite wins (docs: 'another hook's rewrite replaces it'). Interaction with the user's gitnexus PostToolUse hook on Bash and Grep is unverified.
The value is token and context savings, not better decisions. It replaces output that Opus would otherwise see with a lossy view, in a user who runs Opus 5.5 with a large window.
entries.verdict: A real, automatic hook-based Jev integration with native OpenRouter support, low context cost and a fail-open design. It is also brand-new, single-author and lightly tested, and it sends redacted code previews off-machine. Reasonable to try hooks-only (never enable Sweep, and keep it off client repos) after verifying the OpenRouter call and hook ordering with GitNexus; skip the proxy entirely.

verification.note:
Repo re-queried (2026-09-30): 3 stars, 0 forks, MIT, not archived, 26 commits by one author on 2026-09-25, no releases, npm compactio 0.2.3 latest (6 versions, all 2026-09-25). Source read in full and matches the audit's core claims. The OpenRouter call is correct: POST /api/alpha/decisions with Bearer OPENROUTER_API_KEY, model ~typesafe/jev-latest (a documented alias), and the request/response shapes match OpenRouter's Decisions reference. Claude Code side is valid: PostToolUse hookSpecificOutput.updatedToolOutput works for all tools (docs, hooks.md ~line 2026). The hook preserves the tool's output shape via setAt, so built-in tools will not silently discard it. The SessionStart 'compact|clear' matcher and the mcp__.* PostToolUse matcher are valid. The hooks-only path is fail-open, with Jev timeout 1.5 s and hook timeout 5 s. It is the only candidate that uses Jev automatically without a 'use jev' prompt.

Score stays at 6. OpenRouter readiness is now confirmed (upward), but I found gaps the audit missed. Unredacted persistence on disk. Bare `node` vs the user's PATH override. Wide egress of client code and MCP output. /compactio:setup auto-enables a proxy that disables MCP tool search. A floating model alias. A 5-day-old single-author alpha whose real Jev-drop path is untested. It stays below 7 because it needs a manual guardrail setup and the value is lossy context trimming, not decision quality.

Recommended use if adopted: hooks-only. Add OPENROUTER_API_KEY to the protected vars in no-secret-leak. Use absolute node paths, either via a wrapper or by editing the hook command. Pin COMPACTIO_JEV_MODEL. Set OPENROUTER_API_KEY=\"\" in the settings of client repos. Never run /compactio:setup or sweep. Confirm the GitNexus PostToolUse hook does not also rewrite output.

judge.why: The only candidate that is a plain command-hook PostToolUse integration, uses OPENROUTER_API_KEY directly, is fully automatic and fails open. It is the least-bad pick. The Jev-drop path is untested on real Claude Code traffic, and it needs guardrails before use.
pros: Deterministic PostToolUse (Bash|Read|Grep|WebFetch|WebSearch|mcp__.*) returning updatedToolOutput. It preserves the output shape via setAt, so built-in tools will not silently discard it
Fail-open with a 1.5s Jev timeout and 5s hook timeout. Never cuts Read of code files
Redacts the copy sent to Jev, and only outputs of 6k+ chars go out
Choice-based (keep/stub/headtail) with a 0.6 confidence gate, plus a recovery note and CLI show ID
Client repos can disable it with a project-level OPENROUTER_API_KEY="" override
cons: Unredacted original outputs and the last prompt persist forever in ~/.compactio (store, sessions) with default permissions
Bare `node` in hooks.json conflicts with the user's overridden PATH, so hooks exit 127 non-blocking and silently do nothing unless the command is edited to an absolute path
/compactio:setup auto-enables the Sweep proxy (sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, disables MCP tool search and Remote Control, installs a systemd unit). Never run it
Egress covers playwright, gitnexus, WebFetch, git diff and cat output, i.e. client code
The 0.6 gate is untuned. The floating ~typesafe/jev-latest alias needs pinning to typesafe/jev-1.13. Injected text in an output can steer Jev toward hiding the middle
Unlocked session-file writes race under parallel tool calls. Interaction with the gitnexus PostToolUse hook is unverified. The value is only context savings

entries.name: jev-lens
entries.what: Claude Code plugin (monorepo also has a host-independent core and a pi extension). A PostToolUse hook on Read|Bash|Grep intercepts tool results of about 1200 tokens or more, builds candidate views from the output's own lines (outline, focus, testlog, matches, head/tail and others, using tree-sitter for code), and asks Jev (Noul/Choice questions via TypeSafe SDK systemOne) which is the smallest view that still serves the agent's next step. The hook then replaces the tool output via updatedToolOutput, with a footer that points to a `recall` MCP tool for the full text. It never generates or summarizes text. Claimed 79% token reduction on large tool results, measured on 500 OpenHands trajectories via the pi harness. The Claude Code plugin itself is explicitly not yet measured on Claude Code sessions.
entries.autoInvocation: Deterministic PostToolUse hook. It fires on every Read, Bash and Grep result of about 1200 tokens or more, with no model discretion and no prompt needed. The recall MCP tool is model-discretion, prompted by the footer text in the compressed result.
security: MIT licence, 1 author (Didrik Rognstad). Repo created 2026-09-18, 79 commits in about 2 days, 1 star, 1 fork. Several commits are co-authored by Claude.

No postinstall or preinstall scripts (grepped all package.json). Installed through the Claude Code marketplace, which runs npm ci from the standalone packages/claude-code/package-lock.json. Dependencies are jev-lens core, @typesafe-ai/sdk, web-tree-sitter, @vscode/tree-sitter-wasm and @binclusive/tree-sitter-kotlin-wasm (a small third-party wasm package). Supply chain is thin and brand new.
The key is read from env or from key.json (mode 0600 when written by storeKey). It is sent only as an HTTP Authorization header, not in argv. The hook and MCP server take no key argument.
The core's loadDotEnv only reads .env from the package or monorepo root, never from the target project. With the plugin installed under node_modules this is safe.

The MCP server is dependency-free JSON-RPC over stdio. recall and stats read only the local store. Recall ids come from tool_use_id and are used as file lookups. I did not audit sanitization of the id, so path traversal is unchecked.
The hook does no shell execution beyond node. The two logging hooks run `cat >> events.jsonl`.
entries.dataEgress: To api.typesafe.ai, or to OpenRouter if the base URL is overridden, one or two systemOne calls per large (about 1200 tokens or more) Read, Bash or Grep result. The state contains: the first user request (600 chars), the latest user message (400 chars), the assistant text before the call (600 chars), the tool name, the tool args (300 chars, which include file paths and shell commands), and previews of each candidate view (about 900 chars each, the full view up to 1500 chars) drawn from the actual file or command output. For code, a second call sends block signatures plus 240-char previews. Small outputs, Edit, Write, images and MCP tools send nothing. Per-call egress is a few KB of source snippets, command output and prompt text, and this repeats all day on client code. Whether the provider retains or trains on it is unverified. The user's PreToolUse secret guard blocks reads of secret files, but secrets that show up in Bash output (env dumps, logs) would still be previewed to the provider.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open. Any exception, non-2xx response, missing key, or exceeding the 15s per-request SDK timeout (systemOne timeout 15000, SDK maxRetries 2 with backoff, so worst case is far above 15s) ends with exit 0 and no output, and Claude gets the original result. The hard cap is 30s (JEV_LENS_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS), and the hook config timeout is 40s. This means a slow or down provider can stall a large Read or Bash result by up to about 30s before it falls back, so no timeout is tight. Without a key it silently uses a deterministic mock classifier (size and tool-type rules) and still compresses, which is not fail-open in the sense of 'no change'. JEV_LENS_CLASSIFIER=mock or JEV_LENS_DISABLED=1 turns it off.
entries.contextCost: Small. There are 2 MCP tools (recall and stats), and the server sends no `instructions`. Tool definitions are about 150-250 tokens total. The footer added to each compressed result is about 60-100 tokens, but it replaces thousands of tokens. UserPromptSubmit and MessageDisplay hooks print nothing, so nothing is injected. The net effect is a reduction in context. It removes a large share of large tool results, as claimed by the author (79% on the benchmark, 31% on their own sessions). The risk is a lossy view that forces a recall round trip, which costs a tool call.
pros: This is the only candidate so far that gives fully automatic use of Jev inside Claude Code: a deterministic PostToolUse hook on Read|Bash|Grep. There is no prompting and no reliance on the model deciding to call a tool, which is exactly what the user asked for.

The Jev usage plays to Jev's strength: typed Noul questions and a Choice over candidate views return probabilities, with no free text. Code applies the thresholds. Cost is negligible at about $0.042 per 1M input tokens.
Fail-open by design: any error returns the original output. Code is sent in full unless Jev is confident. Every retained line is byte-for-byte original, and a recall tool fetches the rest.
Compression happens before the first send, so it does not break the prompt cache. The author measured that post-send pruning cost 17% more money and left it out of the Claude Code plugin.

The context footprint is tiny (2 MCP tools, no server instructions, no output from the logging hooks), and the net effect is fewer tokens in context. This helps on long sessions on a subscription plan.

OpenRouter routing is likely a config-only change. The code passes no baseURL, and the SDK honors TYPESAFE_BASE_URL and POSTs /v1/systemone, matching OpenRouter's System One path. The model is overridable via JEV_LENS_MODEL.

Tunable and switchable: JEV_LENS_DISABLED=1, per-kind thresholds, min tokens, hook timeout. The stats tool, /jev-lens:stats and the statusline segment let the user measure recall rate before trusting it. Small readable code (about 830 lines in the plugin), MIT, no postinstall scripts, dependency-free MCP server.
cons: Very immature: repo created 2026-09-18, 1 contributor, 1 star, 79 commits in 2 days, partly AI-authored. The Claude Code plugin has explicitly not been measured on Claude Code sessions. The headline 79% comes from an OpenHands/pi benchmark, and even there 2 of 26 later edits missed their block.

Lossy on the main model's inputs. Opus sees a partial Read of client code, and an edit whose old text is a line it never saw fails. The mitigation is thresholds and recall, but the risk is real for a senior dev doing precise edits, and a recall costs an extra round trip and tokens.

Not OpenRouter-native. OpenRouter compatibility rests on the assumption that the /v1/systemone request and response schemas are identical to TypeSafe's. This is unverified, and the model id may need changing to typesafe/jev-1.13. It needs a live test with a real OpenRouter key.

Data egress: previews of source files and command output, plus the user's prompts and assistant text, go to a third party on every large tool result, all day, on personal and client code. This may breach client confidentiality or NDA terms. Bash output can contain secrets that the PreToolUse guard does not stop, since it guards inputs.
Plaintext local copies: events.jsonl (all prompts and assistant messages) and all compressed outputs are kept for 90 days in ~/.claude/jev-lens, and may hold client code and secrets.

Latency and failure timing: 0.5-1s on each large result, and a Jev outage can stall a result for up to 30s (SDK retries plus the 15s timeout) before the fail-open fallback. Silent fall-back to a mock classifier when no key is found means it compresses anyway with crude rules.

Interaction risk with existing hooks: GitNexus already has a PostToolUse hook on Grep|Bash. Two hooks that rewrite or augment the same tool result can conflict, and this needs an ordering test. Also, updatedToolOutput for built-in tools is a newer hook feature that I could not verify on 2.1.285. Two extra hooks (UserPromptSubmit, MessageDisplay) fire on every prompt and message.

Another dependency chain to trust: Node TypeScript execution in the plugin cache, the tree-sitter wasm packages including a third-party Kotlin build, and the marketplace fetching from a single-author GitHub repo (pin a commit or version).

Silent misconfiguration failure modes: missing or wrong key file falls back to a mock heuristic that still compresses (crude size/tool rules), and 4xx errors from OpenRouter (bad model id, exhausted credits) fail open with no user-visible signal except log.jsonl. The user could think Jev is working when it is not; check /jev-lens:stats for mock=false.

Lossy Read of client code interacts badly with precise Edit work in auto and bypassPermissions sessions: an Edit whose old_string spans lines Opus never saw fails, or Opus may guess. The author's own harm data (2 of 26 later edits missed, 2.2% dropped identifier used) is unmeasured on Claude Code.

Per-large-result egress of Read/Bash content to OpenRouter and its upstream provider with no redaction. The existing no-secret-leak PreToolUse guard does not cover tool OUTPUT, so env dumps, logs and secrets printed by Bash are previewed to a third party; prompt text (600+400 chars) and assistant text (600 chars) are also sent. Client NDA risk. Add OPENROUTER_API_KEY and ~/.claude/jev-lens/key.json to the secret guard.

Plaintext local retention: events.jsonl (every raw UserPromptSubmit payload incl. pasted secrets, and every assistant message delta) plus full copies of compressed outputs for 90 days, no redaction. The data dir is CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA when set (~/.claude/plugins/data/jev-lens-*), while the key file is fixed at ~/.claude/jev-lens/key.json.

Upstream instability: OpenRouter /alpha endpoint with no SLA, and the plugin depends on unversioned answer schema fields. The jev-latest alias floats (~typesafe/jev-latest), so behavior can change silently; pin jev-1.13.

Jev injection sensitivity (JevOut: natural context can flip decisions): tool output text is in the Jev state, so a malicious file or log can bias which lines Opus sees (hide lines). Text cannot be injected into Opus, but it can be hidden from Opus.
Extra process spawns on every prompt and every streamed message batch (MessageDisplay), in a stack that already has slow gitnexus hooks.
entries.verdict: The best-fitting automatic integration found so far: a deterministic, fail-open PostToolUse hook that uses Jev's typed decisions in the way Jev was designed for, and it should reach OpenRouter with only TYPESAFE_BASE_URL and JEV_LENS_MODEL overrides (needs a live check). Trial it on personal projects first, watching recall counts and edit failures, and hold off on client code until the data-egress and lossy-Read risks are accepted.

verification.note: Verified: repo facts (1 star, MIT, not archived, 79 commits, created 2026-09-18, last push 2026-09-19); hook events and fields are valid in 2.1.285 (PostToolUse updatedToolOutput, MessageDisplay, UserPromptSubmit) and the Read/Bash shapes match; Claude Code runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts` from a plugin's package-lock.json (binary strings), so the install path holds and no install scripts run. OpenRouter is a config-only switch documented by OpenRouter (TYPESAFE_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api, OpenRouter key, default model jev-latest maps to ~typesafe/jev-latest); no live call made (no key, no candidate code executed). Audit errors corrected: recall path traversal is sanitized (safeName), MCP server is not dependency-free, the gitnexus-conflict con is overstated (that hook never writes updatedToolOutput), MessageDisplay spawns per streamed batch, 4xx errors fail open instantly and silently. Score lowered from 7 to 6: it is the only truly automatic, fail-open candidate with small context cost, but it is 12 days old, single-author, unmeasured on Claude Code, lossy for Read-then-Edit on code (only 31 percent savings on code, with author-reported 2.2 percent dropped-identifier harm), ships client code and command output to a third party on every large result with plaintext local retention, and can silently degrade to a mock classifier. Recommendation: trial on personal projects only, with JEV_LENS_MODEL pinned to jev-1.13, key in key.json (not exported env), key path added to the secret guard, and check /jev-lens:stats for mock=false and recall rate before any client work.

judge.why: Automatic PostToolUse hook on Read, Bash and Grep results of ~1200 tokens or more, with a recall MCP tool. The design is good, but it is lossy for code Reads, and misconfiguration degrades silently.
pros: Deterministic PostToolUse with valid 2.1.285 fields and output shapes. Claude Code runs npm ci --ignore-scripts on install
Recall MCP tool with sanitized ids (no traversal). /jev-lens:stats shows whether Jev or the mock classifier is running
Fail-open on 4xx, timeout bounded at 30s. Retries only on 408/429/5xx
Byte-exact retained lines. The gitnexus conflict concern was overstated because that hook never writes updatedToolOutput
cons: Only 31% savings on code (79% headline is mostly command output). Author-reported 2.2% dropped-identifier-later-used and 2 of 26 later edits missed, which is bad for Opus Read-then-Edit, especially in bypass or auto mode
Missing or wrong key silently falls back to a mock heuristic classifier that still compresses. 4xx from OpenRouter fail open with no visible signal
MessageDisplay hook spawns a shell per streamed batch, and UserPromptSubmit appends every raw prompt. events.jsonl and full copies of compressed outputs are kept 90 days in plaintext
Client code and command output egress with no redaction. The key file at ~/.claude/jev-lens/key.json is not covered by no-secret-leak
MCP server imports the jev-lens npm package (not dependency-free). Floating alias, so pin jev-1.13. Single maintainer, 12 days old, unmeasured on Claude Code

entries.name: maxkimambo/jev-mcp
entries.what: Claude Code plugin (also Codex/pi) bundling an 11-tool MCP server, a skill, a /jev:jev on|off|status command and two hooks. Tools send bulk text (grep windows, whole files, fetched web pages) to Jev and return only typed answers (line numbers, values, verdicts with probabilities), so Claude reads less. Hooks (when switched on) inject a per-prompt reminder and deny the first Grep/rg/grep per prompt toward jev_search and the first WebFetch after a WebSearch toward jev_rank_pages. Off by default.
entries.autoInvocation: Mixed but strongest of the candidates: deterministic hooks (PreToolUse deny of first Grep/rg/grep per prompt and of WebFetch after WebSearch; UserPromptSubmit reminder) plus skill description trigger and model-discretion MCP tools. Requires a one-time manual '/jev:jev on' (off by default by design); after that no user prompting. Read hints are advisory only.
security: No API key in argv: key from env or ~/.config/jev/api_key, file must be 0600 and owned by user or server refuses it; key never a tool argument; key file itself is on the tool file-read deny list. Plugin.json env block deliberately omits the key.

Server-side file reads are confined to allowed roots (default = server cwd, plus ~/.config/jev/roots), containment checked before and after symlink resolution, credential files refused by name (.env*, .ssh, .aws, .gnupg, *.pem, *.key, id_rsa, credentials.json). Name-based only: secrets hardcoded inside ordinary source files are still sent.

Prompt-injection surface: file paths and questions come from the model; fetched pages and grep windows are wrapped with 'treat as data' guards; jev_screen and per-page injection signal withhold sentences from suspicious pages. Jev is a probabilistic classifier, not a guarantee.

jev_rank_pages SSRF protections: https only, refuses private/loopback/link-local hosts on connection and each redirect, JEV_ALLOW_HOSTS opt-out; converters (trafilatura, markitdown) get bytes on stdin only. Shell execution limited to execFile of rg/trafilatura/markitdown (no shell string).

install.sh is a curl|sh installer that also does 'curl astral.sh/install.sh | sh' for uv and 'uv tool install' of ripgrep, trafilatura, markitdown; it is optional (plugin can be added via 'claude plugin marketplace add'). No npm postinstall; CI uses npm ci --ignore-scripts and npm audit.

Committed 1.8 MB esbuild bundle (bundle/index.js, cli.js, pi.js) is what actually runs, including the vendored @typesafe-ai/sdk and MCP SDK; CI checks git diff --exit-code bundle/ against a rebuild, but a reviewer cannot practically audit it. Single maintainer, 5-day-old repo, so supply-chain trust is entirely in one GitHub account (marketplace add pulls main).
entries.dataEgress: While switched on: (1) jev_search sends ripgrep candidate lines with neighbouring lines, in windows, from the searched directory (credential file names filtered) plus questions; (2) jev_locate/jev_extract/jev_ask paths/jev_triage send the entire text of the named files in windows (up to 200k chars per state), never truncated; (3) jev_rank_pages sends fetched page text; (4) jev_classify/score/check/ask send whatever `state` Claude passes. Destination is OpenRouter then TypeSafe (with an OpenRouter key) or TypeSafe directly. Not sent: the user's prompts or conversation as such (unless Claude puts them in state), diffs, or the API key. Source code of client projects is sent as file content, filtered only by file name. README/CLI warn 'Keep it off for private work'. The on/off switch is a single global file, not per project, so client-project safety depends on the user toggling it.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open for hooks: cli.js hook path wraps everything in try/catch and outputs nothing on error; hooks stay silent when switch is off or absent (src/cli.ts:140-151); hook timeout 3 s. The MCP tools fail as classified isError results (authentication, rate_limit, connection, malformed_response, file_access, disabled) and the skill tells Claude to carry on without Jev; defaults are JEV_TIMEOUT_MS=5000 and JEV_MAX_RETRIES=0 (src/lib.ts:46-47), so a slow Jev costs at most ~5 s per request then an error. The search hook is designed so a failed jev_search still lets the retried Grep run (only the first search per prompt is denied), i.e. at most one wasted turn. Missing key means every call errors, hooks would still deny the first grep and redirect to a broken tool if the switch is on.
entries.contextCost: 11 MCP tools; tool defs (title+description+inputSchema+outputSchema strings in src/index.ts registerTool blocks) about 19.7k chars, roughly 4.9k tokens, plus JSON-schema overhead so likely 5-7k tokens if not deferred (Claude Code tool search may defer them). No MCP server `instructions`. Skill: description ~700 chars always loaded, body ~4.5k chars (~1.1k tokens) when triggered. UserPromptSubmit hook injects about 1.0 KB (~250 tokens) as additionalContext on EVERY prompt while on. Deny messages ~500 chars each, and each tool result returns full probability distributions (extra tokens per call). Nothing injected while off except the tool defs and skill description.
pros: Only candidate seen that is genuinely automatic: PreToolUse hook (src/cli.ts:90-93) deterministically steers the first grep of each prompt to jev_search, plus a UserPromptSubmit reminder and skill trigger, so the user never has to say 'use jev' after one /jev:jev on.
OpenRouter supported natively and verified in code: sk-or- key -> https://openrouter.ai/api + ~typesafe/jev-latest over /v1/systemone (src/lib.ts:554-577); works with just ~/.config/jev/api_key.

Sensible safety design: off-by-default global switch, key never in argv or tool args, key file mode enforced 0600, file root confinement with symlink checks, credential-file name deny list, SSRF guard for URL fetching, ledger with no content.
Fail-open behavior: hooks swallow errors, 5 s timeout and 0 retries, classified errors, skill says carry on without Jev, denied grep is allowed on retry.

Tools fit Jev's actual strengths (ranking/locating/extracting over windows, injection screening via Noul) instead of asking it to reason; batching guidance (up to 16 questions per pass) is aligned with TypeSafe's cookbook.
jev_screen / jev_rank_pages injection screening and withholding of suspicious pages is a real security add for a bypass-permissions user browsing the web.

Reasonable engineering hygiene for a young repo: MIT, 12 test files (~2.9k lines) run offline against a stand-in API, CI on Node 20/22/24 with bundle-matches-source check and npm audit, ledger/status command for measuring cost and savings.
cons: Repo is 5 days old (created 2026-09-25, first commit 2026-09-17), 0 stars, 0 forks, no releases, 2 contributors (one wrote 43 of 50 commits), version 0.14.0; no evidence of real-world use.
Ships opaque 1.8 MB committed bundles that run instead of the readable source, and install.sh does curl|sh (uv) and uv tool installs; marketplace add tracks main of a single-maintainer repo.

Sends whole file contents and grep windows to OpenRouter/TypeSafe; secret filtering is by filename only, so hardcoded secrets in source files go out; unsuitable for client/NDA projects and the global switch is not per-project, so the user must remember to toggle it.

Hook denies the first Grep/rg per prompt, adding a failed tool call and extra turn whenever Claude wants an exact-string search; with GitNexus (Grep|Glob|Bash) and secret-guard hooks on the same matchers, hook ordering and duplicated denials are untested. A node process is also spawned for every Grep/Read/Bash/Web call even while off.

Weak value proposition for this user: Opus-class main model with GitNexus graph search and native Grep already reads code cheaply and precisely; Jev is a probabilistic ranker over windows and its own README says to keep deterministic code when it decides correctly and warns it cannot compute; recall failures in jev_search/jev_locate mean silently missed lines.

Per-prompt reminder (~250 tokens) plus 11 tool schemas (~5-7k tokens if not deferred) and tool results that carry full probability distributions partly offset the tokens saved; the instruction 'say in one line when Jev saved you a read' adds chatter.

Uses the System One API (/v1/systemone), not the alpha Decisions API, and requires the user to run '/jev:jev on' manually each install; the TYPESAFE_API_KEY env var, if present, silently outranks OPENROUTER_API_KEY.
Unverified quality claims: no benchmarks of saved tokens or answer recall in repo; Theo's skepticism that Jev may be a small distilled router model is untested here.

Context mismatch: OpenRouter's Jev has a 32k-token context but the tool's default per-state cap is 200k chars, so jev_ask/paths and jev_triage on big files can fail upstream unless JEV_MAX_STATE_CHARS is lowered.

Floating alias '~typesafe/jev-latest' is the default on OpenRouter, so model behaviour and calibration can change without any repo change; pin JEV_MODEL=typesafe/jev-1.13 for reproducibility. The API is also OpenRouter's /alpha-era System One product with no SLA.
Bare 'node' in plugin.json and hooks.json is a risk with the user's overridden PATH; absolute paths are needed for reliability.

The hook denies the first Grep or Bash rg/grep/ag/ack per prompt and the first WebFetch after a WebSearch. Marker files are keyed by session_id, so subagents and headless or workflow runs that share the session_id can consume or trigger the denial. Every subagent or automation that greps pays an extra failed call, even with no benefit.

jev_search uses ripgrep with .gitignore/.ignore honoured and hidden files skipped, so it searches a different file set than the native Grep. Missed hits are silent, and this is on top of Jev's probabilistic-ranking recall risk.

The user's no-secret-leak hook does not protect ~/.config/jev/api_key or OPENROUTER_API_KEY (the brief notes the latter is not in its list). The key file is 0600 and the server denies reading it, but Claude's own Read/Bash tools are not blocked by this plugin.

The npm package named 'jev-mcp' (v0.5.1, rashedInt32) is a different, older project from this plugin repo; the repo says it started from that project. Install via marketplace only; do not npx jev-mcp expecting this code.
Turn-marker files in ~/.claude/jev-think/turns/ are created per session and never cleaned (minor disk litter).
entries.verdict: Best-in-class for the 'automatic, no prompting' requirement (hook-enforced grep and WebFetch redirection plus skill) with native, code-verified OpenRouter support, but it is a 5-day-old single-maintainer alpha that ships opaque bundles and sends file contents to a third party. Worth trialling on personal projects only, after reading src/ and bundle provenance; keep it off (or install per-project) for client work, and check the interplay of its hooks with GitNexus first.

verification.note: Most audit facts hold. Re-queried live: 0 stars, 0 forks, 0 open issues, MIT, not archived, created 2026-09-25, pushed 2026-09-25, no releases. The local clone has 50 commits (43 Max Kimambo, 7 rashed parvez), first commit dated 2026-09-17 (history inherited from rashedInt32/jev-mcp). OpenRouter support is real in code: an sk-or- key gives baseURL https://openrouter.ai/api, model ~typesafe/jev-latest, POST /v1/systemone (bundle/index.js:21912). The env precedence and the 0600 key-file logic are as described. That model id is confirmed in OpenRouter's public catalog with 32k context and $0.042/M input. Hook mechanics are valid for Claude Code 2.1.x: hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision 'deny' plus reason, and UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse additionalContext. Hooks are silent and exit 0 when the switch is off or on any error, so they fail open; a deny fires at most once per prompt. All 11 tools plus the hooks, command and skill exist in source. No telemetry or shell-string execution found; execFile is used only for converters. Corrections: the bundle is about 1.4 MB, not 1.8 MB, and the hook-side cli.js is only 6 KB and auditable. New issues are the 200k-char vs 32k-token context mismatch, the floating alias, bare 'node' vs the user's PATH override, and the global off-by-default switch, which undercuts the 'never prompt' goal. Score is lowered from 6 to 5.5: it is the strongest 'automatic' design but it is an alpha 5-day-old single-maintainer repo, sends client source (filename-only secret filtering) to a third party, and adds deny-retry friction beside the GitNexus and secret-guard hooks. It is fine to trial on personal repos. I did not run or build any code, so bundle-vs-source equality and the runtime hook ordering with the user's existing hooks are unverified.

judge.why: The strongest automatic-nudge design, with 11 Jev tools (search, locate, extract, triage, ask). It is off by default and does not filter tool output. It changes which tools Claude uses.
pros: OpenRouter works out of the box. Hook-side cli.js is only 6 KB and auditable, with no network or child_process code, and a static scan found no telemetry
Hooks fail open (silent exit 0 on error or when the switch is off). A PreToolUse deny fires at most once per prompt
Key file is 0600 and the server denies reading it
cons: Off by default with one global switch (~/.claude/jev-think/state.json). Client work needs a manual flip, which contradicts the 'never prompt' goal
Denies the first Grep, rg or WebFetch per prompt, costing an extra turn. Subagents and headless runs sharing a session_id consume or trigger the denial
jev_search searches a different file set than native Grep (.gitignore and hidden files skipped), so misses are silent. No recall or token benchmark
JEV_MAX_STATE_CHARS default 200k chars exceeds OpenRouter's 32k-token context, so set it to about 80k or less. Bare `node` vs the overridden PATH. Floating alias
Sends client source (filename-only secret filtering) to a third party and adds friction beside the gitnexus and secret-guard hooks

entries.name: tamaratran/jev-pruner (plugin id: fast-jev-output)
entries.what: Claude Code plugin built on Claude Code's early-access "function hooks" (a TypeScript module registering on('tool.call', {tool:'Bash'}) that wraps next()). After a Bash command runs and before the result reaches the main model, if stdout exceeds 10,000 estimated tokens it splits the output into 20-line chunks (max 200) and sends conversation history plus chunks to Jev. It asks one noul question per chunk: does any line here need to remain available. Chunks with a low keep probability become "[N lines omitted]" markers. The full output is archived under .claude/fast-jev-output/ with a recovery footer. Errors, diagnostics, JSON/XML/diffs, source, docs, and cat/jq/git diff output are protected. On any failure the original output is returned. It also ships an opt-in Codex wrapper and an eval/training harness (a Kev-0.8B fine-tune pipeline, marked superseded).
interface: library export trimOutput / buildJevRequest / parseJevResponse (src/index.ts, src/jev.ts)
entries.autoInvocation: Deterministic hook. It triggers on every Bash tool call with no user or model action, gated internally by output size. This is exactly the "automatic, user never asks" behavior, and Jev is used as a real classifier in the hot path.
security: Plugin code runs with hook privileges (fs read/write, http.fetch, session.messages, settings.read) inside Claude Code. It is TypeScript from a 12-day-old, largely AI-authored repo, so review before enabling. I did not audit the whole of src/output.ts (26 KB).
API key: read from plugin option, env, or settings.env, and sent only as a Bearer header via $.http.fetch. The key is never in argv or a process list. The apiKey option is marked sensitive.
The hook reads the entire settings via $.settings.read() but takes only env.TYPESAFE_API_KEY.

Prompt-injection surface: Bash output and history are sent to Jev, which returns only numeric probabilities, so injection can at most bias which lines are dropped. A crafted output could hide lines from the main model (integrity risk), mitigated by the archive footer and protection of error and result lines.

Secret handling is weak. looksSecret (src/secrets.ts) is a regex that only suppresses local archiving. The README says it does not redact or prevent sending content to Jev. Output from cat .env or printenv still goes to the remote API, and the pruned result then states 're-run the command'.
Writes .claude/fast-jev-output/bash-*.txt (full stdout+stderr) in every project, with a self-gitignore. Client-project output persists on disk unencrypted.
entries.dataEgress: Per pruned Bash call, Jev receives {context, task, history, command, chunks, category}. That is the command string, the full stdout or stderr split into chunks (up to about 25k state tokens per request, several parallel requests), the last three user prompts (500 chars each), and the session history from $.session.messages() (up to the newest 4096 messages): user and assistant text, complete tool inputs, and tool-result text and structured data. That includes file contents Claude has read and earlier command output. Requests go to api.typesafe.ai, or to OpenRouter if baseUrl is set, and OpenRouter forwards them to TypeSafe. Requests are not sent for output at or below 10,000 tokens. Most Bash calls are small, so egress happens only for large outputs (builds, test logs, large greps). When it does trigger, it can send a large slice of the whole conversation, code and client data included, to a third party. That is a significant concern for client projects. History is re-sent per request and per history segment.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open, by design. Any exception, missing key, HTTP error, archive-write failure, or unfittable budget returns the original result (catch at hooks/fast-jev-output.ts:283 returns answer). Jev is called only after Bash has finished. However, I found no explicit timeout or AbortSignal in the plugin code (grep for timeout, AbortSignal and Promise.race hits only the toast timeout). It relies on the host's $.http.fetch timeout, so a hung Jev could stall the tool result for the host timeout. The retry policy is a max_tokens_exceeded retry twice with a halved budget, and request count is capped at min(12, ceil(visibleChars/192)). With the key unset, pruning is silently skipped ("missing_key"). Whether the host's function-hook API changes and breaks the plugin is untested, but the try/catch means it degrades to passthrough.
entries.contextCost: Zero added tool definitions: it is not an MCP server, has no skill, and injects no system prompt or instructions. It only shrinks tool results, adding a short footer ("[fast-jev-output full output: <path> ...]") and "[N lines omitted]" markers to pruned results. Net effect on context is negative. The author reports about 83% reduction on synthetic tests and 54% on real captures, but only when a single Bash output exceeds 10,000 tokens (about 40k chars). Claude Code already truncates or persists such outputs to a file with a head preview, so the real saving is mostly about surfacing the relevant part instead of the head, which is the plugin's stated use case (76k-char log example).
pros: It is truly automatic: a tool.call hook wrapping Bash, with no prompting or model discretion, which matches the user's requirement. Jev's noul primitive is an apt fit for a per-chunk 'keep or drop' decision (hooks/fast-jev-output.ts:162; src/output.ts).
Fail-open everywhere: try/catch returns the original result, and a missing key means silent passthrough. It adds no context tokens, since there is no MCP or skill (contextCost zero).

Conservative retention design: errors, diagnostics, test totals, artifact paths, source, docs, JSON/XML/diffs and cat/git diff output are never pruned, dropping requires keep-probability <=0.1, and the full output is archived so the model can Read it (README 'Information retention rules').
OpenRouter-compatible via configuration: baseUrl plus apiKey are already plugin options, and OpenRouter's System One endpoint claims TypeSafe-SDK compatibility with jev-latest mapped to typesafe/.

Already tuned for Claude Code: it handles Claude's persisted-output files (fixing the 'head preview hides the error' problem), uses a native-preview budget cap, and includes a recursion guard for reading archives.
Active development (164 commits, MIT), with extensive tests and evals including paired native-vs-pruner arms.
Cost is small: about $0.042 per 1M input tokens, and it fires only on rare huge outputs.
cons: Depends on the early-access CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS API, which the README says may change between releases. The flag string exists in the installed 2.1.285 binary, but the plugin's types were generated from 2.1.274, and behavior on 2.1.285 is unverified. It could break silently, and fail-open would then hide that.

Data egress is broad. When it fires, it sends the command, the full output and much of the session history (file contents Claude read, tool results) to a third party. Its own README says the secret check does not stop content being sent to Jev. This is risky for client projects, and there is no per-project disable other than not setting the key.

There is no OPENROUTER_API_KEY support. The key must be given as the apiKey option or by putting the OpenRouter key in TYPESAFE_API_KEY. Live OpenRouter compatibility is untested by the author, whose tests target api.typesafe.ai only.

Narrow value: it only helps on the rare single Bash output above 10k tokens (about 40k chars). Claude Code already persists and previews such output, and cat/git diff/JSON/source are excluded. Most daily coding therefore sees zero effect. Real captures showed only 54% reduction, and the savings are a small share of tokens in an Opus session.

Lossy pruning risk: chunks that look like progress noise but hold the needed fact are dropped (the 0.1 threshold is 'a retention policy, not a measured error guarantee'). The model may not know to look at the archive.
History partitioning can generate up to 12 Jev requests with re-sent history, so latency and cost on big logs are unbounded by any explicit timeout. There is no explicit timeout in the plugin code.

Immature and largely AI-written: 12 days old, 3 contributors (98 of 164 commits are Devin AI), 0 releases, no CI, and a 2,000+ line eval scaffold. The repo mixes in unrelated material (Codex, training, macOS demo, login skills). The plugin name (fast-jev-output) does not match the repo name.

Writes full command output, including possible secrets, to .claude/fast-jev-output/ in each project, which is a client-data hygiene concern. It also overlaps with existing hooks: the user's PreToolUse secret-leak guard and GitNexus post-Bash hook also touch Bash results, and ordering or interaction with them is undefined.
Requires modifying settings env (a flag plus the key). Being a TS module loaded by the CLI, it is not sandboxed.
entries.verdict: The only candidate that genuinely uses Jev automatically inside Claude Code, as a deterministic fail-open hook with zero context cost, and it can point at OpenRouter through the baseUrl and apiKey options. The value is narrow (rare >10k-token Bash outputs), it depends on an early-access hook API, and it ships large slices of session history to a third party. It is worth a trial on personal projects only, not client projects; verify the OpenRouter baseUrl and response shape before relying on it.

judge.why: Also automatic and fail-open on large Bash output (over 10k tokens), and the origin of several Pi/omp ports. It is the same function-hook risk as jevprune, plus broad egress.
