entries.name: jevprune (ibrahemid/jevprune)
entries.what: Claude Code plugin (plus CLI and library, npm package jevprune 0.2.0) that prunes long Bash tool results before the model reads them. It uses an early-access "function hook" (module hooks/jevprune.ts registers on("tool.call", {tool:"Bash"}) and post-processes the answer). Selection: keep the last 40 lines, error-signature lines with 3 lines of context; send the remaining lines to Jev in token-budgeted windows (25k tokens, 4 concurrent), one Noul yes/no question per line ("is this line needed for the task?", keep if P>=0.3); collapse dropped runs into markers. The full output is saved to ~/.jevprune/runs/<id>.log and can be recovered with `jevprune show <id> --lines a-b`. Task text = last 3 user prompts (500 chars each) plus the command. Commits: 40 in 3 days (2026-09-18 to 09-21), single author.
interface: CLI: jevprune run --task T -- cmd args
plugin userConfig: apiKey (sensitive, keychain), threshold, diagnostics
entries.autoInvocation: Deterministic hook, fully automatic (tool.call hook on every Bash call), no prompting needed; the skill only helps the model recover dropped lines. Requires CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 in settings env (early access) and a key. This is the only candidate style that meets the "Claude Code must use Jev without me asking" requirement.
security: Not a curl|sh installer: install is `claude plugin marketplace add ibrahemid/jevprune` (marketplace.json source "./"), no npm postinstall script (package.json scripts have only build/test/gate/prepublishOnly), no telemetry code found (grep for telemetry/postinstall empty). child_process spawn is used only in src/runner.ts for the CLI `run` command (no shell) and not in the hook.

API key handling in the hook: read via host $.env.get (env), plugin userConfig (keychain, marked sensitive) or settings.json env. Sent as Authorization Bearer header via host $.http.fetch, so it is not in argv or the process list. Errors are truncated to 200 chars (client.ts:158,193).
Hook runs in the Claude Code function-hook sandbox (no Node, only host fs/http/env/settings/session/process nouns). Plugin can read session messages, settings and env values through those nouns.

Secret guard is heuristic only (src/core/secrets.ts): skips pruning and Jev when the command matches env/printenv/.env/secret/token/password/id_rsa etc. or output contains a PRIVATE KEY block, `api_key|password|access_token|client_secret [=:] value`, or URL credentials. Anything else (source snippets, stack traces, tokens in other formats such as Bearer/ghp_/sk- in logs) is sent to the API.

Prompt injection surface: the pruning decision is made by Jev on untrusted command output, and the Jev question includes task text taken from user prompts. Output is only filtered, never rewritten, so injection risk is limited to a hostile line being dropped or kept. Risk of silently dropping the one relevant line, mitigated by markers and `jevprune show`.
Run logs are written 0600 under ~/.jevprune/runs (full raw command output persisted on disk for up to 200 runs / 256 MiB); credential-looking output is deleted after detection.
entries.dataEgress: For each eligible Bash result (over 60 lines, exit 0, not document, source, JSON, diff or help, not secret-looking, under 16 MiB, not already kept by the rule pass) the following goes to https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone in windows of about 25k tokens: the command string, a task string made of the last three user prompts (500 chars each) from the session, a rubric, and every candidate output line with its line number (blank lines and lines already kept by the rules are omitted). No file contents beyond what the command printed, no diffs (diff-looking output is excluded), and no non-Bash tool output. Locally it also writes full output to ~/.jevprune/runs. For client projects this means build, test and log output plus user prompt excerpts leave the machine (to TypeSafe, or to OpenRouter and its upstream if patched).
entries.failureMode: Fail-open. Missing key means pass-through (one log line per session). Any exception in the hook's prune path is caught and the original answer returned (hook.ts:182-186). Jev timeout, 401, 429, 5xx or malformed response falls back to the rule-based selection (first 40 lines, last 40 lines, error signatures with context) and states the reason in the footer. Per-window timeout 10 s (windowTimeoutMs), 1 immediate retry with no backoff (http-client.ts:114, DEFAULT_JEV_MAX_RETRIES = 1), concurrency 4; worst case blocks a Bash result roughly 20 s per window group before fallback. Note fallback still rewrites (drops) output even though Jev failed, so an outage degrades quality, not availability.
entries.contextCost: Very low and net negative (saves context). 0 MCP tools, no MCP server instructions. One skill with a ~170 char description (about 45 tokens always loaded, body about 1.2k tokens loaded only on trigger). The hook adds per pruned result a footer line plus [jevprune: N lines dropped, run id, lines a-b] markers (about 30-60 tokens each); a toast is shown to the user only, not the model. Intended effect is cutting long Bash outputs (test, build, docker logs) by up to 95 percent (README example 2,979 to 54 lines).
pros: Only candidate reviewed that is truly automatic: a Bash tool.call hook rewrites long results before the model sees them, no user or model prompting (hooks/jevprune.ts:62-73).
Uses Jev for what it is designed for (calibrated Noul yes/no per line, no free text), with a sensible rule layer (tail 40, error signatures, context) so Jev only sees ambiguous lines.

Genuinely useful for daily coding: saves Opus context on npm test, cargo build, docker compose, pytest logs (README/bench: 2,979 to 54 lines) and lossless recovery via run id, `jevprune show` and a skill that teaches the model to read markers.

Fail-open by design: missing key, exception, timeout or malformed answer all degrade to rules or the untouched result; exit-nonzero, interrupted, document, diff, secret-looking and under-60-line outputs are never sent or altered.

Zero MCP tools and about 45 tokens of skill description, so no permanent context tax and no conflict with existing gitnexus, playwright, caveman-shrink servers; hook is a separate plugin mechanism from the settings hooks (secret guard, GitNexus) though interaction with the existing PreToolUse Bash hooks is untested.

Clean, typed, tested code (about 4.5k lines TS, 27 test files including live, hook, http-client, prune-core tests, gate script with typecheck, lint, build), MIT, key stored via plugin keychain option, key not in argv.
Endpoint path /v1/systemone equals OpenRouter's System One path, so retargeting to OpenRouter is a small patch.
cons: Not OpenRouter-ready: in the plugin path the base URL (api.typesafe.ai), model id (jev-latest) and key env (TYPESAFE_API_KEY only, env allow-list in hooks/jevprune.ts:7-12) are hardcoded; you must fork/patch to use OPENROUTER_API_KEY and model typesafe/jev-1.13, and confirm OpenRouter's request/response schema matches. The README also says selection needs a TypeSafe early-access waitlist key.

Depends on Claude Code 'function hooks', an early-access surface that 'may change between releases without notice' (types file written by 2.1.274; user runs 2.1.285), needs CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 env, and can break on any CLI update.

Alpha maturity: created 2026-09-18, 40 commits in 3 days by one author, 2 stars, 0 issues, no CI workflow (.github absent, only local gate.sh), no real-world track record; benchmark publishes no numbers ('run it with your own key').

Data egress for client work: command output lines, the command, and excerpts of your last 3 prompts go to a third party (TypeSafe or OpenRouter and upstream). Secret detection is regex-only and will miss tokens embedded in ordinary logs; needs a per-project opt-out for client repos, which the plugin does not offer (only global userConfig/env).

Lossy: Jev can drop the one line that mattered; only the model calling `jevprune show` (needs the CLI installed or a sed on the log) recovers it. Failed commands pass through unpruned, so the most context-heavy failing test output is not reduced, and dropped ranges under fallback are rule-based.
Adds latency and up to about 10-20 s worst case to every long Bash result during a slow or down Jev; 1 immediate retry with no backoff.

Overlaps with caveman-shrink and possible other context pruners, and unverified coexistence with existing GitNexus Bash post hooks (both rewrite Bash results); writes up to 256 MiB of raw command output to ~/.jevprune (may contain client data at rest).

Narrow scope: only Bash tool results, not Read, Grep, diffs, or any decision-making use of Jev (routing, permission classification, model choice), which is where Choice/Noul/Score would add more value.
entries.verdict: Best-fitting candidate for the automatic, no-prompting requirement: a deterministic Bash-result hook that uses Jev's Noul primitive to cut noisy logs, fails open and costs almost no context. Adopt only as a small OpenRouter-patched fork, on personal projects first, since it needs early-access function hooks, is 12 days old and single-maintainer, and sends command output to a third party.

judge.why: Best-designed Bash-log pruner (rule layer first, Noul per line, recovery via jevprune show). It depends on early-access function hooks and TypeSafe-only config, so the audit's 6.5 is trimmed for this user.
pros: Rules keep tail 40, error signatures and context. Never touches non-zero exit, diffs, source, JSON, secret-looking or under-60-line output
Fail-open with rule fallback. Full output archived in ~/.jevprune/runs. About 45 tokens of skill description, no MCP
Not curl|sh, no telemetry found
cons: Needs CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 (early access, not among the 5 documented hook types) and may break on any CLI update. Fail-open would hide the breakage
Hard-coded TypeSafe endpoint and README mentions a TypeSafe early-access waitlist key. It needs a patch for OpenRouter and OPENROUTER_API_KEY
Worst case ~20s per window group. Fallback still drops lines. Sends command and three prompt excerpts out. No published benchmark numbers

entries.name: ByteBell/jev-filter
entries.what: Claude Code plugin (marketplace "bytebell", plugin jev-filter 0.1.0) bundling a single-file, stdlib-only Python MCP server (also usable as a CLI), a skill, and a /jev-find slash command. After the agent chooses a grep regex, the server runs git grep / rg / a Python walk (or takes paths the agent already has) and sends EACH candidate file's full text (up to 24k tokens) as a separate call to OpenRouter's Decisions API with model typesafe/jev-1.13 and one Choice question with yes/no criteria ("is this file part of this feature / would a dev edit it"). It keeps files with p(yes) >= 0.7, lists borderline ones (0.5-0.7), caches decisions on disk, and reports Jev's billed cost versus an estimated Claude cost. It replaces only the "which grep hits matter" step; the LLM still picks the pattern and reads the kept files.
entries.autoInvocation: Model-discretion only, steered by the skill description ('how does X work / where is Y handled / which files would I change') and the MCP tool descriptions. Not deterministic: there is no hook, so Claude Code decides. The skill's own guidance (>10 grep hits) and Claude's strong preference for built-in Grep, Glob, Explore subagents and the user's existing GitNexus graph hooks means invocation will be inconsistent, and subagents (Explore) may not use it. Satisfies 'user never says use jev' partially; cannot guarantee it fires. Each invocation also makes Claude add a cost-comparison line to its answer (SKILL.md step 5), which is noise for daily work.
security: API key is passed via MCP env (${OPENROUTER_API_KEY} expansion in .mcp.json) and used in an Authorization header only; never in argv, so not visible in the process list. It must exist in the environment that launches Claude Code (not in a settings env file by default).

No shell=True; subprocess is called with an argument list (git -C root grep -l -I -i -E <pattern>, rg ...). The agent-supplied pattern is passed as a positional arg after -E without a '--' separator before it, so a pattern beginning with '-' could be parsed as an option by git/rg (minor argument-injection surface, low impact). Glob is appended after '--' for git but as '-g <glob>' for rg.

jev_filter accepts arbitrary absolute paths and reads them server-side with open(); root is arbitrary. This bypasses the user's PreToolUse secret-leak guard (matcher Bash|Read|Grep|NotebookEdit), which does not match mcp__ tools. A prompt-injected or careless agent could ship ~/.ssh keys, .env, credentials files (any UTF-8 text) to OpenRouter/TypeSafe. No path allow-list, no secret filter.

Even jev_grep_filter can hit secrets: git grep only covers tracked files, but the rg fallback (no --no-ignore, so honors .gitignore) and the pure-Python _walk_grep fallback (skips only .git/node_modules/vendor/... dirs) read untracked files such as .env in non-git dirs. Pattern such as 'key|token|secret' would select exactly secret-bearing files.

Prompt-injection surface: tool output returned to Claude contains only file paths, probabilities and cost numbers (no file content), so injection via returned text is small; but file contents go to a third-party model whose only output is a number. A hostile file could try to game its own p(yes) but that only affects ranking.
Disk cache at ~/.cache/jev-filter (decisions and prices) keyed by sha256 of model, question, path and content; stores only p_yes/cost/latency, not file text. Default perms, minor.
entries.dataEgress: Full text of every candidate file (up to 24,000 estimated tokens = 84k chars each, truncated beyond that; 70% shrink retry on 400 context errors), its relative path, and the natural-language question the agent wrote, sent file-by-file to https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions (then routed by OpenRouter to TypeSafe). Up to 400 files per call (JEV_MAX_FILES). Personal and CLIENT code both leave the machine; README itself warns 'Your code leaves your machine... sent to OpenRouter and TypeSafe.' Client NDA/data-processing concerns apply; OpenRouter data-policy/ZDR settings and TypeSafe retention unverified. Not sent: prompts, diffs, tool outputs, conversation. Also OPENROUTER_API_KEY to openrouter.ai and a GET of the public model list.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open at the agent level, fail-soft per file. No hooks, so nothing blocks Claude's normal tools. Missing key: tool returns isError 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not set' and Claude can fall back to plain grep/Read. Per-file errors are collected in result.errors, other files still judged; 401/402/403 return clear messages without retry. Timeouts: 120s per HTTP request (:222); 429/5xx/network errors retried up to 5 times with exponential backoff capped at 30s plus jitter (:263-266), so a single failing file can stall ~2-3 min; a full 400-file call with 8 workers has no overall deadline, and the MCP server handles tools/call synchronously in its main loop (serve() is single-threaded), so one long call blocks all other requests to this server (and may exceed Claude Code's MCP tool timeout). Failed files are silently absent from 'kept', so a partial outage yields a thin result that looks like a real answer (only a trailing 'N files failed' line). Cost cap: none other than the 400-file limit; no per-call budget guard.
entries.contextCost: 2 tools. Tool defs: jev_grep_filter about 1.4k chars (description ~520 + schema ~880) and jev_filter about 0.9k chars, roughly 600-700 tokens total (deferred via ToolSearch in recent Claude Code so often only names are in context). No MCP server 'instructions' field returned (initialize returns only name/version/tools capability). Skill adds name+description frontmatter (~470 chars, ~120 tokens) always in the skill listing; SKILL.md body (~1.8k chars, ~450 tokens) loads only when triggered. /jev-find command listing ~60 tokens. Hooks inject nothing. Each tool call returns TWO text blocks (summary plus the full indented JSON) plus structuredContent, so a 43-kept/231-candidate result can be several thousand tokens of duplicated output (kept + borderline + errors + cost tables), which partly cancels the token-saving pitch.
pros: Only candidate here that is actually wired to OpenRouter's Decisions API with typesafe/jev-1.13 and OPENROUTER_API_KEY, in ~250 lines of readable stdlib Python; entirely auditable (I read all of it), no deps, no install scripts, no hooks.

Uses Jev for what it is designed for: a typed Choice with per-option probabilities for a yes/no relevance decision, not free-text generation. Request schema (state + questions.choice + criteria) matches the brief's Decisions API, and cost is read from resp.usage.cost.

Good agent-facing design: the skill is description-triggered ('where is Y handled', 'which files would I change') so it can fire without the user saying 'jev'; tools accept an already-run grep (jev_filter) or run grep themselves (jev_grep_filter).

Practical engineering: disk cache keyed on file content so repeat questions are free, 8-way parallelism, retry/backoff on 429/5xx, shrink-on-context-error, borderline list, tests skipped by default, per-file failures do not abort the run.
Key never appears in argv; env-only. MIT license. Fail-soft: missing key or API outage yields an error result and Claude falls back to normal tools, and no hook can block the session.
Threshold knob (0.5 recall / 0.7 precision) is documented and matches Jev's calibrated-probability strength; useful for impact analysis and pre-refactor file discovery on large unfamiliar repos.
cons: Extremely immature: created 2026-09-29 (1 day old), 2 commits, 1 contributor, 1 star, no releases, no CI. The key headline numbers are self-published by the author on a self-built benchmark (31 questions, 6 repos, ground truth = files changed in 3+ commits) and rest on a single run; I could not and did not verify them. The Opus baseline is a judge reading grep lines/outlines with the author's own prompt, and the '~1% cost' compares Jev per-file calls against a modeled Claude estimate (chars/3.5 + 2,000 tokens per file), not a measured bill. Recall is only ~44-50% at best and precision ~45%: it still misses roughly half the right files.

Not automatic in a deterministic sense: pure model-discretion via skill/tool descriptions. Claude Code already has Grep/Glob/Explore/GitNexus (which your hooks push it toward), so the skill will often be skipped, and Explore subagents typically won't use it. No hook integration (e.g. PostToolUse on Grep) to make it fire reliably.

Sends full source of every candidate file (up to 84k chars each, up to 400 files per call) to OpenRouter and TypeSafe on every use. For client projects that is a contractual/NDA risk with no per-repo opt-out, allow-list, ignore-file, or secret filter.

Secret-guard bypass: server-side open() on any path via jev_filter (absolute paths accepted) and untracked-file reads in the rg/os.walk fallbacks are invisible to your PreToolUse guard (matcher Bash|Read|Grep|NotebookEdit). Would need a matcher for mcp__plugin_jev-filter_* or a patched path filter.

Solves a narrow problem (rank grep hits) that Opus with GitNexus graph context largely handles; adds a 30-90 s blocking call on big candidate sets. serve() is single-threaded and synchronous with no overall deadline, so a slow or 429-ing API can stall the server and exceed MCP tool timeouts; failed files vanish silently from 'kept'.

Tool output duplicates itself (human summary plus full pretty-printed JSON plus structuredContent), inflating context by thousands of tokens per call, and the skill forces a cost-comparison sentence into every answer.

Hard-coded DECISIONS_URL to the alpha endpoint (breaking-change risk), no /api/v1/systemone or TypeSafe-direct support, no use of Score or Noul primitives; Jev is used strictly as a per-file classifier, so it does not cover other Jev use cases (permission/risk gating, commit/diff triage, routing) that could be more valuable in daily coding.

Skeptic risk: if Jev behaves like a small routed flash model (Theo's claim, unverified), the per-file 'yes' probability may be less reliable on unfamiliar code than the README benchmark suggests; 24k-token cut may drop relevant tail of large files.
entries.verdict: A genuine, readable, OpenRouter-native Jev integration that is safe to try as a plugin, but it is a day-old single-author POC whose only auto-trigger is model discretion and which ships your full source to OpenRouter/TypeSafe while bypassing your secret guard. Treat it as an optional, opt-in code-discovery helper (after reviewing/pinning the file and extending the guard hook), not the core of an automatic Jev integration.

entries.name: HAR5HA-7663/jev-compact
entries.what: Two plugins: rule-based pruning of old exploration output at session.compact, Jev ranks remaining tool results; trigger plugin starts compaction at a context percentage. Falls back to built-in summary.
entries.autoInvocation: deterministic hook (compaction and post-turn trigger)
pros: Local rules prune first (54% in 19ms, no network); Jev only for judgement calls
Opt-outs per session/repo (.jev-compact-off) and errors/failing tests never pruned
Fallback to built-in summary on any error
cons: Hardcodes api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone and TYPESAFE_API_KEY (reads ~/.env), no OpenRouter path
Only 1 test file; author-specific paths (~/brain archive); regex tuned to author's tools
Function hooks early access

entries.name: GhalebDweikat/winnow
entries.what: Claude Code plugin (v0.5.1) that acts as a context sieve. A function-hook TypeScript module (hooks/winnow.ts) wraps every Read/Bash/Grep tool result over 1500 chars. It posts the result plus the current task (last user request, last assistant sentence) to a resident local Python sidecar on 127.0.0.1:47311. The sidecar splits the text into ~25-line blocks and asks Jev one Noul yes/no question per block ("is this block needed for the current task?"). Blocks with P(needed) < 0.1 are replaced by a 3-line stub (summary by Claude Haiku plus a recall key). Full text is cached in ~/.winnow/cache. Nothing is hidden if the output looks like an error. A second hook (prompt.submit) ranks the project memory files and WINNOW_CONTEXT_DIRS against the prompt with Jev and injects up to 3 files (8000 chars max). It also ships an MCP server with winnow_recall and winnow_stats, a SKILL.md explaining stubs, and offline replay/benchmark/labeling CLIs.
entries.autoInvocation: Deterministic and fully automatic. tool.call function hooks wrap every Read/Bash/Grep call and prompt.submit runs on every prompt, with no model discretion or user prompting. The SessionStart hook starts the sidecar. Only the winnow_recall MCP tool and the skill are model-discretion, and those are used only when a stub appears.
security: API keys live in plaintext in ~/.winnow/env (home dir chmod 0o700 at config.py:72) or in settings.json env; no keys in argv. The sidecar reads the file and injects it into os.environ.

Sidecar HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:47311 (serve.py:236) has no auth token. It rejects requests carrying an Origin header or a non-JSON Content-Type (serve.py:160-182) to block browser CSRF. Any local process or user can still POST to it and spend the judge key. SECURITY.md lists this as in scope.

The SessionStart hook runs 'uv run' on the plugin's pyproject, so each new plugin version resolves and installs dependencies from PyPI (typesafe-sdk, system-one-adapter[anthropic], anthropic, mcp>=2.0) at session start with a 600s timeout. That is a supply-chain surface, and dependencies are unpinned except by uv.lock.

Prompt-injection surface: it rewrites what Claude sees. A crafted tool output, or the judge being wrong, can hide a block the model needed. Recovery is by winnow_recall. The prompt.submit hook injects file contents into the prompt context from memory files, so a poisoned memory file becomes a context-injection vector.

Uses Claude Code early-access function hooks (CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1), an in-process TypeScript module with access to session messages, cwd and http.fetch. It is not sandboxed from the session.

No telemetry found in the source. Only the judge and summarizer endpoints are contacted (grep shows no other outbound URLs). No postinstall, no curl|sh installer. The sidecar is spawned detached (serve.py:302-311).
entries.dataEgress: The README table says winnow sends the following to the judge (TypeSafe, or OpenRouter if repointed). (1) Every Read/Bash/Grep tool output over 1500 chars, chunked into blocks and capped by WINNOW_MAX_STATE_CHARS=120000 chars per call. In practice that is source code, command output, grep hits and possibly secrets in files, plus the tool arguments (paths and commands). (2) A task description: the last user request (up to 1500 chars) and the last assistant sentence. (3) On every prompt of 12+ chars, the prompt text plus the first 600 chars of each candidate memory or context file (up to 60 files). Hidden blocks (up to 20000 chars per group, up to 4 groups) also go to Anthropic for summaries when WINNOW_SUMMARY=1 and an Anthropic key exists. The full text of hidden outputs is stored locally in ~/.winnow/cache with no eviction. For client projects this means routing a large share of client code through a third-party judge. The existing secret-leak guard is a PreToolUse hook, so it does not filter what winnow sends after a tool has run.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open by design. hooks.py docstring: every failure degrades to pass-through. The TS module returns the original result if the sidecar is unreachable, non-2xx or returns non-JSON (winnow.ts:74-110). A missing key posts one 'judge can't start' notice per session. Judge timeout is WINNOW_JUDGE_TIMEOUT=15s with max_retries=1 (judge.py:74-78), so a hung Jev call could stall a tool result for roughly 15-30s before passing through, with no circuit breaker on the tool.call path (serve.py has next_build_attempt backoff only for judge construction). If Jev is slow but not down, every large Read or Bash pays the wait. The function-hook path also depends on an early-access flag: without CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 the module silently never loads.
entries.contextCost: Small static cost. 2 MCP tools (winnow_recall, winnow_stats), about 250-350 tokens for names, descriptions and schemas, plus a server instructions string of about 40 tokens. The skill description is about 90 tokens, with the full SKILL.md (about 500 tokens) loaded only on trigger. Per-turn injection: on prompt.submit up to 8000 chars (about 2k tokens) of memory files when P(relevant) >= 0.5 (top 3), and this hook can conflict with or duplicate the user's existing memory. Stubs replace hidden blocks (about 100 tokens each), so the net effect is fewer tokens only when a rewrite happens. The DESIGN measurements show only about 2% (default question set) to 4.6% (structured set) of text is hidden at the only clean threshold (0.1), so real savings are small, and most results are skipped by the 0.2 minimum prune ratio.
pros: It is the only candidate here that does what the user asked: it is a deterministic, hook-based integration that fires on every Read/Bash/Grep without any 'use jev' prompt (hooks/winnow.ts:120-160).

It fails open. Sidecar down, judge error, missing key or odd tool shape all return the original result, and there is a shadow mode (WINNOW_MODE=shadow) to observe decisions for a week before changing anything.

It uses Jev in the way the model is designed for: batched calibrated Noul yes/no probabilities with thresholds decided in code. Published numbers in the repo: Jev ECE 0.14 versus 0.31 for a lexical baseline, median 86 ms, $0.036 for 300 cases; the most confident bin (p<0.1) had 0% needed on 97 hand labels.

The Jev call goes through the official typesafe-sdk, which honors TYPESAFE_BASE_URL. The /v1/systemone path matches OpenRouter's /api/v1/systemone, so OpenRouter routing is likely a config-only change (unverified).

It has real tests, and CI covers Ubuntu and Windows on Python 3.10 and 3.13, plus 'claude plugin test' for the function hooks. It ships a replay tool to score the judge on the user's own transcripts, and a recall cache so hidden text is recoverable (nothing deleted).
No obvious telemetry, no curl|sh installer, no postinstall, and MIT licensed. SECURITY.md is unusually explicit about the threat model.
Judge cost is tiny (about $0.0004 per 10k-token result).
cons: Little benefit at the safe operating point. At WINNOW_DROP=0.1 the author's own data show only about 2-5% of text is hidden, and results below the 20% minimum prune ratio are not rewritten at all. At 0.3, regret is about 21% of needed blocks (upper bound). Above 0.1, Jev is described as under-confident. For a user on a subscription with Opus, tokens saved translate into little.

Depends on Claude Code's early-access function hooks (CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1, 2.1.260+). The README says the surface may change between releases, and without the flag it silently does nothing. It has not been tested against this user's other hooks (GitNexus post hook on Grep|Glob|Bash, the secret guard, caveman) and may interact with them, since both rewrite or annotate the same tool results.

High data-egress risk for client work. Nearly all large code and command output plus every prompt (when memory files exist) is sent to Jev/OpenRouter, and the secret-leak PreToolUse guard does not cover post-tool output sent by winnow. Stubs also alter Read results: line numbers are renumbered from 1 (SKILL.md), which can confuse edit and navigation workflows.

Requires an Anthropic API key for summaries. The user's OAuth subscription does not provide one, so summaries must be turned off (WINNOW_SUMMARY=0), which degrades stubs to a deterministic digest. The 'adapter' fallback also needs an Anthropic key.

Alpha and young: created 2026-09-16, 29 commits over 2 weeks, effectively 1 maintainer (28 of 29 commits), version 0.5.1, and it has been rewritten once already (PostToolUse to function hooks). Hand labels were made by Claude, not a human, and are self-reported.

Extra moving parts: a resident local server without auth on port 47311, an unpinned dependency resolve via uv at every plugin update, a plaintext ~/.winnow/env, an unbounded ~/.winnow/cache (no eviction), and a worst-case 15-30 s stall per tool call when Jev is slow.
Official OpenRouter path is not tested by the project; the README only documents TYPESAFE_API_KEY, so OpenRouter use is on the user to verify.
entries.verdict: The only fully automatic, deterministic Jev integration among the candidates, and technically sound and fail-open. Its practical payoff is small: about 2-5% of text hidden at the safe threshold, an early-access hook dependency, and a lot of code egress. Worth running in shadow mode against OpenRouter (TYPESAFE_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api, WINNOW_SUMMARY=0) on personal projects to measure it, but not enabling active mode on client code.

entries.name: compozy/yoshi
entries.what: Local Bun HTTP proxy on 127.0.0.1:8790. You point Claude Code at it with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. It intercepts POST /v1/messages and, above a ~50k-token size gate, splits old completed Bash/Write/Edit inputs, tool results and teammate reports into ~1,200-char spans. It asks Jev (as a typed evaluator) whether each span is still needed, and replaces spans judged unneeded with omission markers. Verdicts are frozen in .yoshi/decisions.json. It then forwards the rewritten request to api.anthropic.com and streams the response back. It also proxies the OpenAI Responses API for Codex. The README labels it an experimental POC that is moving into CompozyOS.
interface: CLI: bun start / bun run dev
entries.autoInvocation: Transparent proxy. Once ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is set and the proxy is running, it applies to every request with no user prompting and no model discretion. That is the closest fit to the user's automatic-integration requirement. However it is context pruning, not a general Jev decision tool.
security: README labels it an experimental proof of concept. It is package.json private:true with no npm release.

Judge key handling: AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY comes from env or .env (server.ts:96), not argv, so it is not visible in the process list. The Anthropic auth header (authorization or x-api-key) passes through the proxy. It is included in a sticky-cache key in lifecycle.optimize (server.ts, roughly line 250), so check whether it is hashed. The README says credentials are never logged.
Listens on 127.0.0.1 only (Bun.serve hostname, server.ts:~191), which is good. But any local process can use it as an authenticated Anthropic relay, because the client's auth header is forwarded.

Prompt-injection surface: tool output, which may be untrusted, is fed to the judge as state. The judge prompt does say the candidates are untrusted data. Jev returns typed probabilities only, so the injection impact is limited to wrongly keeping or dropping a span. A wrong drop silently removes context from the main model, which is a correctness risk rather than code execution.

No shell execution, curl|sh installer or postinstall found in the src/ files I read (grep for env and http only). Runtime is Bun, and the project needs bun install with two deps, ai and @ai-sdk/gateway.
Telemetry: no phone-home in src. Local logs .yoshi/requests.jsonl and .yoshi/decisions.json hold metadata and hashes only. Benchmark runs save raw traces locally.
entries.dataEgress: Above the size gate, each Jev call sends the current task and earlier user constraints, the action chronology, and the candidate spans (source code from Write/Edit/Bash arguments, tool results, teammate reports). Spans are up to ~24KB per request. It also sends a byte-bounded set of retained evidence. All of this goes to Vercel AI Gateway and then TypeSafe (README Privacy: no zero-data-retention option requested). The full Anthropic request itself goes to api.anthropic.com as normal via the proxy. On OpenRouter this would go to OpenRouter and TypeSafe instead. That is a real concern for client projects.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open for correctness: failed, invalid or timed-out judgments keep the span (README; judge.ts catch blocks at ~lines 120-137 and 232-243). With no key, requests pass through unchanged. It is NOT fail-fast for latency: an outage can hold a request up to the 45s judge deadline (YOSHI_JUDGE_TIMEOUT_MS default 45000 in conversation scope, server.ts:115). Judging runs on the request path, which blocks the request. The proxy itself is a single point of failure: if bun start is not running, claude fails with a connection error because ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points at a dead port.
entries.contextCost: Adds no MCP tools, hooks or injected text, so it costs zero tokens of tool definitions. It works in the opposite direction: it rewrites the request history sent to Anthropic, and the goal is to reduce input. Real results: Fable diagnostic showed 34% accumulated-input reduction with the gate disabled, while the Sonnet mixed session showed -0.03%, meaning no savings. Rewriting old history can also invalidate Anthropic prompt-cache prefixes, and cache-write behavior differs between arms in the README table. The authors say there is no single validated savings percentage.
pros: It is the only candidate here that is truly automatic and invisible to Claude Code: a transparent proxy, with no prompt or model discretion needed.
Cheap failure semantics for correctness: failed or timed-out judgments retain the span, and an omitted span is replaced with an explicit marker. Tool IDs and paths are kept byte-identical.
Passes auth headers through, so it should work with OAuth or subscription auth (I have not verified this with a real login; the transport is plain passthrough in server.ts).
Benchmarks are unusually honest (two studies, hashes, and explicit statements that no single savings number is validated). MIT license.
The semantic.ts question design (boolean Noul-style plus choice) maps conceptually onto Jev's Noul and Choice primitives, so a port to OpenRouter is plausible.
Includes a YOSHI_DRY_RUN mode to evaluate decisions without applying them.
cons: No OpenRouter support: Jev is reached only via Vercel AI Gateway (typesafe-ai/jev) through @ai-sdk/gateway evaluationModel. Using it needs a Vercel key, or a custom judge.ts rewrite against openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions.
Measured to be about 5x slower than baseline in both trials (39.8s vs 210.5s and 35.1s vs 172.0s), with judge failures in each. A judge outage can stall a request up to 45s.

Savings are unproven. One study showed 34% input reduction with the gate disabled, while the other showed zero. Single trial per arm. Rewriting history may break Anthropic prompt caching, and the Yoshi cost totals are unknown.
Sends source code and tool output from your project to Vercel Gateway and TypeSafe with no ZDR option. That is a poor fit for client projects.
Silently deletes context from Opus's view, so a wrong verdict causes hard-to-diagnose task errors. That is a correctness risk for daily coding.
Solves a narrow problem, context pruning, not the broader uses Jev could serve in Claude Code (permission and risk decisions, routing, and so on). Only relevant in long sessions above 50k tokens.

Requires running a separate Bun daemon and launching claude with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. If the daemon dies, Claude Code breaks. A Claude Code session started normally will bypass it, and the Bun runtime and a second process need managing.

Very immature: created 2026-09-18, 5 commits, 1 contributor, no CI, no releases, and the README says the real version is moving into the CompozyOS repo. The maintainer intends to move away from this standalone form. Already 27 stars and 2 forks, so early interest.
entries.verdict: Automatic and transparent, but it targets context pruning only and does not support OpenRouter. It needs a custom Decisions-API port, and it measured about 5x slower with unproven savings. Treat it as an interesting reference for a Jev judge design, not a daily driver. Do not point client code at it.

entries.name: yctimlin/JevScout
entries.what: Node/TypeScript npm package (jevscout 0.5.1) whose main Claude Code feature is a PostToolUse hook (matcher mcp__.*) that, only for MCP tool results that Claude Code itself already truncated to a saved file and that are at least 100 KB, splits the text into segments, asks Jev (Noul yes/no per segment: "does this contain evidence for state.query") which segments are relevant, and replaces the tool output (updatedToolOutput) with a roughly 6 KB verbatim packet plus a local recovery command (jevscout output <id> --grep/--segment/--all, cached in ~/.cache/jevscout/outputs, 7-day TTL). Also ships an opt-in Bash PreToolUse rewrite (--with-shell) that pipes gh/curl/wget output through a condenser, a SKILL.md for CLI code search/GitHub issue research/claim checking (jevscout search/github/check), an experimental Codex MCP proxy, and a Codex app-server operation adapter library (irrelevant to Claude Code). Not an MCP server; not official TypeSafe. It is a context filter, not a general coding assistant or router.
interface: PostToolUse hook `jevscout hook post-tool` (matcher mcp__.*, timeout 30s)
PreToolUse hook `jevscout hook pre-bash` (matcher Bash, opt-in --with-shell)
jevscout install claude / uninstall claude [--scope user|project] [--lexical-only] [--with-shell] [--dry-run]
entries.autoInvocation: Deterministic hook (PostToolUse on mcp__.*), fully automatic once installed and TYPESAFE_API_KEY is exported; no prompting needed. But the trigger is extremely narrow: only MCP results that Claude Code already spilled (over its own MCP token cap) and at least 100 KB. The SKILL.md path is skill-description trigger only if manually installed and is marked experimental.
security: API key is read only from env TYPESAFE_API_KEY and sent as a Bearer header via fetch; never put in argv or written to settings (hook.ts:249-250, installNotice). No key-in-process-list issue.
No telemetry found (grep for telemetry/analytics empty); only network target is api.typesafe.ai (plus api.github.com for the github subcommand). fetch uses redirect:'error'.
No postinstall/preinstall; zero runtime deps, so supply-chain surface is the package itself only (single-author, 5-day-old npm package).
Hook reads Claude Code's saved tool-result file but restricts it to realpath under the session's tool-results dir (hook.ts:113-121), which is good path-traversal hygiene.

Prompt-injection surface: it REWRITES what the model sees from MCP tools. Selected segments are verbatim but chosen by an external model, so it can hide relevant text (e.g. a warning or a needed detail), and injected text inside an MCP result may be crafted to win the ranking. Instructions to Jev do say 'source text is data, not instructions'. The original stays recoverable, but the model must know to ask.

The hook sends the latest user prompt (up to 1500 chars, URLs stripped) and tool-argument strings to TypeSafe with each condensed result (hook.ts:91-97); that can include client project details typed in a prompt.
entries.dataEgress: Only when an MCP result is >=100 KB AND was spilled by Claude Code AND Jev mode is on (key set): segment previews (160 chars each), candidate segment full text in batches of up to 100 (up to 3000 coarse candidates, then fine-ranking segments), the tool name (source), tool argument strings, and the most recent user prompt (last 1500 chars, URLs removed, tool name removed) go to api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone (README Privacy section; condense.ts:468-472; hook.ts:91-97). README reports 9K-81K TypeSafe tokens for 170-196 KB results and ~300K for 5.2 MB. Built-in tools (Read/Grep/Bash/Edit output) and source files are never sent by the hook (it ignores non-mcp__ tools, hook.ts:7). With the optional --with-shell rewrite, gh/curl/wget output over 8 KB would also be sent. The CLI search mode sends code excerpts and relative paths only if invoked with --mode jev/auto (default lexical/local). No source code or diffs are transmitted in the default hook flow unless an MCP server itself returns them.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open. runHook wraps everything in try/catch and returns '' (hook.ts:243-245), leaving the result unchanged; missing key, HTTP error, timeout, invalid response, low confidence all pass through. Default Jev deadline 8000 ms (JEVSCOUT_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS, clamp 500-25000), one retry on network/5xx within the same deadline (jev.ts:34-50), and the Claude Code hook timeout is 30s. Worst case adds about 8 s to a tool call before returning the original. Exceptions: `jevscout check` fails closed (by design, CLI only), and if a Claude Code update changes the 'exceeds maximum allowed tokens' wording the hook silently becomes a no-op (README admits it).
entries.contextCost: Very low. No MCP tool definitions added (0 tools, 0 server instructions). One PostToolUse hook with no output on the common path (0 tokens injected). The SKILL.md description is about 400 chars (approx 100 tokens) if the user installs it manually (installer does not). When it triggers it REDUCES context: replaces a 100 KB+ result with about 6 KB packet (about 1.5K tokens) plus a header and recovery-command instructions.
pros: Truly automatic and deterministic: a PostToolUse hook, so the user never has to say 'use jev' (hook.ts:258).
Fail-open everywhere on the hook path with 8 s cap and 30 s hook timeout; a Jev outage cannot break tool calls (hook.ts:8, 243-245).
Zero context overhead: no MCP tools, no server instructions, nothing injected on the common path.
Non-destructive: verbatim segments, exact local recovery command, settings backup and clean uninstall, no runtime deps, no postinstall, no telemetry, key never written to disk or argv.

Uses Jev the way its brief describes (typed Noul yes/no per document, no free text), a rare real, sensible use of the primitive; System One body shape matches OpenRouter's /api/v1/systemone surface, so an OpenRouter port is a small patch.
Includes a --lexical-only mode and env knobs for scope, thresholds, budget, timeout and model (JEVSCOUT_HOOK_MODEL can already be set to an OpenRouter-style model id).
cons: No OpenRouter support at all: URL hard-coded to api.typesafe.ai in src/core/jev.ts:3 and src/codex-decision.ts:1, key env is only TYPESAFE_API_KEY. Requires forking/patching, and the user would then own an unmaintained fork of a 5-day-old project.

Very narrow scope: only mcp__ tool results of 100 KB or more that Claude Code already spilled. For this user's MCP set (gitnexus, playwright, caveman-shrink) that will fire rarely (maybe playwright snapshots or large gitnexus graph results); built-in Read/Grep/Bash, which dominate daily coding, are untouched. Expected daily value is close to nil.

Does not do any of what makes Jev interesting for coding decisions (routing, permission/risk classification, next-step choice, commit/test decisions); those live only in the Codex adapter, which does not apply to Claude Code.

Sends the user's latest prompt plus MCP result text (client data) to a third party; the user works on client projects, so this needs consent, and Jev is a beta model. A lexical-only mode avoids egress but then does no Jev work.

Data-loss risk by design: a ranker chooses which 6 KB of 100+ KB the model sees; the model must know to call the recovery command; injected content could game the ranking. Correctness claims (5/5 vs 1/5) are self-reported on 7 tasks by the author, unreplicated.

Immature: 2 stars, 1 contributor, 8 commits in 5 days, three minor versions in 5 days, no CI (.github absent), README self-labels the shell rewrite and search/github CLIs as experimental. Depends on regex of Claude Code's current spill-notice wording (hook.ts:111) so a Claude Code update silently disables it.

Hook config bakes absolute node and CLI paths into settings.json, brittle across Node upgrades; adds a Node process spawn to every mcp__ call; the install flow overwrites/merges into the user's already busy global settings.json (secret-guard, GitNexus, caveman hooks); the optional Bash rewrite would collide with GitNexus and the secret guard.
SKILL.md is not installed by the installer, so the 'search/github/check' CLI features would not be discoverable by Claude without manual setup.
entries.verdict: A well-engineered, fail-open, zero-context-cost PostToolUse hook that is genuinely automatic, but it only fires on 100 KB+ spilled MCP results (rare for this user's MCP set), needs a source patch to talk to OpenRouter instead of api.typesafe.ai, and is 5 days old with one author. Reasonable to pilot as a niche add-on (patched to OpenRouter) but not the core Jev integration for daily coding.

entries.name: apixly-ai/jev-filter (@apixly/jev-filter)
entries.what: Third-party (Apixly / JIA-ss, "Independent of TypeSafe") CLI + Python lib + portable SKILL.md. Runs a collector (exec/search/query/code-search/locate/triage) inside its own process, sends the collected records plus a caller-supplied task to Jev (TypeSafe System One /v1/systemone, typed Choice/Noul/Score questions) and returns only selected IDs, review IDs and compact excerpts (raw output archived locally, recoverable by ID). v0.3 adds hosted execution: browse/desktop/extract/survey (Jev picks among program-enumerated UI controls; runs a browser via CDP/Camofox or Windows/macOS desktop). It is NOT an MCP server and ships no hooks; it is meant to be driven by the agent through Bash following a skill plus a pasted CLAUDE.md routing rule.
interface: jev-filter exec --task T [--analysis spec] -- CMD ARGV
jev-filter batch / list / read / stats / doctor
entries.autoInvocation: Skill description trigger plus a pasted CLAUDE.md routing rule, i.e. model discretion only. No deterministic hook, no transparent proxy, no MCP. Claude Code must itself decide to wrap a collector in `jev-filter exec` inside Bash instead of running Grep/Read directly, and the skill tells it to prefer native tools for exact or short work, so invocations will be infrequent. It would not intercept the built-in Grep/Read/Glob tools, which are Claude Code's main outputs.
security: No shell: exec passes argv array without implicit shell (SECURITY.md, cli.py:329) but runs commands with full user permissions, explicitly not a sandbox
API key read from env or a 0600 non-symlink file (provider.py:29-58); Authorization header only, never in argv (no --api-key flag found), so not visible in process list
Credentials only go to fixed HTTPS TypeSafe endpoint, redirects rejected (follow_redirects=False, provider.py:88), response capped 4 MiB, error bodies suppressed

Redaction of secrets is key-name regex only (tools.py:178 SECRET_KEY on dict keys); SECURITY.md admits it does not cover every secret format, so secrets embedded in log/code text would go to the remote service

Prompt-injection surface: page text, record text and tool output are sent to Jev and steer selection; project itself says injection rules are not a security boundary. Jev output is typed IDs/probabilities only, so injection can hide or surface records (evidence suppression) but cannot produce commands

browse/desktop can drive a signed-in browser via --cdp-port and desktop apps; pauses on pay/send/delete-like actions, refuses terminals/password managers, STOP file; high-privilege capability that a CC user does not need for coding
entries.dataEgress: To api.typesafe.ai only (TYPESAFE_API_KEY, Bearer): the --task text, context/analysis spec, question definitions, and every collected passage/record/log line/page text (up to --max-parts 2048 passages, exec output up to 2 MB) after key-name-only redaction. With exec/search/code-search on a repo this means source code and file contents from client projects leave the machine to TypeSafe (not OpenRouter). Optional JEV_TEXT_* sends goal+page context to whatever OpenAI-compatible endpoint is configured. Nothing goes to Apixly. Local: evidence archives in temp dir, optional numeric stats.
entries.failureMode: Fail-closed per invocation but not blocking Claude Code: no hook, so a Jev outage only makes that CLI call fail. Client timeout 25 s per request (provider.py Client timeout=25), up to 3 attempts with Retry-After (max 5 s sleep) on 429/503/529; other non-200 raises sanitized ProviderError (http_NNN_body_suppressed); strict response validation rejects schema drift (response_invalid_usage_unknown). exec has 30 s collector timeout. Exit 2 = partial results, complete=false, unresolved IDs go to review; missing credentials -> credentials_missing. The agent can fall back to native Grep/Read, but the SKILL says not to retry uncertain collectors.
entries.contextCost: Very low fixed cost: no MCP tools (0 tool defs). One skill: description ~480 chars (about 120 tokens) always listed; SKILL.md body ~4.5k chars (~1.1k tokens) loaded only when triggered, plus references/contract.md and hosted.md on demand. Optional CLAUDE.md routing rule ~800 chars (~200 tokens) per session. No hook-injected text. Per-call cost is the compact JSON packet (README claims 88-97% less tool context in synthetic benchmarks, but cold API-equivalent cost only -20.8% to +0.6%).
pros: Solid, security-conscious plumbing for a 1-week-old project: 0600 key-file handling with O_NOFOLLOW, key never in argv, fixed origin with redirects rejected, 4 MiB response cap, sanitized errors, strict schema validation of Jev responses (provider.py, validation.py)
Zero context tax: no MCP server, no hook, one skill (~120 tokens description); does not collide with existing PreToolUse secret-guard, GitNexus or caveman hooks

Uses Jev's typed primitives properly (Choice/Noul/Score, per-option probabilities, REVIEW option, missing-facts -> review) and does batching (up to 30 concurrent, 56.5% fewer input tokens claimed), which matches Jev's cheap-input pricing model
Keeps originals recoverable by ID (`jev-filter read ARCHIVE --id`), so filtering is auditable and not lossy in the archive
Genuinely relevant use cases for coding: triage of huge logs/CI output (`triage`, `exec`), broad `code-search` with symbol expansion, semantic filtering of many grep hits

MIT, CI matrix on py3.10-3.14 + macOS + Windows, actions pinned by SHA, dependabot, security workflow, 207 test functions across 24 test files, OIDC npm publishing, honest benchmarks that report regressions and that browser success on real sites is only 16/34
Ships a SKILL.md and docs/agents.md with explicit Claude Code setup path
cons: No OpenRouter support at all: endpoint hardcoded to api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone (provider.py:17), key only TYPESAFE_API_KEY, model default jev-1.13.0; zero 'openrouter' strings in repo. Contradicts the user's requirement (OpenRouter as provider) and needs a TypeSafe console key; making it work needs a source patch/fork and a source (not npm-binary) install

Not automatic: the integration is a skill + CLAUDE.md paste, i.e. relies on Opus choosing to call it via Bash; no PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook, no MCP, no proxy. Cannot filter Claude Code's built-in Grep/Read/Glob results, so it will rarely fire in daily coding. Directly contradicts 'CC must use it without me prompting'

Sends source code, logs and file contents from personal AND client projects to a third-party inference service with only key-name-based redaction; conflicts with client confidentiality unless TypeSafe/OpenRouter terms are cleared. If run via OpenRouter patch, egress goes to OpenRouter instead

Solves a problem Opus 5.5 with a 1M-ish context and rg/GitNexus already handles; the project's own benchmark shows cold cost between -20.8% and +0.6% and latency regressions in some cells; the biggest wins are for thousands of records, which is not the typical coding turn

Scope creep and risk surface irrelevant to coding: browse/desktop/survey/extract drive browsers and desktop apps (CDP attach to signed-in profiles, UIA/AX), overlapping with the already-installed playwright MCP

Immature and single-maintainer: repo created 2026-09-22 (8 days old), 14 commits, 1 contributor, 1 star, 0 forks; npm latest 0.2.4 while git is at 0.3.0; README 'we use it in our own environment' is unverifiable; opaque PyInstaller native binary delivered through optionalDependencies cannot be audited from source alone

Latency/effort per invocation: extra process spawn and network round trip(s) with 25 s timeout and up to 3 retries; agent must hand-write an analysis spec with context/requirements for good results (prompt-engineering burden shifted onto Opus each call)

Judgment correctness risk: selecting only 'relevant' records from a 2 MB output can silently drop the one line that matters (prompt-injection or model error); README admits missing facts and easy synthetic data, and real-world hosted success ~47%
entries.verdict: Well-engineered but young CLI+skill that is TypeSafe-only (hardcoded api.typesafe.ai, zero OpenRouter support) and depends on model discretion via Bash rather than any hook or MCP, so it fails both the OpenRouter and the automatic-invocation requirements. At best a reference for how to structure Jev batch calls (or a fork target for a custom log-triage tool); not something to install as the Claude Code integration.

entries.autoInvocation: deterministic hook (Codex PostToolUse); not usable in CC
pros: Line-level Jev filtering with code-protected diagnostics; exact original saved and pointed to
Monitor mode shows what would be removed before filtering; live benchmark 71-95% on shortened results
Rust hook with unit and smoke tests

Whole stress mix only fell 3%; 1 star, updated today

entries.name: pkcoulon/jev-for-flutter
entries.what: Claude Code plugin (Python 3.9+, stdlib only) that calls Jev's System One API to (1) narrow large Dart Reads automatically (PreToolUse hook rewrites Read via updatedInput offset/limit to the chunk Jev picks), (2) search Dart code by intent (lens/jev-flutter CLIs, plus an optional MCP tool find_code, off by default), (3) optionally check edits against user-written convention rules (PostToolUse guard, async rewake) and (4) route project memory/skill notes on prompt submit. Strictly Dart/Flutter scoped and opt-in per project via .claude/jev-for-flutter.json jev.enabled. Not a general-purpose Jev integration.
interface: MCP tool find_code (query, path, limit 1-10, include_tests)
Hook PostToolUse Read|Grep|Glob|Bash|Agent|Task, SubagentStart, Stop, SessionEnd -> code_context.py
entries.autoInvocation: Deterministic hooks (PreToolUse Read rewrite, UserPromptSubmit prefetch, PostToolUse edit guard) for the narrowing and guard features; find_code MCP is model-discretion but off by default. Automatic without the user saying 'use jev', but only for .dart files in projects that ran 'jev-flutter init --enable-jev'.
security: No curl|sh, no npm postinstall; pure-stdlib Python. Hooks and MCP run python3 from the plugin dir.
API key from env or ~/.config/jev-for-flutter/typesafe.key (docs say chmod 600); sent as Bearer header over HTTPS, not in argv (jev.py:145). Child processes inherit os.environ incl. key.

Egress gate is decent: per-project opt-in (jev.enabled default false), user policy.json deny_paths/deny_remotes/allow_remotes (fail-closed on unreadable policy, policy.py:93), secret-file globs (.env, *.pem, *secret*, google-services.json) skipped (policy.py:9-12, 131), regex redaction of tokens/keys/private keys/JWT/URL creds (policy.py:13-20). Docs admit masking is not exhaustive.

Prompt-injection surface: Jev outputs are constrained typed values (chunk id, probabilities), so low; but hooks inject text (SessionStart note, router suggestions from memory/skill descriptions, guard messages) into Claude context. Tainted repo content (rules.json, config in repo .claude/jev-for-flutter.json) is read from the project dir, so a hostile repo could enable Jev/point config; env JEV_FLUTTER_JEV_URL is env-only, not repo config.

A repo-committed .claude/jev-for-flutter.json with jev.enabled=true would send that repo's Dart code to the endpoint once user has a key configured; policy deny lists are the only guard for client repos.
lens 'Q -- cmd' executes arbitrary shell commands (user/Claude initiated, not a hook).
entries.dataEgress: Only when jev.enabled=true for the project AND a key exists: prompt text truncated/cleaned as 'goal' (from transcript or the prompt), redacted chunks of the target .dart file (up to 64 KB, 24k est. tokens per request, up to 24 requests/session), Dart outlines/declarations of files in scope for find/context (up to 150 files, batched 8/request), Edit/Write diffs plus surrounding context and rule text for the convention guard, memory-note and skill descriptions for the router. Non-Dart files, generated Dart, secret-glob files and policy-denied paths/remotes are not sent. Goes to base_url()/v1/systemone (api.typesafe.ai by default; would go to OpenRouter if overridden).
entries.failureMode: Fail-open throughout. hookio.run wraps every hook: any exception or deadline (4s; 2s for code_context) exits 0 with no output (hookio.py:17-37). Hook client uses hook_timeout_s=1.5, 0 retries, and a circuit breaker (3 failures -> 300s pause, jev.py:19-20, 127-131); CLI client 20s timeout, 2 retries. Missing key, policy error or Jev outage means Read stays unchanged. MCP find_code times out at ~35s max and tells Claude to fall back to Grep/Read. Exception: refuse_once nudge mode can deny a Read once (non-default).
entries.contextCost: Very low by default. find_code is hidden (tools/list returns []) unless find.mcp=true; if enabled: 1 tool, about 1.7k chars of description+schema, ~450 tokens. MCP server has no 'instructions'. Skill description ~300 chars always listed (~80 tokens) plus slash command. SessionStart injects ~500 chars (~130 tokens) only in Jev-enabled projects (with extra ~200 chars if find_code enabled); narrowing adds a ~350-char note per narrowed Read; guard/router messages are occasional. Note text is in French.
pros: Genuinely automatic: PreToolUse Read hook rewrites the tool input (updatedInput offset/limit) with no user prompting, exactly the 'Claude Code must use it when needed' behavior requested.
Good use of the right Jev primitives: choice over 200 chunks for locality, noul for 'is this a focused question', with thresholds (0.6/0.85) so uncertain cases leave the Read unchanged.
Fail-open design with breaker, short hook timeouts, and per-session request caps (hookio.py, jev.py, config.py:27); will not hang Claude.
Strong privacy tooling for client work: deny_paths / deny_remotes policy, secret-file globs, regex redaction, per-project opt-in default off (policy.py, USAGE.md Privacy).
Endpoint and model overridable via JEV_FLUTTER_JEV_URL / JEV_FLUTTER_JEV_MODEL, so OpenRouter is plausibly a config-only switch; small readable stdlib Python, easy to audit and fork.
Ships a reusable pattern (typed Jev client, breaker, redaction, Read-narrowing hook) that could be copied into a language-agnostic hook.
Honest docs: benchmarks labeled exploratory, n=3, unblinded, +7% runtime; context prep disabled by default after unfavorable results.
cons: Dart/Flutter only: every feature checks .dart suffix or Dart outline (narrow.py:read, lens_nudge.py:99). Useless for a general multi-language workflow unless forked.
Native to TypeSafe API only; zero OpenRouter references. Key env var is TYPESAFE_API_KEY; OpenRouter parity with the /v1/systemone body is unverified and would need a live test.
Repo is 2 days old, 0 stars, 1 author, 21 commits, no tests directory, no CI (.github absent), no releases beyond own tags; v0.3.6 rebrand from 'dartlens' with legacy shims - churn risk.

Measured benefit is weak: 3 questions, one run each, unblinded; 23% fewer tokens but 7% longer runtime; author's own context-prep feature was turned off after unfavorable results. Opus-class Claude reading 400+ line files rarely needs Jev.
Read narrowing can silently omit relevant code (a 'selected region'), risking wrong answers; also affects Claude Code semantics via updatedInput on a client codebase.
Sends client source (redacted chunks, edit diffs) to a third-party gateway; project-committed config can flip jev.enabled, and redaction is regex-only.

Installing adds ~10 hook registrations (PostToolUse on Read|Grep|Glob|Bash|Agent|Task, Stop, SessionEnd, SubagentStart, 3x UserPromptSubmit) that spawn python3 on nearly every tool call, alongside user's existing GitNexus Grep|Glob|Bash hooks and secret guard; potential interaction/ordering with the secret-leak guard (both on Read) and GitNexus.
Messages injected into Claude are in French; user-facing errors mixed French/English.
Does not use Jev's strengths for general coding decisions (permission gating, model routing, commit/PR triage); it only ranks code chunks.
entries.verdict: Well-engineered, fail-open, genuinely automatic hook integration, but locked to Dart/Flutter, TypeSafe-native (OpenRouter switch plausible via JEV_FLUTTER_JEV_URL yet unverified), and only 2 days old with no tests. Not suitable as the user's general Jev integration; useful only as a code reference for a Read-narrowing/PreToolUse pattern or if the user works in Flutter.

entries.name: rilfi/token-optimizer-jev-mcp-experimental
entries.what: Two things in one repo: (1) a stdio MCP server (token-optimizer-jev-mcp 0.1.0, TypeScript, wraps @typesafe-ai/sdk 0.6.0) exposing 6 read-only tools for Jev typed decisions (batched jev_ask, jev_choice/score/noul, jev_list_models, jev_server_info) with a local context-budget guard and compact answers; (2) a set of six Node hook scripts (hooks/) plus agent-bridge.mjs that call the MCP server over stdio to run Jev decisions at lifecycle events (destructive-command risk gate, failure triage, completion gate, session profile). The hooks were built and benchmarked for the Hermes agent; Claude Code support is a translation shim in agent-bridge.mjs. Not published to npm.
entries.autoInvocation: Two modes. (a) MCP tools: model-discretion only; the author's own three-way benchmark (bench/THREE-WAY.md) found the agent used the Jev MCP tools 0/6 times when the tools merely existed, so this does NOT meet the 'Claude uses it without being told' requirement. (b) Hooks: deterministic (UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop/SessionStart/SessionEnd), which does satisfy automatic invocation, but the Jev decisions are narrow safety/verification gates, and under Claude Code H3 and H4 are effectively dead code because the bridge does not map tool_response to extra.result or provide changed_paths/coding.
security: API key from env only, never a tool argument or in argv; hook client spawns the server with key in env (hooks/jev-client.mjs spawn env), not on the command line. Good.
Key resolution fallback reads Hermes config: ~/.hermes/config.yaml and ~/.hermes/.env by regex (jev-client.mjs resolveApiKey) - irrelevant to Claude Code but reads secret files if present.
MCP server itself: no shell, no fs, no path arguments; stdio only; all tools annotated readOnlyHint (README). Small attack surface.
No postinstall/preinstall scripts (package.json). prepublishOnly only. No curl|sh installer. No telemetry in server or SDK beyond X-TypeSafe-SDK/Runtime headers.

Prompt-injection surface: MCP instructions are benign, but hooks feed untrusted content to Jev (prompts, tool output) and act on its scores; H2 block reasons/H4 push-back text are static templates plus command text echoed back (truncate 160 chars) - low risk.

Deny-list is naive regex: `\b(shutdown|reboot|halt|poweroff)\b` matches anywhere in a command (e.g. `grep -r halt`, a git commit message), causing false blocks; SAFE_HINT is a prefix match so `cat x; <anything>` short-circuits the Jev gate (deny-list still runs first). Not a real security boundary.
entries.dataEgress: MCP tools: whatever `state` and question text the Claude model chooses to send (arbitrary code/diffs/text) to TYPESAFE_BASE_URL only (config.ts; README: only egress). Hooks (if wired): H1 sends the user's prompt (truncated to 4000 chars) on every UserPromptSubmit >=12 chars; H2 sends {tool, cwd, command<=2000 chars} for every non-'safe-shaped' Bash command and non-cwd write path (not file contents, only 'WRITE <path>'); H3 (inert under Claude) would send tool name + 600-char digest of failing output; H4 sends final_response (<=3000 chars) + record digests; H5 sends session-start signals. Commands and prompts can contain secrets or client-confidential text and would go to Jev/OpenRouter. No file contents are read by the hooks themselves.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open by design. Every hook wraps errors and returns {} (hook-common.mjs runHook); Jev errors/timeouts/no key return allow (jev_pre_tool_call.mjs 'no decision'). Per-call timeouts: H2/H3 6000 ms, H1/H4 8000 ms (JEV_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS), Claude hook timeout suggested 20 s; MCP server per-attempt timeout 30 s with SDK retries. Guards: 12 h decision cache, 400 calls/day (JEV_HOOK_DAILY_LIMIT), 25 calls/session (JEV_HOOK_SESSION_LIMIT), kill-switch JEV_HOOKS_OFF or marker file. Worst case a slow Jev adds up to ~6-8 s per Bash call before allowing. Only the regex deny-list is fail-closed.
entries.contextCost: MCP: 6 tools with rich zod-described schemas (each judgment tool carries a 6-field option block and long state/criteria descriptions). Estimated ~11-13k chars of tool defs + ~2.4k chars server `instructions` (identity.ts:19-52) = roughly 3-3.5k tokens of always-on context, or less with tool search deferral. Hooks: H1 injects a one-line additionalContext only when P>=0.6 (rare); H5 injects a session-profile line; H4 push-back injects text and buys an extra turn. Author's own benchmark shows H1/H4 raised model cost 1.44x-3.08x, and lean profile (H2/H3/H5/H6) 1.00x with +12% wall time.
pros: Only candidate found with actual deterministic Claude Code hook wiring for Jev (agent-bridge.mjs maps PreToolUse/UserPromptSubmit/Stop/SessionStart/SessionEnd and Bash/Write/Edit names, decision:block + stderr), so automatic invocation is at least architecturally possible.

Hooks fail open with timeouts, 12h cache, daily and per-session call ceilings, per-hook env kill-switches, and a pure-regex deny-list that works with no network or key - sensible engineering for a hook that must not wedge a session.
MCP server is small, read-only, key never in argv or tool args, no postinstall, clean typed error codes, budget guard, batched jev_ask (one call, many questions) matching how Jev is meant to be used.

SDK path (/v1/systemone + Bearer) equals OpenRouter's System One API, so pointing it at OpenRouter is probably just TYPESAFE_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api, key, and TYPESAFE_DEFAULT_MODEL=typesafe/jev-1.13.

Honest, measured self-benchmarks (including that MCP tools were used 0/6 and hooks raised cost) - useful negative evidence on what does not work; Jev cost itself is negligible (~$0.00001 per decision).
cons: Not published to npm (E404), 1 commit, 1 author, 0 stars, created 7 days before audit, no CI/releases, package.json points to a different repo name: install path in the README does not work and requires cloning and building unreviewed third-party code.
Hooks are Hermes-first: install.mjs is Hermes/Windows only; state goes to ~/.hermes; Claude support is a hand-pasted README snippet with <REPO> paths and a required local build of dist/.

Claude bridge is incomplete: PostToolUse tool_response is never mapped to extra.result and Stop payload has no changed_paths/coding, so H3 (failure triage) never fires and H4 (completion gate) returns 'not a coding turn'; the Stop push-back also ignores stop_hook_active. Real value under Claude Code reduces to H2 + H1 + H5.

Decision value for this user is low: H2 duplicates what bypass/auto permission mode plus a regex deny-list already cover, and the user already has a PreToolUse secret guard; H1's 'irreversible request?' classifier just adds a sentence of warning. Author bench shows accuracy 6/6 with or without Jev, so no measured coding benefit.

Costs real latency on the hot path: ~1.5 s blocking per non-trivial Bash call and per prompt, via double node spawn, versus zero benefit on read-heavy sessions; and sends every prompt and shell command (may contain client secrets/code) to Jev/OpenRouter.

MCP tools alone are not automatic (0/6 agent uses in author's benchmark) and add ~3k tokens of tool definitions to every session; deny-list regex has false positives (word 'halt'/'reboot'/'shutdown' anywhere) and a prefix-based safe-list bypass.
entries.verdict: Interesting as a reference design for wiring Jev into Claude Code through deterministic hooks with fail-open semantics, but it is a one-week-old, unpublished, Hermes-oriented experiment whose Claude bridge leaves half the hooks inert and whose own benchmark shows no coding gain. Do not install it; at most borrow the hook pattern (small local wrapper calling OpenRouter /api/v1/systemone directly with a strict timeout) rather than the code.

entries.name: ilkerulusoy/pi-jev-compact
entries.what: Pi coding-agent extension: Jev scores each tool call/result (two Noul), drops unneeded ones verbatim; optional assistant-prose pruning; /jev-compact command.
entries.autoInvocation: deterministic hook (Pi compaction event)
pros: 85 tests, live-run, honest status note (quality of keep/drop not measured); replay/trace/report modules
Verbatim pruning, no LLM summary; prose pruning opt-in with stricter threshold
Design lineage from tamaratran/fast-jev-compaction which targets Claude Code
cons: Pi extension API only (session_before_compact), not loadable in Claude Code
TypeSafe endpoint only, no license file, 0 stars
Would need a port of tamaratran's Claude-Code original instead

entries.name: joelhooks/pi-fast-jev-compaction
entries.what: Pi extension pruning stale tool calls/results using two Noul questions (keep call, keep result) per tool call via /v1/systemone; verbatim, monotonic decisions, falls back to Pi compaction. Pi only.
entries.autoInvocation: deterministic hook (Pi context event)
pros: Clear layer-1-only design: filters model context but never rewrites session files
Configurable baseUrl (works with OpenRouter /v1/systemone)
cons: Pi extension API; Claude Code has no hook to filter history, so not portable
Only a port; the original fast-jev-compaction is the reference
No PostToolUse equivalent here

entries.name: jev-runway
entries.what: Local HTTP proxy (127.0.0.1:8788) that sits between the OpenAI Codex CLI/app and its upstream (ChatGPT backend, OpenAI API or custom provider). Once at least 32k chars of new tool output accumulate, it asks Jev two Noul yes/no questions per old tool call (does the call still matter; is the full output still needed) and on every later /responses request cuts unneeded outputs to a 300-char head plus a note pointing to an archived copy under ~/.codex/jev-runway/archive. It also drops reasoning items for fully trimmed steps, trims Codex compaction requests, and can use a WebSocket upstream. Codex-only: it parses OpenAI Responses requests, not Anthropic Messages, so it does nothing for Claude Code as shipped. Idea is derived from tamaratran/fast-jev-compaction.
interface: Env JEV_RUNWAY_MODEL / JEV_RUNWAY_DEBUG / JEV_RUNWAY_WEBSOCKET / JEV_RUNWAY_PORT / JEV_RUNWAY_UPSTREAM
No MCP tools, no hooks, no skills
entries.autoInvocation: Transparent proxy (fully automatic once Codex is pointed at it). For Claude Code the equivalent would be ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL pointing at a local proxy, which this project does not implement.
security: API key stored in ~/.config/jev-runway/credentials.json (0600 per README) or read from env; auth set uses a masked clack password prompt, so the key is not in argv; Bearer header only sent to the Jev endpoint (jev.ts:92-95)

Proxy forwards the user's Codex/OpenAI authorization headers to the configured upstream; it listens on 127.0.0.1 only, but any local process can hit it, and it exposes an unauthenticated GET /_jev/status
Sends conversation text and tool INPUTS (commands, file paths, patch args) to Jev with tool outputs reduced to size notes (README Privacy section); a client-code confidentiality concern

Trim decision is driven by an LLM classifier reading untrusted repo content in tool inputs and messages: a prompt-injection or model error can silently hide tool output from the main model; mitigated by 300-char head, archive copy and the note telling the model where to re-read, but the note relies on the model doing so
Archives (full trimmed outputs) and trims.jsonl (first 200 chars of each call input) written under ~/.codex/jev-runway/, 0600, pruned after 7 days; may retain secrets from tool output on disk

No postinstall script seen; npm ships prebuilt native binaries in optional platform packages (opaque, unauditable from source alone); self-update downloads tarball from npm registry (honours npm_config_registry) and verifies integrity hash (update.ts:11,54)
entries.dataEgress: To Jev provider (TypeSafe or Vercel AI Gateway): full conversation text (user and assistant messages, task/goal) plus tool-call names and inputs, with tool outputs replaced by size notes, in batches of Noul questions (judge.ts, README Privacy). Whole request bodies still go to the user's model upstream as before (with trimmed outputs). Local disk: archived full tool outputs, trim ledger. Nothing else observed leaving the machine. If ported to Claude Code, it would additionally see Anthropic OAuth/API auth headers because it must proxy /v1/messages.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open by design: Jev evaluation runs between turns in the background so no request waits on it; on Jev error/timeout (default 15s per call, jev.ts:180, retries on 503) or an unreadable request, the request goes upstream exactly as Codex sent it. A missing key is reported as an auth JevError. The proxy itself is a single point of failure though: if the local service is down while ~/.codex/config.toml points at 127.0.0.1:8788, Codex requests fail (service has KeepAlive/ThrottleInterval 5s restart).
entries.contextCost: Zero MCP tools and zero hook text, so no context cost in Claude Code (it would not run at all there). In Codex it reduces context by trimming stale tool output (author claims 46% fewer input tokens over a real workload, 66-76% on replayed sessions; self-reported, provider-count based). Downside: trimming rewrites earlier history, which changes the prompt prefix and can cost cache hits; author reports 92% cache reads so far on Codex/OpenAI, but that is not evidence for Anthropic cache_control behavior.
pros: Genuinely uses Jev with the right primitive (Noul yes/no per tool output) for a real, measurable problem: stale tool output re-billed every turn
Fail-open, off the request path: Jev is consulted between turns so a slow or down Jev never blocks the coding loop (README, codex-proxy.ts)

Lossless design: full output archived locally and the note tells the model where to re-read it; first message and the 6 newest items never trimmed; includes trims ledger and status/quality metrics (re-run rate 0.9% in author's data)

Clean, well-typed Jev client (jev.ts) with hard deadline that survives fetch ignoring abort, retries, budget-aware batching for the 32k window, and a baseUrl option, so adding an OpenRouter route is small on the Jev side
Substantial test suite (~3.5k lines, mocked Jev) and MIT license; architecture idea is portable and directly relevant to a fully automatic, prompt-free Claude Code integration
No MCP/skill/hook footprint on the context window
cons: Codex-only: parses OpenAI Responses (/responses, /responses/compact) and Codex config.toml/session ids; cannot be pointed at Claude Code, which speaks Anthropic /v1/messages with tool_use/tool_result and cache_control (no such code found in src/)
No OpenRouter support at all (zero references); only TypeSafe direct and Vercel AI Gateway, both closed provider unions; baseUrl exists in code but no env var/CLI reaches it

Would require porting the core (responses.ts, codex-proxy.ts, WebSocket upstream, compact handling) to the Messages API and proxying Claude Code auth; for a subscription/OAuth user the proxy must forward OAuth headers, increasing risk and ToS/stability questions

Trimming old tool_result content invalidates Anthropic prompt-cache prefix; cache savings vs token savings tradeoff is untested for Claude Code, and Claude Code already does its own microcompaction/auto-compact
Very immature: 5 commits over 5 days, 1 author, 3 stars, no releases, no PR CI, npm package first published 2026-09-24; 'private: true' package.json; unverified self-reported savings
Sends full conversation text and tool inputs from client projects to a third-party beta model (Jev), a confidentiality issue for client work; archives of raw tool output kept on disk for 7 days
Persistent background service + rewriting the agent's base URL is invasive and adds a local single point of failure; binary distributed prebuilt via npm (opaque)
entries.verdict: Not usable for Claude Code: it is a Codex/OpenAI-Responses proxy with no OpenRouter route, no MCP/hook/skill surface, and only 5 days of history. Its only value is as a design reference (async Noul 'is this tool output still needed?' with fail-open trimming), which would need a fresh Anthropic-Messages implementation and cache-behavior validation to be useful here.

entries.name: kevinpita/pi-jev-context
entries.what: Pi (pi.dev) extension that asks Jev whether older messages/tool pairs are still useful and hides low-scoring ones from model requests, reversibly; off by default.
entries.autoInvocation: Pi extension context filter (automatic once enabled); not usable in Claude Code
