entries.name: jev-model-router (npm, rajdhakad9826)
entries.what: A ~200-line TypeScript library (npm jev-model-router 2.0.1). Router.route(query) calls TypeSafe Jev via @typesafe-ai/sdk systemOne() with a single Score question ("Which model tier should handle this query?") whose levels are your 2-3 model descriptions. It then applies confidence thresholds to pick a model name. It is NOT a Claude Code integration. It has no proxy server, MCP server, hook, skill or CLI, and the README and source never mention Claude Code. The "right Claude model for every turn" claim belongs to a different project (PyPI jev-router by Akashdb5, not audited here). To use it, you would have to write your own wrapper (hook or proxy) around this library.
entries.autoInvocation: Not automatic. It is a library that only runs when other code calls it. To use it, you would have to build a wrapper (an Anthropic-compatible proxy behind ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, or a UserPromptSubmit hook) yourself.
security: No shell execution, no postinstall/preinstall scripts (only build and prepublishOnly). The single dependency is the official @typesafe-ai/sdk 0.6.0, whose author is evinism.
The API key is read from the TYPESAFE_API_KEY env var by the SDK, not from argv. The SDK sends it only as an Authorization Bearer header to the base URL. .gitignore excludes .env.
No telemetry in the library code. The SDK has a logLevel env var; I did not audit its logging in depth.
Single maintainer, 2-week-old package, no signed provenance beyond the npm registry signature. Supply-chain risk is low because of the tiny code size, but nothing is battle-tested.
The prompt-injection surface is the query text sent to Jev. Jev returns only probabilities, so injected text can bias routing but cannot cause tool execution.
Module-level `new TypeSafeClient()` in classifier.ts runs at import time. It will throw if TYPESAFE_API_KEY is missing, so a wrapper needs to handle that.
entries.dataEgress: The `query` string passed to route(), sent as state.document to Jev, plus the model descriptions as the score levels. For Claude Code that would mean whatever text your wrapper feeds it, most likely user prompts, and possibly code or context if you chose to include it. Nothing is sent automatically because the library has no hook into Claude Code. With the SDK defaults it goes to api.typesafe.ai. It reaches OpenRouter only if TYPESAFE_BASE_URL is overridden.
entries.failureMode: Depends on the caller. If fallbackTier is configured, any error from classify() returns the fallback model with isFallback:true (router.ts:26-38). If not, it rethrows (fail-closed). The SDK timeout defaults to 10 s (index.mjs:518), and maxRetries defaults to 2 (index.mjs:74). The worst case per call is therefore roughly 30 s or more when Jev is down, and the router exposes no timeout or retry override. The Router-level code adds no timeout of its own.
entries.contextCost: Zero for Claude Code as shipped, because it registers no tools, hooks or instructions. Any integration would have to be built separately.
pros: Tiny, readable (~200 LOC), MIT, easy to audit. Only one dependency, the official TypeSafe SDK.
Shows a sound use of Jev's Score primitive for tier classification, with an explicit fail-open fallbackTier option (router.ts:26-38).
Because it uses the SDK's TYPESAFE_BASE_URL and Bearer key, pointing it at OpenRouter's /v1/systemone needs env vars only (untested).
Useful as a reference for building your own Jev-based hook or proxy.
cons: It is not a Claude Code integration: no hook, MCP, skill, proxy or CLI. The discovery summary's 'for Claude Code' claim comes from a different PyPI package (Akashdb5/jev-router). Nothing here changes Claude Code behaviour.

Claude Code with an OAuth subscription cannot switch models per turn through a library. Without a custom Anthropic-compatible proxy on ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (which conflicts with subscription login), the routing decision would have nowhere to apply.
Its model names come from your own config and are arbitrary strings. The examples use gpt-4o-mini and claude-3-5-*, which are outdated and not Opus 5.5.

Zero tests, no CI, no releases. Single author, 31 commits all within 3 days, version 2.0.1 published 2 days after creation, and the scoring approach was rewritten from a cost formula to raw thresholds between v1 and v2.
Only the last user query is classified: no conversation, code or tool-output context. A 'fix the bug' prompt reads as easy even when the repo is huge.

Retries and timeout are not configurable through Router (SDK defaults 10 s x 3 attempts). Without fallbackTier a Jev outage makes route() throw. Import-time client construction throws if the key is missing.
Routing only saves cost across models, and this user runs a fixed Opus 5.5 on a flat subscription, so there is little to gain.
entries.verdict: Not usable as-is: it is a 200-line npm library for routing a query to one of 2-3 model names with Jev's Score primitive, with no Claude Code surface at all. Skip it as an integration. At most, borrow the Score-over-tier-descriptions pattern and the fail-open fallback idea for a custom hook, and note that TYPESAFE_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api is the likely (untested) OpenRouter switch.

entries.name: OpenRouter cookbook: Jev-Verified Cascade
entries.what: A documentation recipe (not an installable package, MCP server, hook or skill). It shows TypeScript code for a RAG app: a cheap model (~openai/gpt-luna-latest) drafts an answer from retrieved excerpts, Jev (typesafe/jev-1.13) via POST https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions classifies the draft as supported/unsupported/declined with a confidence, and a frontier model (~openai/gpt-astra-latest) is called only if the check fails. If the verdict is supported with confidence >= 0.8, the answer is sent. If the verdict is declined, it goes to a human. Otherwise it escalates once, and a second failure goes to a human. It targets customer-support/RAG backends and has nothing to do with Claude Code, coding workflows or agent tooling.
interface: (no MCP tools, hooks, skills or CLI commands)
entries.autoInvocation: Not applicable: it is documentation, so it never runs unless a developer implements it in an application. It is 'only when prompted', and it cannot be triggered by Claude Code on its own.
security: No code is installed, so there is no supply-chain, postinstall or curl|sh risk from the recipe itself.
API key is read from process.env.OPENROUTER_API_KEY (not argv). The recipe adds no telemetry.

Prompt-injection surface: the draft answer and the retrieved excerpts are sent to Jev as state. The recipe does not treat them as untrusted, and Jev outputs only typed labels, so injected text can at most skew the verdict.

Jev is a beta, non-reasoning classifier, and the recipe's own benchmark is small (50 questions, self-graded by an Opus judge, and the page admits 2-answer noise between runs). The 'zero wrong answers at 7% of cost' claim is vendor-authored and unverified.
entries.dataEgress: In the recipe as written: the retrieved excerpts, the customer question and the draft answer are sent to OpenRouter (Jev), and also to the draft/frontier models via chat completions. If it were adapted to Claude Code, whatever text is placed in `state` (code, diffs, file contents, tool output) would leave the machine to OpenRouter and then to TypeSafe. The recipe itself has no Claude Code data flow.
entries.failureMode: No failure handling is shown. `verifyAnswer` throws on an unexpected shape, a missing confidence defaults to 0 (which fails acceptance and escalates), and there are no timeouts, retries or fail-open/closed logic. If Jev is down, answerWithCascade throws. Anyone adapting it must add their own timeout and fallback.
entries.contextCost: Zero for Claude Code: 0 tools, no MCP instructions and no hook-injected text, because nothing is installed. The page itself is about 17 KB of markdown (about 4k tokens) only if the user or Claude reads it.
pros: Confirms the exact OpenRouter wiring for Jev: POST /api/alpha/decisions, model typesafe/jev-1.13, OPENROUTER_API_KEY only, serverURL must be https://openrouter.ai (not /api/v1). This is useful as a reference when writing a custom hook or MCP wrapper.

Provides a concrete, copyable Choice request shape (state object plus criteria labels) and the response shape (answers.<name>.choice, confidence, probabilities). It also gives a threshold-tuning method (start at 0.8, adjust from logged verdicts).
Reports realistic Jev behavior: confidences are often near 0 or 1, and it discloses noise (2-answer differences) and a forced-escalation test.
Needs no install or third-party code, so there is no supply-chain risk.
cons: It is not an integration for Claude Code. It has no MCP server, hook, skill or plugin, and it gives Claude Code no automatic behavior.

It targets grounded-RAG answer verification with a cheap-draft/frontier-escalate cost cut. The user's main model is Opus 5.5 on a subscription/OAuth login, where per-token cascades save nothing, and Claude Code's main loop cannot be intercepted this way without a proxy.
Verifying that an answer is 'supported by excerpts' has no clear daily-coding equivalent. It would need a source-grounded ground truth, and code tasks do not have one.
It is TypeScript-only, assumes @openrouter/sdk, and has no timeouts or fail-open handling.
The performance numbers (0 wrong at about 7% of the cost) come from a small, vendor-authored 50-question benchmark graded by another LLM.
Jev is in beta and only supports a 32k context, so large diffs or files would not fit.
entries.verdict: Reference documentation for a support-chatbot RAG cost pattern, not a Claude Code integration. Skip it as an integration, and use it only as a wiring example for the OpenRouter Decisions endpoint. For automatic use inside Claude Code, look at the sibling OpenRouter cookbook 'Auto-Approve Coding Agent Permission Prompts with Jev' (listed in llms.txt), which targets Claude Code permission prompts.

entries.name: Flam1ngFir3ball/jev-claude-router
entries.what: Claude Code plugin built on the early-access "function hooks"/mods API (TypeScript module hooks/register.ts, needs CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1). On every user prompt (turn.start) it POSTs the prompt to Jev's System One endpoint with a Choice question (tier haiku/sonnet/opus/fable) plus a Score question (effort), then rewrites the model and effort of every request in the turn (turn.step), also routing subagents (agent.spawn). Policy layers: confidence bar 75% (90% for upgrades past 100k ctx), prompt-cache price checks, $1 upgrade cap, context-window guard, effort ceiling xhigh, named-tier override ("use opus"), go-ahead shortcut. Optionally replaces Claude's summary compaction by asking Jev (noul questions) whether each tool call and output still matters. Prints a route line plus cost summary in each reply. Fork of satviksinha/jev-model-router; compaction vendored from tamaratran/fast-jev-compaction.
entries.autoInvocation: Deterministic engine-level hooks (turn.start, turn.step, agent.spawn, session.compact) that fire on every turn without any prompting or model discretion. This is the only fully automatic, zero-prompt integration style, but requires function hooks enabled.
security: API key read via $.env.get and sent only as Bearer header, not in argv or process list; key is scrubbed from error text (jev.ts withoutKey/withoutBearer) and keys with odd characters are refused

Base URL allowlist (*.typesafe.ai, https only) unless JEV_ROUTER_ALLOW_CUSTOM_BASE=1; README warns a project-level settings file could redirect key+prompts if both vars are set there, so OpenRouter override must live only in ~/.claude/settings.json

Third-party TypeScript runs inside the Claude Code engine with power to read every prompt, rewrite model/effort of every request, and alter reply text; this is a much larger trust grant than an MCP tool. 8 days old, 2 stars, heavily AI-authored (48 Claude + 17 Cursor Agent commits of 148), no external review

Depends on early-access function hooks API that Anthropic says 'may change between releases without notice' (anthropics/claude-code mods/README.md); a Claude Code update can silently disable it (README: broken module load means every turn runs unrouted)

No curl|sh installer, no postinstall, no shell execution or child_process found in hooks/; only outbound hosts in source are api.typesafe.ai and ai-gateway.vercel.sh; no telemetry found. npm script `types` curls a d.ts from raw.githubusercontent (dev only)

Prompt-injection surface is small: Jev returns typed probabilities only, so text cannot choose arbitrary actions; worst case is a wrong tier. Named-tier override parses user prompt, ignoring quoted/pasted text
entries.dataEgress: To the configured provider only (TypeSafe direct, Vercel gateway, or OpenRouter if overridden): (1) each user prompt, first 12,000 chars (hooks/jev.ts:37); (2) each subagent task text as the model wrote it; (3) one-line finished-task summaries only if JEV_ROUTER_NOTIFY_CONTINUE=0; (4) at compaction (on by default with a TypeSafe/OpenRouter key): conversation text messages plus each tool call's input truncated to 1,000 chars, which includes Write/Edit content, i.e. code; tool result contents are not sent, only size and error flag. Diffs and file reads are not sent directly, but pasted code in prompts and code in Write/Edit inputs are. For client projects this means client code/prompt text reaches OpenRouter and its upstream (TypeSafe); /jev compact off and JEV_ROUTER_COMPACT=0 remove item 4.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open. Default 1500 ms timeout (JEV_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_MS, clamp 100-8000). On timeout, HTTP error, bad JSON or missing key the turn stays on the tier already running (or session model if none) and the route line states the reason (jev.ts:257-372). Caveat: engine $.http.fetch takes no abort signal so a timed-out request still completes and is billed (~$0.00003). Hook budget is 10 s. Compaction falls back to engine summary on >8 s, error or <25% reduction. Silent total no-op if function hooks flag is missing or the module fails to load.
entries.contextCost: Effectively zero tool-definition cost: no MCP server, no tools, no server instructions, no skill descriptions loaded into context. Cost is output-side: a route line (~20 tokens) at the start of each reply and a summary line (~30 tokens, more with agents) at the end are written into the reply text and so remain in conversation history; /jev quiet hides them. No text injected into the system prompt found.
pros: Truly automatic: fires on every prompt via engine hooks, the user never says 'use jev', which matches the stated requirement exactly
Uses Jev for what a System One classifier is good at (Choice tier + Score effort in one request, typed probabilities, ~0.4-0.8 s, ~$0.00003 per call) rather than as a chat model
Economically aware routing: price checks against prompt-cache warmth, $1 upgrade cap, window guard, sticky 75% bar; avoids the classic router failure of cache-thrashing model switches
Fail-open with named reasons and 1.5 s cap; nothing blocks Claude if Jev/OpenRouter is down
Zero MCP context cost, no tools registered, does not collide with gitnexus/playwright/caveman MCPs or the existing classic PreToolUse/GitNexus hooks (function hooks are a separate mechanism)
Provider is code-level compatible with OpenRouter via env-only override (TYPESAFE_BASE_URL + ALLOW_CUSTOM_BASE + pinned model), with compaction following the same endpoint
Strict env-based key handling (not argv), key scrubbing in errors, base-URL allowlist
Broad test suite (~695 cases, register.test.ts drives real hooks), detailed README, per-session /jev controls, tiers can be excluded (e.g. JEV_ROUTER_EXCLUDE=fable,haiku) and ceiling capped
Optional Jev-based compaction keeps conversation verbatim and prunes only tool calls, potentially better than lossy summaries
cons: Depends on Claude Code's early-access function-hooks API ('may change between releases without notice'); unverified that 2.1.285 with CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 loads it, and an update can silently turn it into a no-op

It overrides the model for every request: the user's chosen Opus 5.5 gets downgraded to haiku/sonnet or bumped to fable per Jev's opinion, which changes quality/behaviour and, on a subscription login, whether fable/haiku are even allowed on the plan is unverified; it hardcodes model IDs claude-haiku-4-5, claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-opus-5-5, claude-fable-5-1
Value is mainly cost/usage savings; benefit is unproven and Jev's quality is contested (Theo claims it behaves like a small flash router); tier/effort calibration is only tuned on ~6 sample prompts

OpenRouter is not a first-class provider: needs 4 to 5 env vars incl. a misleadingly named TYPESAFE_API_KEY holding an OpenRouter key and the ALLOW_CUSTOM_BASE flag that widens key exfiltration risk; OpenRouter response compatibility and model-id spelling (jev-1.13 vs typesafe/jev-1.13) untested by me

Sends every prompt (12k chars) and, at compaction, Write/Edit tool inputs (1k chars each) to a third party on client projects; also stores 400 chars of every prompt on disk; needs client-confidentiality sign-off
Very young and low-trust: created 2026-09-22, 2 stars, single main author, mostly AI-written commits, no CI, no marketplace packaging; unusual install path (~/.claude/skills/) from README
Adds 0.4-1.5 s blocking latency to every typed prompt, plus visible route line and cost summary noise in every reply (hideable with /jev quiet)
Bug class where a module load error silently disables everything; ~8k lines of TS in a hot path is a large surface for a tool that just picks a model
Free-form Jev limits: it only sees the first 12k chars of the prompt, not repo state, so routing is on prompt wording alone (a short prompt about hard code can be routed cheap; README admits this)
entries.verdict: The only candidate that is genuinely automatic and uses Jev as a typed classifier at the right moment (per-turn model/effort routing, zero context cost, fail-open), and it should work with OpenRouter by env vars alone. But it needs an experimental engine API, overrides the user's main-model choice, sends prompts and some code to a third party, and is an 8-day-old AI-heavy project, so pilot it read-only first (e.g. JEV_ROUTER_EXCLUDE to limit tiers, /jev compact off, personal projects only) before trusting it on client work.

entries.name: davila7/claude-code-templates (Claude Mods: jev-model-router, jev-skill-suggestion, jev-auto-mode, jev-guardrails, jev-vercel-sandbox)
entries.what: Marketplace/CLI repo (npm claude-code-templates v1.29.6) that vendors "Claude Mods": Anthropic function-hook plugins (register(on, options) middleware, Claude Code >=2.1.259, needs CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1). Five are real Jev integrations under cli-tool/components/mods/: (1) productivity/jev-model-router 0.4.2 sends each prompt to Jev (choice tier, score effort, noul risky) and rewrites subagent model at agent.spawn and main-loop effort (optionally model) at turn.step. (2) productivity/jev-skill-suggestion withholds the engine's skill listing (prompt.attachment) and at prompt.submit runs two Jev requests (rank all skills + gate nouls, then rerank top 3 with SKILL.md excerpts) and injects the winning SKILL.md as a <skill_relevance> block. (3) security/jev-auto-mode is a Jev-judged permission layer on tool.call. (4) security/jev-guardrails screens prompts/replies. (5) security/jev-vercel-sandbox. Also games/chess uses Jev. The candidate's two named items (jev-model-router, jev-skill-suggestion) both exist and are genuine. Backends are TypeSafe direct (api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone, model jev-latest) or Vercel AI Gateway (evaluation-model); OpenRouter is not coded but is a config-only change.
interface: jev-auto-mode: tool.call, tool.check, command.run, skill.prompt, turn.start, session.start
entries.autoInvocation: Deterministic hooks in Claude Code's engine (prompt.submit, turn.step, agent.spawn, prompt.attachment): fire automatically on every prompt/subagent spawn with no model discretion and no user phrasing needed. This is the only candidate found so far that genuinely meets 'Claude Code must use Jev when needed without being told'. Caveats: Jev only makes routing/selection decisions, it does not add capabilities; the router's changes are invisible to the status line.
security: API key: stored in plugin option typesafeApiKey/gatewayApiKey marked sensitive:true in plugin.json userConfig; sent only as Authorization: Bearer header via $.http.fetch (policy.ts:152), never in argv/process list. Plaintext in ~/.claude/settings.json pluginConfigs unless /config stores it securely. No env-var support, so OPENROUTER_API_KEY in env is NOT picked up automatically.

No shell execution in model-router (grep found only $.http.fetch, no exec/spawn). jev-skill-suggestion reads SKILL.md files from disk ($HOME/.claude/skills, project .claude/skills, plugin paths) and injects them into the prompt; setup command asks Claude to Edit ~/.claude/settings.json (goes through normal permission prompt, but user runs bypass/auto mode so it would apply without prompt).

Prompt-injection surface: jev-skill-suggestion injects skill bodies into a <skill_relevance> block the user never sees, and a project-level .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md from an untrusted client repo can be selected and injected; Jev decisions are typed (no free text) so Jev itself cannot inject. jev-model-router's output is constrained to tier/effort enums.

Mods load from project .claude/skills only in a trusted project; --plugin-dir avoids that. Function hooks are an early-access surface that may change between releases (d.ts header says written by 2.1.283).

Installer npx claude-code-templates pulls a large npm CLI with a tracking-service and analytics modules (cli-tool/src/index.js requires ./tracking-service) - not needed if you copy the mod directory manually. No postinstall/preinstall scripts found in cli-tool/package.json.

Open upstream issues on the Jev mods: 'an unset effort skips the downgrade bar, and a null body throws', 'default 800ms timeoutMs loses the second request on a large catalogue', 'catalogues over 255 skills get HTTP 400 from TypeSafe on every prompt (choice limit)', 'setup blocks skills that their authors let the model run'.
entries.dataEgress: jev-model-router: full text of every user prompt (main loop) and, for subagents, the subagent prompt + description + agent type, to the configured base URL (OpenRouter -> TypeSafe/Jev if patched). No code diffs, file contents or tool outputs (README Privacy). jev-skill-suggestion: prompt text + name and one-line description of every candidate skill (request 1), then first 700 chars of SKILL.md of top-3 skills (request 2). jev-auto-mode/jev-guardrails send tool-call summaries / prompts and replies (broader: commands, file paths, assistant replies) to the judge. Client prompts may contain client-confidential text, so this matters for client projects. With no key configured nothing leaves the machine (falls back to engine's own classifier).
entries.failureMode: Fail-open for model-router and skill-suggestion: non-2xx, timeout (Promise.race with $.clock.sleep(timeoutMs), default 800 ms), malformed body or thrown error leaves the request exactly as the engine built it (jev-model-router.ts:167-181; README 'never blocks a turn'). The timeout race does not cancel the fetch. jev-guardrails fail-open by default (timeout 1500ms, failClosed optional). jev-auto-mode timeoutMs 2500 with onError default 'ask' (would prompt the user in auto/bypass mode; can set passthrough/allow) and denies on internal module error. If flag CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS is off or project untrusted, the mods silently do not load.
entries.contextCost: Zero MCP tools, no MCP instructions. jev-skill-suggestion REDUCES context: withholds the skill listing (README: 5,496 input tokens saved on a 40-skill roster; ~9,127 chars for 58 skills in the log example) but adds a per-prompt injected <skill_relevance> block containing the chosen SKILL.md (e.g. ~4.2k chars, ~1k tokens, only when a skill wins; repeated picks are only named). Requires running /jev-skill-suggestion:setup to hide skills from /context accounting. jev-model-router adds no model-visible text (decisions applied as request parameters); status row + log lines only in UI. Plugin-shipped skills stay listed regardless.
pros: Real, automatic, hook-based integration (prompt.submit/turn.step/agent.spawn) - the user never says 'use jev'; matches the stated requirement better than any MCP tool the model must choose to call.

OpenRouter switch is config-only: typesafeBaseUrl='https://openrouter.ai/api' builds https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone (policy.ts:100-103), Bearer auth and {model,state,questions} body match OpenRouter's documented 'change base URL and key only' TypeSafe-SDK compatibility.

Sound decision policy: asymmetric confidence bars (0.3 to spend more, 0.6 to spend less), risky>0.7 forces deep tier, main-loop model routing OFF by default to protect prompt cache, bare slash commands skipped.
Fail-open everywhere for router and skill suggestion with 800 ms cap; no key = falls back to built-in classifier, nothing leaves the machine.

Skill-suggestion cuts a fixed per-session listing cost (~5.5k tokens/40 skills) and follows TypeSafe's own cookbook (vendor-claimed wrong-load 16.8%->7.3%); user has many skills (gitnexus-*, caveman:*, design skills), so real savings.
Active, well-tested code: CI typecheck against Anthropic's mods d.ts, policy unit tests, MIT license, 32k stars, commits within days (2026-09-25 fix).
Cheap: Jev ~$0.042/1M input tokens, output free; a prompt-sized classification costs a fraction of a cent.
cons: Depends on early-access function hooks: needs CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 and a rollout flag (tengu_plugin_hooks_modules); $ API 'may change between releases' (it already changed in 2.1.278 and 2.1.283). Silent no-op if untrusted project or flag off.

Value for this user is modest: Opus 5.5 main model on subscription, and routeMainModel is off by default, so the main saving is lowering reasoning effort and pushing subagents to haiku/sonnet. Effort/model changes are request parameters that the status line never shows (README), making behaviour hard to audit.

Sends every prompt verbatim to a third party (OpenRouter -> TypeSafe); on client projects this is a data-handling/NDA concern. Skill-suggestion also ships all skill names/descriptions and SKILL.md excerpts.

Skill-suggestion is invasive: hides the skill listing, edits ~/.claude/settings.json (skillOverrides, disableBundledSkills), injects SKILL.md out of sight of the user; a malicious client repo's .claude/skills could be injected. Open issues: second request dropped by the 800 ms default on big catalogues, HTTP 400 over 255 skills, setup wrongly blocks some skills.

Two sequential Jev calls per prompt for skill suggestion, one for router; both block prompt start, adding ~0.2-1.6 s per user message; Theo's 'DeepSeek flash router' skepticism means accuracy is unproven (only vendor-cited numbers).

No OpenRouter-specific testing or env var support: key must sit in pluginConfigs under the right plugin id (@skills-dir vs @inline) or it silently falls back to the built-in classifier; OpenRouter confidence-field parity unverified.
Installer is the large npx claude-code-templates CLI with analytics/tracking code; hard rule prevented running it, so recommend copying the directory by hand.
jev-auto-mode/guardrails would send tool-call details and assistant replies to Jev and conflict with user's existing PreToolUse secret-guard/GitNexus hooks and bypass mode; not advised.

Router classifies with state = {prompt: e.text} only (jev-model-router.ts:172), no conversation history or repo context. Short follow-ups ('yes do it', 'continue', 'fix that') look mechanical and can score fast/low effort with confidence >=0.6, silently lowering the main loop's reasoning effort on Opus and routing subagents down to haiku/sonnet. Independent evals show Jev overconfident on unanswerable inputs, which is exactly this case. Quality regression risk on real work, invisible in the UI (status line does not move).

Skill-suggestion has no key-less or outage fallback for skills: hides listing regardless (jev-skill-suggestion.ts:164,231; ask() returns null if !active), so skills vanish for the main model when Jev is down, slow (>800ms), rate-limited/unfunded (OpenRouter 402), or the roster exceeds 255 (open issue #965).

Skill-suggestion reads SKILL.md from the project's .claude/skills and HOME and injects the body unseen as context (fileOf at :300-330); in an untrusted client repo that is a prompt-injection path, and Jev's own spec notes injected instructions in state can move answers. Runs in bypass/auto sessions with no prompt.

Early-access surface confirmed in the 2.1.285 binary (CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS, tengu_plugin_hooks_modules GrowthBook flag): server-side rollout flag can disable it, silent no-op; d.ts header 'written by 2.1.283' and vendor CLAUDE.md say the API changed in 2.1.278 and 2.1.283. Project-level auto-load only in trusted projects; put mod in ~/.claude/skills or use --plugin-dir.

Non-blocking timeout race does not cancel the fetch and still blocks prompt start up to 800ms (model-router) or 2 x 800ms (skill-suggestion) per user prompt, plus one call per subagent spawn; OpenRouter /api/v1/systemone has no SLA and p95 ~600ms is close to the 800ms cap, so tail requests will often be dropped and fall through silently.

Egress on OpenRouter: every user prompt verbatim, every subagent prompt and description, and (skill-suggestion) all skill names/descriptions plus 700-char SKILL.md excerpts go to OpenRouter->TypeSafe. Client-confidential prompts and possibly pasted secrets in prompts are not scrubbed by the mod, and the user's no-secret-leak hook (PreToolUse) does not see prompt.submit traffic.

Repo is a 32k-star marketplace where the mod is one of ~10 early-access items; installer CLI (npx claude-code-templates) includes analytics/tracking-service modules (cli-tool/src/index.js:16,22). Manual copy of the mod dir avoids it, but the user must manage updates by hand.

Router changes a main-loop 'effort' per prompt, which conflicts in intent with a user who deliberately runs Opus 5.5 at a chosen effort; downside (lower effort) is more likely than upside for this user, since Opus is already the top tier and upgrades only raise effort.
entries.verdict: Best automatic Jev integration found: jev-model-router and (optionally) jev-skill-suggestion are deterministic hooks that already speak the exact /v1/systemone wire format, so pointing typesafeBaseUrl at https://openrouter.ai/api with the OpenRouter key and model typesafe/jev-1.13 is a config-only change. Adopt model-router (subagent model + main effort, leave routeMainModel off) first, verify one live call and the log lines, then consider skill-suggestion; skip auto-mode/guardrails and be aware of the early-access flag and prompt-egress on client repos.

verification.note: Repo facts re-verified (MIT, not archived, pushed today, v1.29.6; jev-model-router 0.4.2 last touched 2026-09-24). entries.name: satviksinha/jev-model-router (jev-router)
entries.what: Claude Code "hooks module" plugin (TypeScript, early-access function hooks). On every user turn (turn.start) it POSTs the raw prompt text to Jev /v1/systemone with two typed questions: a Choice "tier" (haiku, sonnet, opus, fable, each with a criteria string) and a Score "effort" (5 levels). In turn.step it rewrites the model request to the chosen model id and effort level (MODEL_OF: claude-haiku-4-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-opus-5, claude-fable-5-1) for all steps of that turn. It also prefixes the reply with a route line, appends a footer with usage and cache ratio, adds a SessionMode footer label, and registers a /jev command (status, on/off, quiet/loud, sticky). This is a model router, not a decision-support tool for code tasks. It fits the "automatic, no prompting" requirement well, but it changes which Claude model answers, which is a big behavioural side effect.
entries.autoInvocation: Deterministic engine hook (turn.start/turn.step modules) that fires on every user turn with no model discretion and no user prompting. Requires only the plugin installed plus CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 in env.
security: No shell execution, no child_process, no postinstall; package.json has only devDependency typescript and scripts; nothing is installed or fetched at plugin load.

API key comes from $.env.get (settings.json env block); sent only as an Authorization Bearer header via $.http.fetch, so it is not in argv or the process list. It goes to whatever TYPESAFE_BASE_URL says (default api.typesafe.ai), so a poisoned env could exfiltrate it.
No telemetry beyond the Jev call itself.

Prompt-injection surface: the raw prompt (including <\task-notification> XML wake-ups) is the Jev 'state'; Jev returns typed enum output, so injection can at most steer the model tier and effort, not execute anything. Route line and footer are written into the reply text that the model sees on later turns (README admits this) which pollutes the transcript slightly.
No prompt redaction: pasted secrets in a prompt go to the provider. The existing PreToolUse secret guard does not cover this path.

Requires CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1, an early-access engine feature. Verified the strings exist in installed Claude Code 2.1.285 (~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.285): 'hooks modules are not turned on for installed plugins ... early access'. The plugin runs TS in-engine with $ capabilities (http, env, agent list, command, ui); it only uses those, per source.
entries.dataEgress: Only the text of each human-typed user turn (e.text, plus <\task-notification> XML text for background-agent wake-ups) plus static tier and effort criteria strings and the API key. No code, diffs, file contents, tool outputs, or transcript history are sent (register.ts:197 state: e.text). Subagent loops are not sent. But whatever the user pastes into a prompt (code, secrets, client data) leaves for Jev via the provider. With OpenRouter this means OpenRouter plus TypeSafe see it; check OpenRouter data-policy settings for client projects.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open. Missing key: no request is made. Timeout default 1500ms (JEV_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_MS), implemented as a Promise.race against $.clock.sleep (jev.ts:251-261; note the fetch is not aborted). HTTP error, non-JSON, no answers, or a tier not offered means the turn runs on the session model unchanged, with an '⚠️ unrouted · reason' line in the reply. Worst case adds 1.5s to the turn. Blocking: turn.start awaits Jev before the turn proceeds.
entries.contextCost: Zero MCP tools, zero tool definitions, no server instructions, no skill descriptions. The only cost is text it writes into the conversation: one route line per reply (~20-30 tokens) plus a fenced footer (~40 tokens) per finished reply, both persisted in the transcript and seen by the model; /jev quiet removes them. Also registers one slash command. Much larger indirect cost: switching model per turn invalidates the per-model prompt cache (README documents 4% cache hit after a switch on 128k context), so mixed routing on big contexts can cost more tokens/quota than staying on Opus.
pros: Truly automatic: turn.start/turn.step hooks fire on every prompt, zero prompting, zero MCP tools and zero tool-definition context cost.
Uses Jev exactly as designed: typed Choice plus Score with calibrated probabilities, no free text, tiny payload (prompt text only).
Fail-open with named reasons, 1500ms cap, one call per turn (not per step), tests for policy/provider/jev/register/status (5 test files, ~60KB) using injected fetch and fake engine.
OpenRouter reachable with config only: TYPESAFE_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api yields openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone (provider.ts:55); at worst a one-line model id patch.
Policy is a plain editable table (TIER_CRITERIA, policy.ts:384) and JEV_ROUTER_EXCLUDE can drop tiers, so it can be tuned to only route between opus and lower tiers or only adjust effort.

Sticky mode (/jev sticky) holds shaky switches to protect prompt cache; /jev shows history, actual answering model and cache ratio, so effect is measurable. Key never in argv; no shell exec; no postinstall.
Secondary value for a subscription user: routing trivial prompts to haiku/sonnet can save quota.
cons: Not a decision-support integration for coding tasks (no branching, gating or review decisions); it only picks a Claude model, and could downgrade the user's Opus 5.5 main model: MODEL_OF maps opus to claude-opus-5 (policy.ts:373-378), and haiku/sonnet tiers will answer real work at lower quality. Model ids are hardcoded and must be edited to match the user's models.
Model switching per turn busts the prompt cache (per README, cache 4% after switch), which can cost more than it saves in long client sessions; requires sticky tuning.
Writes a route line and footer into the assistant's reply text, which is recorded and re-read by the model; noisy for a daily driver (mitigated by /jev quiet).

Depends on an early-access engine API (CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS, hooks modules, 'claude-code' types) that can break across releases; README targets 2.1.275, installed is 2.1.285, so compatibility is unverified.

Very immature: created 2026-09-20, 7 commits, 1 contributor, 4 stars, no releases, no CI, tests not run by me. Heuristic tier criteria were tuned on 10 prompts; Jev quality is unverified (Theo's 'flash-router' claim is unverified) and the sample shows odd combos such as haiku·xhigh.
Adds 0.4-0.85s blocking latency to every human turn (up to 1.5s); the fetch is not aborted on timeout.
Ships the whole prompt to a third party with no redaction; for client projects this needs OpenRouter/TypeSafe data-policy consideration.
No native OpenRouter support: the env var is named TYPESAFE_API_KEY and errors say 'gateway'; the model id 'jev-latest' is untested on OpenRouter. Subagents are never routed.
entries.verdict: The only candidate here that meets the "fully automatic, never say use jev" requirement, via a deterministic turn hook with no context cost and a fail-open design, and it can reach OpenRouter by setting TYPESAFE_BASE_URL. But it is a model router that swaps the Claude model per turn, so it needs its model table and sticky settings tuned to avoid downgrading Opus 5.5 or breaking cache, and it sits on an early-access API and week-old code. Try it only as an opt-in experiment (fork it, fix the model ids and the OpenRouter model name, use sticky mode).

entries.name: gargpratyush/jev-router
entries.what: Node CLI wrapper (jev-claude, jev-codex) that starts a loopback HTTP proxy on 127.0.0.1:<random port>, launches the real `claude` with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL pointed at it, and registers a "Jev Router" sentinel model (jev-router) in /model. For each fresh user turn the proxy makes one Jev System One call (choice over the account's exact Claude model ids plus 3 score questions: task complexity, reasoning, tool complexity), applies a policy (explicit "use opus" override, low-confidence no-downgrade, no downgrade if context >20k tokens, tier clamping) and rewrites body.model to Haiku/Sonnet/Opus (Fable opt-in) before forwarding to api.anthropic.com with the CLI's own auth headers. It routes the main model per turn (cost saving), it does not give Claude a Jev tool. It injects a status line showing the chosen model, and bundles a user-only /jev-explain skill.
entries.autoInvocation: Transparent proxy: fully automatic per user turn once Claude Code is launched through `jev-claude` (or alias) with the Jev Router sentinel selected in /model. No prompting required and no model discretion involved. Not automatic if the user runs plain `claude`; picking any other model in /model pauses routing; typing 'use opus/sonnet/haiku' in a prompt overrides.
security: No npm install/postinstall scripts; single runtime dependency (@typesafe-ai/sdk, MIT, TypeSafe-owned, published 2026-09-12, 3 versions); no telemetry found (grep of src/bin).
API key is read from env/files, never put in argv; the SDK sends it only as a Bearer header to the base URL. SDK logLevel pinned to 'warn' so prompt bodies are not logged (router.mjs:22).

Claude/Anthropic auth headers are forwarded verbatim by the proxy (proxy.mjs:282) and not stored; proxy listens on 127.0.0.1 random port, no auth on the proxy itself (any local process can use it as a header-passing Anthropic relay).

bin/jev-claude.mjs:75-85 calls process.loadEnvFile on the CURRENT DIRECTORY's .env, then copies process.env (line 113) into the claude child: a client project's .env values (incl. secrets and any ANTHROPIC_*/TYPESAFE_BASE_URL) leak into Claude Code's environment, and a hostile repo .env could redirect Jev calls (prompt exfil) via TYPESAFE_BASE_URL or set JEV_API_KEY. Real risk given client projects.

Writes prompt text + full Jev request/response to ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/jev-claude/<session>.json (dir 0700, files 0600, up to 20 entries, pruned after 7 days); JEV_DEBUG writes prompts to ~/.jev-claude.log; JEV_DUMP writes full request bodies (off by default).
Edits ~/.claude/settings.json on exit (restoreSavedModel) - modifies a user file (only the model key, only if sentinel present).
entries.dataEgress: To Jev (TypeSafe or OpenRouter, depending on TYPESAFE_BASE_URL) once per fresh user turn (router.mjs:33-39): the user's typed prompt text (system-reminder blocks stripped; but if the user pastes code/logs it is included in full), session.current_model, approximate context_tokens (chars/4 of messages), environment.available_models (model id list), plus the fixed question text/model guidance. NOT sent to Jev: file contents, diffs, tool outputs, assistant messages, system prompt (README 'Limitations': only prompt text). Everything else (full conversation, code, tool results) still goes to Anthropic exactly as before, via the local proxy. Additionally the local proxy sees all traffic in cleartext (localhost). Also loads cwd .env into process env.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open by design. router.mjs: per-attempt timeout 1500 ms, 1 retry (150-400 ms backoff), hard deadline 3000 ms via AbortController (config.mjs THRESHOLDS); any exception returns null and policy.decide keeps the current model (default 'opus' at conversation start). Missing key: starts plain claude with a warning. Body parse errors pass the request through unmodified. Worst case adds ~3 s to the first request of a turn when Jev hangs. Proxy dying mid-session would break Claude Code (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points at it; 502 on upstream errors). Other silent failure: issue #48 (open, fix in unmerged PR #56) - with Claude Code 2.1.283+ hook output is appended as trailing system messages so newTurnPrompt returns null and routing NEVER fires (session just sits on Opus); this user has SessionStart/other output-producing hooks (GitNexus, caveman), so unpatched master likely no-ops silently. Issue #42: routing down to Haiku on >200k-token conversation can produce a 400 from Anthropic (downgrade guard only for >20k tokens, so mostly mitigated, but upgrade/older-catalog edge cases remain).
entries.contextCost: Effectively zero token cost: no MCP server, no tools, no server instructions, no hooks, no injected additionalContext. Adds one skill (jev-explain, ~90-char description, disable-model-invocation so hidden from model) via --add-dir of the package root, and a status line. Indirect cost: may change conversation to a cheaper model and rebuild cache on tier switches.
pros: Only candidate reviewed that satisfies 'no prompting, automatic' literally: deterministic proxy in front of Claude Code, Jev consulted on every fresh turn, zero model discretion (proxy.mjs:205-273).

Genuinely uses Jev for what it is good at (typed choice + score primitives, calibrated confidence) with a well-designed policy: low confidence never downgrades, downgrade refused when context >20k tokens to avoid cache rebuild (config.mjs THRESHOLDS), explicit overrides win, tool-loop turns keep the tier, sub-agents pinned separately.
Fail-open with tight timeouts (1.5 s/3 s deadline, 1 retry) rather than the SDK default 10 s x2 retries (router.mjs comments).
Near-zero context cost: no tools, no hook injection; all changes are outside the context window.

OpenRouter works with env-only config: SDK honours TYPESAFE_BASE_URL and OpenRouter's /api/v1/systemone accepts the same body and bare 'jev-latest' id, so no fork needed (SDK dist/index.mjs:513,554; OpenRouter docs).
Sends only the user's prompt text to Jev, not code/tool output; Claude auth headers are passed through so subscription/OAuth login keeps working.
MIT, small readable codebase (~1.4k lines src), no postinstall, no telemetry, decent unit tests (65+), clean revert (just run plain claude).
Handles real compatibility problems (MCP schema exclusiveMinimum, stripping thinking/effort for Haiku), and provides /jev-explain and a status line so routing is auditable.
cons: Its value is cost/speed saving by downgrading models, not better decisions inside a coding session. For a user who chose Opus 5.5 as main model on client work, silent per-turn downgrades to Sonnet/Haiku are a quality risk; benefit on a flat-rate subscription is mostly usage-limit headroom.

Routing is only first-turn-of-prompt and cache-sensitive; downgrades refused once context >20k tokens (config.mjs:downgradeMaxContextTokens), so in long daily sessions it will mostly stay on Opus anyway - small realised savings.

Likely silently broken for this setup: issue #48 (open) - Claude Code >=2.1.283 appends hook output as trailing system messages so newTurnPrompt returns null and Jev is never called; user runs GitNexus/caveman/secret-guard hooks on 2.1.285. Fix exists only in unmerged PR #56 (same PR also adds JEV_UPSTREAM_URL/ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL honoring). README tested only on Claude Code 2.1.101.

Requires launching via `jev-claude` (alias) rather than a hook/plugin, and hijacks ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (overwrites any existing base URL on master, proxy.mjs:19 hard-codes api.anthropic.com), CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY, custom model option env vars, ANTHROPIC_MODEL, --add-dir and --settings; depends on undocumented request shape (README admits it) and can break on any Claude Code update.
Loads cwd .env into environment inherited by Claude Code (jev-claude.mjs:75-85,113) - leaks client project env vars and lets a repo's .env redirect Jev traffic; bad for client projects.
Bypass/auto permission mode is unaffected but the proxy sees all Anthropic traffic in cleartext and writes prompts to /tmp/jev-claude/*.json and optionally ~/.jev-claude.log.

Immature and churny: created 2026-09-16, last commit 2026-09-19, 48 commits, 2 real authors, 13+ open issues incl. cache/400/UTF-8 bugs, no releases, CI on PRs only, fast-moving hype (498 stars) rather than proven usage.

OpenRouter support is unofficial (env trick, undocumented on master); model routing relies on Jev's behaviour which skeptics say resembles a cheap flash router, and its confidence on prompts is admitted to be blunted by noise (proxy.mjs:52-53). Jev's beta and 32k context are irrelevant here but quality of the model-choice is unmeasured for Opus 5.5-era model catalog.
Does not expose Jev to Claude as a decision primitive (no gating of risky commands, no Noul/Score tools); only useful for model selection.
entries.verdict: The only fully automatic, zero-context-cost Jev integration in the Claude Code path (transparent proxy, fail-open, OpenRouter reachable via TYPESAFE_BASE_URL with no code change), but it solves model-cost routing rather than giving Claude a Jev decision tool, is likely silently no-op on Claude Code 2.1.285 with this user's hooks until PR #56 is applied, and its cwd .env loading and base-URL hijack are poor fits for client projects. Consider as an opt-in alias (patched fork, no .env loading) if downgrading Opus is desired; not the primary Jev integration.
