entries.name: @ruban24/switchboard
entries.what: Node/TypeScript CLI (`switchboard claude` / `switchboard codex`) that launches Claude Code behind a local loopback proxy. On each new conversation it extracts the user task, sends it to Jev (System One, one request with about 6 Choice questions: taskType, complexity tier, sufficientContext, per-model effort) and applies a local deterministic policy to pick model (Haiku, Sonnet, Opus 5.5, Fable) and reasoning effort. It rewrites the model and effort fields in the /v1/messages request forwarded to api.anthropic.com and pins that pair for the whole conversation. Jev is used only as a model/effort router, not as a general decision tool.
interface: Claude hook UserPromptSubmit + SessionStart (temp settings, exec-form node claude-hook.js)
entries.autoInvocation: Transparent proxy plus deterministic hooks, but only when Claude Code is started through `switchboard claude` (no way to activate inside a plain `claude` process; needs a shell alias `claude=switchboard claude`). Once launched, no model discretion and no prompt phrase needed: every new conversation is classified by Jev automatically.
security: Classifier API key: read from env or plaintext connection.json (0600); never passed in argv. Keys are stripped from the child claude env (launcher.ts:393-394, 349). Docs admit plaintext storage.

Proxy binds 127.0.0.1 on random port with per-launch secret header token; hook URL validated to be loopback http (claude-hook.ts:14-16). Other same-user processes are out of scope by its own admission.

Proxy sees every Anthropic request including the OAuth/API-key auth headers and forwards to https://api.anthropic.com (proxy.ts:29); it is a full MITM of the native traffic, in user space, code is small (328 lines) and readable.
Hooks run outside Claude's sandbox but are exec-form (no shell), fixed-purpose; prompt goes via stdin to local proxy.

Prompt-injection surface: only the user's task text (up to 16,000 chars) is sent to Jev; Jev returns typed choices only, so injected text can at most skew tier/effort selection; no free text is fed back into Claude context (hook stdout empty).
No telemetry (grep for telemetry/analytics empty; docs/privacy.md says none). No curl|sh, no postinstall.
entries.dataEgress: To OpenRouter/Jev: only the extracted user task text (truncated at classifier.maxContextChars=16000) plus policy-derived question definitions, once per new conversation and once per later recognized user turn (recommendation only, does not change route). No repo scan, no diffs, no tool outputs, no full transcript. No redaction, so pasted code or secrets in the prompt are sent. To Anthropic: unchanged native traffic via the proxy. Local disk: routing metadata under ~/.config/switchboard (prompts only if history.capturePrompts=true).
entries.failureMode: Fail-open on the classifier: 3000 ms deadline (defaults.ts classifier.timeoutMs, session.ts:68); any error/timeout yields reason 'classifier-unavailable' and the configured `uncertain` fallback route (default claude-opus, i.e. Opus 5.5 at high effort) is pinned, so the user is never blocked by Jev being down. No retries (maxRetries 0). Fail-closed on local plumbing: if the UserPromptSubmit hook cannot reach the proxy it exits 2 and blocks the prompt (claude-hook.ts:7-12); malformed/missing explicit settings abort launch; resume without saved route errors. Router never retries a failed coding request on another model.
entries.contextCost: Zero tools and zero MCP instructions. Hooks inject nothing into model context (hook stdout empty by design). Only a statusLine line is appended for the user, not the model. Effectively 0 tokens of context. One side effect: the model is set to a `switchboard` alias, and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_UNKNOWN_MODEL_WINDOW_ENFORCEMENT=1 is set; Claude may log an unknown-model diagnostic.
pros: Only candidate that is genuinely automatic and zero-prompt: proxy + UserPromptSubmit/SessionStart hooks decide model and effort with no instruction to Claude and zero context tokens.

OpenRouter supported first-class in code (classifier.ts:38-42, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, base https://openrouter.ai/api -> /v1/systemone), matching the user's chosen provider; model ID overridable to typesafe/jev-1.13 via SWITCHBOARD_MODEL.
Preserves the existing OAuth/subscription login: classification is separate and Anthropic auth headers are just forwarded (docs/classifiers.md: connections are for classification only).
Fail-open on Jev outage with a 3 s deadline and Opus 5.5 fallback, matching the user's current main model, so worst case equals today's behavior.

Ships policy controls that fit this user: excludedModels, effort caps, confidence thresholds (0.70), fallback model; `explain` gives auditable reasons; pins model per conversation to protect prompt cache.
Data egress is narrow (task text only, no repo/tool output), no telemetry, no postinstall, small readable source (about 4k lines) and 291 tests with CI on ubuntu/macOS.

Real use of Jev's calibrated confidence (Choice primitive with confidence thresholds), which is exactly Jev's intended niche, and can save subscription quota/cost by sending routine tasks to Haiku/Sonnet.
Wraps existing statusLine and merges existing hooks rather than replacing them; original settings files untouched (temp settings via --settings).
cons: Not a coding-assistance tool: it only picks model and effort. Gives no Jev decisions for other in-session choices (e.g. whether to run tests, risk scoring, plan vs act).

Not fully automatic inside a stock session: requires launching via `switchboard claude` or aliasing `claude`; IDE/desktop/remote/background/--bare/--safe-mode sessions are unsupported (launcher.ts:195-201).

Overrides the user's deliberate Opus 5.5 default: easy tasks will be downgraded to Haiku or Sonnet, which the user may not want (mitigate via excludedModels for haiku/sonnet or set policy so tiers all map to Opus with effort-only routing). Routing quality is unbenchmarked; 'classify once on first prompt' can mis-tier a conversation whose first message is trivial (e.g. 'hi', 'continue') and then stays pinned.
Fixed for the whole conversation, so it cannot escalate mid-session; only recommends a stronger route for a new conversation.

Uses ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS and refuses to start if either is already set (launcher.ts:150-190), which conflicts with any other proxy or gateway setup; also rejects settings.env overriding ANTHROPIC_MODEL.

The UserPromptSubmit hook is fail-closed: if the proxy/hook breaks, prompts are blocked with exit 2. Adds a second UserPromptSubmit hook and a statusLine override alongside the user's GitNexus/caveman/secret-guard hooks (ordering and interaction untested).
Sends the user's prompt text to OpenRouter/TypeSafe with no redaction; problematic for client projects under NDA unless policy allows it. Plaintext key in connection.json.

Extremely young: repo created 2026-09-20, 19 commits, single author, 15 stars, v0.2.0; tested only up to Claude Code 2.1.283 (user has 2.1.285); a proxy handling OAuth traffic from a fresh solo npm package is a supply-chain concern (pin the version, review dist).

It is an MITM of Anthropic traffic: Claude Code API changes (request schema, effort fields, title requests) can silently break routing; compatibility depends on reverse-engineered protocol handling (native/protocol.ts).
Does not use the OpenRouter Decisions API or Jev Router model; only System One /v1/systemone with jev-latest.
Adds Jev classification latency (0.5 s typical, up to 3 s when degraded) to every user prompt, not just the first, and the classify call is on the request path.

ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to a non-first-party host disables MCP tool search by default, so all gitnexus and playwright tool schemas load up front. It also disables Remote Control, and gateway hint headers are off.

Unknown model alias `switchboard`: the assumed context window is 200K, and switchboard sets DISABLE_UNKNOWN_MODEL_WINDOW_ENFORCEMENT, which turns off proactive auto-compaction, leaving only reactive compaction after an API too-long error.

Auto mode compatibility is unverified and not addressed by the audit. Claude Code's auto mode requires a supported model, and the user's defaultMode is 'auto'. The session's model string is the unrecognized alias `switchboard`. If Claude Code gates auto mode on that name, the session silently starts in Manual, which would be a serious regression. Also untested: server-side auto-mode classifier review passing through a local proxy. Verify by running `switchboard claude` in a scratch dir and checking the mode indicator.

Proxy is fail-closed on session identity: 409 on missing hook data, resume of non-switchboard sessions, or identity mismatch. `claude --resume` of existing sessions and IDE, desktop, remote and background sessions cannot use it.

Default policy routes the demanding tier to Fable, which may need usage credits on a subscription, and routine tasks to Haiku 4.5. Haiku is not eligible for auto mode, and the pinned model is invisible to Claude Code. Needs excludedModels for haiku, sonnet and fable to keep the user's Opus 5.5 default.

Plaintext classifier key in ~/.config/switchboard/connection.json, readable by the agent, and not covered by the user's no-secret-leak hook. Prefer the OPENROUTER_API_KEY env var, which is stripped from the child claude environment.
Doubles up on the UserPromptSubmit and SessionStart hooks alongside the existing caveman and gitnexus hooks. Its UserPromptSubmit hook blocks the prompt with exit 2 if the proxy is unreachable.

Integration is only model and effort selection through a full-traffic loopback proxy on OAuth-authenticated Anthropic requests. That is a large trust surface for a 10-day-old, single-maintainer, 15-star package, against a narrow benefit.
Default classifier model is `jev-latest` (~typesafe/jev-latest on OpenRouter, a moving alias). Routing behavior can change silently with Jev releases. Set SWITCHBOARD_MODEL=jev-1.13 to pin it.
entries.verdict: Best-in-class for the literal requirement (zero-prompt, automatic, OpenRouter Jev, fail-open, no context cost) but it only solves model/effort routing and needs launching via `switchboard claude`, so it is a useful optional layer for cost/quota savings rather than a general Jev integration. For an Opus-5.5-by-choice user, use it only with tight excludedModels/effort-only policy after reviewing the v0.2.0 tarball and pinning the version.

verification.note: Verified from source that OpenRouter support is real and tested. src/classifier.ts:38-42 uses OPENROUTER_API_KEY, base https://openrouter.ai/api and default model jev-latest. The SDK appends /v1/systemone, and test/classifier-connections.test.ts:27-28 asserts the URL https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone with a Bearer key. OpenRouter's docs (https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/community/typesafe-sdk) confirm POST /api/v1/systemone and that jev-latest routes to ~typesafe/jev-latest and jev-1.13 to typesafe/jev-1.13. It does not use /api/alpha/decisions. Repo metadata re-queried on 2026-09-30 and matches the audit: 15 stars, 1 fork, Apache-2.0, not archived, created 2026-09-20, last push 2026-09-28T23:16Z, 19 commits, 1 contributor, v0.1.0 and v0.2.0 releases, npm 0.2.0, no lifecycle scripts in package.json and none in package-lock (hasInstallScript count 0). The runtime needs Node >=22.18. Deps are @typesafe-ai/sdk 0.6.0, ai 7.0.106, @clack/prompts and smol-toml. Source is 4053 lines. Docs say it was verified with Claude Code 2.1.283, while the user has 2.1.285. Security claims verified: exec-form hooks, loopback-only hook URL, per-launch token, keys stripped from the child env, jailbreak-resistant question instructions, and no telemetry found. The score drops from 6 to 5 for these reasons, all missed or misstated by the audit. (1) Classification is awaited on every prompt, so the latency claim is wrong. (2) The proxy is fail-closed in several ways. (3) The non-first-party ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL disables MCP tool search and proactive auto-compaction, and assumes a 200K window for the alias, which contradicts the '0 context cost' claim. (4) Unverified but plausible auto-mode incompatibility with the alias model, and the user's defaultMode is auto. (5) It only picks model and effort, and the user deliberately runs Opus 5.5. It is still the only candidate that is truly automatic and has first-class OpenRouter support, so it stays mid-tier rather than lower. Recommendation: do not adopt by default. If trialed, pin the version, set SWITCHBOARD_MODEL=jev-1.13, set excludedModels for haiku, sonnet and fable, provide the key through the env var rather than connection.json, verify that auto mode and tool search still work, and set ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true only after testing.

judge.why: The only proxy with first-class OpenRouter support and tests. The adversarial pass found it is not the 'zero-cost, worst case = today' tool it claims, and it dropped its score to 5.
pros: Real, tested OpenRouter support; no telemetry; keys stripped from the child env; exec-form hooks
Pins one route per conversation, so no cache-busting mid-conversation switches
Truly automatic inside `switchboard claude`
cons: Classifier call is awaited on every prompt (0.5 s typical, up to 3 s when degraded)
Proxy is fail-closed: 409/502 on resume of non-switchboard sessions, identity mismatch, or crash
Non-first-party ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL disables MCP tool search (gitnexus and playwright schemas load up front) and Remote Control; assumed 200K window and disabled proactive compaction
Unverified auto-mode compatibility with the alias model; the default demanding tier maps to Fable
Key file ~/.config/switchboard/connection.json is readable by the agent; use the env var instead; all OAuth traffic passes through a 10-day-old binary

entries.name: dirien/jev-router (@ediri/jev-router)
entries.what: Local Node.js pass-through proxy (Anthropic Messages for Claude Code, OpenAI Responses for Codex). Claude Code is pointed at it via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL in ~/.claude/settings.json. Once per NEW HUMAN MESSAGE it sends a small scrubbed state plus one 4-option Choice question (mechanical/routine/complex/deep) and two Noul guards (routing_claim_present, alters_sensitive_state) to Jev over the System One API. Jev's answer is mapped by asymmetric thresholds to a model tier (default Claude-only config: fast=Haiku 4.5, balanced=Sonnet 5, frontier=Opus 5.5) and the request's `model` field is rewritten. Tool-loop steps, subagents and compaction follow the session tier, and the tier only ratchets upward within a session. Background calls go to Haiku. Streams pass back byte for byte. It also ships a live decision view on :4100, a `report` command, a systemd user service installer, a secret scanner, and a Docker Sandboxes kit. Jev here is used as a cost/quality tier selector, not as an in-workflow decision oracle.
interface: jev-router doctor / report / ui / init / uninstall / version
entries.autoInvocation: Transparent proxy: fully automatic on every human message once ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points to it. No user prompting, no model discretion, no hook. Deterministic, code-driven.
security: Keys are stored in ~/.config/jev-router/env (0600) and read from env/file, not passed as CLI args, so they do not show in argv/ps; the README explicitly advises JEV_ROUTER_UI_TOKEN over a flag because flags show in ps.

Binds 127.0.0.1 only and refuses non-loopback unless JEV_ROUTER_TOKEN is set; rejects foreign Host headers (DNS rebinding) and any request with an Origin header; no admin API; /healthz exposes only counters.

Claude OAuth/login header is forwarded only to targets marked clientAuth (api.anthropic.com); other upstreams receive minimal headers and no metadata. If ANTHROPIC_API_KEY exists in the router env it overrides the OAuth login and is billed (src/router.mjs:1058-1062).
Refuses to point Claude Code at itself when another gateway's credentials (ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN/API_KEY/apiKeyHelper) are present, so foreign creds are not leaked to Anthropic.

Deterministic secret scanner (src/secrets.mjs, includes sk-or-v1 pattern) on human messages; a hit pins the session to the 'trusted' target and redacts bodies for untrusted upstreams (Ollama). Regex list is admitted to be 'a floor, not a guarantee'.

Prompt-injection surface: the routed text steers Jev; the author cites an independent eval where one sentence moved Jev's answer 73.5%. Mitigated by 'text is data' framing, routing_claim guard and sensitive-state override, and impact is bounded to picking among Anthropic tiers (cost/quality), not tool execution.
entries.dataEgress: To Jev (TypeSafe/OpenRouter), once per human message: a scrubbed state with the latest human message (harness text removed, secrets scrubbed, code blocks replaced by one-line summaries like '[code block (python), 40 lines]', cut to 4,000 chars), up to two earlier human messages (600 chars each), the last assistant message only when the new message is under 30 words, and session metadata (harness name, depth bucket, recent tool-call counts). Never tool output, file contents, diffs, or the system prompt. Claude traffic itself (full prompts, code, tool results) flows through the local proxy to api.anthropic.com only, same data as today; there is no other third-party egress unless the Ollama option is chosen (then fast-tier prompts go to Ollama Cloud with redaction). Local logs hold routing metadata, hashes and costs, not prompts.
entries.failureMode: Jev failure is fail-open with soft fallback: 1.2 s timeout per attempt, 2.5 s deadline per decision, one retry, TypeSafe then OpenRouter, timeout channel skipped 30 s, 401/402/403 skipped 5 min. A new session falls back to the default tier 'balanced' (Sonnet 5, NOT Opus) and stays provisional (retries Jev up to 3 times); an ongoing session keeps its tier. policy.failClosed=false by default. BUT the router itself is a hard single point of failure: setup points ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL at 127.0.0.1:4000 for every session, and when nothing listens Claude Code fails with connection errors (docs/activation.md:235). Mitigated by systemd user service with Restart, but it gives up after 5 failed starts in a minute; and the service only runs while logged in unless linger is enabled. Per-session `launch claude` avoids the global dependency.
entries.contextCost: Zero MCP tools, no hooks, no skills, no server instructions: nothing is injected into Claude's context by the router. It only changes settings env vars. Side effect: ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true is forced (to keep MCP tool search on behind a gateway) and CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=160000 which makes auto-compaction occur earlier than with Opus 5.5's native window. Claude sees no text about Jev at all.
pros: Only candidate that meets the 'fully automatic, never say use jev' requirement with zero prompting and zero context cost: it is a transparent proxy, not an MCP tool or skill Claude must choose to call.

Real OpenRouter support in code (channel 'openrouter', https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone, model typesafe/jev-1.13, OPENROUTER_API_KEY), usable as the sole Jev provider; TypeSafe direct optional as failover.

Works with subscription/OAuth login: the client's own credential is passed through to api.anthropic.com only, no Anthropic API key needed (README + src/router.mjs:1058-1062). Claude Code 2.1.285 exceeds the required 2.1.273.

Careful design: decides only at human turns, ratchets upward only, keeps prompt cache, routes background calls to Haiku, adapts 5 request shapes that break on Haiku 4.5 (thinking, effort, max_tokens, system-message folding, 1M beta), which is the hard part of Claude Code model routing.

Sends Jev only a small scrubbed state (never tool output/file contents/system prompt) and has a deterministic secret scanner pinning secret-bearing sessions to a trusted target: reasonable for client projects.

Good hygiene: zero runtime deps, Apache-2.0, ~200 tests with coverage gates, SHA-pinned CI, npm provenance, loopback-only with DNS-rebind/Origin protections, keys not in argv, clean `uninstall` that restores settings.json, `launch claude` for per-session opt-in, and a live decision view plus `report` for auditing.

Composes cleanly with the user's existing hooks and MCP servers: it touches none of them (no PreToolUse/GitNexus/caveman interaction), and it forces ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH which helps the user's several MCP servers.
Explicit manual overrides (#frontier, /model opus, x-jev-tier) let the user pin Opus when they want it.
cons: Its value is cost/quota saving via downgrading, not extra intelligence: with Opus 5.5 as the user's main model, easy turns get silently rerouted to Sonnet 5 or Haiku 4.5. A senior dev prioritising quality on client work may not want that; a mis-route to a cheap tier hurts the whole session (author's own data: all 12 observed Jev misses were too cheap).

Very young and single-maintainer: repo created 2026-09-24, v1.6.0 on 2026-09-25, 118 commits in 2 days, 6 stars, 1 contributor, SECURITY.md still lists 1.5.x as latest supported. It sits on the path of every Claude request and the OAuth bearer token, so any bug or compromise is high impact; no third-party audit.

Global router is a hard single point of failure: if the service is down or crash-loops (systemd gives up after 5 starts/min) every claude session fails to connect, and the user must undo ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. Mitigation is `launch claude` per session, but then it is not automatic for plain `claude`.

Changing ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL alters Claude Code behaviour: forces CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=160000 (earlier compaction than Opus 5.5's native window), ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true, and uses undocumented gateway hint headers. Anthropic states model routing through gateways is unsupported for non-Claude models; behaviour with subscription OAuth may change with Claude Code updates.

Unverified quality claims: the routing accuracy figures come from the author/LiteLLM benchmark on author-written prompts, and the Jev prompt-injection sensitivity (73.5% flip in an independent eval) plus Theo's skepticism mean thresholds need tuning on the user's own prompts (docs/evaluation.md).

Sends the user's (scrubbed, truncated) prompts to a beta third-party model on each human turn; for client projects with confidentiality terms this is extra egress beyond Anthropic, though limited to text of the messages, not code or tool output. Regex secret scanning is admitted incomplete.
Tier switch invalidates prompt cache for that model (first request after an upward move is cold), and the ratchet means long sessions drift to Opus anyway, reducing savings.

Setup mutates ~/.claude/settings.json, installs a global npm package and a systemd user unit (bypass-permission users get no prompt on these). Codex and Ollama parts add unused surface; Jev is not exposed to Claude for in-task decisions (no Choice/Score/Noul tools for e.g. permission gating).

Auto-mode classifier and other `auxiliary` requests (classifiers, summaries) are re-routed to Haiku 4.5 with thinking and effort stripped. This is a risk for a defaultMode 'auto' user (src/router.mjs:77, 515-523).

The router disables Claude Code Remote Control (any non-Anthropic ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL). Fast-mode and WebFetch preflight checks still call api.anthropic.com directly. Source: code.claude.com llm-gateway-connect.

Open issues #2 and #3: interrupted setup leaves temp files containing API keys, and each setup run overwrites the only settings.json backup, so the original is lost. Five open issues in total within 6 days.
The OPENROUTER_API_KEY lives in ~/.config/jev-router/env, readable by Claude's Read/Bash tools. The user's no-secret-leak hook does not cover this path.
A Jev outage or missing key sends new sessions to Sonnet 5 by default instead of Opus 5.5, so the user's chosen main model is overridden precisely when Jev is unavailable.

Anthropic's gateway docs say a gateway must keep up with Claude Code's evolving headers and body fields, and Anthropic 'doesn't endorse, maintain, or audit third-party gateway products'. The author's own request shapes were captured from 2.1.281, and the user runs 2.1.285. Regression risk on every Claude Code update, with a single 6-day-old maintainer who ships several releases a day.

OpenRouter side of Jev is used only through the System One /api/v1/systemone endpoint, which the brief lists as /alpha status with no SLA, on the critical path of every human turn (bounded by a 2.5 s deadline).
entries.verdict: The only reviewed option that is truly automatic with zero context cost and first-class OpenRouter support, but it is a cost-downgrade router on the critical path of all Claude traffic, from a 6-day-old single-maintainer project. Worth trying via per-session `jev-router launch claude` (or with the Fable/Opus-biased config and #frontier override) rather than a global settings.json install, and it does not give Claude access to Jev decisions for hooks or permission gating.

verification.note: Verified by reading source (nothing was run). OpenRouter support is real: channel 'openrouter' in config/anthropic-only.json, baseUrl https://openrouter.ai/api, model typesafe/jev-1.13, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, and POST ${baseUrl}/v1/systemone with a Bearer key (src/jev.mjs:~290). It uses System One, not /alpha/decisions. Confirmed dataEgress limits: 4000 chars for the latest message, 600 chars each for earlier turns, and the last assistant message only if the new message is under 30 words (src/jev.mjs:52-80). Confirmed there is no telemetry and no postinstall script, and that the audit's stats and failure-mode details are accurate. Lowered from 6 to 5: it is a cost-downgrade router, not a way for Claude to use Jev decisions. It sits on the path of all Claude traffic, from a 6-day-old single-maintainer project. The auxiliary/classifier-to-Haiku re-routing affects the user's auto mode. Remote Control breaks, the key file is exposed to Claude's own tools, and setup has open bugs. My reading that auto-mode classifier calls arrive as request class `auxiliary` rests on the Claude Code docs wording, not on a live capture. If the classifier instead arrives as `main`, that concern falls away, but the rest of the score stands. Best use is `jev-router launch claude` per session with the Opus-biased or #frontier override, not a global settings.json install.

judge.why: The most careful proxy design: cache-aware, background calls to Haiku, override syntax, 1.2 s per-channel and 2.5 s total Jev deadline, OpenRouter native. It is still a global-traffic proxy, and the check found it downgrades your auto-mode classifier and defaults to Sonnet.
pros: OpenRouter-native, no telemetry, no postinstall, Apache-2.0
Documented fail-open with deadlines; opt in per session with `jev-router launch claude` rather than globally
Sends only limited context to Jev (4000 chars of the latest message)
cons: Auxiliary requests (session titles, auto-mode classifier) go to Haiku 4.5 with thinking stripped, a safety-relevant downgrade for defaultMode auto
Jev outage or missing key puts new sessions on Sonnet 5, not Opus 5.5
Disables Remote Control; setup overwrites the only settings.json backup; temp files can hold keys (issues #2 and #3)
Key sits in ~/.config/jev-router/env, unprotected by no-secret-leak; ships several releases a day; Claude Code header drift risk

entries.name: drewpayment/jev-route
entries.what: Claude Code "hooks module" plugin (TypeScript, early-access CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1). On every eligible prompt it sends the redacted prompt (<=20k chars) plus previous tier to Jev's /v1/systemone with a Choice question (tier fast/balanced/powerful) and a Noul question (risky). It then rewrites model (and optionally effort) of every API request of that turn via turn.step (fast->haiku, balanced->sonnet, powerful->opus), with hysteresis, prompt-cache-aware switch lock (downgrades blocked above 50k context) and risky>=0.7 forcing powerful. It is a cost/capability router, not decision support for coding actions. Fails open to the session model.
entries.autoInvocation: Deterministic hook (engine-level prompt.submit/turn.step hooks module): runs automatically on every prompt with no model discretion and no user prompting. This is the only candidate style that fully matches 'Claude Code must use it without me saying so', but it uses Jev only as a model-tier router.
security: No shell execution, no MCP server, no npm deps, no postinstall, no curl|sh; static-scanned module may only import own files and 'claude-code' (docs/ENGINE-API.md).
Only network egress is one $.http.fetch to the configured base URL (register.ts:237); jev_base_url must be https (http only loopback), userinfo redacted in output (config.ts:281-292).

API key is a sensitive userConfig (secure storage), no process argv exposure at runtime; fallback reads key in plaintext from settings.json env (register.ts:154-166). Installing with --config jev_api_key=... exposes key in argv/shell history at install time.
Regex redaction of secrets (sk-, AKIA, ghp_, JWT, PEM, password=, Bearer, URL userinfo) is best-effort (eligibility.ts:8-53); client code, names, and business context in prompt text are not redacted.

Prompt-injection surface is small: prompt text is graded as data (TIER_INSTRUCTIONS says treat as data), output is constrained to 3 tiers so the worst injection outcome is a wrong model tier, though a crafted prompt could force cheaper model or trigger extra spend.

Early-access API requires CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1; hooks modules run inside the Claude Code process with access to $.settings.read (it reads settings env for keys), i.e. the plugin can read your settings env block, so an update pulled from a malicious upstream would be powerful. Pin the version.
entries.dataEgress: Text of each user prompt only (secrets regex-redacted, head+tail truncated to 20,000 chars) plus previous_tier label plus tier/risky question text, sent to the configured Jev endpoint (OpenRouter if custom). No files, diffs, tool outputs, prior messages (README Privacy; jev.ts:40-51; register.ts prompt.submit). Prompts of client projects would flow to OpenRouter/TypeSafe; /route off stops it. With no key, the built-in classifier keeps everything local.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open everywhere: every hook is wrapped in try/catch; any error, non-2xx, unparseable response, or timeout means no decision and the session model runs (register.ts:236-253, prompt.submit catch). Hard deadline timeout_ms default 800 ms (clamped 50-5000) covering fetch+body+parse with AbortController. Status line shows 'route: on' and /route status shows last error. If Jev is slow every prompt is delayed by up to 800 ms before failing open.
entries.contextCost: Zero MCP tools and zero tool-definition tokens; no server instructions; no text injected into the model context (prompt passed through untouched, only status line/toasts in the UI). Registers one slash command (/route) only. Effectively 0 context tokens. Side effect: switching model per turn can invalidate prompt cache (mitigated by switch lock and hysteresis).
pros: Only candidate that is fully automatic and deterministic: prompt.submit/turn.step hooks fire every turn with no user 'use jev' prompting and no MCP tool-choice by the model.
Zero context cost: no MCP tools, no injected text.
Fail-open with hard timeout (default 800 ms), so Jev/OpenRouter outage never blocks coding.

Clean, small, readable code (1448 lines, no deps, no shell exec); wire format uses Choice+Noul primitives exactly as Jev is designed (typed tier + risky probability), a genuinely good use of Jev's strengths.
OpenRouter reachable via provider=custom with base https://openrouter.ai/api (yields /v1/systemone) and typesafe/jev-1.13 model id; parser lenient about response keys.

Sensible engineering: secret redaction, cache-aware hysteresis and switch lock, subagent turns untouched, /route kill switch, decision toasts, per-tier model mapping configurable, defaults already use claude-sonnet-5-5 / claude-opus-5-5.
Can save quota/cost by sending trivial prompts to Haiku while keeping Opus for risky work; MIT license.
cons: Brand new and single-author: created 2026-09-29, 6 commits, 1 star, 0.2.0, 2 issues (self-filed); alpha. Author states developed/verified against 2.1.283/2.1.284, user is on 2.1.285 (untested).

Depends on Claude Code's early-access, undocumented 'hooks modules' API needing CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1; docs/ENGINE-API.md says 'recovered notes' from the binary; API may break in any release. I could not verify this feature exists in the user's build.
No OpenRouter support out of the box: no OPENROUTER_API_KEY fallback, README documents only TypeSafe and Vercel gateway; OpenRouter wire-equivalence of /api/v1/systemone unverified (docs fetch 404).

Does not use Jev for anything besides picking Haiku/Sonnet/Opus. For a user whose main model is Opus 5.5 on subscription, downgrading turns to Haiku/Sonnet may lower quality and, on OAuth subscription, saves little money (only rate-limit quota); Jev latency +0.4-0.8 s per prompt with a benefit only if routing helps.

Routing model classifier judges only the prompt text ('yes', 'continue' rely on previous_tier), with no repo/context awareness; skeptics say Jev behaves like a small router, so tier quality is unproven.
Switching models per turn breaks prompt cache in the first turn of a switch (mitigated but not eliminated) and downgrades stop after 50k context, so it is most useful in short sessions.
Client-project prompt text goes to a third party (OpenRouter -> TypeSafe); redaction is regex best-effort only.
Installing with --config jev_api_key puts key in argv; settings.json env fallback stores it in plaintext.
Tests are mocks only; CI validate steps are continue-on-error, so plugin validity in real engine is not enforced.
entries.verdict: The only fully automatic, zero-context-cost, fail-open Jev integration found, but it is a day-old single-author plugin on an undocumented early-access hooks API and uses Jev purely for Haiku/Sonnet/Opus routing, which is of limited value on an Opus subscription. Worth trying with provider=custom against OpenRouter (after pinning the commit and reading the code, which is small) as an experiment; not something to depend on.

entries.name: claude-jev-model-router
entries.what: Local Node HTTP proxy (127.0.0.1:8787) placed between Claude Code and api.anthropic.com via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. For the first request of each subagent (x-claude-code-agent-id header) it sends the delegation prompt (latest user turn, max 4000 chars) plus 6 fixed Noul yes/no questions to Jev /v1/systemone, combines P(yes) with hand-set weights in code into a score, and maps it to Haiku/Sonnet/Opus tiers with margin gates. Only the `model` field is rewritten; everything else is relayed byte-for-byte and streamed. Main conversation is never touched by default. Observe-only by default (logs what it would do); --enable applies routing. Does model-cost routing for subagents, not code intelligence.
entries.autoInvocation: Transparent proxy: fully automatic once ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is set and the daemon runs; no prompts, hooks or tool calls needed. Only acts on subagent requests (x-claude-code-agent-id), never the main thread by default. This is the only category in the candidate set that satisfies 'Claude Code uses Jev without being asked', but what it automates is model-tier routing for subagents, a narrow use of Jev.
security: No postinstall/preinstall scripts (npm scripts only dev/build/check/prepublishOnly); only 2 runtime deps (undici, smol-toml); no child_process/eval in src.
Binds 127.0.0.1 by default (config.ts defaultConfig), but --host is configurable; no auth on the local listener, so any local process can use it as an Anthropic relay.

Proxy sees every request incl. the OAuth/Bearer Authorization header and the full conversation; it forwards headers unchanged (relay.ts buildUpstreamHeaders) and does not log them. Decision log (decisions.ts, server.ts:110-125) records metadata only (ids, models, tool counts, tokens, reasons), no prompt text.

API key handling: README's first-listed method is `--env TYPESAFE_API_KEY=...` on the command line, which exposes the key in the process list / shell history; safer options are env var or ~/.claude-model-router/.env.

envfile.ts loads ./.env from the CURRENT DIRECTORY first (index.ts loadDotEnv ['.env', ~/.claude-model-router/.env]) into process.env, so launching the proxy from a client project dir pulls that project's .env into the proxy process (not sent anywhere, but surprising).

Prompt-injection surface is small: Jev output is only numbers (P(yes)) combined by fixed code; a malicious delegation prompt can at worst bias the tier choice. Readonly tool sets skip Jev entirely; mutation-capable downgrades to Haiku need margin >=0.3.
entries.dataEgress: To Jev (TypeSafe direct as shipped; OpenRouter after patch): once per new subagent that has exec or mutation tools, the latest user-turn text (the delegation prompt Claude Code wrote for the subagent, truncated to 4000 chars, context.ts MAX_TURN_CHARS) plus turn index, model id and 6 fixed question strings. No transcript, files, diffs or tool outputs by design, but the delegation prompt often contains file paths, symbol names and task descriptions, which matters for client projects; with OpenRouter it passes through OpenRouter and its provider. Read-only subagents send nothing. To Anthropic: the normal Claude traffic (all of it) transits the local proxy unchanged except model. Local: JSONL log ~/.claude-model-router/decisions.jsonl (metadata only, no prompt text). Auth header is forwarded, not stored.
entries.failureMode: Jev failure is fail-open: 3000 ms timeout (router_timeout_ms; code default in JevRouter is 400 but config passes 3000), HTTP >=400, non-JSON or no answers become RouterError, caught in policy.consultRouter, and the request falls back to the static tier (cheap for readonly/exec agents, mid for mutation-capable). Low margin also falls back. Jev being down never breaks a Claude request. BUT the proxy process itself is a single point of failure: if it is not running while ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points to it, all Claude Code API calls fail (connection refused); upstream failure returns 502 (server.ts:146-159). Needs a supervised service. Observe mode still calls Jev for every subagent request each time (not sticky), adding latency without benefit.
entries.contextCost: Zero tokens in Claude's context: no MCP tools, no hooks, no skill, no injected text. It is a transparent network proxy. Indirect effects: setting ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to a non-Anthropic host may change some Claude Code client behaviour (e.g. features gated on first-party base URL such as MCP tool search); unverified, worth testing. Also the GET /v1/models catalogue returned by the proxy lists only the 3 tier IDs.
pros: Truly automatic and zero-prompt: transparent proxy triggered by the x-claude-code-agent-id header, no MCP/hook/skill overhead in context (0 tokens).
Uses Jev the way its brief says it should be used: typed Noul questions to get calibrated P(yes), with arithmetic and thresholds in deterministic code (signals.ts:141-164) and nothing free-text.

Conservative design: main thread never touched, sticky per-subagent decision protects prompt cache, tool-set gates (readonly capped cheap, Write/Edit agents need margin >=0.3 to go to Haiku, fallback mid), fail-open on any Jev error.
Observe-only by default with JSONL decision log and a `savings` report; you can watch decisions for a day before --enable.

Request body handling is careful: only `model` rewritten, undici.request for byte-exact relay, backpressure, unbuffered SSE, error bodies untouched, anthropic-* headers forwarded as an open list; passes the OAuth Authorization header straight through so subscription login should keep working.
Tiny, readable codebase (~2k LOC src, 2 deps, no postinstall), easy to audit and to patch for OpenRouter.
Jev call happens once per subagent so cost is negligible (~400 tokens at ~$0.042/M input).
cons: Hardcoded to api.typesafe.ai and TYPESAFE_API_KEY with no OpenRouter path; needs a local patch/fork (trivial, but you then own an unmaintained fork of a 10-day-old, 6-commit, single-author, 1-star project).

No LICENSE file despite MIT metadata, no CI, git package.json (0.1.2) lags npm (0.1.3), README says subagent_router defaults to jev but code default is none (config.ts defaultPolicy) unless a TOML config is passed.

Narrow value: only affects subagent model choice. Gains are cost/quota savings on Explore-type subagents; for a subscription/OAuth user there is no per-token bill, only quota, and Opus 5.5 subagents may be deliberately wanted. No help with code intelligence, review, or decisions in the main loop.

Classifier only sees the delegation prompt (README admits this), so difficulty is prompt-level; wrong downgrades to Haiku on editing agents are possible. Six hand-tuned weights and thresholds are unvalidated, and the author's own comments show tuning trouble (400 ms timeout on every call, margin 0.25 rejecting nearly all).

Operational burden: a persistent local daemon must be running (systemd user unit) or every Claude Code call fails; ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL must be exported in the environment or settings.json env; non-first-party base URL may alter Claude Code features; the proxy handles your OAuth bearer token and all conversation content for personal and client projects.

Hardcoded tier IDs (claude-sonnet-5.5, claude-opus-5.5, claude-haiku-4-5) use dotted names not verified against the real API IDs used by Claude Code 2.1.285; a mismatch would make routed subagents error (model-not-found) once --enable is on. Unverified, must check the observe log's model_in values first.
Delegation prompt text (possibly client code names/paths) goes to a third-party inference endpoint; only mitigated by size cap and readonly-skip.
--env KEY=... documented as the first option leaks the key to the process list; ./.env from cwd is auto-loaded.
entries.verdict: The only genuinely automatic, zero-context-cost Jev integration in this set, and its design is careful and fail-open, but it automates just subagent model-tier routing, is 10 days old with a single author, and needs a small patch to use OpenRouter instead of api.typesafe.ai. Worth running in observe mode with a patched OpenRouter key only if you spawn many subagents and want quota savings; not a general Jev integration for daily coding.
entries.license: MIT declared in package.json/npm, but repo has no LICENSE file (GitHub licenseInfo null) and the npm tarball also ships none despite files[] listing LICENSE

entries.name: OpenRouter Jev Router (typesafe/jev-router)
entries.what: A hosted OpenRouter model slug (typesafe/jev-router), not a repo or package. Jev reads the conversation, scores task type, difficulty, precision and how much a stronger model would help. OpenRouter then serves the request from the cheapest pool model that meets that bar, choosing reasoning effort too. It is described as cache-aware: it switches model only when the expected gain outweighs the lost prompt cache. It works over Chat Completions, Responses and Messages (streaming and non-streaming). Claude Code's Messages traffic can therefore hit it through OpenRouter's Anthropic-compatible endpoint with no local code. An optional `jev-router` request plugin (models / allowed_models / excluded_models, up to 1,024 wildcard patterns each) narrows the pool. The `X-OpenRouter-Metadata: enabled` header exposes the decision (resolved_models, list_fallback, list_tier_cap, max_fallback).
entries.autoInvocation: Transparent proxy. Once ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points at OpenRouter and the model is typesafe/jev-router, every main-loop and subagent request is routed with no user prompting and no model discretion. It is the only candidate type that satisfies 'never say use jev' literally. The cost is that it replaces the model choice rather than adding a capability.
security: No local code is installed: no npx, hook, MCP or postinstall surface. Risk sits in the account and the network path.

The OpenRouter key goes in ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN (sent as a Bearer header). It stays out of argv if set in the shell profile or the settings.json `env` block. OpenRouter's own doc warns against committing it and suggests loading it from a keychain.
Putting the key in project .claude/settings.local.json risks leaking it into a client repo. Use ~/.claude/settings.json or a shell wrapper instead.

OpenRouter docs say Claude Code + OpenRouter is only guaranteed to work with the Anthropic first-party provider. If the router picks another provider, tool-use or thinking quirks are possible. Silent switching to non-Anthropic models is a behavioural and compliance surprise.

The router decides using conversation content, including pasted logs and issues. Content in tool results could in principle steer routing (for example, low-difficulty framing pushes a cheap model). Third-party coverage says the router claims to see the conversation, so this is an untested prompt-injection surface.

Data-policy and ZDR details for the router are not stated on the doc pages I could read. The Auto Router docs mention honoring account ZDR and guardrails; whether Jev Router does the same is unverified.
entries.dataEgress: Everything Claude Code sends in each Messages request leaves the machine. That is the system prompt and CLAUDE.md content, the full conversation, file contents from Read/Grep, Bash outputs, diffs and tool results, plus images if present. It goes to OpenRouter, to Jev (TypeSafe) for the routing decision (the docs say Jev 'reads the conversation'), and to whichever upstream model provider is picked. That is potentially non-Anthropic and non-US, and the pool is not enumerated in the docs I read. Versus today's Anthropic-only path, this adds OpenRouter, TypeSafe and possible extra model vendors. That is a real issue for client code. The existing PreToolUse secret guard only blocks tool input, not what tool results carry onward, and it does not reduce this exposure.
entries.failureMode: Fail-closed. Claude Code talks only to openrouter.ai, so an outage, 5xx or 502 upstream stops the session with no fallback to Anthropic (docs: 502 for upstream failure, 'failed generations are not billed'). Exclusion lists that empty the pool return 404, but Claude Code cannot send the plugin. OpenRouter advertises provider failover across Anthropic providers for Anthropic models. The Auto Router docs say it 'degrades gracefully' if classification is unavailable; I found no equivalent statement for Jev Router. The router's own decision latency is claimed at 70-500 ms for Jev; there is no documented timeout for it. Mitigation: keep a separate wrapper or profile so plain `claude` still uses the subscription.
entries.contextCost: Zero added Claude Code context: no tools, no MCP server instructions and no hook-injected text. It only changes which endpoint and model string are used. Indirect cost: Claude Code's model-specific prompt tuning, cache_control and thinking behaviour may degrade when the served model is not Opus or Sonnet. Also, supported_parameters is empty and pricing is dynamic, so tool-calling support is asserted only in third-party summaries ('streaming, tools, thinking and prompt caching pass through untouched').
pros: Only truly automatic option evaluated: no hook, MCP or prompt discipline. Set two env vars and the model string, and it just runs (OpenRouter claude-code-integration.md).
Zero context and zero local attack surface: no tools, no server instructions, no hooks, no installer or npm supply chain (contrast with wrapper proxies that run localhost code).

Cache-aware by design: it holds a model while the prompt cache is warm and switches only if the gain exceeds the lost cache. This addresses the biggest failure of naive per-turn routers in Claude Code's long agentic loops.
Can lower spend by sending mechanical turns to cheap models. Pricing is the underlying model's cost with no separate router fee ('costs nothing to invoke' per coverage).
OpenRouter-native, so it fits the user's OpenRouter-only constraint, with the Activity dashboard, budgets and response.model giving per-request visibility into what was chosen.
Works with the Messages API that Claude Code speaks, streaming supported, and the pool can be restricted with the jev-router plugin (for API callers).
cons: Does not work with the subscription/OAuth login. OpenRouter's guide requires blanking ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, setting ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and running /logout, so all traffic bills per token. Leaving the flat-rate Opus 5.5 subscription for a heavy all-day user could cost far more.

It replaces the user's chosen Opus 5.5 with whatever the router picks; the user would lose deterministic quality on hard tasks. Jev's role is a cheap decision model, and the benefit claimed is cost/speed, not better code.

Evidence is thin and maker-reported. The model was created about 2026-09-25, is beta, and the pool/tier composition is not documented in the pages I read. Benchmark claims conflict across sources (237 vs 130 tasks in the announcement summary; 221 vs 73 in the JevMade summary), and the skeptics' claim that it is a small-model router is unresolved.

Tool-calling support is not confirmed by structured metadata (supported_parameters is []; /endpoints returns empty). Claude Code's heavy tool-use and thinking loop on non-Anthropic models is explicitly not guaranteed by OpenRouter ('only guaranteed to work with the Anthropic first-party provider').

Cannot pass the jev-router plugin from Claude Code, so restricting the pool to Anthropic models, or excluding weak models, is not possible per-request. It would need OpenRouter account-level provider/model restrictions, and whether Jev Router honors these is unverified.

Fail-closed dependency on OpenRouter for every keystroke, and conversation content goes to OpenRouter, TypeSafe and unknown upstream vendors. That is a compliance risk for client projects, and pointing settings at a single endpoint affects all projects unless scoped.
Cache loss risk remains when a switch happens, since a switch discards the prompt cache. With Claude Code's large system prompt and tool schema, a bad switch is expensive.
Could not be tested here (no OpenRouter key; live checks limited to the public /models listing and the docs).
entries.verdict: The only genuinely zero-prompt, zero-context integration, but it swaps your model rather than adding Jev as a capability, forces API billing instead of the Opus 5.5 subscription, and sends all code to OpenRouter, TypeSafe and unknown upstream providers. Worth trying as a scoped opt-in profile (separate wrapper or settings for personal, low-stakes projects) after a small paid trial to check tool-use reliability. It is not a good global default for client work.

entries.name: xafold/jev-router
entries.what: Rust binary (jev-router 0.5.8) that wraps `claude`. `jev-router claude` starts a loopback HTTP proxy (127.0.0.1:random) and launches Claude Code with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL pointed at it and a sentinel model "jev-router". On the first request of each user turn the proxy calls TypeSafe Jev (POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone, model jev-1.13.0) with about 40 Noul/Choice/Score questions. It maps the answers through rule trees to a model and effort (Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 5/5.5, Opus 5.5), rewrites the /v1/messages body, and forwards it to api.anthropic.com. It reuses Claude Code's own auth headers (API key or OAuth). It also has cache-aware switching, safety floors (security, concurrency and irreversible work get at least Opus), per-message effort system messages, a local dashboard, a status line wrapper, and feedback-based auto-tuning. It uses Jev only for model and effort routing. It gives Claude Code no Jev tool for decisions.
interface: No MCP tools, hooks or skills
entries.autoInvocation: Transparent proxy. Once Claude Code is started via `jev-router claude` (the user would alias claude to it), every turn is routed with no prompting and no model discretion. It is not a hook, MCP tool or skill. Plain `claude` is not covered, and there is no installer that wires it into settings.json. It only chooses which Anthropic model and effort serves the turn. It does not give Claude Code access to Jev decisions for other purposes, such as tool-use gating, commit or test triage, or risk scoring.
security: The proxy sees every Claude Code request in full: prompts, file contents, tool results, and the Authorization or x-api-key header (the OAuth token for a subscription login). It forwards them unchanged to the upstream, api.anthropic.com or the user's ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (src/main.rs:111-112, src/proxy.rs:826+). Risk is contained by binding only to 127.0.0.1 with a random port (src/proxy.rs:714). Any local process can still reach that port and use the proxy as an authenticated relay.

The TypeSafe key is read from env or ~/.config/jev-router/.env and sent as a Bearer header via ureq. It is never put in argv, so it does not show in the process list. It is in the environment of the jev-router process only. Claude Code is spawned with the parent env, so it inherits TYPESAFE_API_KEY from `jev-router claude` if it was exported.

Prompt egress is partly redacted by regex only, which the source calls a 'ponytail' shortcut (src/jev.rs:35-46). It catches key=value pairs, common token prefixes and 40+ character tokens. It will miss many secrets, so it is not a substitute for the user's existing secret-leak guard hook.

It writes full Jev state and answers (prompts, up to 7 turns) to ~/.local/share/claude-router/decisions.jsonl at mode 0600, plus proxy.log and usage.jsonl. That is a persistent local plaintext prompt log, including for client projects.

It modifies ~/.claude/settings.json on exit: restore_saved_model rewrites the 'model' key if it equals 'jev-router' (src/main.rs:27-46). A crash could leave 'jev-router' as the saved default model. It also injects a statusLine via --settings and runs the user's own statusLine command through `sh -c` (src/main.rs:167). That command comes from the user's own settings, so it is not third-party code execution.

No curl|sh installer, no npm postinstall, no telemetry other than Jev and Anthropic calls, and no build.rs. The dashboard is loopback-only with Host and Origin checks. The only shell execution is the user's statusline command. The Anthropic /v1/models lookup reuses the user's auth headers against the same upstream. It has no license, and the release tarball was not inspected or verified.
entries.dataEgress: To Jev (api.typesafe.ai, or OpenRouter if patched) on each user turn: the new user message (clipped to 2000 chars, regex-redacted), up to 7 earlier user and assistant text turns (2000 chars each, no tool output), the repo folder name, and the first up to 800 chars of CLAUDE.md or README.md (redacted). The last is off with JEV_ROUTER_REPO_SUMMARY=off (src/jev.rs:73-125, README 'What goes to api.typesafe.ai'). Internal side requests and 'continue'-style replies skip Jev. No code, diffs or tool output are sent to Jev unless the user pastes them into the prompt. Everything else, including the OAuth or API credentials and the full conversation, flows unchanged through the local proxy to Anthropic as usual. With OpenRouter as the provider, the same prompt text would also pass through OpenRouter and is subject to its logging policy. That matters for client projects.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open. Jev has an 8 s timeout per attempt with 1 retry after 500 ms (408, 429, 5xx and transport errors), so a hung Jev costs up to about 16.5 s on that turn (src/jev.rs:25-26, 155-176). On error, the failure is logged to proxy.log. The turn uses the previous rung if one exists, else Sonnet medium for agent turns (AGENT_FALLBACK = S_MED) or Haiku for tool-less auxiliary calls (src/proxy.rs:28-31, 641-657). Nothing is retried per turn, so each new turn pays the timeout again while Jev stays down. A missing TYPESAFE_API_KEY makes `jev-router claude` start plain claude with no proxy. If the local proxy process dies mid-session, Claude Code gets connection errors because its base URL is dead, so this part fails closed. Upstream transport errors return 502.
entries.contextCost: Zero MCP or skill context: no tools, no server instructions, no hook-injected text. It does inject effort-only role:system messages mid-conversation and moves the cache breakpoint on Opus 5.5. It sets CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS=200000, which caps the context window (a shrink if the user runs a larger-window Opus). It also replaces the status line, wrapped around the user's own.
pros: The only candidate seen that is truly automatic and prompt-free: it sits at the API layer, so no 'use jev' phrasing is ever needed.

Uses Jev's strengths correctly: about 40 typed Choice, Noul and Score questions per turn (request type, depth, breadth, security, failed-fix) turned into a deterministic rule ladder, with logged probabilities and a dashboard for auditing each decision.
Fail-open on Jev errors (8 s timeout, 1 retry, fallback rung), loopback-only bind, log files 0600, and catch_unwind around the rewrite so a bug forwards the request unmodified.

Cache-aware switching, safety floors (security, concurrency and irreversible work get at least Opus) and a manual /model override that passes through. This is careful engineering for the prompt-cache cost problem.
Zero context tokens: no MCP tools, no schemas, no hook text.
Small, readable single-purpose Rust codebase (about 4.6k lines with tests) that is easy to audit. One file, src/jev.rs, holds all Jev I/O, so an OpenRouter patch is a few lines if the schema matches.
Works with a subscription/OAuth login: auth headers are passed through unchanged, and the /v1/models lookup uses the same OAuth beta header.
cons: Does not support OpenRouter. The URL, model id (jev-1.13.0, not typesafe/jev-1.13) and key (TYPESAFE_API_KEY) are hardcoded, and the TypeSafe key is waitlisted. Using OpenRouter means a local fork built with cargo, and OpenRouter's System One schema match is unverified.

No license (licenseInfo null, no LICENSE file), so forking or patching it is legally unclear. It is also 5 days old, with 5 stars, 0 forks, no CI, and no independent review. It shipped 8 releases in 5 days and depends on undocumented Anthropic betas and Claude Code behavior, so it is likely to break on Claude Code updates.

Not really 'inside' Claude Code: the user must always start Claude Code with `jev-router claude` (or an alias), and there is no hook, settings or plugin install. Any plain `claude`, IDE or Desktop launch bypasses it. It also runs as an extra wrapper process for every session.

It downgrades the user's chosen Opus 5.5 to Haiku 4.5 or Sonnet for 'simple' turns, and it overrides the user's model choice, effort setting and /model default. That changes quality and behavior on client work. The 200k CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS cap can also shrink the window. The value is mostly cost saving, which matters little on a flat subscription, so the payoff is uncertain for this user.

Sends recent conversation text and the repo folder name plus CLAUDE.md/README.md intro to a third party on every turn. The only redaction is regex ('ponytail') redaction. That is a real concern for client projects, and it comes on top of the existing secret-guard hook. The prompts are also logged in plaintext to decisions.jsonl.

Sits in the path of the OAuth credentials and all traffic, so a bug or supply-chain compromise of the binary would expose the Anthropic credentials. The prebuilt release binary would need trust, or a source build.

Modifies ~/.claude/settings.json on exit (model key restore) and replaces the status line; it may interact badly with any existing statusLine or with the hooks the user already has. Interaction with the GitNexus and caveman hooks is untested. Sub-agent turns may share one status file.
It exposes no Jev decision to the agent (no tools or hooks), so it cannot serve other uses such as risk scoring or gating tool calls. It is model-routing only.
entries.verdict: The closest thing to hands-free Jev in Claude Code, and the only router found that does model and effort switching silently. It is TypeSafe-only, unlicensed, days old, and does not support OpenRouter without a Rust fork. For a Opus 5.5 subscription user its payoff is mostly cost routing with some quality risk, and it sends prompts to a third party on client work. Treat it as a reference design to patch or reimplement (hooks or a minimal proxy) rather than something to install as-is.
entries.license: None. GitHub reports licenseInfo null and there is no LICENSE file in the tree, so it is all rights reserved by default. Do not fork or redistribute without asking the author. Personal patching is a grey area.

entries.name: moukrea/automodel
entries.what: Go binary (one binary: local proxy on 127.0.0.1:8788, hooks, statusline, ledger/eval). Installer sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to the proxy and adds a selectable model 'Jev (auto)'. For sessions on that model, the UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse[Agent]/PreToolUse[Workflow] hooks ask Jev on OpenRouter (Score over tiers, Noul per mode, warm-turn continue/informs Noul), and the proxy rewrites model and effort in the upstream request to api.anthropic.com (OAuth headers forwarded unchanged). Subagent model alias is rewritten via updatedInput, workflow agent() calls get injected model/effort, and 'ultracode' mode injects an additionalContext that pushes Claude toward Workflow orchestration.
entries.autoInvocation: Fully automatic and deterministic once installed AND the session model is 'Jev (auto)': hooks fire on every prompt/Agent/Workflow without the user asking. It does NOT provide 'Claude uses Jev when it adds value' generally; it only uses Jev for the single question of which Claude model/effort to run. It replaces the user's Opus 5.5 default when jev is selected (could be made default via settings 'model': 'jev'), and does nothing for permissions, risky-command gating or other Jev use cases (no PermissionRequest hook).
security: Key handling: OpenRouter key stored plaintext in ~/.config/automodel/config.toml (0600); 'key set' reads from stdin (no argv exposure); installer reads key with stty -echo and pipes to key set; $OPENROUTER_API_KEY overrides. Key sent only as Bearer to jev_url. Proxy dump mode (AUTOMODEL_DUMP_DIR, off by default) redacts authorization/x-api-key/cookie headers but writes full request bodies to disk (proxy.go:153-165).

Proxy is a full MITM-position component for ALL Claude Code traffic (every session, including ones on plain opus, because ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is global in settings.json env). It sees OAuth bearer tokens and all prompts/code in plaintext over http://127.0.0.1:8788 (no TLS, loopback only by default; any local user/process could also use it as a forwarder to api.anthropic.com, but it holds no credentials itself).

Installer is curl|sh but does verify sha256 from the release checksums.txt; no signature/attestation, so a compromised GitHub release or account (single maintainer, 0 stars, 4 days old) means arbitrary code in the auto-updater path running as the user and sitting in the API path. Auto-update every 6h applies new releases unattended.

Installer modifies ~/.claude/settings.json (env, hooks, statusLine, permissions.allow adds blanket 'Workflow' allow) and adds slash commands; backs up first. It replaces user's statusLine command (chains old one via sh -c).

Hooks return permissionDecision 'allow' for Agent and Workflow PreToolUse (agent.go:94, workflow.go:~120), which bypasses permission prompts for those tools on jev sessions; combined with rewriting workflow scripts (jsscan-based regex injection) this is a script-mutating hook. Low impact for this user (auto/bypass mode) but a trust expansion.

Prompt-injection surface: prompt text, recent prompts, last assistant reply, compaction summary, first ~N chars of CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, diff stat are sent to Jev; injected instructions there can bias the tier choice (worst case: wrong model/effort, or ultracode notice injected). Jev output is typed and validated, so no free-text injection back into Claude; only tier/mode. UltracodeOn additionalContext text is static, but Jev's Noul answer can turn on an instruction to 'Author and run a workflow for every substantive task', which raises token spend.
entries.dataEgress: To Anthropic: unchanged Claude traffic via local proxy (model/effort/max_tokens and effort-only system messages rewritten). To OpenRouter/TypeSafe per decision (privacy='full' default): truncated current prompt, last few prompts, start of last assistant reply, compaction summary after /compact, session size, repo signals (languages, file count, diff stat, head of CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md via repo.go:73). For subagents: truncated Agent prompt; for workflows: agent() call site info. privacy='metadata' (config or per-repo .automodel.toml, which can only tighten) sends only sizes, kind hints, tier and languages. To GitHub: release check every 6h. For client projects, default full mode ships client prompt text and CLAUDE.md excerpts to a third party (OpenRouter -> TypeSafe); metadata mode would be required. Local ledger, per-decision states (2MB/session) and hooks.log stay on disk.
entries.failureMode: Mostly fail-safe for Jev: hooks always exit 0 on error (hooks.go header, Run), Jev timeout 4s (config.go:127, warm 4s) then falls back to default tier with statusline warning; missing/rejected key, credit or rate-limit errors also fall back to the default tier. BUT the architecture adds a hard single point of failure: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points every Claude Code request (all sessions, all models) at http://127.0.0.1:8788, so if the proxy dies Claude Code stops working entirely; mitigation is SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit hooks that redial (300ms) then restart the service once (4s) and otherwise BLOCK the prompt with instructions (guard.go), systemd user unit auto-restart, and 'automodel uninstall'. Mid-turn crash or a proxy bug (SSE tapping, body rewrite) would break in-flight requests. Without a systemd user session the proxy is not restarted after reboot. Because env is global, a crash affects sessions not on jev too.
entries.contextCost: Zero MCP tools and no tool definitions, no skills. Hook-injected text: only when ultracode mode fires (UltracodeOn ~700 chars, ~175 tokens, repeated after each compaction, plus an 'off' notice) and decision notices via additionalContext (decide.go:276). Two slash command files (/why, /flag) add small skill/command listing entries. Effort-only system messages are inserted into the API request by the proxy (cache-safe by design). Statusline segment is not model context. Net context cost is very small.
pros: OpenRouter-native and correct: uses https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions with model typesafe/jev-1.13 and Bearer OPENROUTER_API_KEY (config.go:126, jev.go, catalog.toml:11); uses Score/Noul primitives well, one call per decision asking multiple typed questions with calibrated thresholds, cost-aware policy with confidence gating.

Careful failure handling for Jev itself: 4s timeout, fallback to default tier with visible statusline reason, hooks never fail the user action (hooks.go), proxy health check and auto-restart guard, doctor command, install --dry-run, settings backup, uninstall.

Substantial engineering for a 4-day-old project: ~11.8k LOC non-test Go, 31 test files, eval harness with labeled cases (testdata/eval), flag/report/why for measuring routing quality and savings, spend caps, privacy=metadata mode, per-repo .automodel.toml floors/ceilings, user override pins (/effort, [effort:X], [model:X]).

Keeps subscription/OAuth traffic on Anthropic unchanged; sets _CLAUDE_CODE_ASSUME_FIRST_PARTY_BASE_URL to preserve Opus 1M window; covers subagents and Workflow agent() sites, which is a genuinely automatic integration point not needing 'use jev' prompts.
Zero MCP/tool-definition context cost; MIT licensed; no telemetry claimed; checksum-verified binaries; the router is tunable via catalog (no hardcoded model IDs).
cons: Global ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL proxy is a single point of failure and total-visibility choke point for ALL Claude Code traffic including OAuth tokens and every prompt, for personal and client work; a bug or compromised auto-update (unsigned, same-release checksums, single maintainer, brand new, 0 stars, 113 commits in 4 days, v0.15.2 already) is high blast radius.

Solves a narrow problem for this user: model/effort routing. The user already runs Opus 5.5 by default in auto/bypass mode; value depends on unproven routing quality vs always-Opus and on savings; switching to 'jev' model replaces default and Haiku/Sonnet downgrades risk worse output. It does not address permission gating, risky-command review, or general 'Jev when it adds value' decisions.

Default privacy=full sends prompt text, recent prompts, last assistant reply, compaction summary and CLAUDE.md head to OpenRouter/TypeSafe on every decision; unacceptable for client projects unless privacy='metadata' is forced globally (reducing accuracy).

Auto-injects permissionDecision 'allow' on Agent and Workflow PreToolUse and adds blanket permissions.allow 'Workflow', rewrites workflow scripts by regex (jsscan.go), and its ultracode mode instructs Claude to run Workflows for every substantive task, which can inflate spend; stacks with user's existing hooks (gitnexus, no-secret-leak) in unknown ways and replaces the statusLine.

Adds latency to every UserPromptSubmit (up to 4s Jev + Go startup) and Jev calls per subagent/workflow site; /alpha endpoint has no SLA and Jev has known overconfidence and injection sensitivity; installer is curl|sh with self-updater running unattended; key stored plaintext in config.toml (0600) outside of no-secret-leak protections.
Windows/other paths irrelevant; without systemd user session no restart after reboot. Not runnable/verified here (static audit only), so quality claims (98% cache hit, accuracy) are author-reported.
entries.verdict: Well-engineered, OpenRouter-native Jev router for model/effort selection that genuinely runs automatically via hooks and a local proxy, but it is a brand-new single-maintainer tool that puts a global unsigned-auto-updating proxy in front of all Claude traffic (including client work) and sends prompt text to OpenRouter by default, for a narrow benefit the user (already on Opus 5.5) may not need. Worth trying only in an isolated setup with privacy=metadata, pinned version and auto-update off; not recommended as the primary Jev integration.

judge.why: The most thoroughly engineered proxy and the only one on the exact /alpha/decisions endpoint, but it has the largest blast radius. It does not fit a cautious setup.
pros: Native OpenRouter alpha/decisions; per-decision Score and Noul with a cost-aware policy and eval harness
Metadata privacy mode; 4 s Jev timeout with fallback; settings backup and uninstall
Covers subagents and Workflow agent() sites automatically
cons: Global proxy for ALL sessions (crash means Claude Code stops); unsigned auto-updater every 6 h from a 0-star, 4-day-old repo
curl|sh installer rewrites settings.json, replaces statusLine, adds blanket permissions.allow Workflow, and hooks return permissionDecision allow
Default privacy=full sends prompts and CLAUDE.md excerpts to a third party; unacceptable for client work without metadata mode
Ultracode mode can inflate spend by pushing Workflow use

entries.name: xinyao27/jevonian
entries.what: Local Node/Hono proxy (127.0.0.1:8787) that speaks Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Chat and Responses. Claude Code is pointed at it via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. For the virtual model jevonian/auto it makes one Jev call per routed turn (choice questions: which routing tier plan/execute/utility/chat, and thinking effort) using a compact session-state snapshot, then forwards the turn to whichever configured provider/model wins. It also records a local ledger and dashboard, tracks quota, keeps session affinity for cache reuse, and offers an optional RTK-based tool-result compressor. Jev is the routing brain, not a coding assistant.
entries.autoInvocation: Transparent proxy. Once ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points at it and model is jevonian/auto, Jev is consulted automatically on every turn with no prompting by the user or model. Genuinely satisfies the no-prompt requirement, but the thing Jev decides is model/effort selection, not code decisions.
security: Sits on the critical path of ALL Claude Code traffic (every prompt, file content, tool result passes through a v0.x 11-day-old AGPL proxy); the trust surface is the whole session, not just a routing side call

Reads Claude Pro/Max OAuth token from ~/.claude/.credentials.json, refreshes it at console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token and writes rotated tokens back (src/oauth.ts:427-433, README provider table). README itself warns subscription use via third-party clients is outside vendor terms and can break; real ToS/account-risk for a subscription login
Also reads ~/.codex/auth.json, Antigravity and Devin credentials if those providers are enabled

Stores provider and brain keys in ~/.config/jevonian/credentials.json (0600); Jevonian API keys hashed (sk-jev-...); `jevonian add openrouter --key sk-or-...` puts the key in argv (visible in ps), dashboard paste avoids this
Auth: loopback-only sentinel token jevonian-local accepted from loopback peers (src/server.ts ~249); with no Jevonian key created the proxy is open on localhost; any local process can use it
Stores full request bodies (prompts, code, tool results) in ~/.local/share/jevonian/bodies/ (0600, newest 1000) unless JEVONIAN_CAPTURE_BODIES=0; a client-project secret-leak concern
entries.dataEgress: To the OpenRouter Jev brain on every auto turn: compact state with last user message, last assistant message, session goal, last few messages, recent tool calls AND tool results, candidate list, token counts; with fullPrompt:true a verbatim transcript of all messages including system prompt (up to 400k chars). Separately the full request (entire conversation, code, tool outputs) goes to whichever provider actually serves the turn (Anthropic via OAuth, OpenRouter, etc.). Full bodies are also written to local disk. Nothing else (no telemetry) found in source. Sending code from client projects to a beta OpenRouter alpha endpoint is a confidentiality decision.
entries.failureMode: Brain timeout default 8000 ms (src/config.ts:433) with retries (also retries 429/5xx, brain.ts:469-495). If all brains fail after retry budget, routing.ts:1753-1776 falls back to heuristic classifyPhase routing (fail-open on the brain), although docs/brain.md and docs/routing.md still claim 502 error, so docs are stale/contradictory. If the proxy process itself is down (non-macOS runs only in foreground, no service manager on Linux), Claude Code gets connection refused because ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is pinned in settings.json (fail-closed for the whole agent). Upstream provider failures are retried and rerouted around (quota failover, refusals).
entries.contextCost: Zero MCP tools, zero hooks, zero added context tokens in Claude Code itself; it is a transport-level proxy. Side effects: model picker entries renamed (Jevonian Auto), and if tokenSaver/promptPolicy are on the prompt content is rewritten on the wire. Cost is instead in the brain call tokens (compact state per turn at ~$0.042/M input, cheap).
pros: Only candidate found so far that is truly automatic with zero prompting: Jev is invoked in code on every turn via proxy (routing.md line 3, 'one brain call per routed turn'); Claude never has to decide to call it

OpenRouter is a first-class Jev channel with the right endpoint and model id (brain.ts:61-66, /api/alpha/decisions, typesafe/jev-1.13) and reads OPENROUTER_API_KEY; multi-channel failover (TypeSafe direct, Zen, Vercel, Cloudflare, local Kev) is built in

Real Claude Code integration code: jevonian launch claude is a non-persistent, per-session env launch that changes nothing on disk (claude-code.ts:333), and Restore reverts the persistent settings write
Fail-open on brain outage in code (heuristic fallback, routing.ts:1753+) and explicit jevonian/<tier> aliases and x-jevonian-phase bypass Jev entirely
Good observability: response headers x-jevonian-model/reason/brain, local ledger with cost per turn
Careful engineering signals: 60 test files, smoke script, keys hashed, 0600 file modes, loopback binding, no postinstall, no telemetry SDK found, brain prompt treats text as evidence
Very active (70 commits in 11 days, release v0.3.3 yesterday) and cache-aware (switch penalty in state)
cons: It is a model router, not a coding-quality decision tool: it would replace or split your Opus 5.5 main model across other models per turn, changing answer quality on client work in ways you do not control

Puts a v0.x, 11-day-old, 16-star AGPL proxy on the critical path of every prompt, tool result and file read, including client projects; a bug or outage takes Claude Code down (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL pinned globally in settings.json, no service manager on Linux, foreground only)

Your subscription/OAuth login is a poor fit: to keep Opus on the subscription it must read ~/.claude/.credentials.json and replay the OAuth token as a third-party client, which the README itself calls outside vendor terms and breakable; setting ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and blanking ANTHROPIC_API_KEY also displaces the native login

Adds a Jev round trip (8 s timeout, retries) to each turn and sends recent messages plus tool results to OpenRouter's alpha Decisions endpoint; fullPrompt mode sends everything; bodies also persisted to disk
Docs contradict code on failure behaviour (docs say 502, code falls back to heuristics), a sign the docs and code are moving fast

Overwrites the user's persistent global settings.json env, overlapping badly with existing setup (custom model mapping of opus/sonnet/haiku/subagent to jevonian/auto, attribution header off, error reporting off)

Potential breakage of Claude Code features tied to first-party API (beta headers, prompt caching semantics, fast mode) is untested for this user; compatibility claims are limited to protocol shape ('compatibility of a specific client's extras is not implied')

Needs ongoing multi-provider config (Anthropic, OpenRouter models) to be worth routing, otherwise Jev has a single candidate and adds only latency; the 'DeepSeek flash router' skepticism is moot here since Jev only picks among your candidates
entries.verdict: The only fully automatic, hook-free Jev integration in this batch and it does support OpenRouter, but what Jev decides is which model/effort serves a turn, which for a single-model Opus 5.5 subscription user adds latency, risk and OAuth-replay ToS exposure for little gain. Use only as an experiment via 'jevonian launch claude' in a throwaway session with an OpenRouter key and multiple cheap models, not as a global daily-driver setting.

Jev only as optional judge, ~$0.00025 per 6k-token call; proxy speaks /v1/messages so ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL works
cons: Claude Code hooks only do session/task control, not per-turn model switching; real routing needs ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL proxy, which the OAuth user avoids
