entries.name: adarshmishra07/jcm-router
entries.what: Bun/TypeScript local HTTP proxy on localhost:8787. Claude Code is pointed at it via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. For each new user turn on /v1/messages (requests with tools), it sends Jev the user message (max 6000 chars) and the previous assistant reply (max 2000 chars). Three questions: model (choice: fable/opus/sonnet/haiku), effort (choice: low..max) and is_followup (noul). It then rewrites the model and output_config.effort in the request and forwards it to api.anthropic.com with the original OAuth headers. A cost guard always routes subagents, but only switches the main chat when the prompt-cache re-write is cheap (under 100K context and under $0.25 extra). The default ROUTER_UPGRADES=off means it can only downgrade. It includes a supervisor with passthrough fallback, a dashboard, a statusline script, an eval harness and a tuner.
interface: bun run dashboard / report / tune / eval
entries.autoInvocation: Transparent proxy (fully automatic, no prompting needed). It sits in the request path once ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is set, and every new turn and every subagent is classified automatically. Overrides via !opus etc. are optional.
security: No third-party runtime dependencies, no postinstall script, no curl|sh installer, no telemetry. The only network calls are to Anthropic and TypeSafe.

Jev API key is read from env and sent as a Bearer header in fetch (not in argv). The key is never logged, and /healthz exposes only a jev_key boolean (src/env.ts:96-97). If it is placed in .env, it is stored on disk in plaintext.

The proxy forwards Claude Code's Authorization / OAuth headers to ANTHROPIC_UPSTREAM (src/proxy.ts:92-100). The upstream is env-configurable, so a poisoned env would exfiltrate the subscription token. It listens on localhost:8787 with no auth, so any local process or browser page that can reach it can use it as an authenticated Anthropic relay (but cannot read the token).

Bun.serve({port}) without an explicit hostname binds all interfaces by default, so the unauthenticated relay may be reachable from the LAN (src/server.ts:150-152). This is not verified at runtime, but it is a real concern on a shared network.
scripts/env-on.sh edits ~/.claude/settings.json with jq (backup made first, atomic mv). It is a global change that affects every Claude Code session, including client projects.

Prompt-injection surface: Jev sees the user message and the previous assistant reply, which can contain tool-derived text. Jev only returns typed choices and probabilities, gated by confidence thresholds, and the model alias must be in the allowlist, so the damage is limited to a wrong model or effort pick. The default upgrade-off means it cannot escalate spend.
entries.dataEgress: To TypeSafe (or OpenRouter after a patch), once per new user turn: latest_user_message (first 6000 chars of the prompt) and previous_assistant_reply (first 2000 chars), plus the previous routing, alongside the policy questions (src/routing-policy.ts:166-186, src/server.ts:63-71). This does not include diffs, file contents or tool outputs, unless the user pastes them into the prompt or the assistant's previous reply quotes them. To Anthropic: the full original request, unchanged except for model/effort. Locally: 300-char prompt previews in ~/.claude-router. Not sent for continuations (tool loops), for turns skipped by the context gate, or when both model and effort are overridden with !flags. Client code snippets in prompts would go to a third party (TypeSafe/OpenRouter), which matters for client work.
entries.failureMode: Jev side is fail-open: askJev never throws, has a 2.5 s timeout (src/jev.ts:4,57), and any HTTP error, bad shape or timeout forwards the request unchanged. Rewrites rejected by Anthropic with a 4xx (except 401/403/429) are retried once with the original request. Proxy side is fail-closed by design: with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL pointing at localhost and nothing listening (supervisor killed, reboot, sleep, port conflict), Claude Code cannot reach the API at all. A supervisor respawns the router and after 3 crashes in 60 s degrades to plain passthrough. Recovery from a hard kill is manual (env-off.sh plus restart). The proxy is a new single point of failure for the entire Claude Code session. It streams the response body, so streaming works.
entries.contextCost: Zero tokens in Claude Code's context: it is a transparent proxy with no MCP tools, no skill and no hooks. The optional statusline command adds no model context. Cost side effects: changing the model or effort mid-conversation invalidates the prompt cache (documented $19.53 loss on 309 requests), which the guard mitigates by mostly refusing main-chat switches.
pros: Truly automatic and zero-prompt: a transparent proxy needs no CLAUDE.md, skill or tool-call cooperation from the model, which is exactly the 'Claude Code must use it when needed' requirement (src/server.ts:79-148).
Works with the subscription OAuth login: it forwards Claude Code's own headers, and the README explicitly says ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not needed (README Install/Environment).
Zero context tokens: no MCP tool defs, no hook-injected text. It does not interact with the existing PreToolUse secret-guard, GitNexus or caveman hooks.

Honest, evidence-driven design: it documents a measured $19.53 loss from routing the main chat, then adds a cache-aware cost guard (src/cost.ts, routing-policy.ts:150), subagents-only scope (ROUTER_SCOPE=subagents), upgrades off by default, and confidence gates (0.7). It is the only candidate that uses Jev's calibrated probabilities as designed (Choice/Noul with confidence thresholds).

Robust operational design: Jev calls are fail-open with a 2.5 s timeout, 4xx rewrite rejections retry with the original request, and the supervisor falls back to passthrough. Plus /healthz, ROUTER_DRY_RUN for observing without acting, a dashboard and a tuner.
Small, readable codebase (~1.5k lines of src), MIT, no runtime dependencies, no postinstall or telemetry; a decent test suite with a fake-upstream integration test and CI.
Configurable endpoint (TYPESAFE_API_URL) with the same /v1/systemone path as OpenRouter's System One API, so the OpenRouter patch is about 3 lines.
cons: No OpenRouter support today: it hard-requires TYPESAFE_API_KEY with an 'apikey_' prefix (src/env.ts:57-59) and sends model 'jev-latest' (src/jev.ts:56). It needs a local patch or fork (prefix check, model id 'typesafe/jev-latest'), and the OpenRouter response schema is unverified.

Its value proposition (saving cost by downgrading to Haiku/Sonnet) is weak for this user: a single long Opus session in the main chat, where its own README says 'Probably not' and the guard refuses most switches, so it adds Jev latency to every turn for mostly no-ops. It only pays for subagent-heavy fan-out.

Routes between Claude models, which is a different problem from making Claude Code decisions better. Downgrading the main model away from Opus 5.5 risks quality on client work, and the hardcoded model IDs (claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-fable-5-1, src/routing-policy.ts:9-33) may not match the user's Opus 5.5 setup, causing 4xx rewrite rejections and fallbacks.

Single point of failure for the whole Claude Code session: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to localhost fails closed on reboot, sleep or supervisor kill. It requires Bun (not in the user's stack) and a process kept alive (no systemd unit; only a macOS launchd plist is documented, and the README targets macOS: brew, launchd). On Linux you write the systemd unit yourself.

Global change affecting every session, including client projects: scripts/env-on.sh mutates ~/.claude/settings.json, and the proxy sees all Anthropic traffic and OAuth headers. The unauthenticated relay on localhost:8787 may bind to all interfaces (Bun.serve default). Client prompt text goes to a third party (TypeSafe/OpenRouter), and 300-char prompt previews are written to ~/.claude-router by default.

Very immature: created 2026-09-17, 32 commits all on one day by a single author, 9 stars, no releases, and not battle-tested. The README claims (savings, 41-case eval) are self-reported. New-turn detection is tied to Claude Code 2.1.x request shapes and may break on 2.1.285.
Adds 0.3-1 s of blocking Jev latency to every new turn and every subagent, which is directly felt in daily interactive use.
entries.verdict: Well-engineered but narrow: a transparent auto-invoking Jev proxy that routes Claude model and effort. It only really helps subagent-heavy cost saving, which fits poorly with a subscription plus Opus 5.5 main-chat workflow, and it needs a small patch for OpenRouter (prefix check and model id). Worth considering only as an opt-in, subagents-scope, dry-run experiment, and not as the primary Jev integration, because of the fail-closed proxy risk and the client-prompt egress.

entries.name: Yaxin9Luo/spending-effort-with-jev
entries.what: UserPromptSubmit plugin: Jev rates the effort each prompt needs and prints a one-line /effort verdict; optional ask_first makes Claude ask before switching. Suggests only, never switches.
entries.autoInvocation: deterministic hook (advisory)
pros: Has a labelled eval (160 prompts, 3 annotators, kappa 0.82) and a bench harness
Skips trivial prompts locally without calling Jev, low cost
Never changes settings, so safe failure mode
cons: TypeSafe key only; README has no OpenRouter mention, so OPENROUTER_API_KEY would need patching
Advisory only: user must manually run /effort, limited value with Opus 5.5 as fixed main model
Plugin key config stored via /plugin, not env

entries.name: stas4000/claude-subagent-router
entries.what: A PreToolUse hook on the Agent tool (router/hook.py). For builder briefs, router/pick.py sends the description plus the first 1000 chars of the brief and long routing instructions to a Jev System One Choice question (3 options: s55-builder, s55-builder-deep, o55-builder-precise). It takes the top probability and rewrites updatedInput.subagent_type. If the key is unset or the call fails, a regex keyword picker answers instead. router/guard.py denies any Sonnet agent whose file lacks a valid effort, or that has effort max. The hook also forces run_in_background to false and logs each pick to .router/picks.jsonl. It ships 6 agent files, a verifier_guard hook and a report script. It is a sub-agent model router, not a permission or general decision helper.
interface: Agents s55-builder, s55-builder-deep, o55-builder-precise, s55-verifier, o55-reviewer, s55-scout (.claude/agents)
entries.autoInvocation: Truly deterministic for the events it hooks: a PreToolUse hook on the Agent tool with no model discretion. But it only fires on Agent calls that name its s55-/o55- builder agents. The user has none of these, so they would have to adopt the agent set and add CLAUDE.md instructions telling the lead to use them. It does not cover Bash permissions, planning, commit checks or anything else.
security: Key handling is good. It travels only in an Authorization header (never argv), only to an https URL, and redirects are blocked (pick.py:115-120). Errors redact the key (pick.py:281-283).
No subprocess, eval or exec anywhere in router/. The only file I/O is reading /proc, reading agent files and appending the ledger with mode 0600.
No telemetry beyond the Jev call. The default host is api.typesafe.ai, and JEV_URL can be any https host, so a poisoned environment could redirect the key.

Prompt-injection surface: the brief text (up to 1000 chars) goes into Jev state, and Jev is known to be steerable by injected state. The worst outcome is a downgrade of a builder from Opus to Sonnet. The guard still enforces Sonnet effort, and the tool permissions of the picked agent still apply.

Hook 'allow' decisions carry updatedInput, and a PreToolUse allow can bypass the normal permission prompt for that Agent call. This is low impact for Agent, but it is a behaviour change to be aware of.

The guard is not scoped to this repo's agents. Any Agent call with a model override containing 'sonnet' and no matching agent file is DENIED (guard.py:73-78). That can break built-in agents such as Explore or general-purpose that the user runs with model:sonnet.
entries.dataEgress: Per builder-agent call only: the Agent call's description (200 chars) and the brief text with whitespace collapsed, truncated to 1000 chars, plus a fixed routing-instructions text (~2.5k chars). All of it goes to the Jev endpoint (api.typesafe.ai by default, or whichever JEV_URL points to). The bearer key is sent only to that URL. Briefs written by the lead can quote client code, paths or business details, so client projects need review. Non-builder Agent calls send nothing. Nothing else leaves the machine, and without JEV_API_KEY nothing leaves at all.
entries.failureMode: Fail-safe. Any Jev error, timeout (12 s cap enforced by a daemon thread, with a 30 s hook timeout) or unparseable answer falls back to the regex picker, and if that fails the lead's pick stands. Malformed stdin or an exception exits 0 with no output. The one deliberate fail-closed path is the guard: a Sonnet agent without a valid effort, or a Sonnet model override without an agent file, is denied. Worst-case added latency is about 12 s per builder Agent call when Jev hangs. The docs claim a 0.44 s median.
entries.contextCost: Zero MCP tools and no injected hook text. The cost is in the six agents, which add roughly 3k chars of description each to the Task/Agent tool listing (about 2-3k tokens in total). The README's suggested CLAUDE.md paragraph is small. The rewritten subagent choice is invisible to the model apart from the permissionDecisionReason string.
pros: Well-engineered hook: stdlib only, no subprocess/eval, key never in argv, redirects blocked, errors redact the key (pick.py:115-120, 281-283).
Real automatic invocation through a PreToolUse Agent hook, with two fallbacks (regex picker, then the lead's pick) and a 12 s deadline that runs on a daemon thread.

Uses Jev the right way: one Choice question with probabilities and no free text. The system-one request shape (model/state/questions) is close to what OpenRouter's /api/v1/systemone should accept, so JEV_URL/JEV_MODEL/JEV_API_KEY can point it at OpenRouter without code edits.
83 test functions, a pick ledger with cost accounting and a report CLI. MIT license. The author reports live data (92 picks, 0.44 s median, about $0.00004 a pick).
Model ids (claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-opus-5-5) and the effort frontmatter match the user's Claude Code version.
cons: Narrow value for this user. It only routes between Sonnet and Opus builder sub-agents, and the user runs Opus 5.5 main on a subscription, where cost savings matter less. Routing quality is only 0.71 on the author's private held-out briefs, and the routing prompt encodes the author's own domain rules (messaging engines, voice/earpiece, a 'brain') that will not fit this user's projects.

Requires adopting its own six agents plus CLAUDE.md wording. Nothing fires unless the lead uses the s55-/o55- builder names, and the regex fallback and the INSTRUCTIONS are tuned to the author's projects.

Intrusive side effects: it forces every background Agent call to the foreground (unless ROUTER_FOREGROUND=0). It also denies any Agent call with a 'sonnet' model override and no agent file, which could break built-in agents.

Not OpenRouter-native: it needs JEV_API_KEY, the default host is api.typesafe.ai and the default model 'jev-latest' is unverified on OpenRouter. It targets neither /alpha/decisions nor OPENROUTER_API_KEY, and the user would need to duplicate the key into the hook's environment and extend no-secret-leak.
Ships briefs (first 1000 chars) to a third party, a data egress risk for client projects, and writes a .router/ ledger into each project.
Brand new: 4 commits, 1 contributor, 7 stars, created on 2026-09-29, no release or plugin/marketplace packaging (manual copy and manual settings merge).
entries.verdict: The code is clean and safe-failing, and it is one of the few real automatic Jev hooks. It solves a narrow problem (Sonnet vs Opus builder routing), needs a wholesale adoption of its agents and conventions, and has intrusive side effects (forced foreground, Sonnet-override denials). It is switchable to OpenRouter only by env overrides. Treat it as a reference implementation of the pattern (a PreToolUse Agent hook with a Jev Choice question, an offline fallback and a deadline), not something to install as-is.

entries.name: WXK-AI/jev-opus
entries.what: Node/TypeScript CLI (npm jev-opus, v0.4.8) that wraps Claude Code. `jev-opus claude` starts a local 127.0.0.1 gateway, sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to it (plus a token header), adds a "Opus 5.5 · Jev" entry to /model and launches the normal interactive claude with --model jev/claude-opus-5-5. For each /v1/messages request on that model the gateway calls Jev (Choice/Noul/Score questions) and inserts a per-message effort statement (low..high by default) into the transcript, replayed byte-identically from a journal to keep the prompt cache valid. Also offers a headless driver mode (Agent SDK) and a 2-skill plugin (/jev-opus:jev, /jev-opus:jev-route) that shell out to `npx -y jev-opus@latest`. It only controls Opus reasoning effort; Jev is not used for any other coding decision (no routing of files, tools, commits, review).
entries.autoInvocation: Transparent proxy (gateway on ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL) active automatically on every request once `jev-opus claude` is launched and the 'Opus 5.5 · Jev' model is selected (launcher selects it by default via --model). Not a hook in the user's existing session: it requires launching Claude Code through `jev-opus claude` (alias `claude`), and other models pass through untouched. The plugin skills are description-triggered only on explicit 'with jev' wording and run a separate process, so they do not meet the no-prompting requirement.
security: API keys: read from ~/.config/jev-opus/.env (init writes it) or env; sent only in Authorization header of fetch, never argv. childEnv() strips OPENROUTER/JEV/TYPESAFE keys and ANTHROPIC_/CLAUDE*/MCP_/OTEL_ vars from the spawned claude process (src/claude/env.ts:14-40); ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=false in driver mode only.

Gateway sits on the Claude auth path: binds 127.0.0.1 ephemeral port, requires random x-jev-gateway-token header (ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS, visible in child env), forwards all requests including the user's OAuth/API-key Authorization headers to api.anthropic.com with redirect:'manual'. Any bug or compromise of a 0.x single-author package therefore sees every prompt, all code and tool results in plaintext locally.

Plugin skills execute `npx -y jev-opus@latest` at runtime: unpinned, auto-updating remote code execution from npm on every use; the /jev skill runs it with --permission-mode auto in a separate agent process. Supply-chain risk on a 1-week-old, 5-star, single-maintainer package.
Skill arguments passed through a quoted heredoc (JEV_TASK) so shell injection from the task text is avoided; but skill text is model-triggered by description phrases.

No postinstall script (package.json scripts: only start/build/test/typecheck/validate:plugin/prepack). No curl|sh installer. No telemetry endpoints found: only URLs are openrouter.ai/api.typesafe.ai/api.anthropic.com. Journal (~/.config/jev-opus/journal) 0600, hashes only.

Prompt-injection surface: tool output flows into local reducer and (only if JEV_OPUS_EVALUATOR_CONTENT=full) into Jev state; questions.ts explicitly warns Jev not to follow tool text. Worst case is a wrong effort level, not tool execution; Jev output is schema-validated.
entries.dataEgress: To Jev (OpenRouter /api/alpha/decisions, pinned to typesafe provider, or api.typesafe.ai): by DEFAULT only a synthetic summary: task type, difficulty score, stakes, keyword cues, prompt length, tool NAME whitelist, success/failure flags, step number, effort in force; 'No request text is included' (src/router/router.ts:55-95). With JEV_OPUS_EVALUATOR_CONTENT=full it sends up to 3000 chars of the user prompt, 800 chars conversation note, agent's notes, tool call summaries (200 chars) and tool result excerpts (400 chars each, could contain code/secrets). To Anthropic: the entire normal Claude traffic passes through the local gateway to api.anthropic.com unchanged except inserted effort statements. Nothing else leaves the machine; the local journal/gateway.log/traces hold hashes/decisions, not prompt text.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open for Jev: client.ask never throws; 2.5 s overall deadline (JEV_DEADLINE_MS), 0 retries by default, circuit breaker opens after 3 consecutive failures for 30 s, then falls back to local heuristics/reducer. Jev is only consulted at task start and on failure / proposed downgrade / unclear steps, otherwise decided locally. Fail-CLOSED for the gateway itself: if the local gateway crashes, Claude Code loses its ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL target and all requests fail; if journal write or journal recovery fails, the request is NOT forwarded and an error is returned (README lines on prepared-decision flush and corrupt-journal replay). The gateway is a single point of failure for the whole session.
entries.contextCost: Effectively zero tools: no MCP server, so 0 tools and no server instructions. Plugin adds 2 skills (descriptions ~330 + ~290 chars, about 150-200 tokens in the skill listing). Gateway inserts a short per-message effort statement at governed turns (small, persistent in transcript). Optional JEV_OPUS_NARRATION appends a system-prompt line and extra output tokens (off by default). Status line and badges are display-only, not in model context.
pros: Genuinely automatic and prompt-free: once started via `jev-opus claude`, Jev picks effort at task start and after failing/passing checks with no user instruction, which matches the 'Claude Code must use it when needed' requirement for the one thing it does.

OpenRouter supported in code (src/config.ts:105-113): set OPENROUTER_API_KEY only, defaults to typesafe/jev-1.13 with provider pinned to typesafe and allow_fallbacks:false; uses the /api/alpha/decisions Decisions API with Choice/Noul/Score primitives correctly.
Works with the user's subscription/OAuth login (gateway forwards client auth; README says tested with claude.ai subscription) and targets Opus 5.5 on Claude Code >= 2.1.280 (user has 2.1.285).

Privacy-conscious defaults: Jev only sees a synthetic summary with no prompt text, commands or tool output unless JEV_OPUS_EVALUATOR_CONTENT=full; API keys stripped from child env; journal is hashes only, 0600 files.
Fail-open Jev with 2.5 s deadline, circuit breaker and selective querying (routine steps decided locally), so Jev slowness cannot stall work; cost trivial at $0.042/1M input and output free.

Serious engineering for a young repo: 15 test files, CI on Node 22/24, single small dependency, no postinstall, audit command with per-decision evidence, cache-preserving design verified live per README.
cons: Scope is narrow: Jev only chooses Opus reasoning effort (low..high). It does not use Jev for other coding decisions (which files, whether to run tests, review risk, commit/PR gating, permission classification), so it only partially answers 'integrate Jev into Claude Code'.

Invasive architecture: all Claude traffic (prompts, code, OAuth headers) flows through a third-party local proxy, and the gateway is fail-closed (dead gateway or journal error = Claude Code cannot make requests). Risky for client projects and heavy compared with a hook or MCP.

Not truly transparent to the user's normal `claude`: must be launched as `jev-opus claude` (alias needed) and the 'Opus 5.5 · Jev' model kept selected; the plugin cannot change the current session's effort (README states this) and its skills spawn a separate `npx -y jev-opus@latest` agent with --permission-mode auto, only when the user says 'with jev' - fails the no-prompting requirement and adds unpinned npm remote-code execution.

Depends on unpublicized Opus 5.5 per-message effort statements and Claude Code custom model env vars; tightly coupled to Claude Code internals (MessageDisplay hooks, ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION) and could break on Claude Code updates. Injects its own statusLine/hooks via --settings, colliding with the user's existing PreToolUse guard/GitNexus/caveman setup potential conflicts (hooks appended, statusLine overridden).

Very immature and single-maintainer: repo created 2026-09-23 (7 days old), 45 commits, 1 contributor, 5 stars, 0 forks, 8 releases in a week (0.4.8 today), so API/behavior churn likely. README admits the effort policy is unproven vs fixed medium/high on cost and quality. Value is mostly cost/latency tuning, not quality gain; the user runs Opus 5.5 on a subscription where per-token savings are not directly visible.
Overlaps with Claude Code's own effort/adaptive thinking; cap default max effort is 'high' so xhigh/max never used unless configured; effort badges and hook notices add UI noise.
entries.verdict: The only candidate here that is truly automatic and OpenRouter-ready, but it does one narrow thing (Jev picks Opus effort) by inserting a fail-closed local proxy in front of all Claude traffic from a week-old single-author package. Worth trying on personal projects via `jev-opus claude`, not something to make the default for client work, and it does not replace a broader Jev decision-hook integration.

entries.name: BeLazy167/typesafe-mod
entries.what: Claude Code plugin using the early-access "function hooks" feature (TypeScript module running inside the agent loop, not a shell hook). Two routers calling Jev via POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone. (1) Decision router on tool.call for AskUserQuestion (on by default): sends the agent's this-or-that question and its options to Jev, then shows per-option probabilities as a transcript line and a panel over the dialog, and can auto-answer via deny when TYPESAFE_AUTO_ANSWER=1 and confidence >= 0.75. (2) Skill router on prompt.submit (opt-in, TYPESAFE_SKILL_ROUTER=1): ranks all installed SKILL.md descriptions against the user prompt (Choice plus a Noul "needs a procedure") and injects one advisory context line naming the winning skill if confidence >= 0.6. Fails open everywhere.
entries.autoInvocation: Deterministic hooks, no model discretion and no user prompting needed: the Claude Code harness fires prompt.submit and tool.call(AskUserQuestion) function hooks automatically once the plugin is installed, CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 is set and a key is present. The skill router still needs TYPESAFE_SKILL_ROUTER=1 to be on. Jev's output is advisory only by default.
security: API key read via $.env.get from Claude Code's env and sent as a Bearer header via $.http.fetch inside the engine; never placed in argv or a subprocess command line (the only subprocess is the fixed find/sed scan, register.ts:50, suggest.ts:51-58)
Only shell execution is a static hard-coded sh -c find/sed command; no user or model input interpolated into it
No install scripts, no npm deps, no postinstall, no curl|sh; plugin is pure TS loaded by Claude Code (hooks.json -> ./register.ts). No telemetry beyond calls to TypeSafe

Prompt-injection surface: skill router injects only a skill name chosen from the local roster (advisory line); the decision router only accepts an answer that is one of the offered options (README 'checks that the answer is one of the options'). SKILL.md descriptions are sent to Jev as criteria, so a malicious skill description could skew ranking but not inject free text back
Auto-answer mode uses deny so the agent sees an error string; that text is built locally by decisionNote, not from Jev free text (Jev returns none)

Author is one small maintainer (BeLazy167) with a collaborator merging PRs; unaudited third-party code that runs in-process with hook privileges inside Claude Code and can run processes ($.process.run) and read env; pin a commit and review before enabling
entries.dataEgress: Decision router (default): question text, option labels/descriptions for every AskUserQuestion dialog, and the working directory path, sent to api.typesafe.ai (README/register.ts:150-155). Roughly 374 input tokens. Skill router (opt-in): the full raw user prompt text on every submit (register.ts:96, buildRequest state.user_request) plus the names and first 80 chars of description of every locally installed skill/plugin SKILL.md. No code, diffs, file contents or tool outputs leave. For a client-project user, prompts and cwd paths (client names in paths) go to a third party, TypeSafe (or OpenRouter after patching), when the skill router is on.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open on every path: missing key, HTTP error, JSON parse failure, throw, or timeout all fall through to next(e) (register.ts:82, :141, :101-114, :194-199). Each call races $.clock.sleep(4000) (budgetMs 4000 in suggest.ts:43) because the engine has an uncatchable 10 s dispatch budget. So worst case per affected event is a 4 s stall, then continue. Below-threshold confidence also falls through to asking the user. Auto-answer edge: only a lone confident question is answered.
entries.contextCost: Zero MCP tools and no tool definitions. No server instructions. Default mode injects nothing into model context (advisory output goes to the transcript UI/log only). With skill router on, one short advisory line is appended per confident prompt (a few dozen tokens); the skill list itself is unchanged so prefix caching is preserved (README). Auto-answer adds a short deny note as a tool error. Negligible context footprint overall.
pros: Genuinely automatic: registered as in-process function hooks, so Jev is invoked with no 'use jev' prompt, which matches the user's core requirement

Correct conceptual use of Jev's typed decisions (Choice + Noul with calibrated probabilities) rather than free-text; sensible confidence floors (0.6 skill, 0.75 auto-answer) and a check that the answer is one of the offered options
Zero context cost: no MCP tools, no schema tokens, no server instructions; advisory output goes to the UI, prefix cache preserved
Fail-open everywhere with a self-imposed 4 s race under the engine's 10 s budget; cannot wedge a turn

No dependencies, no install scripts, no argv secrets; static ~590-line pure-function core with about 7 test files (batch, edge, render, scan, suggest, switches) and CI running 'claude plugin validate' and 'claude plugin test'

MIT license, tiny surface (3 source files) so a fork pointed at OpenRouter is a few-line patch; installed Claude Code 2.1.285 binary contains the CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS gate, so the mechanism exists on the user's version (string found in the binary)
Complements, rather than conflicts with, existing Bash/Grep PreToolUse hooks: different events (prompt.submit, AskUserQuestion), so no interaction with the secret guard or GitNexus hooks
cons: No OpenRouter support: endpoint, model id and key env var are hardcoded to api.typesafe.ai and TYPESAFE_API_KEY (suggest.ts:27-28, register.ts:81,140); needs a fork or local patch, and OpenRouter's response envelope is unverified

Relies on early-access function hooks (env flag CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1), an unstable API that can change or break with any Claude Code update; the README itself notes loader restrictions on '$'

Low value for this user's daily flow: the default-on decision router only fires on AskUserQuestion, which is rare, and in bypass/auto permission mode is often not asked at all; the skill router (the only frequent path) is off by default and adds 166-420 ms to every prompt for a one-line hint the model mostly gets from skill descriptions already
Does not touch the high-value decisions in coding (permission/safety classification of Bash commands, plan-vs-act, which file to edit, commit-worthy?), so Jev is used only for weak advisory signals
Auto-answer is awkward: it must use deny, so a successful decision renders as a red error and the agent may argue with it (author admits this); and it only handles a single non-multiselect question

Skill router sends every raw user prompt plus the whole installed-skill list to a third party on every turn; on client projects this is a data-handling concern, and it is ~6.8k input tokens per prompt

Very young, effectively a proof of concept: created 2026-09-17, last push the same day, 25 commits by 2 people (18/7, the second mostly merging PRs), 4 stars, 0 forks, no releases, no tagged versions (plugin.json 0.5.1), no issues history; cookbook-derived design with no evidence of use at scale
Runs arbitrary in-process code with $.process.run and $.env access in the user's session; needs a personal review and pinned commit before trusting on client machines
Version mismatch in README test commands: refers to 'typesafe-skill-mod' name that differs from the plugin name typesafe-mod (minor docs sloppiness)
entries.verdict: The only candidate here that hooks Jev into Claude Code with no prompting, and with zero context cost and fail-open behavior. But it is a day-old POC on an early-access hook API, hardcoded to TypeSafe direct (not OpenRouter), and its default path (AskUserQuestion) rarely fires. Best treated as a reference implementation to fork for OpenRouter, not something to install as-is.

entries.name: flaviusapop/jev-router
entries.what: npm launchers (jev-claude/codex/grok/opencode) run a localhost proxy that rewrites model and reasoning effort per turn via Jev; sub-agent routing; independent fork of gargpratyush/jev-router.
entries.autoInvocation: proxy (via wrapper launcher)
pros: Most complete router: model plus effort tiers, sub-agent routing, override vocabulary, status line, tests
Documents credential handling (localhost only, token forwarded verbatim)
Node 22, npm package, MIT
cons: Hardcodes api.typesafe.ai in router.mjs (TypeSafe key only, no OpenRouter path, signups reportedly closed)
Wrapper launcher plus ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL proxy; skips step when ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL set; cache and Opus 5.5 downgrade concerns
Written 2026-09-18 and untouched since; JEV_DUMP writes prompts to disk

entries.name: 455-dIAO/jev-codex-router-skill

entries.name: jev-effort
entries.what: Node CLI wrapper (`jev-effort [claude args]`) that starts a local 127.0.0.1 proxy on a random port, launches `claude` with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL pointing at it, and before each main-model /v1/messages step asks Jev (two Choice questions: which reasoning effort low..max, and a lease of 1/2/5/10 steps) via OpenRouter /api/alpha/decisions. It applies the answer by appending an effort-only system message (beta mid-conversation-output-config-2026-07-01) as the last message, re-inserting earlier markers so the prompt cache prefix is preserved. Jev may only lower effort below the session /effort by default. It is a cost-saving research tool that also ships `stats` (spend breakdown), `bench` (6 coding tasks) and `doctor`. It does NOT give Claude Code any Jev-powered decision tools, review, routing of model choice, or planning help; it only tunes thinking effort.
entries.autoInvocation: Transparent proxy, fully automatic once Claude Code is started through `jev-effort` (alias claude=jev-effort). No prompting, no model discretion; it acts on every model step. Caveat: it is a launcher wrapper, not a plugin or settings.json entry, so plain `claude`, IDE extensions and the desktop app are not covered unless `jev-effort serve` plus ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is set. Setting ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL in ~/.claude/settings.json makes it step aside.
security: No postinstall/preinstall scripts and no runtime dependencies (package.json scripts only has test); no curl|sh installer.

Proxy binds 127.0.0.1 on random port for the session only (src/proxy.mjs:277 listen host default 127.0.0.1); Claude credentials (OAuth bearer / API key) pass through untouched and are stated as never stored or logged. Any local process that finds the port could still send requests through it but the proxy adds no creds.

Jev key: stored in ~/.config/jev-effort/config.json mode 0600 (config.mjs:209-218), or read from env/file; setup takes --key-file/--key-stdin/hidden prompt, so the key is never in argv (setup.mjs:46-84). Key only sent as Bearer to the configured route with redirect:'error'.

Prompt-injection surface: tool outputs/prompts are fed to Jev as state, but Jev returns only a constrained choice (parseDecision validates effort in allowed list and lease in allowed set, jev.mjs:58-71) and instructions mark history as untrusted; worst case is a manipulated effort level, not code execution. Jev can never exceed session effort by default.

Rewrites API requests: appends a system message and beta header; on API 400 it resends the original, and after two rejections disables rewriting (proxy.mjs:235-241, docs/how-it-works.md failure table).
Unofficial dependency on undocumented Claude Code request shape (per-turn-control-2026-07-01 beta); TESTED_CLAUDE_CODE = 2.1.280 while the user runs 2.1.285. doctor warns on newer versions.
entries.dataEgress: To OpenRouter/Jev per uncached decision: model name, allowed efforts, latest user prompt (up to 8,000 chars), original task plus up to 5 earlier prompts (trimmed), up to 8 of Claude's visible replies since latest prompt, and the last 6 tool calls with inputs and head+tail output previews (~1,000 tokens each). That is real code, file contents, command outputs and client-project text (typically ~1-5K input tokens per call, README says avg ~5K in long sessions). No thinking traces. Also everything to Anthropic goes through localhost proxy unchanged except the appended effort message. Client projects: source excerpts leave to OpenRouter and TypeSafe (provider pinned to typesafe, no fallback) on every non-leased step, with no secret redaction; the user's existing secret-leak PreToolUse hook does not cover this path.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open by design. Jev error or timeout (default 5 s, jevTimeoutMs, min 500) -> that step uses Claude Code's own effort (policy.mjs fallback). Circuit breaker: 3 consecutive failures -> Jev skipped for 2 minutes (jev.mjs:83-105). Internal errors forward the original request; API 400 on rewrite -> resend original, after 2 rejections drop to shadow. Missing key -> plain claude. But the proxy itself is in the critical path of every Anthropic request: if the proxy process crashes mid-session, Claude Code is stuck with a dead ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (no automatic fallback).
entries.contextCost: Zero tools, zero MCP instructions, zero hook-injected text, no SKILL.md. The only prompt effect is the tiny appended effort-only system message (empty content). Side effects are worse than the cost: any custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL makes Claude Code disable MCP tool search (README measured 27K -> 281K-500K token fresh sessions); jev-effort mitigates by setting ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true, fine-grained tool streaming and gateway hint headers when upstream is api.anthropic.com (environment.mjs:190-210), and about 4K fewer tokens per request because claude.ai-backed tools drop. The user already has gitnexus and playwright MCP servers (large tool sets), so relying on the ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH restoration matters.
pros: Genuinely automatic once aliased: no per-prompt instruction, decides per step with leases, and its own docs claim it never resets the prompt cache (0 unexpected misses in 411 checked steps).

Real OpenRouter support in code: openrouter route with sk-or- auto-detect and OPENROUTER_API_KEY (src/jev.mjs:5-8, src/config.mjs:170,221), matching the user's chosen provider, and it is the only Jev use that leverages Jev's Choice primitive in the way it was designed (typed decision, probabilities).

Careful engineering for a small tool: zero deps, no postinstall, localhost-only, key never in argv, 5 s timeout, circuit breaker, fail-open, 400-retry fallback, shadow mode to try it with zero effect, doctor and stats.

Honest, reproducible research: the author's own results say at high effort the saving is about 1% and the real-session estimate is 4-9% at max; it can be evaluated in shadow mode before applying anything.
Restores MCP tool search under the proxy (ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true) which matters for the user's gitnexus and playwright MCP servers; adds no tools or context of its own.
Cheap: Jev costs about $0.12 for 470 steps of a 92-minute session.
cons: Only tunes reasoning effort; it does not give Claude Code any Jev decision capability (no code-review gating, no risk scoring, no routing between models or subagents). Most of the 'use Jev when it adds value' idea is not delivered.

Savings are small for this user: at high effort about -1%, and even at max only 4-9% in a long session because cached context is ~82% of spend; and the user is on a subscription so dollar savings are not billed, and quality risk at max on real client work is 'untested' per the author.

Wrapper/proxy architecture: must launch via `jev-effort`; behind ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL Claude Code disables Remote Control, server-managed settings and claude.ai-backed tools such as Artifacts (usage.md limitations) and changes auto-mode review behavior (needs CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=0), which the user relies on daily (auto permission mode, Artifacts). Explicit warning: don't use if a client org relies on server-managed settings.

Fragile coupling to undocumented Claude Code internals: verified only on 2.1.280 and Opus 5.5 (user is on 2.1.285); the marker must be the last message and depends on beta headers per-turn-control-2026-07-01 and mid-conversation-output-config-2026-07-01, so a Claude Code update can silently disable it (falls back to no-op, not breakage).

Sends prompts, replies and 6 tool-output previews (real code, potentially secrets from command output) to OpenRouter/TypeSafe every non-leased step with no redaction; bad fit for client projects and bypasses the user's secret-leak hook.
Adds 0.6-0.75 s median (3.8 s p95) wait per non-leased step in apply mode.
Very immature: created 2026-09-23, 15 commits by 1 author, 3 stars, no releases on GitHub, npm latest (0.1.6) lags repo HEAD (0.1.7); README itself says 'isn't recommended as a way to save money'.

The 'function hooks' native path (CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1, turn.step) documented in how-it-works.md would remove the proxy but is early-access and unimplemented here; sibling repos (jev-opus, jev-model-router, effort-router) cover the same niche.
entries.verdict: Technically sound, safe-by-design (fail-open, localhost, no deps, OpenRouter supported) but it only tunes thinking effort with a 1-9% saving that the author himself says does not justify using it, and the ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL proxy costs this user Artifacts, Remote Control, server-managed settings and pipes code excerpts to a third party. Worth running once in --jev-shadow mode as a measurement, not as the daily integration.

entries.name: rlcd-gateway
entries.what: Self-hosted Go binary (npm/PyPI wrappers around prebuilt binaries) that sits between Claude Code and the model provider via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. It forwards Anthropic/OpenAI-format traffic, keeps the subscription login as passthrough, and can (a) prune stale tool_result blocks from context, (b) route requests to other models via rules, (c) proxy/audit Jev-style System One calls (POST /v1/systemone) with calibration stats, mirror and dashboard. Jev is used in three ways: as the 'economy model' selector that scores per-block keep probabilities (noul questions) for pruning, as the answerer for 'decision rules' that route requests (choice/score/noul), and as an audited passthrough for the user's own apps. It is a general LLM gateway that uses Jev as an optional decision backend, not a Jev tool for coding tasks (no code review/commit/permission gating). A small MCP server (rlcd_recall) lets the model restore pruned blocks.
interface: CLI: rlcd-gateway, setup <agent>, undo <agent>, keys create, help
entries.autoInvocation: transparent proxy. Once ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points at the gateway, Jev is consulted automatically and invisibly (pruning epochs, decision rules) with no user prompt and no model discretion. But it is infrastructure-level (token/cost optimization and model routing), not a coding-value feature: Jev never gates commits, reviews diffs, classifies user intent for skills, or acts inside Claude Code's decision points.
security: Sits in the path of ALL Claude Code traffic including the subscription OAuth bearer (passthrough route forwards Authorization untouched) -- a full man-in-the-middle by design; trust rests on a 1-week-old single-maintainer, 2-star project with prebuilt binaries you cannot audit at runtime

log_bodies defaults to true (config.go:206): full prompts, file contents, tool outputs (including anything the model read: .env, keys, client code) are written to ~/.rlcd-gateway/ and kept 14 days / 2 GB; README says 'Logs contain full prompts'. Credentials are masked in logs but secrets inside bodies are not. Bad fit for client projects and bypasses the spirit of the user's PreToolUse secret-leak guard
Enforce-mode pruning requires log_bodies (recall reads logged bodies)

Loopback-only by default with Host-header check (DNS rebinding defence), non-loopback Origin rejected on MCP endpoint; beyond loopback requires gateway keys, admin token min 24 chars (guard.go); gateway keys stored as SHA-256 in keys.json mode 600
API keys via env vars (token_env) or stored in config; API never returns tokens (has_token only); keys not put in argv by the launcher (npm bin just spawnSync with user args)

No npm postinstall script (package.json has only bin; platform binary via optionalDependencies); npm package has SLSA provenance and signatures; no curl|sh installer, README suggests curl of release tarballs
entries.dataEgress: To the LLM provider: unchanged Claude Code requests (or pruned in enforce mode; or rerouted to another provider/model if a rule/route says so, in which case the subscription is dropped and an OpenRouter/other key is used). To the Jev backend (prune selector, plan.go:160-163): state {goal = up to last 3 user turns, each head 1200 + tail 300 chars, recent_activity = last 8 tool-call summaries (tool name + file path/command/pattern/url clipped to 100 chars)} plus one noul question per candidate old block whose instructions contain the block's description and a 1000-char (700 head + 300 tail) excerpt of the tool result/text, per epoch. For decision rules (router/decision.go): latest_user_text/goal/recent tool calls/context_tokens/client per rule (default only on conversation start). So code snippets, file excerpts, command output and user prompts do leave the machine to the Jev backend (OpenRouter if configured) in addition to Anthropic. Local disk: full request/response bodies under ~/.rlcd-gateway/.
entries.failureMode: Two layers. Jev-side: fail-open. Prune selector timeout 3000 ms (selector_timeout_ms, max 30 s) and any error keeps everything (ReasonFailOpen, plan.go:~170); decision rules have timeout_ms 2000 with else-branch/next-rule on error, timeout or low confidence; selector HTTP client timeout 30 s with one retry on connection failure (selector.go:58,95). Gateway-side: fail-closed for the whole session. If the local gateway process is not running or crashes, Claude Code with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL set to 127.0.0.1:4777 cannot reach the API at all (no autostart, no built-in fallback to api.anthropic.com from the client side). It has upstream error recovery (clamping, backoff, route fallbacks) but a single point of failure and an extra hop for every request including streaming.
entries.contextCost: Zero tool-definition cost by default: the recall MCP server is optional and exposes one tool (rlcd_recall, roughly 100-250 tokens of schema/description); no hooks; no injected text. Net effect on context is negative-cost when pruning is enforced (replaces stale tool_results with ~40-token markers), with prompt-cache invalidation risk that the project mitigates with sticky decisions and epochs. Default mode is shadow, so no change to what Opus sees until switched to enforce.
pros: Truly automatic and prompt-free: base-URL proxy is the only approach that needs no model cooperation, matching 'Claude Code must use it when needed' literally
Keeps subscription/OAuth login (passthrough route forwards credentials unchanged), with documented settings-level and credential-order handling in setup/claude.go
Jev usage is fail-open: 3 s selector timeout, error keeps all context; decision rules fall to else/next_rule on timeout or low confidence

Jev endpoint config is free-form: base_url https://openrouter.ai/api + auth key + token_env OPENROUTER_API_KEY + model typesafe/jev-1.13 produces the exact OpenRouter POST /api/v1/systemone URL (selector.go:82), so OpenRouter-hosted Jev is a config change

Decision rules give a real, concrete Jev use case: route trivial vs hard requests (score) between Haiku and Opus, or keep sensitive data local (noul), with min_confidence and audit/calibration (ECE) of every Jev answer
Pruning starts in shadow mode (default) so you can see 'would have saved' before enforcing; sticky per-conversation decisions and epoching designed around Anthropic prompt-cache economics
Reversible install: setup writes a timestamped backup and 'undo' restores the previous ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL; no npm postinstall; npm provenance attestation; Apache-2.0; 46 test files
Loopback-only with Host/Origin checks, gateway keys hashed (SHA-256), tokens never returned by the API
Good observability dashboard for token/cost per request, which helps evaluate whether Jev-driven routing actually saves money
cons: Not a Jev integration for coding value: Jev only scores 'keep this old tool_result?' and 'how hard is this request?'. It does not review code, gate destructive commands, triage tasks, or decide commit/PR actions
Single point of failure for every Claude Code call: if the local process is not running, Claude Code cannot reach the API (fail-closed at the proxy level); no autostart/systemd unit found

Man-in-the-middle for the subscription OAuth token and all client code, from a repo created 2026-09-23 with 1 contributor, 2 stars, 3 npm versions in 13 minutes on 2026-09-24; prebuilt binaries via optionalDependencies cannot be inspected at runtime

log_bodies defaults to true: full prompts, file contents and any secrets Claude reads are persisted to ~/.rlcd-gateway for 14 days (2 GB); unacceptable default for client projects, and it sidesteps the user's secret-leak PreToolUse guard because the proxy sees tool_result contents after the fact
Code excerpts (1000 chars per candidate block plus last 3 user turns) are sent to the Jev backend/OpenRouter in addition to Anthropic; extra third party in client-data flow

Enforce-mode pruning changes what Opus sees; a 700+300-char preview decides drops permanently per conversation ('a kept block is never reconsidered'), quality risk on long agentic sessions; Jev's fitness for judging code relevance is only validated on tiny self-run sets (12, 10, 20 prompts) by the author

Model-routing rules that send requests to OpenRouter models require a 'key' route, which drops the Claude subscription for those turns (spend real money) and switching models mid-conversation invalidates prompt cache and signed thinking blocks (their own warning)

OpenRouter-hosted Jev is not documented or tested by the project: defaults and pricing labels assume api.typesafe.ai/TYPESAFE_API_KEY; provider label falls back to 'open-rlcd' unless overridden; you must manually configure decisions backend, token_env and model id
Prune value is small for this user: subscription billing means token savings are not cash savings, and Opus context savings do not justify added latency (up to 3 s per epoch) and risk
No CI test workflow; release-only pipeline; alpha (v0.1.2); heavy scope (33k LOC, dashboard, resilience, keys) to trust for a security-sensitive position
Overlaps with existing tooling (caveman-shrink MCP, GitNexus context hooks) that already reduce context without a proxy
entries.verdict: The only candidate that is fully automatic (transparent ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL proxy, fail-open Jev calls, OpenRouter reachable via a config-only backend), but it uses Jev merely for context pruning and request-complexity routing, adds a fail-closed single point of failure and logs full prompts to disk by default, and comes from a 1-week-old single-maintainer repo. Reasonable to trial in shadow mode on personal projects with log_bodies=false, not something to put in front of client work or your subscription login yet.
