entries.autoInvocation: deterministic hook per prompt (opt-in via /jev on)
pros: Tiny, readable bash (curl to /v1/systemone, jq) so switching URL to https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone and model typesafe/jev-1.13 is a 2-line edit
Fail-open with 5s max-time; sends only prompt text, no files; explicit off switch
cons: Routing is by advisory context line and subagent delegation, cannot change the main model; user runs Opus 5.5 and prompts often depend on context so value is dubious
Adds a network call per prompt and prompt text leaves the machine; static tier config, no calibration; 6 stars, one-day project

entries.name: MongLong0214/jev-gate
entries.what: Single Claude Code plugin (also native Codex) that uses Jev (System One, Choice/Score questions) for cost-oriented task routing rather than code intelligence. Five parts: Gate (Jev admits a request as direct/single/orchestrated, then dispatches to subagent workers and denies the root session's own tools while a job is admitted), Router (changes root-turn effort and subagent model/effort per decision), Compact (local extractive compaction, no Jev), Output (folds passing vitest logs, no Jev), Evidence (MCP tool jev_evidence: semantic source-window search, Jev-ranked). The aim is to save tokens by delegating to cheaper models.
interface: Hook PreToolUse (no matcher, so every tool call spawns node)
Hooks PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure (matcher ^Agent$), Stop, SessionStart
CLI: node dist/cli.js doctor | dashboard | explain
entries.autoInvocation: Mostly deterministic hooks, which suits the goal of no prompting. UserPromptSubmit and PreToolUse hooks run on every prompt and every tool call. Router and Compact are transparent function hooks that patch requests and compaction. Evidence is a model-discretion MCP tool: the model may call it, and nothing forces it. The skill is manual-only.
security: No LICENSE file and GitHub licenseInfo is null. That means all rights are reserved, which is a problem for client projects.

Gate 'auto' sends the user request and the composed task contract, which can include source excerpts, file names and constraints, to TypeSafe. docs/advanced-usage.md states: 'There is no secret scrubber and no zero-retention promise.'
Router does screen outbound strings with looksSecret (mods/router/hooks/client.ts:~148) and sends nothing if a match is found. It is a pattern filter, not a DLP.

The API key goes in the Authorization header only (src/jev.ts). It is not in argv. It comes from the env TYPESAFE_API_KEY or the sensitive plugin option (kept in secure storage). Traces are documented as not receiving the key.

A project-level .claude/settings.json can set TYPESAFE_API_KEY and JEV_EVIDENCE_CONFIG, so a hostile repo could redirect the key or the Evidence config (README). pluginConfigs in project settings are ignored.

fetch uses redirect:'error', a 128 KB request cap, a 1 MB response cap, and strict validation of the response (probabilities sum, argmax). Jev output is typed, so the injection surface is small. However, Evidence returns raw source text into the model context, and the skill tells the model to treat it as source, not instructions.
entries.dataEgress: To api.typesafe.ai only (no OpenRouter path). Gate auto: the user's prompt verbatim at admission, and the task contract plus predecessor summaries at each planner/worker dispatch (can include source excerpts and file names). Router: the text of the decision being asked (a root-turn prompt or a subagent prompt), after the looksSecret check. Evidence semantic: goal, constraints, and a page of source windows (only when remote is true, which is the default when a key is present; exact-symbol and read-back are not sent). Compact and Output send nothing. Whole repos and transcripts are not uploaded. In lean mode, prior conversation-history groups are sent.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open by design. callJev is one POST, one deadline, zero retries. Router preparation budget is 800 ms by default (routerTimeoutMs); past it the request runs natively. No key, timeout, 4xx/5xx, malformed answer, low confidence or a tie all mean the call stays native. After a 401 or 402 the Router stops asking for the rest of the activation. Hook timeout is 5 s. The exception is that a Gate job that is already admitted keeps the root guard on. If the host cannot run a foreground worker, the doctor warns, and 'auto' skips the request instead of failing.
entries.contextCost: One MCP tool (jev_evidence) with a large schema (goal, constraints, roots, queryTerms, exactSymbols, mode, limit, offset, expectedSnapshot, sources), plus a dynamic description listing the allowed roots. Estimate is about 800-1,200 tokens (src/evidence/server.ts is 11.6 KB, with most of the schema and description being tool text). The skill is disable-model-invocation, so it costs 0 in the listing. The MCP server sets no 'instructions' field (capabilities: {tools:{}}). Hooks add additionalContext only when Gate admits a job (a coordinate directive, size not measured). Plugin agents (planner, workers) add a few agent descriptions to the Agent tool listing. Each admitted job also spends worker-subagent context and cost. Real cost driver: it changes how the session runs (root guard, delegation), not just tokens.
pros: It is the only candidate that fits the wanted model (automatic, with no prompt to Claude): deterministic UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse hooks and transparent Router/Compact function hooks. It is also the most thought-out design for using Jev as a typed decider (Choice/Score with calibrated-probability thresholds, uncertainty means native).

Strict fail-open client: one POST, deadline, zero retries, 128 KB request cap, 1 MB response cap, strict validation of the answer schema (src/jev.ts). Every uncertain, timeout or key-less path keeps the native behavior, and 401/402 trips a circuit breaker.

Explicitly supports the subscription OAuth login (src/auth.ts isSubscriptionOAuth) and warns on ANTHROPIC_* conflicts, which matches the user's setup. Each of Gate, Compact, Output and Router has its own off switch, and the Router never changes the root model unless routeMainModel is true.

Unusually honest documentation: it publishes unfavorable results (V4 forced delegation cost more, the depth ladder was withdrawn, no saving guaranteed), with a local dashboard, doctor and trace explain. Router does a local looksSecret check before sending anything.
Native Codex support also ships, and 58 test files plus CI show engineering discipline.
cons: Wrong problem for this user: it optimizes token cost by downgrading effort/model and delegating. The user runs Opus 5.5 on a subscription and wants Jev value in daily coding, not cheaper models. Open issue #132 records that the Router cut effort xhigh to medium/low and 'savings come from doing less work' (55 s/$1.02 vs 462 s/$5.60 for a review with a shorter output), and #135 records that Gate A predicts tool calls at about 1/10 of the measured value and never delegated in the bench.

OpenRouter is not supported. The endpoint api.typesafe.ai and the model 'jev-1.13.0' are hardcoded, and a strict model-equality check would discard OpenRouter's 'typesafe/jev-1.13' answers. Using OpenRouter needs a fork and a rebuild of at least 3 files, and loses marketplace updates. The user would need a separate TypeSafe key and billing.

Invasive to a bypass/auto-permission workflow: while Gate admits a job, the root session's tools are denied by PreToolUse (only read/task/Agent/MCP tools pass), the work goes to subagents, and Gate requires foreground workers (CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=0 and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1), which changes how all subagents run. Each of those can conflict with the existing GitNexus, secret-guard and caveman hooks.

Depends on CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1, an experimental host feature verified only against Claude Code 2.1.282-2.1.284 types. It may break on 2.1.285 or later, and the README says the mode resolver was checked on 2.1.284 only.

Data egress on client projects: the user prompt, task contracts and source excerpts are sent to TypeSafe with no scrubber in Gate and no retention promise (the docs say so). Evidence semantic search is on by default when a key exists. The repo has no license, which is unsuitable for client work.

Very young and single-author: created 2026-09-17, 61 commits in 13 days, 1 contributor, 4 stars, v0.7.0 released hours ago; it changes fast (6 policy fixes on the last day). A node process is spawned on every tool call (unmatched PreToolUse), and the marketplace release is a pinned zip you cannot inspect from the marketplace entry alone.
The Evidence tool duplicates Grep, the existing GitNexus graph and local search. Its value is low next to GitNexus, and being a model-discretion tool it is not guaranteed to be used.
entries.verdict: The most complete automatic (hook-based) Jev integration for Claude Code, but it is a cost-routing and delegation harness pointed at TypeSafe's own API. It does not fit an Opus-on-subscription user who wants Jev as a decision oracle, it has no OpenRouter path (a fork is needed), and its root guard and effort downgrades conflict with a bypass-permission daily flow. Mine it for design ideas (the strict fail-open client, and thresholding of Choice/Score probabilities) rather than installing it.
entries.license: None (no LICENSE file; GitHub licenseInfo null)

entries.name: reflex-router
entries.what: Node/TypeScript CLI (`reflex`) that launches the real `claude` behind a loopback proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL -> 127.0.0.1) with a temporary merged --settings file. At the start of each user-typed prompt or subagent it sends a redacted, truncated task to Jev (POST {base}/v1/systemone, Choice question for the cheapest adequate tier haiku/sonnet/opus plus a Score question for reasoning demand). In the default shadow mode it only records what it would do. In opt-in route mode it rewrites the model field to a cheaper Anthropic model, with a prompt-cache cost guard. It also records outcome signals (correction, failed test, reverted edit) and has `reflex report`. It is a cost/latency model-router, not a way for Claude to consult Jev for coding decisions.
interface: Hooks (injected via --settings, not ~/.claude): UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse(Agent only), PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure(Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit|Bash), SubagentStart, SubagentStop, Stop

Env: REFLEX_MODE(shadow|route|off), REFLEX_BACKEND(jev|laya), REFLEX_JEV_BASE_URL, REFLEX_JEV_MODEL, REFLEX_JEV_DEADLINE_MS(1500), REFLEX_MAIN_CHAT, REFLEX_UPGRADES, REFLEX_EFFORT, REFLEX_ESCALATE, REFLEX_AB, ...
entries.autoInvocation: Transparent proxy plus injected hooks: fully automatic once `claude` is aliased to `reflex` (no prompting needed). But Jev is only used to pick a model tier for each turn, not consulted by Claude for coding decisions, and it does nothing if you start plain `claude`.
security: Sits in the path of ALL Claude Code traffic (loopback proxy); Anthropic credentials are forwarded untouched, said not to be read/stored/logged (CLAUDE.md rules); fine with OAuth in principle but any proxy bug affects every request. Fail-open door forwards straight to the API if the worker dies.

TYPESAFE_API_KEY is only in env / ~/.reflex/env (mode-checked), stripped from the claude child env (config.ts:245 isReflexEnvName), sent only in the Authorization header, never in argv; errors never include key or response body (jev.ts:1-4, 192).

Redaction of task text before egress (sk- keys, AWS, GitHub, JWT, PEM, .env NAME=value lines, home prefixes) is best-effort, per docs/privacy.md; client project code pasted into prompts can still leave the machine.
No telemetry; only two connection kinds (Anthropic, decision backend). `reflex share` writes a file, never uploads. Local logs ~/.reflex 0700/0600, rotated; prompt preview off by default.

No curl|sh, no postinstall, no shell exec beyond spawning claude (launch.ts:69, shell only when needed for Windows .cmd). Zero runtime deps, small supply-chain surface, but young single-maintainer package (npm install -g runs its bin with full user privileges).

Hook answers carry nothing except optional delegation hint and a model-change notice; injects hooks via --settings so ~/.claude/settings.json is untouched, but they merge with the user's existing hooks (secret guard, GitNexus, caveman) - interplay not tested in the repo.
entries.dataEgress: To Jev (only at start of work: typed main-chat prompt or a subagent's first request): JSON {state:{task (user prompt, default cap 4000 chars head+tail, redacted), previous_assistant_reply (main chat only, last 1000 chars tail, redacted), context:{requesting_tier, is_subagent}}, model, questions}. No system prompt, tool list, file contents, tool outputs, diffs or session ids (docs/privacy.md, asserted by tests). Plus a keyless HEAD / to the backend host at startup and every 60 s keep-alive. To Anthropic: the normal Claude Code traffic through the proxy (byte-identical in shadow mode). Locally: ~/.reflex/decisions.jsonl with hashes/counts/tiers, no prompt text by default.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open by design and by tests. Decision deadline REFLEX_JEV_DEADLINE_MS default 1500 ms (hard, includes connect); on timeout/HTTP error/invalid response the request is forwarded unchanged on the requested model (jev.ts:159-211, BackendError). Circuit breaker (src/worker/breaker.ts), worker supervisor with restart backoff, crash loop -> passthrough, front door forwards directly to the API. No key -> passthrough (effective-mode.ts:21). Caveat: a new turn waits up to 1.5 s in route mode; a killed launcher ends the session connection; pins are lost on worker restart.
entries.contextCost: No MCP tools, no skills: 0 tool-definition tokens. Hook-injected text: none by default; with opt-in REFLEX_DELEGATE=1 about 3 lines (~80-100 tokens) added per typed prompt. Hidden cost risk: proxying via a non-first-party ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL makes Claude Code disable MCP tool search, so reflex sets ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true (launch.ts:53-59) to avoid the README-measured 32k -> 67k /context inflation. Route mode can also break prompt cache continuity when switching models (cache write penalty, guarded).
pros: The only candidate so far that is truly automatic: a transparent proxy/hook layer needing no 'use jev' prompt once claude is aliased.

Real Jev wire client in src/backend/jev.ts with strict answer validation, keep-alive, hard deadline, no retries, key and body never logged; base URL is configurable (REFLEX_JEV_BASE_URL) and the path /v1/systemone matches OpenRouter's.

Well-engineered fail-open design (front door, supervisor, breaker, byte-identical passthrough), tested under a network-blocking guard, CI on 2 OSes x 3 Node versions; MIT; zero runtime deps; no telemetry; no postinstall.
Shadow mode default: can observe for a few sessions what Jev would decide, with `reflex report`, before enabling any rewriting.
Privacy controls: allow-listed state, char budgets, secret redaction, 0600 logs, TypeSafe key stripped from child env.
Honest documentation: README says no cost saving has been measured; maintainer's own 3-day log showed net about $0.03 estimated saving.
cons: Wrong use of Jev for this user's goal: it only routes Anthropic model tier (Opus->Sonnet/Haiku) and reasoning effort; it does not let Claude Code use Jev typed decisions during coding (permission triage, file choice, etc.).

Value is cost saving, but the user appears to be on a subscription/OAuth login with Opus 5.5 as main model; per-token savings are moot, and the author's own data says 73% of tokens are main-chat tool-loop continuations that routing cannot touch, with 2-turn sessions all judged opus.

No OpenRouter support in code: key must start with apikey_ (config.ts:352), model regex ^jev- rejects typesafe/jev-1.13 (config.ts:259), only TYPESAFE_API_KEY; OpenRouter's System One schema not verified equal, so a fork/patch is required and untested.

Puts an alpha, 10-day-old, single-maintainer proxy in the path of every Claude Code request for personal and client work; wire format 'is not a public contract', fixtures only up to CC 2.1.284 while user runs 2.1.285; route mode degrades to shadow on major version drift.
Route mode risks: Sonnet 5.5 refusals that poison the session, prompt-cache losses on switch, up to 1.5 s added wait per new turn, pins lost on worker restart.
Prompt text (up to 4000 chars per turn, from client projects) goes to a third party (Jev/OpenRouter) even in shadow mode; redaction is best-effort.

Requires launching via `reflex` (alias) and injects its own --settings hooks/status line, which may clash with the user's existing statusLine and hook stack (GitNexus, secret guard, caveman); README notes it skips its status line only if the user has their own, and hook ordering interplay is untested.
Adds ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true and a proxied base URL; any Anthropic-side change to request shape, beta headers or OAuth handling can break passthrough.
entries.verdict: Best-engineered automatic Jev integration found, but it solves a different problem (cheaper-model routing) than making Claude Code consult Jev, gives little for a subscription Opus-main user, needs a fork to work with OpenRouter, and puts an alpha proxy in front of all traffic. At most run it in shadow mode on personal projects to see what Jev decides; do not adopt for client work.

entries.name: jev-classifier
entries.what: Local Node HTTP gateway (default port 8080) that sits between Claude Code and api.anthropic.com via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:PORT/oauth/claude. For every POST /v1/messages that carries tools, it rebuilds a compact state (user texts, actions taken, tool results clipped to 600 chars) and calls Jev (choice over ALL tool names/descriptions plus a 'done' noul). In enforce mode it rewrites the request body to tool_choice={type:tool,name:X} before forwarding upstream; if confidence is below MIN_CONFIDENCE (0.5) it uses tool_choice auto and appends a 'Routing hint' to the system prompt. Every decision is appended to a JSONL log. The MCP mode (advisory jev_choose_next_tool) exists only for Cursor and Antigravity, not for Claude Code. It launches via a wrapper (jev-classifier run claude), not through hooks or plugins.
interface: CLI: config <agent>, serve, stop, status, doctor [--check], logs [--follow|--decisions], settings, proxy on|off, startup enable|disable, connect cursor|antigravity, mcp, dashboard
entries.autoInvocation: Transparent proxy: once ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points at the gateway, it classifies and rewrites every tool-bearing request with no prompting and no model discretion. That is the closest match to the 'automatic, never say use jev' requirement of all candidate types. But it is not a Claude Code hook or plugin. Startup requires either the 'jev-classifier run claude' wrapper or a persistent ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, and it needs the daemon running (startup enable gives a desktop autostart on Linux).
security: No install or postinstall scripts (package.json scripts: build/test/start/prepack only); no curl|sh installer.

Jev key stored in plain text in ~/.config/jev-classifier/config.json (dir 0700, file 0600, src/settings.ts:96-103); keys are entered via setup prompt or env, not argv. Child agent env is stripped of JEV/TYPESAFE/OPENROUTER/AI_GATEWAY keys (agents.ts:78).

With OAuth mode the gateway receives and forwards Claude Code's subscription bearer token. It forwards headers except hop-by-hop ones (server.ts:69-85), does not persist them, and the optional --capture mode stores only allow-listed non-credential headers plus the full request body to .jev-classifier/captures. The gateway listens on a local port, so any local process that can reach it can use it as an authenticated relay to the user's Anthropic account when the user's token is attached. It does not attach the token itself, so risk is low.

OAuth path is locked to https://api.anthropic.com by default and rejects '..' and encoded dot segments (upstream.ts:36-40). Upstream/base URLs can be overridden by env or config (UPSTREAM, CLAUDE_OAUTH_UPSTREAM). A config poisoned to point elsewhere would exfiltrate the subscription token.
Jev call uses redirect:'error' and does not put provider error bodies into logs (jev.ts:91-101). Decision log stores tool names, confidences and timings, not content.

Prompt-injection surface: tool results and user text are sent to Jev as data and only steer which tool is forced. In low-confidence mode it appends a fixed 'Routing hint' to the system prompt built only from tool names. Injected text in a tool result could bias Jev toward a chosen tool name, and enforce mode then makes Claude call that tool, although with any tool's arguments still model-generated.
entries.dataEgress: To OpenRouter (POST /api/alpha/decisions, jev.ts:79-90) on EVERY Claude Code /v1/messages request that has tools (that is basically every main-loop turn, including subagents): (1) the concatenated text of ALL user messages in the conversation, not clipped and joined with '---' (router.ts buildState; this includes Claude Code's injected system-reminder blocks such as CLAUDE.md and hook output, since those live in user-message text blocks); (2) every tool call's name and full raw input (not clipped: file paths, bash commands, edit contents, written file bodies); (3) every tool result clipped to 600 chars each (file snippets, command output, grep hits); (4) assistant text clipped to 300 chars each; (5) the name and full description of every available tool (Claude Code built-ins plus gitnexus, playwright, caveman MCP tools, roughly 60 to 80 tools; descriptions of built-ins run to thousands of chars each). The system prompt is not sent. Code and client data therefore go to OpenRouter and TypeSafe on each turn, on top of Anthropic. The direct Anthropic traffic still flows as normal. That is a real problem for client projects under NDA.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open for Jev errors: any classify exception (missing key, HTTP 4xx/5xx, invalid or incomplete probability distribution, timeout) is caught and the original body is forwarded unchanged (server.ts:206-212). Jev fetch timeout is 30 s (jev.ts:83), so a slow OpenRouter stalls each turn up to 30 s before falling through. Fail-closed for the gateway itself: if the local daemon is down or the port is taken, Claude Code (pointed at ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL) gets connection refused and cannot reach the API at all, and with upstream errors returns 502 (server.ts:233-238). There is no circuit breaker or negative cache, so each turn repeats a failing Jev call (for example, a 32k-context overflow error) and pays its latency. A launch with 'run claude --no-proxy' or JEV_PROXY=0 bypasses it.
entries.contextCost: Zero MCP tools and no hooks in Claude Code, so no extra tool-schema tokens (MCP server exists only for Cursor/Antigravity). The real costs are elsewhere. (a) In enforce mode the gateway changes tool_choice per request, and Anthropic invalidates cached message blocks when tool_choice changes, so prompt-cache hit rates and subscription usage suffer. I inferred this from Anthropic's documented caching rules and did not measure it. (b) Forcing {type:tool} means the model cannot emit text or thinking before the call. (c) Extended or adaptive thinking (which Opus uses in Claude Code) is documented as incompatible with tool_choice any/tool and returns an HTTP 400. grep -rn -i thinking over src finds no handling in the adapter (only 'shadowReason' for OpenAI previous_response_id), so enforce mode will very likely break turns with thinking on. Low-confidence turns append a small system-prompt hint (about 30 tokens).
pros: Truly automatic: transparent proxy on ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, so no user prompt or model cooperation is needed. Claude Code's model, login and OAuth stay unchanged, and the docs say the OAuth token is only forwarded, never stored (src/upstream.ts, server.ts:69-85).
First-class OpenRouter support: JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, model ~typesafe/jev-latest, endpoint /api/alpha/decisions (jev.ts:5). Set-up is a one-key change.

Shadow mode (JEV_MODE=shadow) classifies and logs whether Jev's pick matches what Opus actually called (record.actual and match, server.ts:288-297), so you can measure Jev's value on real sessions before enforcing anything. That is a useful evaluation harness.

Fail-open on Jev errors and validates probability distributions strictly; only forces a tool when confidence >= 0.5, else falls back to auto plus a hint. Also a 'done' gate stops premature respond_to_user.
No install scripts, MIT, small readable codebase (about 2.5k LOC src), cross-platform CI, per-session env injection instead of editing ~/.claude, key stripped from the child env.
Local decision log and metrics/dashboard (jevMs p95, match rate), and a doctor --check command.
cons: Forces tool_choice={type:'tool'} on Claude Code's main loop. Per Anthropic's API rules this is incompatible with extended/adaptive thinking (Opus 5.5) and there is no thinking check in the adapter (src/adapters/anthropic.ts:57-59 just sets body.tool_choice). Expect 400 errors or degraded behaviour, and no text/plan before tool calls. Not verified by running (static-only audit).

Semantically wrong fit: Jev sees only Claude Code's tool NAMES plus descriptions and picks one, overriding Opus 5.5's own judgement on what to do next. A cheap router picking tools for a stronger model reduces quality (Bash vs Edit vs Task vs MCP), and it has no notion of arguments, so a forced Read or Bash still relies on Opus to fill them.

Payload size: sends the entire tool catalog (built-ins plus gitnexus, playwright and caveman MCP tools, likely 60-80 tools, ~15-30k+ tokens of descriptions) and unclipped user messages and tool inputs on every turn to a 32k-context beta model. Likely to hit HTTP 400/context limits often, and with no circuit breaker each turn repeats the failing call. Also 255-option cap silently truncates the tool list (router.ts:limitOptions), dropping tools beyond the first 254 in order of appearance.
Serial extra latency on every turn (Jev + OpenRouter alpha routing), up to 30 s on timeout; adds real wall-clock cost over long agent sessions.

Data egress: full user text (including CLAUDE.md/system-reminder content and hook output), raw tool inputs and 600-char tool results go to OpenRouter/TypeSafe every turn. Unacceptable for client projects without a data-processing agreement.

Fail-closed for the gateway: if the daemon dies or the port is used, Claude Code cannot reach Anthropic at all. The user must keep a background service running and set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL globally. Breaks the 'simple subscription OAuth' setup if the env leaks into other tools.
Changing tool_choice per request breaks Anthropic prompt-cache reuse for messages, raising subscription usage and latency (inferred from documented cache invalidation rules).

No Claude Code MCP or hook integration: the MCP server refuses any client except cursor and antigravity (mcp.ts:14), and it's not a plugin or skill. Very immature: 6 commits over ~1 day, 1 contributor, 4 stars, v0.1.2, no release notes; derivative of jev-eval-agent; depends on a beta model and on the 'alpha' OpenRouter endpoint.

Interaction risk with the existing tooling: forced tool selection would collide with the GitNexus and secret-guard hooks' assumptions, and with the ToolSearch/deferred-tool flow, subagents and plan mode, none of which are tested.
entries.verdict: The only candidate that is truly automatic in Claude Code (a transparent ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL proxy with native OpenRouter support). But it forces tool_choice on every turn, which very likely conflicts with Opus thinking and prompt caching, and it ships the whole conversation and tool catalog to a 32k-context beta model on each request. Use it at most in JEV_MODE=shadow on a personal project to measure Jev's agreement with Opus; do not enforce it for daily or client work.

entries.name: aaronshaf/opencode-jev-orchestrator
entries.what: OpenCode plugin keeping a cheap sticky parent model and using Jev to flag hard turns, escalating via jev_escalate/jev_parallel child subagents; quota-aware.
entries.autoInvocation: OpenCode plugin hook per turn (deterministic in OpenCode)
pros: Well-built TypeScript plugin with tests, schema, CI, npm release, /jev-status and /jev-explain
Sticky-parent plus escalation design preserves prompt cache; fail-safe release when Jev is down
cons: OpenCode plugin API only; not portable to Claude Code, and Claude Code cannot swap subagent models per Jev flag automatically
Uses TypeSafe key (JEV_KEY), OpenRouter only as model ref parsing

entries.name: iamvatsalpatel/tiershift
entries.what: TS and Python cost router: Jev picks cheapest sufficient tier per LLM call (YAML policy), escalates on evidence, has an OpenAI-compatible local proxy; benchmarked on 120 prompts.
entries.autoInvocation: proxy
pros: Mature: npm+PyPI, conformance suite, CI, SECURITY.md, cost and quality benchmark
OpenAI-compatible proxy with model auto and explicit reasons per route
cons: For apps you build; cannot reroute Claude Code on subscription/OAuth (its own README points to jev-router for CLIs)
Own benchmark is single-turn only, admits agentic tasks are untested
TYPESAFE_API_KEY, no OpenRouter path

entries.name: trietphan/jev-claw
entries.what: OpenClaw plugin: jev_route tool plus opt-in auto-route hook; Jev classifies task type/complexity/risk and JS policy maps it to a model route, enforced on sessions_spawn.
entries.autoInvocation: deterministic hook (auto-route) + model-discretion tool
pros: Good pattern: Jev classifies, testable JS code decides the route, with a prefilter skipping casual turns
Offline unit tests (auto-route, decide); small zero-dependency code
cons: Targets OpenClaw, not Claude Code; needs a port
Endpoint hardcoded to api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone in route.js

entries.name: FrancoisChastel/jev-router
entries.what: A local Node HTTP relay (127.0.0.1:4141) that sits between Claude Code (also Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Pi, Cursor) and the model provider. On each request it picks a model tier (fast/mid/frontier) and reasoning effort and rewrites ONLY the model field. It uses tool-outcome heuristics (NVIDIA Switchyard style) and, when the situation is ambiguous or a new user turn arrives, one Jev call. Jev answers 5 task questions or 3 execution questions about a bounded summary. Claude Code is pointed at it via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-code/auto written into ~/.claude/settings.json. It is a cost-saving downgrade router, not a way to give Claude Code Jev-as-a-tool. Jev only judges which model to use.
entries.autoInvocation: Transparent proxy plus HTTP hooks (sensors). Fully automatic once setup runs, with no prompting needed. Every Claude Code request passes through it. Jev is called by the relay deterministically on new user turns or ambiguous signals, not at Claude's discretion. It is the only candidate type that fits "automatic without prompting", but what it automates is model selection, not giving Claude Jev decisions for code tasks.
security: Not an MCP server and no Jev tool for the model. It is a transparent proxy in the path of EVERY Claude Code inference request (all prompts, code, file contents, tool results pass through a local Node process). This is high blast radius for a 3-star, 3-day-old, single-author project.

OAuth handling: with a claude.ai login it forwards Claude Code's own bearer token unchanged to api.anthropic.com (docs/harnesses.md, SECURITY.md). It does not store the token, but a third-party process now handles the subscription OAuth bearer in memory. Routing subscription traffic through a non-official base URL may also conflict with Anthropic terms/behavior; unverified.

Judge key stored in plaintext in ~/.jev-router/env (mode 600). The key is not in argv unless the user passes --judge-key (setup flag, visible in ps/shell history). The systemd unit and hooks run node with a script path only.

Writes ~/.claude/settings.json (env block ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/ANTHROPIC_MODEL, modelPicker, statusLine, hooks) with .bak backup. It would collide with the user's existing hooks and env configuration, and changes the global model to claude-code/auto for ALL projects including client work.

Claimed redaction hook is a no-op: src/core/dossier.ts:38 defaults redact to identity, and the daemon/relay never passes dossier.redact (decide.ts:364 uses input.dossier ?? {}; grep finds no other caller). SECURITY.md line says 'A redaction hook runs before anything leaves the process', which is misleading. Secrets in the last user message or tool-output excerpts would be sent to OpenRouter/Jev unredacted. The existing secret-leak guard hook does not cover this path.

Hardening present: loopback bind by default, --token required for non-loopback, content-type application/json required on POST (CSRF defense in 0.3.0). Publishing via `jev-router expose` creates a public cloudflared/ngrok tunnel (Cursor only, opt-in).
entries.dataEgress: Judge (OpenRouter /api/alpha/decisions): a bounded dossier of at most 12,000 chars: the harness name, the last user message (first 2000 chars), the tail of the assistant's intent (400 chars), up to 40 tool names, up to 8 recent tool outcomes with 200-char excerpts, and an images flag. It never sends the full conversation, file contents or system prompt, but the excerpts of tool output and the user's task text can contain secrets or client code, unredacted (redaction is not wired). Plus session_id. Inference: the relay forwards the ENTIRE request (full conversation, files, tool results) to whichever upstream the policy selects. With the OAuth egress it goes to api.anthropic.com, so nothing new leaves; with a gateway key it goes to OpenRouter (and to non-Anthropic models such as openai/gpt-6-luna on the fast tier). Local disk: ~/.jev-router/decisions.jsonl with digests and token counts.
entries.failureMode: Documented and coded as fail-open for the judge: 1500 ms per-attempt timeout, 1 retry (250 ms x 2^n jittered backoff) for 429/5xx/timeout/network, then falls back to tool-signal-only routing or the default model (src/judge/http.ts, policy timeout_ms 1500). Missing key means deterministic routing only. Hooks have a 2 s timeout and never block tools. BUT the relay itself is a single point of failure: if the local daemon or systemd service is down, Claude Code with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=127.0.0.1:4141 gets connection refused on every request (fail-closed for Claude Code), and there is no bypass. Recovery means removing env keys from settings.json. Cascade retry is off by default.
entries.contextCost: Zero MCP tools and zero server instructions. Hooks are HTTP hooks with no injected additionalContext text, so no context tokens. Only 1 slash command (/jev-router:status, about 100 tokens in the command list). The real cost is not context but quality and cost of the MODEL: the default claude-code/auto policy starts on Sonnet 5 and routes routine turns to the fast tier (Haiku on a subscription; openai/gpt-6-luna on a gateway), escalating to Opus only when it deems it necessary. That silently DOWNGRADES the user's chosen Opus 5.5 main model.
pros: Genuinely automatic and Jev-native: Jev is the judge for model routing via OpenRouter Decisions (src/judge/http.ts openrouter transport, OPENROUTER_API_KEY), one key for judge and inference, and the user's no-prompting requirement is met.

Careful engineering for a young repo: 46 test files, CI (typecheck, biome, bun test, build, cancel smoke, npm pack install test), 19k LOC, MIT, detailed DESIGN.md/SECURITY.md/CHANGELOG, and honest 'unproven savings' disclaimers.

Judge fail-open with 1.5 s timeout and retries; the judge is called sparingly (holds/leases, tool-signal shortcut, judge only on new user turns or ambiguity). Cost of Jev is negligible (about $0.00003 per decision).

Subscription-aware: reads Anthropic 5h/7d rate-limit headers and caps tier at 80%/95% of window. Also adds statusline, stats/replay/why for cost auditing, and --shadow mode that serves one model while logging what the router WOULD have done. That last is a safe way to evaluate without changing behavior.
No context-window cost (no MCP tools, no injected hook text), local-only, no telemetry, .bak backups on settings edits, an uninstall path documented.
cons: It solves a different problem than the user's goal: it routes to cheaper models (Haiku/Sonnet/gpt-6-luna) to save money. The user runs Opus 5.5 as the main model on a subscription, so the default policy will silently downgrade quality on personal and client work. Savings are also weak on a flat-rate subscription.

Sits in the critical path of every Claude Code request as a localhost proxy and rewrites ~/.claude/settings.json globally (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-code/auto). If the daemon dies, Claude Code is dead (fail-closed at the transport level), and it competes with the user's existing settings and hooks.

Handles the claude.ai OAuth bearer for the subscription and forwards it to api.anthropic.com from a 3-day-old, 3-star, single-author project. Client code and prompts transit the relay, and for client projects this needs explicit consent. The router might also send inference to non-Anthropic models via OpenRouter, changing the data-processing chain on client code.

SECURITY.md claims a redaction hook, but redact is identity by default and never wired (src/core/dossier.ts:38; no caller sets dossier.redact). The Jev dossier can carry the last user message and 200-char tool-output excerpts, potentially secrets, to OpenRouter unredacted; the user's PreToolUse guard does not cover it.

Very young and alpha: repo created 2026-09-27, v0.3.0 on 2026-09-30, 46 commits by one author, 3 stars. Benchmarks have not been run (README: 'treat any savings figure as unproven'), and live runs against TypeSafe direct and Vercel have not been done. The OAuth-relay approach depends on Claude Code internals (modelPicker/behavesAs, gateway hint headers) that may break across Claude Code releases.

Does not give Claude Code Jev's typed decisions for coding tasks (e.g., 'is this change risky', 'which file to edit'); Jev is used only internally as a router judge, so it does not deliver the broader 'use Jev whenever it adds value' goal. Model switching also risks losing prompt cache and mid-session behavior consistency; cascade/retry semantic side effects.
Adds up to ~3.3 s worst-case latency on turns where the judge times out twice; it can also conflict with the user's Opus-first workflow through effort/model changes mid-task.
entries.verdict: Technically the most complete and automatic Jev integration (OpenRouter Decisions as judge, transparent proxy, fail-open judge, tests and CI), but it is a cost-saving downgrade router that would swap the user's Opus 5.5 for cheaper models and puts a 3-day-old third-party proxy in front of every request and the OAuth token. Do not install it as-is; at most try it in --shadow mode or borrow its judge client and question design.

entries.name: Mandrilsquad1441/jev-model-router
entries.what: Claude Code / Codex / Claude Desktop plugin (single bundled Node MCP server + 3 skills + 1 slash command + CLI). It uses Jev (via OpenRouter Decisions API or TypeSafe) only to classify a task text (category, difficulty, reasoning, I/O size, tools/vision/latency/volume/web needs, stated priority) with 11 Choice/Noul/Score questions in one call. Pure local code then ranks live OpenRouter catalog models plus bundled benchmark scores and returns "use /model X + /effort Y" or a subagent model alias. It is a "which LLM should do this task" advisor, not a code-decision helper. Nothing is executed or switched automatically; it only recommends.
entries.autoInvocation: Model-discretion MCP tool + skill description triggers only. Server instructions and the route skill say to call recommend_model when the user asks which model to use, wants to save money/time, or before delegating to a subagent. It is not deterministic (no hook), and for a user who never asks such questions it will rarely fire; it never intercepts prompts, never switches models by itself. /delegate is manual (disable-model-invocation: true).
security: No install script/postinstall/curl|sh: plugin ships a committed, unminified esbuild bundle (dist/server.mjs 1.7 MB, includes MCP SDK); marketplace install just copies repo. I did not execute it; bundle-vs-source check is CI-only (git diff --exit-code on dist), I did not independently rebuild it, so auditing dist/ means trusting CI or diffing yourself.

API key: passed to the MCP child via env (JEV_ROUTER_OPENROUTER_API_KEY from plugin userConfig, sensitive:true, stored in keychain), not argv, so not visible in ps args. `setup` CLI reads key from stdin/hidden prompt and writes a file chmod'd owner-only (src/cli.ts imports chmodSync). Key only sent as Bearer to openrouter.ai / api.typesafe.ai; errors summarised/truncated, keys masked to last 4 chars (config.ts:216-220). Base URLs overridable by env (OPENROUTER_BASE_URL) so a hostile env could redirect the key, standard risk.
Shell execution: none found (grep for child_process/exec/spawn in src/*.ts returned nothing). File writes limited to cache dir (catalog/intel JSON) and config file.

Runtime remote-data dependency: fetches https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mandrilsquad1441/jev-model-router/main/data/model-intel.json daily (src/config.ts:67-68, intel.ts) - data-only JSON validated by isIntelData, but it steers which model is recommended and is controlled by a single unknown author's main branch. Can be disabled with JEV_ROUTER_INTEL_URL= (empty) or JEV_ROUTER_OFFLINE=1.

Prompt-injection surface: tool output is Markdown built from catalog model names/descriptions (OpenRouter catalog, third-party strings) and skills tell the agent to act on it; low risk since tools are read-only and cannot execute, but delegate command launches a subagent with model chosen from tool output.

Single anonymous author (GitHub Mandrilsquad1441 / Juan Beltran), 2 commits, 2 stars, no independent review. No telemetry per README/SECURITY.md and none found in code (only catalog, intel and Jev endpoints).
entries.dataEgress: To Jev via OpenRouter (or TypeSafe): the 'task' string that Claude itself writes when calling recommend_model/compare_models (clipped to 6,000 chars, src/jev/analyze.ts:166-173) plus optional 'context' notes (first 1,500 chars). Not whole files, diffs or tool outputs unless Claude puts them in the task text; but because the LLM composes the text from the conversation, client project details (repo names, function names, error messages, occasionally secrets) can leak into it. Your existing secret-leak PreToolUse hook matcher (Bash|Read|Grep|NotebookEdit) does NOT cover MCP tool calls. Also outbound anonymous GETs: openrouter.ai/api/v1/models and raw.githubusercontent.com model-intel.json (no user data). Sent to OpenRouter also: Authorization key, HTTP-Referer/X-Title app-attribution headers.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open. Jev client timeout min(config.timeoutMs 15s, 12s) per attempt with 3 attempts and jittered backoff (max 4s) on 408/425/429/5xx (src/jev/client.ts:62-71, http.ts:45); worst case roughly 36s+ blocking the tool call before offline keyword heuristic takes over (router.ts:138-143, result annotated 'Jev was unavailable'). Auth/402 errors also fall back to heuristics silently apart from a note. Since it is only an advisory tool, failure never blocks coding. Catalog falls back to cache then bundled snapshot.
entries.contextCost: 4 MCP tools (recommend_model with ~20 params incl. nested constraints/weights, compare_models, search_models with 11 params, router_status) plus 1 prompt. Estimated tool names+descriptions+schemas approx 6-8k chars = roughly 1.7-2.2k tokens if loaded eagerly (less if Claude Code's MCP tool search defers them). Server instructions ~640 chars (~160 tokens) always injected. Plugin skills add 3 descriptions (~250 tokens) and 1 command. Total roughly 2-2.6k tokens standing cost per session; no hook-injected text per turn.
pros: Genuinely uses Jev the way TypeSafe recommends: many narrow Choice/Noul/Score questions in one call, with code (not the model) making the decision (src/jev/analyze.ts, client.ts).

First-class OpenRouter support: config.ts:170-179 hits openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions with model ~typesafe/jev-latest using OPENROUTER_API_KEY - matches the user's intended provider with no patching; TypeSafe direct also works.
Safe design: read-only tools, no shell execution, no hooks that can block your session, fail-open to offline heuristic, key passed by env not argv, keychain-stored userConfig, MIT license.
Reasonably tested for a new project: ~135 test cases across 9 test files (node --test), CI on ubuntu/windows/macos x Node 22/24 plus Node 20 bundle job, dist-must-match-source check, secrets scan.
Low cost: about $0.08 per 1,000 decisions per the author; negligible standing context (~2k tokens) and zero per-turn overhead.
Delegation path exists (/jev-model-router:delegate sets Agent tool model alias) - the only way this can act on a recommendation inside a subscription session.
cons: Solves a different problem than 'use Jev automatically when it adds value': it routes tasks to an LLM (haiku/sonnet/opus/fable) rather than giving Claude Code calibrated yes/no or choice decisions (e.g. is this diff risky, which file to open) during coding.

With a Claude subscription/OAuth login and Opus 5.5 as the fixed main model, there is nothing to route per turn: Claude Code cannot switch main model mid-turn from a tool, so the output is advice the user must apply manually via /model and /effort, or via subagent alias.

Not automatic: no hook, no proxy. Firing depends on Opus choosing to call the tool when the user asks 'which model'; the user explicitly does not want to prompt for it, so it will mostly sit idle while costing ~2k standing context tokens.

Extra hop is often net-negative: an extra Opus tool round-trip to choose a cheaper model for a task Opus is already executing; its own cost-saving claims (-4% vs Opus 5 high, -49% vs Fable) are modelled by the author on 42 tasks and are irrelevant on flat-rate subscription.
Data egress through the LLM-authored task string (6k chars) to OpenRouter is not covered by the user's secret-leak hook (matcher excludes MCP tools) - risky for client projects.

Immature and single-maintainer: created 2026-09-18 (12 days old), 2 commits, 1 contributor, 2 stars, version 1.0.0, Jev/OpenRouter Decisions API itself is alpha/beta; committed 1.7 MB bundle and daily remote intel JSON from the author's main branch are unreviewed supply-chain trust.
Config gotcha: a TYPESAFE_API_KEY in env silently takes priority over OpenRouter unless JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter; worst-case fallback latency ~36s on outage.

Model catalog/score data contains fictional-looking or fast-moving entries (e.g. 'Claude Fable 5.1'); recommendations depend on the author's curated scores that may drift from what the user has access to.
entries.verdict: Well-built, safe, OpenRouter-native Jev integration, but it is a model-selection advisor that fires only when asked, so it does not deliver automatic Jev use during daily coding and is of little value on a subscription with a fixed Opus main model. Worth at most a manual /delegate experiment for cost-tiering subagents; not the core integration.

entries.name: jev-model-router (jev-claude)
entries.what: Python stdlib launcher `jev-claude` that starts a 127.0.0.1 HTTP proxy, sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to it, and spawns the real `claude` with a sentinel "JEV Router" model (jev-router) in /model. On each genuinely new user turn it strips system-reminder blocks, POSTs the prompt plus current model and context size to Jev (System One choice question plus 3 score questions), applies a local policy (confidence floor, no downgrade on big context, prompt overrides like "use opus"), and rewrites body.model to a Haiku, Sonnet or Opus id before forwarding to api.anthropic.com. It is a per-turn Claude model router and does nothing else. It has no MCP tools, hooks, or skills for Claude Code (only a Codex skill).
entries.autoInvocation: Transparent proxy, but only when Claude Code is launched through `jev-claude` (or an alias that replaces `claude`) AND the "JEV Router" sentinel model is the active model. Plain `claude` is never affected, so the user must change how they launch. Picking a real model in /model turns routing off (proxy.py:294). There is no hook, MCP or skill route. Once launched, it is fully automatic per turn with no user prompting.
security: API key is read from env or a .env file, never put in argv, so it is not visible in the process list. Loader order is cwd/.env, ~/.jev-router.env, ~/.jev-claude.env, and existing env wins (env_file.py:28). A project-local .env in any client repo is auto-read, so a malicious repo could plant TYPESAFE_API_KEY or override JEV_ENDPOINT. That is a config-injection vector, and JEV_ENDPOINT is read at import time from the environment.

Local proxy binds 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port with no auth (proxy.py:265). Any local process can use it as an Anthropic forwarder, but it holds no credentials and only forwards the caller's own headers.

Claude Code's Authorization / x-api-key OAuth token passes through the proxy to api.anthropic.com. The proxy also reuses those headers for its own GET /v1/models call (proxy.py:165-222). It stays on the local machine and there are no third-party hops, but the proxy sits in the trust path for all model traffic.

Modifies ~/.claude/settings.json on exit: restore_saved_model rewrites the file if the sentinel model got saved (settings.py:35-42). It reads settings.json for statusLine detection. It writes a temp --settings file with a statusLine command, in a verified 0700 dir under /tmp/jev-claude.

Status files at /tmp/jev-claude/<session>.json contain the full prompt and the exact Jev request/response for the last 20 turns. They are 0600, owner-checked, and pruned after 7 days (status.py). JEV_DEBUG=1 additionally logs prompt excerpts to ~/.jev-claude.log.

No shell=True. It only runs `claude` via subprocess.run with a list, and no curl|sh or postinstall. No telemetry found in the source (grep for http hits only the proxy, the Jev call and the Codex proxy). Pure stdlib means a small supply-chain surface.
entries.dataEgress: To api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone (or a JEV_ENDPOINT override such as OpenRouter) on each new user turn goes the user's typed prompt text with system-reminder and slash-command blocks stripped and NOT truncated (proxy.py:103, stdlib_router.py:89-92), plus current model id, an estimated context token count and the list of available model ids, plus the routing question text. Tool results, file contents, diffs and prior assistant messages are not sent, but any code the user pastes into a prompt is sent. Nothing is sent for tool-loop continuation requests or resent turns. The Bearer key goes to the Jev host. All normal Claude traffic (full conversation and code) still goes to api.anthropic.com, now via the local proxy. Nothing goes to other third parties. For client projects this is a new third-party (TypeSafe/OpenRouter) recipient of prompt text.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open. Per-attempt timeout is 1.5 s, wall-clock deadline 3 s, and there is one retry for 5xx/timeout only (config.py:90-92, stdlib_router.py:98-113). Any error, missing key, malformed response or unknown choice yields the model already in use, and the first turn falls back to Opus (policy.py:202-203, config.py:36). Any routing exception falls back to the account's newest Opus (proxy.py:369-376). Upstream Anthropic failure returns a synthetic 502. So a slow Jev adds up to about 3 s to the first request of a turn. Only the Jev call is fail-open. The local proxy itself is a new single point of failure for all Claude traffic if it crashes.
entries.contextCost: Zero MCP tools, zero hook-injected text, and no skill for Claude Code. The context cost is nil. The side effect on Claude Code is NOT nil: setting ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to a non-first-party host changes client behavior. The repo itself needed sanitize_schema hacks for MCP tool schemas because Claude Code skips its normal conversion behind a custom base URL (proxy.py:54-73). I expect other first-party-only client features to degrade, such as MCP tool search / deferred tool loading, which is not verified in this audit but is worth testing with the user's gitnexus and playwright MCP servers. The repo was verified only against Claude Code 2.1.281/2.1.282, and the user is on 2.1.285.
pros: Only candidate here that is truly automatic and prompt-free: a transparent per-turn decision with no 'use jev' phrasing. This matches the user's core requirement in mechanism.
Uses Jev exactly as designed, as a typed Choice plus Score decision with confidences, and the 3 s fail-open deadline means Jev outages never block work (stdlib_router.py:98-113, proxy.py:369-376).
Handles the subscription/OAuth login. It forwards Claude Code's own credential and reads /v1/models with the same headers, so no separate Anthropic key is needed (proxy.py:188-222).

Zero dependencies, no shell execution, no postinstall, key kept out of argv, prompt-only egress with no code or tool outputs, private 0600 status files. All of it is small enough to audit in an hour (about 1.5k lines of source).

Sensible guards: never downgrades on low confidence or big context, keeps a model for the whole tool loop, honors manual /model choice and 'use opus' overrides, Fable is opt-in (policy.py, config.py:74).
Tunable in one file (config.py) and JEV_ENDPOINT is env-overridable, so pointing at OpenRouter is a small patch. MIT license, about 100 tests, CI, signed commits, releases.
cons: Wrong goal for this user's daily coding value: it only chooses Haiku, Sonnet or Opus per turn to save cost. It adds no Jev decisions inside the coding workflow. The user runs Opus 5.5 by choice, and the router will actively downgrade turns to Sonnet or Haiku, risking quality on client work.
Requires launching via `jev-claude` and selecting the sentinel model, so it is not automatic inside a plain `claude` session. It cannot be enabled through settings.json hooks.

No OpenRouter support: the endpoint defaults to api.typesafe.ai and the key var is TYPESAFE_API_KEY only. The model id `jev-latest` is hard-coded (config.py:166), so OpenRouter needs a patch or fork (JEV_ENDPOINT plus a model-id change). Compatibility of OpenRouter's /api/v1/systemone response shape with `answers.model.choice` is unverified.

Puts a custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL in front of Claude Code. Risk of degraded first-party features, MCP tool-search behavior, and breakage on Claude Code updates. It was validated only up to 2.1.282 and relies on undocumented env vars (ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION*, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_UNKNOWN_MODEL_WINDOW_ENFORCEMENT), and the sentinel still triggers an 'unrecognized_model' warning (bin/jev_claude.py:35-39).

Prompt text of client projects goes to a third party (TypeSafe or OpenRouter) on every turn, unstripped and untruncated. Model switches cost about 23.6k tokens of cache rebuild per switch (config.py:83-86), so a per-turn router can cost more than it saves on a subscription.
Very young and thin: repo created 2026-09-24, 2 stars, 1 fork, effectively one maintainer with 19 AI-authored commits, SECURITY.md stale, no evidence of tests against real OpenRouter or Jev.

Modifies ~/.claude/settings.json on exit and auto-loads a .env from any cwd (config injection risk on untrusted repos). Together with the existing PreToolUse and GitNexus hooks, the status-line injection is a further interaction to check.
Subscription users gain little from cost routing: the subscription is flat-rate, and downgrading mainly reduces usage-limit burn, not spend.
entries.verdict: Real, well-written, and the only fully transparent Jev integration found, but it solves cost-routing between Claude tiers, not helping day-to-day coding, and it needs a `jev-claude` launcher, a base-URL proxy, and a fork patch for OpenRouter. For a user who wants Opus 5.5 by default, it is a low-priority optional add-on, not a core integration.
