entries.name: griffinwork40/claude-jev
entries.what: Claude Code plugin (marketplace name claude-jev, v0.27.0) that hands small judgments to Jev via typed questions: UserPromptSubmit routing hint (intent/scope/needs_tools), PreToolUse Agent|Task model-tier pick via updatedInput plus a brief-completeness check that can deny a spawn once, per-edit PostToolUse judging of edits against rules parsed from CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.claude/rules (blocks at >=0.80 with file:line), Bash git-worktree snapshots so the Stop hook can judge turn-level rules, and an experimental session.compact function hook that replaces the compaction summary with Jev-selected verbatim transcript rows. The GitHub repo is a fork whose HEAD (44b6ff3) is the same as upstream 0x7067/claude-jev v0.27.0. Griffin Long authored only 4 commits (docs and the AFK adapter, upstreamed as PRs) and none of the code is fork-original. Runtime is now TypeScript on Node with --experimental-strip-types (commit 3a393b7 "The plugin runtime is TypeScript"); the README still says "Python stdlib". Python remains only for register.ts pane helpers, stats and evals.
interface: PostToolUse Bash and PostToolUseFailure Bash -> src/rules.ts
entries.autoInvocation: Fully automatic and deterministic: hooks fire on UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse and PostToolUse (Agent, Bash, edits), PostToolUseFailure Bash and Stop with no user prompting. Every feature is on by default and only gated by a key being present (no key means silently off). Compaction and the /claude-jev pane additionally need CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 (undocumented) on Claude Code 2.1.278 or later. This matches the user's want of automatic use, but it is opinionated automation. It does not use Jev as a tool the agent can call.
security: Key handling: Bearer key is sent only in an Authorization header via fetch (jev-client.ts:~176), never in argv or logs. jev-calls.jsonl logs provider, model, ms and error only, with the error truncated to 300 chars. The key is read from the environment, or from a plugin userConfig field 'typesafeApiKey' (plugin.json) that lands in Claude Code's plugin option storage. plugin.json does not set a sensitive flag, so where it is stored is up to Claude Code. Prefer the env var.

No secret redaction anywhere: grep of src/, hooks/ and adapters/afk/src/shared/ finds no redact/secret/.env filtering. Edit hunks, Bash-produced diffs, the previous turn and user prompts go to the provider verbatim, so any secret in a diff or prompt leaves the machine.

Prompt-injection surface: file content, hunks, prompts and CLAUDE.md text are placed into Jev state. Injected instructions can move scores. Consequences are bounded: worst cases are a false block or a suppressed rule check, a wrong subagent tier, or a deny-once. Jev cannot execute anything.

Blocking behavior: rules.ts emits decision:block on PostToolUse (edits are already written, so this only feeds a repair reason back to the agent) and on Stop (max 2 per session). The README's own numbers show 23/247 (9.3%) of previously accepted real edits blocked, i.e. measured false positives. docs/stop-hook-false-positive.md records a real incident with two false Stop blocks caused by stale hunks.

Shell exec: fixed argv git commands via spawnSync (rules.ts:330), no shell string interpolation of tool input. Bash snapshot runs 'git add -A' against a scratch GIT_INDEX_FILE, which writes loose blob objects into the repo's .git/objects on every Bash call, with two or three runs per call. It leaves object-store garbage in client repos, and hashes untracked non-ignored files such as a stray .env.

Installer or downloader: an optional detached process downloads a 51MB ast-grep 0.45.3 release to ~/.claude/jev-bin, sha256-pinned, the first time an edit needs it. A background network fetch of a binary that then executes on user files.
entries.dataEgress: To https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone (Jev pricing is about $0.042 per 1M input tokens). (1) Every prompt: the prompt plus up to 300 chars of the earlier user message and the last 600 chars of the assistant reply (prompt-router.ts buildState). (2) Every edit: the old->new hunk (max 2000 chars), the 4 lines around the edit (max 1200 chars), the last prompt tail (max 400 chars) and rule texts; sibling module names for import rules. About 14% of edits get a second call that adds the enclosing function read from disk. State is capped at 8000 chars. (3) Every Agent/Task spawn: the subagent brief. (4) Stop: up to 16000 chars of turn hunks, including Bash-produced diffs. (5) Compaction: up to 300 transcript rows, 1200 chars each, roughly 200k+ chars. No redaction. Client-project code and prompts therefore reach OpenRouter and TypeSafe. Check client contracts before enabling on client repos. If the only per-call token cost matters, the cost is trivial. The bigger issue is confidentiality.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open by design. Each entry point wraps main() in try/catch that swallows errors (rules.ts:1186-1205, subagent-router, prompt-router, compactor). A missing key raises and produces no output. Hook timeout is 10s in hooks.json, with an internal budget of 9s for rules (HOOK_BUDGET). The Jev client timeout is 8s (jev-client.ts DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS), 4s for compaction chunks. Compaction falls through to the built-in summary. Caveats: (a) Bare 'node' in the hook command, so with PATH overridden in settings env node may not resolve and the hooks silently never run. Use an absolute path via an override or a wrapper. (b) It fails open only on errors. It does fail closed in the sense of intentionally blocking: PostToolUse edit blocks and Stop blocks (max 2 per file per session, 2 for Stop), and the brief check can deny an Agent spawn once. In bypassPermissions sessions, decision:block still feeds feedback to the model. (c) A Jev outage costs up to about 9s per edit plus retries, which is a latency failure, not a hard failure.
entries.contextCost: No MCP server, so zero tool-definition tokens. No skills are shipped by the plugin (the .claude/skills dir at repo root is for repo dev only). Hook-injected text: a one-line routing hint (about 15-25 tokens) only on lookup/fix prompts and some no-tools prompts, silent otherwise. Rule block reasons appear only on violations (up to 3000 chars each). Subagent deny reasons and systemMessages are rare. Compaction replaces a summary with about 3.2-3.9k tokens of verbatim rows (per README), which is comparable to a normal summary. The Claude Code plugin has no SessionStart digest (that exists only in the AFK adapter). Overall very low steady-state context cost.
pros: Already OpenRouter-ready in code: sk-or- key routes to https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone, and jev-latest is confirmed served there by the CHANGELOG. The user needs only OPENROUTER_API_KEY in the environment (jev-client.ts:70-133).
Genuinely automatic, and it targets a real gap for this user: per-edit CLAUDE.md rule enforcement, including the user's own ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, with file:line citations.
Broadly fail-open: all entry points swallow errors, a missing key means off, and there are hard timeouts (10s hook, 9s internal budget, 8s client).

Unusually evidence-driven: eval/ with 2,464 prompts and 250 real edits, honest reporting of false positives (9.3% real edits blocked), and incident write-ups (docs/stop-hook-false-positive.md). Dev CI runs tsc, oxlint, ruff and smoke tests on hooks with malformed stdin.
Very low context cost: no MCP tools and no injected skill listing; hint text appears only on some prompts.

Per-feature toggles (promptRouter, subagentRouter, rules, compaction) in plugin.json userConfig allow adopting only the useful subset. Cheap Jev calls, and the local pre-filters cut the number of calls.
Active and fast-moving: 180 commits in 12 days with a versioned CHANGELOG and MIT license. Upstream is the same code, with a release tag v0.27.0.
cons: The fork adds nothing: 0 stars, no releases, created 2026-09-21, and HEAD equals upstream 0x7067/claude-jev v0.27.0 (19 stars, 4 forks, a release). Install and track upstream, not this fork, to avoid divergence and supply-chain risk.

Egress of code to a third party with no redaction: edit hunks, Bash diffs, prompts and the whole transcript (compaction) go to OpenRouter and TypeSafe. That is a real issue for client projects, and it is not covered by the user's existing no-secret-leak hook. OPENROUTER_API_KEY is also not in that hook's protected vars.

False-positive blocks: 9.3% of previously accepted real edits are blocked, and the README's own measurement shows 17 came from one repo's comment-ban rule. Stop-hook false blocks are documented. Rules-blocking is annoying in autonomous auto/bypassPermissions sessions and can waste Opus turns.

Subagent router overrides model via updatedInput and defaults to cheaper tiers (matches the user's pick only 160/300 times, 89 dearer, 51 cheaper). With an Opus 5.5 main model this can silently downgrade Explore/Plan/general-purpose subagents to haiku/sonnet, and can deny a spawn once for missing commit policy. Rule text mentions a 'fable' tier that may not exist for this user.

Compaction replacement needs the undocumented CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS flag and runs in-process. It replaces Claude Code's native summary with truncated rows, which is a risky change to a core behavior. It also brings the /claude-jev pane. Not recommended.
Per-Bash-call overhead: 2-3 node spawns plus git add -A into a scratch index, which writes blobs into .git/objects, on top of the existing gitnexus Bash hooks. Slow on large repos.

Hook commands use bare 'node --experimental-strip-types'. With PATH overridden in the user's settings env, node may not be found and the hooks silently do nothing. It would need absolute-path wrapper commands. README is stale ('Python stdlib', 'python3 only'), and the runtime is now TypeScript on Node 24, which is fine for this user but an inconsistency.

Prompt routing hints have low value: 14.1% coverage and 48% accuracy on the hints shown, lift +5.2 points. It costs a network call on every prompt. Independent Jev evals also warn of overconfidence and injection sensitivity in state.
Optional 51MB ast-grep binary auto-download in a detached process.
No unit tests. Validation is offline eval scripts on the author's own private transcripts (not committed), and CI only smoke-tests malformed input.
entries.verdict: Functionally the most complete, automatic Jev integration and OpenRouter-native with fail-open hooks, but this specific repo is a 0-star fork identical to upstream 0x7067/claude-jev, so adopt upstream. Enable only the rules check (and maybe the subagent brief check) after testing on non-client repos, since it sends diffs to a third party without redaction, has a measured about 9% false-block rate, adds Bash-hook latency, and its subagent-downgrade and function-hook compaction features are risky for an Opus-main setup.

entries.name: danielhirt/truthsayer
entries.what: Rust workspace (library crate `truthsayer` + CLI binary `truthsayer`) shipped with a Claude Code plugin. The plugin registers hooks (SessionStart, PreToolUse on Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit, PostToolUse *, PostToolUseFailure *, Stop) that pipe the event JSON to `truthsayer hook`. The binary builds a redacted, capped observation (task from transcript, constraints from config, tool input/output, up to 12 earlier calls), sends 1-2 requests of Jev Noul questions ({model,state,questions}) to TypeSafe or OpenRouter /alpha/decisions, applies threshold rules from JSON rubrics in code, and in enforce mode emits deny/ask/additionalContext/block/system messages. Rubrics: edit (changes_behavior, violates_constraint, outside_task), tool-result (failed, relevant, injected_instructions), progress (repeating, momentum), turn-end (claims complete, unverified_claim, needs user). Also has replay/label/report/eval tooling for threshold tuning from recorded JSONL.
entries.autoInvocation: Fully deterministic hook: triggers automatically on every matched tool event and Stop with no user prompt or model choice. Matches the user's wish for automatic use, but Claude never 'uses' Jev; the harness does, and only enforce mode feeds results back to Claude.
security: Key handling: API key read only from env var (hook.rs judge_from l.449-455, http.rs bearer_auth); never on argv and not written to records; the detached log-mode child inherits env. Consequence: OPENROUTER_API_KEY must sit in Claude Code's own environment, so the agent's Bash can read it via env/printenv; add it to no-secret-leak.cjs protected vars (and consider a dedicated low-limit key).

Egress control: project .claude/truthsayer.toml cannot set backend/endpoint/model/api_key_env/timeout; a project file containing them is ignored entirely (docs/claude-code.md:99-101; config.rs test with attacker.test endpoint l.323). Good defense against malicious repos redirecting data.

Shell exec: none of the model output is executed. The only spawn is Command::new(current_exe()) for log-mode background (main.rs:432-459) with fixed args. Shim script only execs TRUTHSAYER_BIN, PATH truthsayer, or ~/.cargo/bin/truthsayer; a PATH-planted binary would run as hook, standard risk.

Installer: cargo install --git HEAD of a 0-star, 11-commit repo, no release/tag, so unaudited supply chain and floating HEAD unless pinned with --rev; Cargo.lock committed and --locked used. No install.sh, no telemetry besides the Jev call, no other network endpoints found in source (grep).

Prompt-injection surface: tool outputs (web pages, files) are fed to Jev as state; injected text can try to suppress the injected_instructions flag (per Jev brief, injected instructions in state can move answers). Since code rules decide and the model only returns probabilities, the blast radius is limited to missed/false flags, not arbitrary actions. Findings returned to Claude are prefixed as automatic, possibly-wrong checks (hook.rs for_claude).

Redaction is regex best effort (sk-*, apikey_, gh tokens, AWS, Slack, Google, JWT, PEM, URL creds, NAME=value with SECRET/TOKEN/PASSWORD/API_KEY etc, Bearer/Basic) and secret files (.env, *.pem, *.key, .netrc, .pgpass) are withheld only when the tool path names them (hook.rs withhold_secret_files). Bash `cat .env` or secrets in code/prose outside those patterns still leave the machine. Authors state redaction is not exhaustive.
entries.dataEgress: Per checked event, to OpenRouter (then TypeSafe): current user prompt capped at 2000 chars, configured constraints, tool name and tool input (each string capped 4000 chars, secret-file content withheld), tool output/error capped at 4000 chars (head+tail kept), up to 12 earlier calls in the turn (name/input/output each string capped 200 chars), and at Stop the final assistant message capped 4000 chars; all passed through regex redaction. X-Title: truthsayer header sent. For PostToolUse * this means source code from Read/Grep/Bash output, diffs and command output of client projects are transmitted on essentially every tool call except bookkeeping tools. Mitigation: mode=off in .claude/truthsayer.toml per client project (a project file can lower mode) or globally off and enable per personal project via TRUTHSAYER_MODE. Cost approx $0.00003 per check per README.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open everywhere: any error (missing key, timeout, HTTP error, bad JSON, missing answer, missing binary) prints nothing and exits 0 (hook.rs header, main.rs hook_main, docs/claude-code.md Failures section; shim exits 0 if binary absent). Judge timeout 8000 ms default inside a 15 s hook timeout; HttpJudge retries 429/5xx up to 3 times with 0.8/1.6/3.2 s backoff or retry-after up to 10 s (http.rs:25-27,185-200) but the outer tokio timeout caps total at timeout_ms. Reqwest client timeout 30 s but outer cap dominates. Enforce-mode false positives are the real failure: edit rule violates_constraint >=0.7 denies edits, uncertain (0.3-0.7) asks the user; repeating judge false-positives on verify-after-change calls (0.78-0.88 in author eval) produce warn noise; injected_instructions >=0.7 escalates and can decision:block PostToolUse. Caveat I could not verify (docs fetch hit rate limit): emitting hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext with hookEventName Stop and relying on it to make Claude continue once (hook.rs:373-380) may not be honored by Claude Code 2.1.285, since Stop is documented to continue via decision:block/reason; test in log/advise before trusting the stop-verifier behavior.
entries.contextCost: Zero MCP tools, zero skills, no SessionStart context injection (only a user-visible systemMessage on misconfig). Hook-injected text only when a finding acts (mode enforce): about 250-500 chars (~60-125 tokens) per finding set, e.g. the 'truthsayer, an automatic check by a separate model...' preamble plus reason and hint lines. Log/advise modes inject nothing to the model. Negligible skill-budget impact.
pros: OpenRouter is first-class in code: /api/alpha/decisions with Bearer OPENROUTER_API_KEY, model/endpoint overridable in user config (http.rs:36-57, config keys in docs/claude-code.md:75-81); no patching needed.

Safe rollout by design: default mode log (background, records only, no behavior change), then advise, then enforce; per-project mode=off and TRUTHSAYER_MODE env override give a cheap kill switch for client repos.
Strong fail-open behavior and shim no-ops if binary missing; project config cannot redirect endpoint/key/model (config-injection defense with a test), Stop nudge limited via stop_hook_active.
Redaction plus secret-file withholding before send and before record; records 0600; key only via env, never argv.
Zero MCP/skill context cost; injected text only on findings and clearly labeled as fallible automatic check.

Covers ground the user lacks: Stop verification of unsupported success claims, injected-instruction detection in tool output, constraint enforcement on edits, loop detection; includes replay/label/report tooling to tune thresholds from own sessions with no extra judge calls.

Decent engineering hygiene for a new repo: CI with clippy -D warnings, shellcheck, MSRV, SHA-pinned actions, mock-server HTTP tests, published eval run with honest caveats (14 misses listed, synthetic labels admitted).
cons: Brand new and unproven: 0 stars, 1 author, 11 commits over 9 days, no releases or tags; cargo install from git HEAD builds unaudited third-party code (pin --rev if used).

OpenRouter path never exercised live by the author: eval and README examples used TypeSafe direct; default OpenRouter model alias `~typesafe/jev-latest` unverified against the user's brief (typesafe/jev-1.13), so set model explicitly and test with `truthsayer doctor` plus a log-mode run.

Data egress is broad for client work: prompt, tool inputs and up to 4000 chars of every tool output (file reads, Bash output) go to OpenRouter then TypeSafe on almost every tool call; regex redaction is admittedly incomplete; also duplicates content into a local records.jsonl.
OPENROUTER_API_KEY must be in Claude Code's own environment, exposing it to agent Bash; user's no-secret-leak.cjs does not yet protect it. Also TypeSafe key silently wins if both set.

In advise/enforce every PostToolUse adds ~0.5 s (new process and TLS handshake each time) on top of existing gitnexus hooks; log mode has no latency but then Claude gets no benefit, so value only appears after enforce, which risks false-positive denies/blocks from an alpha-endpoint, imperfectly calibrated model (author's own repeating false positives 0.78-0.88; eval labels model-written, synthetic).

The Stop-hook re-prompt relies on hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext for Stop, which I could not confirm Claude Code honors (Stop normally uses decision:block); PreToolUse 'ask' decision behavior under bypassPermissions/auto is also unclear, so parts of the enforce design may be no-ops for this user's frequent bypass sessions.
Author explicitly says no evidence yet that it improves cost, speed or task success (benchmark only planned).
entries.verdict: Best-in-class conceptual fit (automatic hook-driven Jev checks, native OpenRouter, fail-open, log-first rollout), but it is a 9-day-old single-author alpha whose OpenRouter path is only mock-tested, sends up to 4000 chars of every tool output off-machine, and needs a cargo build plus the API key in Claude's env. Reasonable to trial in log mode on personal projects (pinned commit, explicit model, mode=off for client repos, add OPENROUTER_API_KEY to no-secret-leak.cjs) rather than enforce it.

judge.why: Best safety design of the deep-audited suites: log-first rollout, per-project kill switch and a project config that cannot redirect the endpoint or key. But it is a Rust build from unpinned git HEAD, and it egresses the most content.
