entries.name: 0x7067/claude-jev
entries.what: Claude Code plugin (marketplace 0x7067/claude-jev, v0.27.0) that wires Jev into lifecycle hooks with no MCP server and no skills. (1) UserPromptSubmit: classifies each prompt (intent/scope/needs-tools) and injects a one-line additionalContext hint ("one search", "focused edit"). (2) PreToolUse Agent|Task: picks a subagent model tier (haiku/sonnet/opus/fable) and rewrites the call's model via updatedInput; also denies the spawn once if a file-changing brief lacks paths, acceptance criteria, verification, or commit policy. (3) PostToolUse Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit plus Stop: parses CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.claude/rules/.cursor/rules into rules and asks Jev batched Noul yes/no questions ("does this hunk violate rule X"), blocking at p>=0.80 with a file:line citation and flagging at 0.50-0.80 (second escalation call). (4) Pre/PostToolUse Bash and PostToolUseFailure: snapshots the git working tree in a scratch index so Stop can judge shell writes. (5) Optional experimental session.compact function hook, gated by CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1, which replaces Claude's LLM summary with the transcript rows Jev scores as worth keeping (verbatim, no summary). Also a /claude-jev settings pane, eval harness, a stats report, and an AFK-host adapter. Runtime is Node type-stripping TypeScript (src/*.ts) for hooks; the Python scripts are mostly eval/stats/reference.
interface: hook PreToolUse + PostToolUse + PostToolUseFailure Bash -> src/rules.ts
entries.autoInvocation: Deterministic hooks: fully automatic, no user prompting and no model discretion. UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse Agent|Task, PostToolUse edit tools, PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure Bash and Stop all fire on every matching event. Compaction fires via the experimental session.compact function hook when CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1.
security: API key sent as Authorization: Bearer header from process env/fetch, not argv; the ast-grep fetch is detached Popen with sha256 pin (scripts/comparators.py:125). Saved key stored via plugin userConfig (exposed to hooks as CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_TYPESAFEAPIKEY).

No npm postinstall, no curl|sh; package.json is private with dev-only deps. Hooks run node from the plugin dir. One runtime binary download: ast-grep zip from github.com/ast-grep releases, sha256-verified, into ~/.claude/jev-bin, triggered automatically the first time an edit needs it.

Local telemetry only: writes ~/.claude/jev-calls.jsonl, jev-router-log.jsonl (includes first 200 chars of subagent prompts and prompt hints), jev-compact-log.jsonl, rules cache; no third-party telemetry found. JEV_BASE_URL env can redirect all traffic.

Prompt-injection surface: repo instruction files and diffs are fed to Jev as state; Jev only returns typed probabilities (no free text), so injection can at most flip a yes/no; but a false positive blocks edits and a false router decision silently downgrades subagent model. Hook outputs (additionalContext, deny reason) are plugin-authored templates, not model text.

Hooks run with the user's privileges on every Bash call (git snapshot via scratch index with GIT_INDEX_FILE) and read the full transcript file (~/.claude/projects) for context; installing it adds 6 hook entries that execute third-party code on every prompt/tool use on personal and client repos.
Compaction uses an undocumented experimental function-hook flag; author's own research doc records what was verified only for Claude Code 2.1.278.
entries.dataEgress: To Jev endpoint (OpenRouter or api.typesafe.ai): (a) every prompt you type (minus slash/#/<3 chars) plus the previous user and assistant turn text (tail of transcript, up to 400 lines scanned); (b) for each Edit/Write: old->new hunks (<=2000 chars each), surrounding lines (<=1200 chars), the last prompt tail (400 chars), sibling module names for import rules, function context on escalation, plus the text of your CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.claude/rules rule sentences (up to 40 rules/call, state capped ~8000 chars); (c) at Stop, all turn hunks up to 16000 chars including shell-made diffs from git snapshots (so untracked new files' contents can be included); (d) subagent prompt text (~600 chars task) and agent type; (e) on compaction, transcript blocks (user messages, tool calls and results, up to 3000 chars each, 300 rows) including file contents and command outputs. Client-project code, instruction files and secrets that appear in diffs/tool output will reach OpenRouter and its upstream (TypeSafe) provider; the existing secret-leak guard hook does not sit in this path.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open by design: no key -> silent no-op; HTTP error/timeout/no answers -> hook prints nothing and exits 0 (jev-client.ts:156-190, README). Default per-call timeout 8s (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS=8000), hook timeout 10s in hooks.json, rules.ts overall budget 9s (HOOK_BUDGET), compaction ask 4s then built-in summary. Retry once on fast network failure (Python client; TS deadline-based). Worst case a slow/down Jev adds up to ~8-10s to a prompt or edit before failing open. Only fail-closed behaviours are intentional decisions: rule blocks (p>=0.80) and one-time subagent-brief deny. Exception: the Bash PreToolUse git snapshot runs even without a key? enabled('rules') gate only; unverified if snapshot skips when key missing.
entries.contextCost: Zero tools and zero MCP instructions (no MCP server, no skills), so no standing tool-definition tokens. Injected text: UserPromptSubmit adds one short line only for lookup/fix prompts (~15-25 tokens, roughly 14% of prompts show a hint per the README); rule blocks/flags add a systemMessage or block reason with file:line citations (~50-200 tokens, on ~9% of edits); subagent hook adds a systemMessage line per spawn (~20 tokens) and a deny reason on poor briefs. Compaction, if enabled, produces rows (3.2-3.9k tokens) instead of an LLM summary. Net context cost is very low; the real cost is hook process spawns.
pros: Only candidate reviewed that is truly automatic: pure hooks, so Claude Code uses Jev without any 'use jev' prompt and without adding tools to the context window (zero MCP tool tokens).

OpenRouter is a first-class provider in code (jev-client.ts:69-72: openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone, sk-or- prefix autodetect, provider pin, plus optional alpha/decisions backend); author ran the full evals through OpenRouter. Setup is one env var.

Uses Jev for what it is actually good at: typed yes/no and choice decisions with calibrated probabilities (rule-violation Noul checks, tier Choice), with local pre-filtering, ast-grep context, thresholds (0.80 block/0.50 flag/0.10 quiet) and a twice-per-file block cap to avoid loops.
Fail-open everywhere with explicit timeouts (8s call, 10s hook, 9s rules budget, 4s compaction) and fallback to Claude's built-in summary; stats/logs let you audit calls (jev-calls.jsonl).
Compaction replacement is a concrete high-value use: ~1s vs 30-120s, verbatim keep of user constraints (author's planted-constraint probe 97.8%, buried restatement 96.6%).

Enforces your existing CLAUDE.md rules as a second-opinion reviewer (author: catches 16/29 hand-written violations at 0.80 with 9% false-block on accepted edits), pairs well with your global instructions.

Active, well-documented, MIT, 182 commits in 10 days, releases with changelog, honest about weak labels and negative results (e.g. router hints only +5.2 lift over constant guess), per-hook on/off toggles.
cons: Very new and single-author (171 of 182 commits, 19 stars, created 2026-09-18, 27 minor releases in 10 days); no unit tests, only self-run evals with weak labels; README is stale (still says Python-only while hooks.json runs Node type-stripping TS), Windows issue open.

Broad data egress: your prompts, previous assistant turn, edit diffs, surrounding lines, git-snapshot diffs incl. untracked file contents, subagent briefs and (with compaction) tool outputs go to OpenRouter and TypeSafe. Problematic for client projects/NDAs; your secret-leak guard does not cover this path. No per-repo allowlist found (only global toggles).

9.3% of previously accepted real edits would have been blocked (author's own number), and 8 of 16 human-labeled router hints disagreed 5/16; blocks are PostToolUse so the write has already happened and Claude must repair it. In bypass/auto permission mode a false-positive loop costs turns (capped 2 per file).

Subagent router rewrites model via updatedInput: on an Opus 5.5 main model it goes cheaper 51/300 times but dearer 89/300 in author's own replay; on a subscription this saves little money and can silently downgrade quality. Can also deny the first spawn of any file-changing brief lacking commit policy etc., which is intrusive.
Prompt router hints are weak: accuracy 48% on the hints shown, only +5.2 points over guessing, 8 harmful hints in 2,464; adds a blocking network call to every prompt for tiny value.

Hook overhead on every Bash call (git scratch-index snapshot before and after, plus PostToolUseFailure) and every edit/turn stop; stacks on your existing Bash hooks (secret guard, GitNexus pre/post) and may slow agent loops in large repos.

Compaction (the best feature) needs undocumented CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1, only trusted-workspace, never subagents, verified only on 2.1.278; could break on 2.1.285 updates. It also discards LLM summaries entirely, a risky trade.

Default model id is bare 'jev-latest' rather than OpenRouter's typesafe/jev-1.13 / ~typesafe/jev-latest; alias acceptance on OpenRouter is claimed by changelog but not verified here. If TYPESAFE_API_KEY exists it silently wins over OpenRouter unless provider pinned.

Downloads and executes a 51 MB ast-grep binary automatically in a detached process (sha256 pinned, but still unrequested code execution on a client machine); Jev is a beta, skeptic-questioned model and the plugin makes real blocking decisions on its output.

Bash hooks (Pre, Post, PostToolUseFailure) run git add -A into a scratch index on every Bash call even with no API key; this writes loose objects into the real .git/objects (including unignored untracked secrets) and re-hashes untracked files twice per command. In linked worktrees (`git rev-parse --git-path index` returns an absolute path, then path.join(root, abs) is wrong, src/rules.ts:1007-1010) the index copy likely fails so the scratch index starts empty and the whole tree is re-hashed each time (medium confidence, not run).
All 8 hook commands use bare `node`; this user's overridden PATH in settings env will break them unless node is on that PATH; failures are noisy on every prompt/tool call.

No secret redaction on any egress path (prompts, Edit/Write hunks, git-snapshot diffs, compaction tool output) and the user's no-secret-leak hook does not match Edit/Write or UserPromptSubmit; OPENROUTER_API_KEY is also not in its protected-vars list, and this plugin makes the key resident in every hook process env.

UserPromptSubmit sends every prompt to OpenRouter and blocks submission up to 10s on an outage or slow call (no circuit breaker; each hook repeats the full 8s timeout independently), for hints the author's own eval shows barely beat guessing.

Stop hook can block turn end (decision:block) on a probabilistic judge, up to 2 times per session; in bypassPermissions/auto sessions this adds unattended repair loops driven by an 'accuracy a bit below mid-price LLMs, overconfident' model, and repo instruction files/diffs (untrusted content) are model input so an injected instruction can flip a block.

Plugin is a single-author 10-day-old project with rapid churn (README stale vs hooks, runtime rewritten Python->TS at 0.24.0 on 2026-09-26); auto-updating plugin means new third-party code runs in every hook with user privileges.
Auto-fetches a 51 MB ast-grep binary in a detached process with no consent prompt (sha256 pinned, adapters/afk/src/shared/comparators.ts:15,117-119,186).
entries.verdict: Best-fitting candidate for the 'automatic, no prompting' requirement: hook-based, zero context cost, OpenRouter supported in code, fail-open. Adopt selectively on personal repos with OPENROUTER_API_KEY, keep rules + compaction (and maybe stop-time checks), disable promptRouter and subagentRouter, and avoid on client repos unless you accept diffs and tool output leaving the machine.

verification.note: Repo facts re-verified via gh: 19 stars, MIT, not archived, pushed 2026-09-28 (b04c634), 182 commits (171 Pedro Guimaraes), 2 open issues (#23 Windows fcntl, #24 AFK), created 2026-09-18. OpenRouter support is genuine in code: TS client posts {state,model,questions} with Bearer to https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone (jev-client.ts:70) or opt-in https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions (jev-client.ts:147), env OPENROUTER_API_KEY; TYPESAFE_API_KEY wins under auto (jev-client.ts:120-133). Default model string is bare 'jev-latest' (jev-client.ts:50), not the brief's jev-1.13; changelog line 40 says OpenRouter served it, but I did not make a live call, so alias acceptance is only author-asserted. Claude Code correctness checked against installed 2.1.285 binary: hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput (applied independently of permissionDecision), UserPromptSubmit additionalContext, PostToolUse decision:block, Stop decision:block, PostToolUseFailure, and the session.compact function hook gated by CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS all exist, so the audit's Claude Code claims hold. Most audit numbers (thresholds 0.80/0.50, 8s/10s/9s/4s timeouts, char caps, ast-grep sha256, local-only telemetry) match source. Score lowered 7 to 6: the audit's own verdict already excluded client repos and two of the four routers, and the corrections add unconditional per-Bash git object writes, bare-node PATH breakage under this user's env override, no redaction and no coverage of Edit/Write by the secret guard, and unattended Stop-block loops in bypass mode. It remains the most on-target automatic integration (no tools, zero standing context, real OpenRouter path), so not lower than 6. Recommend only with promptRouter and subagentRouter off, rules on selectively, and absolute node path and secret-hook coverage fixed first.

judge.why: Most complete automatic suite with real measurements and fail-open hooks, but it egresses code unredacted, has a measured 9.3% false-block rate and its subagent router can silently downgrade models on an Opus setup. Adopt only the rules check, if anything.
pros: Fully deterministic and OpenRouter-ready; per-feature toggles (promptRouter, subagentRouter, rules, compaction)
Per-edit CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md rule enforcement with file:line, which targets a real gap; blocks the same file at most twice per session
Fail-open with hard timeouts; near-zero standing context (no MCP, no skills); honest eval reporting and incident write-ups
MIT, active, versioned changelog
cons: No redaction anywhere: edit hunks, Bash diffs, prompts and the whole transcript (compaction) go to OpenRouter and TypeSafe
9.3% of previously accepted real edits were blocked, and Stop-hook false blocks are documented; noisy in auto and bypass sessions
Subagent router rewrites `model` via updatedInput and matches your own pick only about half the time, so it can downgrade Explore/Plan subagents from Opus

Per Bash call, 2-3 node spawns plus git add -A into a scratch index (writes blobs into .git/objects) on top of gitnexus. Hook commands use bare `node`, and your PATH override may silently disable them
Prompt-routing hints have 48% accuracy on the hints shown; compaction replacement needs the undocumented function-hook flag; no unit tests; optional 51 MB ast-grep download

entries.name: jev-harness (dansya-arsana)
entries.what: Not a real plugin.json/marketplace plugin but a skill + hooks + subagent bundle installed by symlink into ~/.claude. Three Python stdlib hooks call Jev via /v1/systemone: (1) PreToolUse permission gate on Bash/Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit (regex hard deny/ask rules, fast-allow list, and only for the gray zone one Jev call with 4 noul plus 1 choice question; never emits allow), (2) UserPromptSubmit prompt router (Jev picks at most one skill from the installed skill roster and fires user-defined conditional instruction rules, injecting additionalContext), (3) PreToolUse Agent|Task dispatch router that rewrites the subagent_type of jev-* dispatches. Also ships 9 jev-* effort-tiered subagents pinned to claude-opus-5-5, a jev-orchestrator SKILL (route/stuck/dedupe CLI, context packs) and a browser-QA tool (jevqa.py, needs the separate browser-use/jev-ultrafast repo). Evals reported: gate 64/64 held-out, routing 47/50 (self/model-labelled, no real traffic).
entries.autoInvocation: Deterministic hooks (PreToolUse gate on Bash/Write/Edit, UserPromptSubmit router, PreToolUse Agent|Task dispatch router) fire automatically without any user prompting; the skill/subagent orchestration part (jev.py route/dedupe/packs) is only skill-description-triggered and model-discretion. Prompt router only suggests skills; it does not force them.
security: No npm postinstall, no curl|sh; install.sh is local-only but rewrites ~/.claude/settings.json (with backup), symlinks into ~/.claude/skills and ~/.claude/agents, and mv's conflicting files to ~/.claude/backups. It is zsh and macOS-oriented (sips, /Library, /Users patterns, csrutil) so Linux behaviour is only partly exercised.

API key never put in argv: sent as Authorization header over HTTPS via urllib (jevlib.py:48-51); read from env or .env / ~/.config/typesafe/.env. Key for the QA tool is put into os.environ of the jevqa process.
Egress redaction is regex-based (bearer, sk-/ghp_/xox tokens, key=value patterns, PEM) and best-effort; not a guarantee.

Prompt-injection surface: prompt_router injects additionalContext built from skill descriptions / SKILL.md openings (from all installed plugins) plus user-defined condition text/files; Jev sees untrusted file content (script_contents up to 8000 chars, agent dispatch prompt 1500 chars) and its answer can only pick among fixed options, so injection can at worst bias allow/ask/deny or the tier. Gate never outputs allow, so a manipulated Jev cannot auto-approve; it can only downgrade an ask to silence (gray-zone commands fall through to the normal permission flow, which is bypass for this user).
Dispatch router emits permissionDecision allow with updatedInput for Agent calls, which could bypass ask prompts from other hooks for Agent tool (minor).

Gate regexes are heuristic: in bypass mode the only protection for gray commands is Jev's opinion; fast-allow list includes plain git push, npm install, pip install -r, docker build/compose up; obfuscated commands go to Jev. Overlaps with, and may conflict in ordering with, the user's existing secret-leak PreToolUse guard.
entries.dataEgress: To the Jev endpoint (OpenRouter then TypeSafe, per the override): (a) every user prompt >=15 chars that is not a filler/harness/slash message, redacted, first 4000 chars, plus names and 220-char descriptions of all installed skills (project, ~/.claude/skills, ~/.agents/skills, plugin cache) and the text of the user's condition questions, on every prompt (second call adds top-3 skill descriptions and 1200 chars of each SKILL.md); (b) each gray-zone Bash command (redacted, up to 4000 chars) plus cwd, permission mode, and up to 8000 chars of the script file it would run; Write/Edit calls are only checked locally by regex; (c) Agent/Task dispatch description plus first 1500 chars of the subagent prompt for jev-* dispatches; (d) when the model runs the CLI: subtask text, context_from_main_agent, recent agent activity for stuck checks, and code chunks for jevpack slices (whole function/class chunks of project files, secrets files skipped). Not sent: full diffs or the whole transcript automatically; transcript tail is only read locally for path matching. Client code can reach OpenRouter/TypeSafe via (b) and (d); no zero-data-retention guarantee verified.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open by design everywhere. jevlib.ask retries only on 429/5xx/connection errors (default 3 tries with sleep up to 5s, but hooks pass retries=1). Gate: 4s timeout, on Jev error falls back to regex only and emits ask only if command combines network with script/secret/obfuscation, else passes silently; hook timeout 10s; hard-deny regexes need no network. Prompt router: 5s per call, 8s overall deadline, on error injects nothing, exits 0 (hook timeout 15s). Dispatch router: 4s, any error means no rewrite. Missing key raises JevError inside try and is swallowed, so a misconfigured OpenRouter setup silently degrades to regex-only gate plus no routing (visible only in ~/.claude/jev logs / jev.py report). Worst-case added stall per event is bounded to about 4-8s.
entries.contextCost: Zero MCP tools and no MCP server instructions. Standing context: skill jev-orchestrator description (~700 chars, about 175 tokens in the skill list; body about 15 KB / 3.8k tokens loaded only when invoked); 9 subagent descriptions in the Agent tool listing (about 9 x 40-60 tokens, roughly 400-600 tokens); per-prompt hook text is a single <skill_relevance> line (~50 tokens) only when a skill is suggested, plus user-defined condition text (up to 8000 chars cap, typically none). Subagent bodies only cost when spawned. Overall roughly 600-800 standing tokens plus rare injections.
pros: The only candidate seen so far that is truly automatic: three hooks wired to Jev with no user prompting, matching the 'Claude Code must use it when needed' requirement.

OpenRouter switch is one choke point (jevlib.py:14-15) already env-overridable: TYPESAFE_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api yields /api/v1/systemone, the same System One route OpenRouter documents; only key/model-id env changes, no fork needed (pending a curl smoke test).
Uses Jev correctly per its brief: typed Choice/Noul questions, thresholds in code, Jev never writes text; response reading matches answers[q].choice/probabilities/noul.

Fail-open everywhere with bounded timeouts (4-8s), hard-deny regex layer works offline, gate never emits allow, README claims deny honoured in bypassPermissions (relevant since user runs bypass/auto).
Small readable stdlib-only Python (about 3.5k lines), no MCP tools, no npm/uvx install, so cheap on context (about 600-800 tokens) and easy to audit; MIT.

Useful for a bypass-mode user: gray-zone command review by Jev with script-content inspection, secrets-file edit ask, and force-push/reset --hard/sudo ask rules add a safety net complementary to the existing secret-leak hook.
Has unit tests, held-out evals with committed results, and honest write-up of overfitting and negative results (context packs cost +7-25% tokens).
Backups plus uninstall script; every hook has an env kill switch (JEV_GATE, JEV_ROUTER, JEV_DISPATCH).

The hook input and output fields it uses are valid in Claude Code 2.1.x: PreToolUse hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision (deny/ask), UserPromptSubmit additionalContext, updatedInput, and the permission_mode input field. It never exits 2.
Zero-dependency Python stdlib, about 3.5k lines and small enough to audit. The API key goes in the Authorization header, not argv, and there is no telemetry beyond the configured endpoint.
Clean single choke point (jevlib.API_URL and MODEL), so any schema fix is a few lines.
Fast path: routine and read-only commands are decided locally in about 45 ms with no network call.
cons: Bus factor and maturity: 4 commits, 1 author, 0 stars, created 6 days before audit, no release, no CI, PoC by its own description; evals are self/model-labelled, not real traffic.

Adds about 1-2 s to nearly every user prompt (skill routing for a benefit that is only a hint) and about 1 s to gray-zone Bash calls, serially; the user already has many skills so the roster call is large and re-sent every prompt.

Data egress is broad for client work: every prompt (4000 chars), the full installed-skill roster, gray-zone commands and script contents, subagent prompts go to OpenRouter/TypeSafe; regex redaction is best-effort; local jsonl logs keep prompt/command snippets.

Much of the value overlaps with things the user has: an existing PreToolUse secret guard (ordering/duplicate asks) and Claude Code's own skill matching; in bypass mode 'ask' outputs are unverified to be honoured (README only demonstrates deny), so gray-zone protection may reduce to deny-only.

Orchestrator half (jev-* agents, route/dedupe/stuck, dispatch router) is opinionated: it only fires if the model chooses jev-* subagents, forces claude-opus-5-5 pinned agents with a custom effort doctrine, and the dispatch router only rewrites jev-* types, so it does nothing for normal Task/Agent use; SKILL.md is ~15 KB.

macOS-centric: install.sh is #!/bin/zsh, discover() scans ~/Library/Application Support, regex uses /Users /System paths and macOS-only commands, jevqa uses sips; on Linux the core hooks work but this is untested by the author, and the QA tool depends on a second unaudited repo.

Misconfiguration is silent (missing key or wrong OpenRouter model id degrades to no-op with errors only in ~/.claude/jev logs); model id in code default is 'jev-latest' not OpenRouter's 'typesafe/jev-latest' so must be overridden.

install.sh --hooks mutates ~/.claude/settings.json and moves existing files; must be read/hand-applied given the user's custom global hooks, and I could not confirm OpenRouter's System One schema equals TypeSafe's.

Possible OpenRouter schema mismatch (noul criteria field on every noul question and dict-valued state versus the documented string state and criteria-less noul). If rejected, all Jev features silently no-op while the regex layer keeps running, and the user may believe Jev is active.

Regex hard-deny layer is macOS-tuned and prone to false positives with no override in bypass: SECRET_REF matches any mention of .env, .pem, .ssh or .claude/settings.json, and NET_SEND matches git push, gh api, curl or a bare socket. Example: git rm --cached .env && git push is denied outright, and a Jev deny in bypass mode blocks a command the user chose to run without prompts.

Jev is documented as overconfident on unanswerable input and injectable through state. The gate feeds it untrusted script contents (8000 chars) and command text. In auto mode any Jev ask or deny choice under 0.8 becomes a prompt, so miscalibration becomes friction in the user's default mode.

Ask-to-silent-pass in bypass mode means the Jev gray-zone review adds latency (about 1 s per gray command) and egress in bypass sessions but only ever blocks on hard deny, so its benefit there is small relative to cost.

Gray-zone Bash commands and script contents (client code, up to 8000 chars, regex-redacted) go to OpenRouter, and every user prompt of 15+ chars (first 4000 chars) is sent on UserPromptSubmit, for client projects with unverified retention. OpenRouter also sees the roster of installed skill names and descriptions.

Ownership drift: the newest commit came from a second account (ronel) with an AI co-author trailer, pushed the same day as this check, so reviewed code can change quickly. Pin to a commit SHA and re-review before updating.

Key is read only from TYPESAFE_API_KEY (env or .env files), not OPENROUTER_API_KEY, so the user must alias the OpenRouter key under that name, and the user's no-secret-leak hook does not protect this variable. Putting it in the settings.json env block also puts it in a file the gate itself treats as secret.

Only the permission gate and prompt router yield automatic value. Skill routing overlaps with Claude Code's own skill matching, though it may help since skillListingBudgetFraction 0.02 truncates the skill list. The rest (jev-* agents pinned to claude-opus-5-5, dispatch router, jevpack, jevqa needing a second repo, sips) is inert or macOS-only for this user.
entries.verdict: Best-in-class for the 'automatic, no prompting' requirement because it is real hooks, and it is nearly OpenRouter-ready via TYPESAFE_BASE_URL/TYPESAFE_DEFAULT_MODEL env overrides, but it is a 6-day-old single-author PoC with broad prompt/command egress and 1-2 s per-prompt latency. Adopt selectively: hand-install only the permission gate (and possibly the prompt router with JEV_ROUTER off initially) after a curl smoke test against OpenRouter, skip the jev-* agent/effort doctrine and browser QA.

verification.note: The audit's core facts are mostly right: 0 stars, MIT, no OpenRouter string anywhere in the repo, TYPESAFE_BASE_URL override at jevlib.py:14, hook events valid. Stale: 5 commits, 2 contributors, and the 2026-09-30 commit that turns ask into a silent pass in bypass mode. Wrong: the must-override-model-id con. Missed: bare python3 in hook commands with a PATH override, and the OpenRouter schema risk. I score it 5.5, not 6.5, because OpenRouter compatibility is unproven and would fail silently, the deny paths are regexes with no override in bypass and are macOS-tuned, egress of every prompt and gray-zone command is broad for client work, and it is a 6-day-old PoC still changing. It remains the only candidate that is automatic through real hooks. If adopted, take only the permission gate, with absolute paths, a pinned commit SHA and a curl smoke test first, with JEV_ROUTER=off, and skip the agents, dispatch router and QA. Re-clone is at <scratch path> Nothing was executed.

judge.why: The only candidate here with a genuine Bash permission gate through real hooks (regex hard-deny layer plus a Jev gray-zone review), but its OpenRouter compatibility is unproven and would fail silently, and its regex denies are macOS-tuned.
pros: Valid Claude Code hook I/O (permissionDecision, additionalContext, permission_mode); stdlib-only Python, about 3.5k lines, auditable; key in the Authorization header
Fast local path for routine commands (about 45 ms, no network call); single choke point (API_URL, MODEL) for fixes
Since 2026-09-30, 'ask' becomes a silent pass in bypassPermissions, so only hard denies bite there
cons: If OpenRouter rejects the noul criteria field or dict state, every Jev call 400s and the hooks quietly degrade to regex-only while you believe Jev is active; a smoke test is mandatory
Regex hard denies are prone to false positives and cannot be overridden in bypass: a mention of .env, .pem, .ssh or settings.json plus git push, curl or gh api is denied outright
Sends every prompt of 15+ chars and gray-zone commands and scripts (up to 8000 chars) to OpenRouter
Hook commands use bare python3 and ~ paths, so under a PATH override they need absolute-path rewrites; install.sh is zsh/macOS-oriented and rewrites settings.json, so hand-merge instead
Key read only from TYPESAFE_API_KEY, so an alias is needed and it is not protected by no-secret-leak; jev-* agents, dispatch router, jevpack and QA are inert or macOS-only for you

entries.name: CaptainDigitals/jev-copilot
entries.what: Claude Code plugin (marketplace + plugin.json) bundling a zero-dependency stdio MCP server (13 tools), lifecycle hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd), 4 skills, 15 slash commands and a verifier subagent. On each substantive prompt a hook sends the redacted prompt (plus a small git repo summary) to OpenRouter's Decisions API (typesafe/jev-1.13) and injects a typed task profile plus a requirement contract as additionalContext. A local deterministic regex classifier (no Jev call by default) triages Bash/Write/Edit calls. A Stop hook runs a Jev completion review over changed-file names, test outcomes and Claude's last message, and can block the stop to force up to 2 repair loops. It also ships a YouTube transcript research engine (yt-dlp) that is unrelated to daily coding.
entries.autoInvocation: Deterministic hooks, with no model discretion needed. UserPromptSubmit fires for any non-trivial prompt and injects a Jev task profile automatically. Stop fires after edits and runs a completion review that can block. PreToolUse fires on every mutating tool call for regex hard rules (Jev only for high-impact actions if governance is enabled). The MCP tools, skills (description-triggered) and slash commands are supplementary and model-discretion. This is one of the few candidates that meets 'never say use jev' literally.
security: API key handling is good: the key reaches the MCP server as an env var from plugin userConfig (sensitive:true, .claude-plugin/plugin.json), so it does not show in argv. Fallback file ~/.jev-copilot/credentials.json is written mode 0600 (credentials.ts). A project .jev-copilot.json cannot override apiKey or endpoint (config.ts:206). The endpoint is https and host-allowlisted to openrouter.ai (client.ts:17).

Outbound redaction of ~15 secret patterns (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, GitHub, AWS, Slack, Stripe, Google, JWT, private keys, bearer, connection strings, *_SECRET/TOKEN= assignments) via redactValue before every call (runtime/index.ts). It is regex based, so custom or low-entropy secrets pasted into a prompt can still leak. Excluded paths (.env, *.pem, .ssh, .aws, credentials*) are never summarised.

No shell execution in the hook or MCP path. Only execFileSync('git', ...) with a 4 s timeout (context/discover.ts:16) and execFile for yt-dlp with an option allowlist (youtube/ytdlp.ts). No curl|sh, no postinstall (private package, zero deps; the only devDependencies are typescript and @types/node).

Telemetry is local only (telemetry.jsonl in the plugin data dir) and holds hashes, ids, latency and cost, not prompt text. No third-party analytics endpoint in dist (host grep shows only openrouter.ai, youtube.com and github.com strings).

Supply-chain risk: the committed dist/*.js is what runs, not the TypeScript. CI checks dist is not stale, but any install trusts a single anonymous account's compiled JS on every hook with the ability to read your prompts and inject context. It is a 3-day-old repo with no releases, so pin a commit SHA and review dist before installing.

Prompt-injection surface: the hook injects model-derived text into Claude's context (task profile, and Stop-hook 'reason' listing deficiencies). Content is generated from typed numbers and fixed templates, so the surface is small. The YouTube path handles untrusted captions with an explicit neutraliser (youtube/untrusted.ts) and is not relevant unless used.
entries.dataEgress: To openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions, per call: model id, the redacted user prompt (up to 12,000 chars, on nearly every prompt of 40+ chars), a repo summary (up to 40 top-level paths, top 6 file extensions, up to 20 git-diff --name-only changed files), on Stop the request (6000 chars), requirement texts, up to 40 changed-file paths per category, last 10 test commands (300 chars each) and outcomes, and Claude's last assistant message (4000 chars). With jev_context or jev_rank_context: up to 24 candidate paths with summaries (symbol names) and 600-char redacted head excerpts of source files. With tool governance on (off by default): the classified command/path state and the task text (2000 chars). Never full diffs or whole files. OpenRouter and TypeSafe therefore see your prompts and file paths. That matters for client projects: client code names and paths leave the machine, and a per-project .jev-copilot.json can set mode off. HTTP-Referer and X-Title headers identify the app. Response cache and telemetry stay local.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open by design in assist and enhance. No key means a degraded notice and no calls. Timeout is 8 s per attempt with 1 retry (400 ms base backoff, Retry-After honoured, capped 30 s), so the worst case is roughly 16 s of stall. The runner enforces a wall-clock budget (UserPromptSubmit 15 s, Stop 25 s, PreToolUse 10 s, PostToolUse 3 s), and on budget expiry the hook silently returns nothing (hooks/runner.ts:8-38). Any exception exits 0 with no output. A session budget of $0.25 skips optional calls. Strict mode is the only fail-closed variant: hard tool rules deny, and a Stop review outage tells Claude to flag manual review. Hidden costs: a blocking 20 s UserPromptSubmit hook can freeze the prompt when OpenRouter's alpha endpoint stalls, and the Decisions API is an /alpha path that can change its schema. Responses are schema-validated, and a malformed response is treated as failure and skipped.
entries.contextCost: MCP: 13 tools (7 general and 6 YouTube). Tool names, descriptions and schemas are about 6.7K chars, roughly 1.7K tokens (my regex estimate of src/mcp/server.ts and youtube-tools.ts register blocks), and the server sets no MCP 'instructions' field. Skills: 4 descriptions of roughly 400-600 chars each (about 0.5K tokens always loaded), bodies 2-4.4 KB on trigger. 15 slash commands add small frontmatter descriptions (about 0.5K tokens), and 1 agent description adds about 0.1K. Total always-on overhead is about 2.5-3K tokens, of which about 1K is YouTube-only clutter. Hook-injected text: SessionStart is about 2 lines (about 120 tokens) once per session. Each substantive prompt injects an ~8-10 line profile plus the requirement line (about 200-300 tokens per turn, accumulating in the transcript). A Stop repair block adds about 150-400 tokens plus the extra Opus turn that follows. It coexists with the existing gitnexus tool set, but the user already pays context for many MCP tools, and YouTube tools have no value here.
pros: Fully automatic without prompting: hooks.json wires UserPromptSubmit, Stop and PreToolUse to dist/src/hooks/runner.js, so Jev runs on prompts and at completion with zero user phrasing. This matches the stated requirement.

OpenRouter-native and correct for this user: endpoint https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions and model typesafe/jev-1.13 (defaults.json:3-4), with the key from OPENROUTER_API_KEY or the OS credential store. It does not need a TypeSafe account.

Fail-open and bounded: 8 s timeout, 1 retry, hard wall-clock budgets in hooks/runner.ts, an exit-0 catch-all, a $0.25 session budget and a local content-addressed decision cache. A Jev outage will not break Claude Code in enhance mode.

Solid privacy engineering for a young project: secret redaction on every outbound state, excluded paths, no file bodies or diffs in hooks, telemetry without prompt text, key in env not argv, project config cannot change the endpoint or key, mode 'off' available per project.

Zero runtime deps, no postinstall, no shell exec beyond execFileSync('git') with a timeout, tests plus a CI stale-dist check on three OSes. Cost per session is negligible (about $0.00002-0.00003 per call).

Good design principle in policy code: Jev only supplies typed probabilities, deterministic rules outrank Jev for tool safety, and JEV never invents file paths in context ranking. The Stop hook repair loop is capped at 2.
Removable per project (.jev-copilot.json mode off) and per plugin via the standard plugin uninstall, so client projects can opt out.
cons: Very immature and single-author: created 2026-09-27, 4 commits, 1 contributor, 0 stars/forks, no releases or tags, version 0.2.1, three days old on 2026-09-30. There is no community vetting, and the docs (PRD, roadmap, handoff) read as AI-generated scaffolding. The committed dist/ JS runs on every hook, so a supply-chain review or SHA pin is mandatory.

Scope creep: 6 of 13 MCP tools, 7 of 15 commands and a whole skill are a YouTube research engine irrelevant to coding. This costs about 1K tokens of always-on context and extra attack surface (yt-dlp exec).

Weak signal for its cost: the Stop-hook review sees only changed-file names, test outcomes and Claude's last message, never diffs or file contents (runtime/index.ts:155-176). Jev returning 'implementation complete' or 'regression likely' from filenames is close to noise, and each false 'repair' forces another Opus 5.5 turn (real tokens and time). The default thresholds are documented as uncalibrated starting points (defaults.json thresholds, README 'starting points for calibration, not truth').

The UserPromptSubmit profile (task type, complexity, tests needed) largely restates what Opus 5.5 infers itself, while adding a blocking network hop on every prompt (up to ~16 s if OpenRouter stalls) and ~250 tokens per turn. The value for an expert Opus workflow is marginal.

Sends every prompt of 40+ chars, plus file paths and Claude's last message, to OpenRouter and TypeSafe on client projects. Regex redaction will not catch client names, proprietary identifiers or non-key secrets. The user needs a per-project opt-out policy.

Hook overlap and friction with the existing setup: a node process spawns on every Bash/Edit/Write on top of the secret-leak guard and GitNexus hooks. Its hard rules (credential path access, download-and-execute, recursive delete) duplicate the secret guard and return permissionDecision 'ask', which could interrupt unattended bypass or auto-mode runs. Whether 'ask' overrides bypass mode was not verified.

Depends on OpenRouter's /api/alpha/decisions (alpha, beta model). Schema drift breaks it, though it fails open. Session-id matching for MCP/CLI uses the most recently modified session file (runtime/index.ts currentSessionId), which can attach to the wrong session with concurrent Claude Code windows.
No releases or CI-proven history, and the manifest pins no marketplace version. The README says npx-less, but the plugin cache path is hard-coded to version 0.2.1 in the docs.

Skepticism about Jev quality (Theo: 'a DeepSeek flash router') would apply directly here, since all value comes from Jev's calibrated probabilities on vague semantic questions and none is verifiable locally.
entries.verdict: The only candidate seen that is OpenRouter-native and automatic via hooks, and it is well engineered (fail-open, redaction, budgets, tests). It is still a 3-day-old solo project whose Jev signals (filename-based completion review, prompt classification) add latency, tokens and possible spurious repair loops for little gain over Opus 5.5. Worth trying only with SHA pinning, tool governance and Stop-block disabled or assist mode, and off on client repos. Otherwise treat it as a pattern to copy, not something to depend on.

judge.why: OpenRouter-native, automatic via hooks, with redaction, budgets and tests. Audit-only evidence; too new to trust.
pros: OpenRouter-native and hook-driven with fail-open behaviour
Redaction and spend budgets built in; tests present
cons: Three days old, 0 stars, single author, no verification
Hooks stack with gitnexus and no-secret-leak; egress of prompts or commands for client work not vetted

entries.name: reflex-hooks
entries.what: npm package reflex-hooks (TypeScript, Node>=22): a Claude Code (and Codex / Vercel AI SDK) hook layer. `reflex init [--global]` writes a hook entry into .claude/settings.json (or ~/.claude/settings.json) for PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest, UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart and PreCompact, all with matcher '' and 3 s timeout, via a shim at ~/.reflex/bin/reflex-hook. Cheap deterministic checks find candidates (destructive commands, including ones hidden in scripts; duplicate reads; polling loops; oversized output). Jev is then asked boolean or choice questions (outOfScope, destructive, irreversible, and a requested/needed/unrelated/forbidden verdict) about the proposed call against the task, the constraints and the last 8 calls. A fixed policy turns the answer into allow, note, ask (native permission prompt), deny or skip. It also trims large tool output through updatedResponse, restates constraints on each prompt, and re-injects a session ledger after compaction. Alpha, single author, released 2026-09-21.
interface: CLI reflex doctor | report | stats | watch | replay --last N [--import] | clean | serve
entries.autoInvocation: Deterministic hooks. Nothing has to be prompted: after `reflex init --global` and a restart, every tool call goes through the hook, and Jev is consulted automatically when a candidate is found. There is no model-discretion path.
security: No curl|sh installer and no npm postinstall. The npm package is a plain compiled dist and matches the source. There is no telemetry: the only network URL in src is api.typesafe.ai (grep of fetch and https across packages/reflex/src).

Key handling: the key is read from env or ~/.reflex/secrets.json. `reflex key` writes it in plaintext (mode 600, dir 700). It travels in the Authorization header, not in argv, but `reflex key jev <key>` puts it in argv and shell history. Setting it through the settings.json env block avoids that.

Redaction before sending or logging (state.ts:51-58) is regex-based: sk-, ghp_, AKIA, JWT, PEM blocks, and KEY=value pairs with sensitive names. The author admits it misses unlabelled secrets. It runs on the state sent to the provider (critic.ts:236).

`reflex init` writes to settings.json with JSON.parse and no backup. If the file has comments or invalid JSON, init throws and does nothing. It replaces the file with plain JSON, so it could reformat the user's existing global settings. Back the file up first, or hand-write the hook entries.

The shim ~/.reflex/bin/reflex-hook is a shell script that execs the global reflex-hook or a hardcoded node path, and it runs on every tool call. The paths are checked against a safe charset (cli.ts:55). Trust is the same as for any global npm package.

PostToolUse can rewrite tool output the model sees (trim, or a collapsed 'identical' line). This is a correctness risk if a trim hides needed lines. Error lines are kept, and the original is archived under ~/.reflex/archive with redaction applied (secrets are redacted in the archive, not only in what is sent).
entries.dataEgress: To the provider (Jev at api.typesafe.ai by default, or wherever TYPESAFE_BASE_URL points), only for calls that reach the model. At level ask these are destructive-pattern hits and writes, exec, vcs and db calls. Reads are only judged at level ultra. Payload: the first prompt and latest prompt (up to 600 chars), the extracted constraints, the last 8 tool calls as one-line summaries (160 chars) with 80-char result digests, and the proposed call's summary. Postcall judging also sends a 600-char result digest. All of it goes through regex redaction. Full file contents and full tool outputs are not sent, but command lines, file paths and prompt text are, and on client projects that includes client task text. Locally, everything is logged to ~/.reflex (sessions jsonl, archive of trimmed outputs, decision cache). No other telemetry.
entries.failureMode: Fail-open. providerTimeoutMs is 1500 (config.ts:83) via AbortSignal.timeout (critic.ts:245). Any provider error is caught and the call proceeds with deterministic signals only. The hook's own timeout is 3 s. handleHook wraps everything in try/catch and returns undefined, logging to ~/.reflex/errors.log. The provider retries once on a 429 (waits up to 2 s, which can exceed the 1.5 s abort, so the retry is often cut short). A missing key means 'LIMITED' mode, with deterministic checks only. Caveat: the deterministic parts fail closed for the user. Duplicate reads are denied and destructive patterns go to a permission prompt regardless of Jev. In bypass permissions mode, a hook 'ask' may still surface a prompt, and 'ask' at level ask conflicts with the user's habit of bypass or auto mode. This is untested here.
entries.contextCost: Zero MCP tools and zero tool-definition tokens. Injected text comes only from hooks. A UserPromptSubmit line '[reflex] Constraints still in effect...' appears on each prompt, but only when imperative constraints were detected (tens of tokens). Ledger text after compaction or resume is bounded. '[reflex] ...' notes and deny reasons are one line each. The context gauge is a user-facing systemMessage. The net effect can be negative on tokens, since trimming reduces context (author claims of 63% fewer input tokens and a $1.75 to $0.28 routing saving apply to the AI SDK adapter, not to Claude Code).
pros: It is the one candidate here that meets the requirement of automatic use without prompting. It is a real, working hook set on 7 Claude Code events, written into settings.json, and Claude never has to be told to use Jev.

It uses Jev for what a System-1 model is suited to: typed boolean and choice questions about whether a destructive command or a constraint-violating edit fits the stated task. Each judged call is one small round trip and returns probabilities only.

The endpoint path in the code (`/v1/systemone`) is the same as OpenRouter's System One path. OpenRouter is reachable with only three env vars (TYPESAFE_BASE_URL, TYPESAFE_MODEL, TYPESAFE_API_KEY) and no source changes, if the JSON schema matches.
Fail-open with a 1.5 s cap, so a slow or down Jev never blocks the session. Handler errors are swallowed and logged to errors.log.
Zero MCP context cost, no postinstall, no curl|sh, no telemetry. The tarball matches the source.
Has a shadow mode (level watch) and `reflex replay --last 20`, so the value can be measured on the user's own history before any enforcement.
Redaction of secrets before anything is sent or logged, plus private file modes. It targets the same kind of risk as the user's secret-leak guard, so there is a natural pairing.
It ships tests (about 87) and CI, and the README lists measured results, including negative ones (reads judged at coin-flip quality, so they are off outside ultra).
cons: Very immature: repo created 2026-09-20, npm 0.1.0 published 2026-09-21, 0 stars, 0 forks, 1 contributor, 57 commits in about a day, no releases. The 'measured' claims are the author's own and cannot be checked from here.

OpenRouter is not a supported provider. It works only through undocumented env overrides, and the request/response shape is explicitly unverified against real docs (jev.ts:4-7). There are no integration tests, and errors are swallowed, so a schema mismatch would look like 'Reflex is running' while judging nothing. `reflex doctor` only checks that a key is present, not that calls succeed.

The key variable is named TYPESAFE_API_KEY, and the OpenRouter key would have to be stored under that name. `reflex key` stores it in plaintext in ~/.reflex/secrets.json, and the hook processes do not inherit the shell env unless the settings.json `env` block or secrets.json is used.

Sends prompt text, command lines and paths to a third party (OpenRouter and then TypeSafe) from client projects. Regex redaction is admitted to be incomplete. Check client contracts before enabling it globally.

Most of the value is deterministic and does not need Jev (duplicate-read blocking, output trimming, constraint restatement, a ledger). The Jev-specific part is a narrow gate on destructive commands and writes. The user already runs bypass or auto permission mode, where Jev's 'ask' output is either suppressed or interrupts an intentionally unattended flow, and the author says the Jev decisions 'prompt only when it matters' relies on the native permission system.

Intrusive behaviours on a daily workflow: PostToolUse rewrites what the model sees, and duplicate reads and writes are denied ('identical call already made'). These can conflict with the existing GitNexus PostToolUse graph-context hook and the caveman plugin, since three or four global hooks would all act on the same Grep/Glob/Bash outputs. Hook order and interaction were not tested (static reading only).
`reflex init --global` rewrites ~/.claude/settings.json as plain JSON after JSON.parse, with no backup, and adds 7 hook groups with matcher '' (every tool, every event), each spawning a Node process.
Uses a hardcoded 3 s hook timeout. The 429 retry can wait up to 2 s, longer than the 1.5 s abort budget.
Skeptic point: an unverified router-like model behind the gate means its 0.75/0.70/0.97/0.99 scores come from four hand-picked contexts, not a benchmark.
entries.verdict: The only fully automatic Jev integration found: deterministic hooks in Claude Code plus fail-open Jev judging of destructive commands and edits against the task. Its OpenRouter route is unofficial (three env vars, `/v1/systemone` path matches, JSON schema unverified) and the project is one day old with a single author. Worth a supervised trial in `watch` or `ask` level with a project-level init and one live curl test of the OpenRouter endpoint. It is not something to install globally on client projects yet, and mostly redundant with the user's bypass/auto workflow and existing hooks.

judge.why: Two near-identical guardrail hook sets: a regex floor combined with Jev via Math.max so Jev can never loosen hard rules, shadow mode by default. Idea worth copying, unproven code.
pros: Deterministic PreToolUse, PostToolUse and Stop hooks; shadow mode default; fail-open on Jev error; decision log for later threshold tuning
Regex floor cannot be loosened by Jev, which is the right safety direction; MIT and CI, no build step
cons: 8 Noul questions on every tool call: latency and cost, and fail-open conflicts with a fail-closed secrets posture
0-1 stars, days old, no third-party testing; default model jev-latest and api.typesafe.ai need manual env overrides

entries.name: kerpopule/hermes-jev-skills
entries.what: Stdlib-only Python `jev` CLI (jevkit) plus 11 portable SKILL.md files and a Hermes plugin. For Claude Code, install.py copies the 11 skills to ~/.claude/skills (and ~/.codex, ~/.agents if present), 4 lane subagents (jev-lane-small/medium/high/escalate = haiku-low / sonnet-medium / opus-medium / opus-high) to ~/.claude/agents, a delimited ~1.9k-char "Model lanes" block to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (backed up first), and a `jev` symlink in ~/.local/bin. The CLAUDE.md block tells the orchestrator to run `jev lane classify --task ...` before delegating and `jev lane step --run <tests>` after each cycle. Automatic features (per-turn model routing, web-result injection screen, skill suggestion, command gate shadow) are Hermes-plugin-only; nothing is wired into Claude Code hooks.
interface: jev route / rerank / compact-select / pick-skill / choose / search / plan / triage / mail / supervise / ladder / spend / replay / dashboard
jev decide / score / route-to / gate / batch / shadow / ledger / policies / switches
Hermes plugin hermes-jev (not usable in CC)
entries.autoInvocation: Skill descriptions and one CLAUDE.md block, both at the model's discretion; no hooks (no PreToolUse/PermissionRequest/UserPromptSubmit/Stop wiring for Claude Code). The Hermes plugin's real automatic behaviours (pre_llm_call routing, web result screen, decide_tools) do not run in Claude Code. Claude Code only auto-picks lanes if Opus 5.5 chooses to follow the instruction when it delegates to subagents; the main-thread model is never switched.
security: Key handling is good: keystore.py resolves env then OS secret store then 0600 file; Linux store uses `secret-tool store` with the key on stdin (keystore.py ~195), not argv; macOS `security ... -w value` briefly puts key in a child's argv (acknowledged in a comment, irrelevant on Linux). `jev setup-key` serves a one-time localhost page with Host-header check, so the agent never sees the key. Caveat: store() also writes the key into every ~/.hermes profile .env if that dir exists.

OPENROUTER_API_KEY is read from process env first; if the user exports it via settings env, every Bash subprocess (and the agent) can read it; it is not in no-secret-leak.cjs protected list yet (user-side gap, not the candidate's).

Shell exec: `jev lane step --run <cmd>` runs the agent-supplied string with shell=True, cwd=repo, 900s timeout (lanes.py:145) - equivalent to Bash tool, but it bypasses Claude Code Bash permission rules/hooks matching, since the permission sees only `jev lane step ...`. Under bypass/auto mode this is a permission-laundering path for the arbitrary command in --run.

Installer modifies ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (backup + marker block, additive and removable via --uninstall), writes ~/.claude/agents and skills, symlinks ~/.local/bin/jev to the checkout (executes code from the clone on every call; a compromised update = code exec). Also touches ~/.codex/~/.agents skills and Hermes config if present. --check dry-run and --no-claude-md exist.

Prompt-injection surface: skills instruct the agent to pass task text to a third-party model; Jev's outputs are typed (closed action ids, thresholds in code), and code-first pre-rules/risk words are enforced locally; jev rerank has an injection screen for passages. Independent evals say injected instructions in state can move Jev answers - mitigated only partly by local rails.

No telemetry found: outbound hosts in code are the four Jev providers, models.dev/api.json (catalog, key names only), key-setup links; plan.py has an OpenRouter v1 base for a computer-use planner (chat completions, separate feature). Logs hold decisions only, per README. Not exhaustively audited (678-line installer, ~50 modules, 216 files).
entries.dataEgress: For Claude Code lane use: `jev lane classify` sends the task text you pass (redacted, capped 3,000 chars) plus optional --context line; `lane step` sends task text, a diff stat and the last ~15 lines/1,200 chars of each check's output (redacted; sensitive-looking text is withheld); paths outside the diff stat and whole logs/files are not sent; `facts` never sent. Other commands per README: route sends the redacted turn up to 2,500 chars; rerank 900 chars/passage; search question + result snippets; gate command up to 2,000 chars with comments stripped. Everything goes to openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions (when JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter), with HTTP-Referer github URL and X-Title 'Hermes Jev Skills'. `jev models` fetches models.dev/api.json (no data uploaded). A separate `jev doctor` verify call sends a synthetic sentence. Client work is included in task text whenever the agent writes it into --task, so client-project use needs a private-profile equivalent (only Hermes `private_profiles` exists).
entries.failureMode: Fail-open everywhere by design: no key, timeout (lane commands default 4 s, routing 2.5 s), 4xx/429/5xx, malformed reply, or low confidence all yield keep_current/no_opinion/verify-yourself (client.py JevError codes, retry loop bounded by total wall-clock budget; state_too_large at 60k chars; every reply validated against the asked question). Gate never approves on Jev failure (gate.py header). Caveat: fail-open here means 'do nothing extra', and since invocation is by model discretion there is no hard enforcement either way. `lane step` failures in the subprocess check (exit 124/127) are reported as evidence, not hidden.
entries.contextCost: No MCP tools, no hook-injected text. Always-on cost is static: CLAUDE.md lanes block ~1.9k chars (~480 tokens) every session; 11 skill descriptions (~150-250 chars each, ~2.3k chars, ~600 tokens incl. names) against the 2% skillListingBudgetFraction; 4 subagent descriptions (~250 chars each, ~250 tokens). Total roughly 1.3k tokens of standing context. Loading a full SKILL.md when triggered: 4.8k-16k chars each (jev-computer-use 16k = ~4k tokens; model-routing 9.5k = ~2.4k tokens). Each `jev` call adds a Bash tool call plus JSON result (~200-500 tokens).
pros: OpenRouter is a first-class, native backend: client.py:30-31 posts {state, model, questions} to /api/alpha/decisions with Bearer OPENROUTER_API_KEY; JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter selects it; no patching needed.

Strong engineering for safety and privacy: per-feature egress documented and enforced by redaction, secret-looking text never sent, question-shape validation, reply validation against the asked question, fail-open codes, risk words never route cheapest, gate never approves on failure.
Key handling well designed: secret-tool with stdin (no argv leak on Linux), one-time localhost setup page, --tty mode, JEV_PROXY_API_KEY isolation so provider keys never go to override hosts.
Installer is additive/removable: --check dry run, CLAUDE.md marker block with timestamped backup, --no-claude-md, --uninstall, agents only overwritten if they carry the managed marker.

Broad offline test suite (59 files, incl. test_install, test_lanes, test_custom_endpoint, test_gate); shadow-mode + `jev shadow report` culture and measured evals (lane replay: Sonnet lane -51% cost on 9 commits with parity, honest that Haiku was not cheapest).

jevkit is a reusable stdlib CLI: `jev decide`/`jev gate` with JSON policies could be wrapped by the user's own PermissionRequest hook (gate-strict/gate-task policies already model command-risk questions and return approve/ask_human/deny/no_opinion).
cons: No Claude Code hooks: nothing runs unless Claude decides to; this fails the user's core requirement of automatic use without prompting. Main automatic value (per-turn routing, web-injection screening, skill suggestion) is Hermes-only.

The Claude Code value proposition is downshifting delegated subagents to Haiku/Sonnet; with Opus 5.5 main and subscription billing this saves subscription usage only marginally, adds a Bash round-trip before each delegation, and the author's own data shows lanes barely help when work already runs at a mid model (-3.9% on 2,656 runs; 9-commit replay is a tiny sample).

Standing context ~1.3k tokens (CLAUDE.md block + 11 skill descriptions + 4 agent descriptions), much of it irrelevant to daily coding (mailbox, social research, computer/browser use, frontier-work Hermes ladder).

`jev lane step --run <cmd>` executes shell=True commands outside Claude Code's permission/hook matching; combined with bypassPermissions/auto and the existing fail-closed no-secret-leak hook, this is a hook-bypass path unless jev is denied or wrapped.

Provider precedence: TYPESAFE_API_KEY, keychain and credentials file win over OpenRouter unless JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter is set; installer symlinks ~/.local/bin/jev into a git checkout (unpinned code exec on update) and writes ~/.claude and ~/.codex; OPENROUTER_API_KEY not yet protected by user's leak hook.

Very young (created 2026-09-18, v0.22.0 in 11 days, 114 commits, 89 by one author, some bot-like committers), large surface (50 modules, 216 files) for a small useful core; uses ~typesafe/jev-latest moving alias on an /alpha endpoint with no SLA; Jev evals show calibration and injection weaknesses, and client-project task text would leave the machine with no private-profile control outside Hermes.
entries.verdict: Well-built, OpenRouter-native and fail-open, but for Claude Code it is only skills plus a CLAUDE.md nudge and lane subagents with no hooks, so it will not deliver automatic use and its lane routing adds ~1.3k standing tokens for marginal gain on an Opus-main subscription setup. Best treated as a source of reusable pieces (jevkit client, gate/decide policies, question-writing docs) rather than installed wholesale.

entries.name: QuentinCody/interlinked-cli
entries.what: Local guard harness for Claude Code/Codex: deterministic PreToolUse rules, audit log, skills; opt-in fail-open Jev checks (Stop claim-evidence nudge, test-title, doc-claim liveness).
entries.autoInvocation: deterministic hook (PreToolUse guard; Jev Stop nudge opt-in, may have been removed from daemon Stop dispatch per docs/e2e-testing.md)
pros: Real Claude Code hook integration, heavy CI/benchmarks, uninstall/disable exit ramp
Jev use is warn-only, fail-open, default OFF, tighten-only, so safe
Deterministic core blocks destructive commands/secrets/unvetted deps in ms
cons: Jev endpoint hardcoded api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone with TYPESAFE_API_KEY; needs patch/endpoint override for OpenRouter
Large invasive installer that overlaps existing no-secret-leak and would add hooks alongside gitnexus
Jev part is minor; installed via npm from GitHub (supply-chain review needed)

entries.name: savinofiore/lexi
entries.what: TDD-first workflow plugin (mechanical test-first guard) with an optional bundled jev plugin: session/subagent model+effort router hook, verbatim tool-call compaction hook, and Jev diff code-review skill.
entries.autoInvocation: deterministic hook (router, compaction) + skill/command for review
pros: Covers three categories in Claude Code: router per session/subagent, compaction that keeps tool calls verbatim (Jev keep/truncate/drop), code review with verdict computed in code
Falls back safely (native summary) on timeout/error; router is once-per-session so prompt cache is preserved; has router/compact/review tests
Jev is opt-in per project via .lexi.json; key in settings env
